forceful-blow|function.name: Forceful Blow
forceful-blow|function.summary: 15 feet is a decently large distance, easily putting nearly any enemy out of reach of your allies. The ability to follow them for free means that you can remain in melee with them after pushing them. Note that this says “straight away”, not just “away”, so you can’t use it to launch enemies into the air without some extra steps.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(187); });

hamstring-blow|the-only-reach-weapon-wit.name: Hamstring Blow
hamstring-blow|the-only-reach-weapon-wit.source:
the only
		reach weapon with the Slow mastery
hamstring-blow|the-only-reach-weapon-wit.summary: 15 feet is a big speed penalty. If you expect to apply other speed penalties, such as from the Slow mastery, you can make it effectively impossible for enemies to move away from you in order to attack your allies. If you’re using a whip (the only reach weapon with the Slow mastery), you can apply hit-and-run tactics and slow enemies enough that they can’t catch up to you, effectively eliminating melee-only enemies with no effort.

staggering-blow|unknown.name: Staggering Blow
staggering-blow|unknown.summary: If you can land this, your target is vulnerable to the next save-or-suck effect that your party can hit them with. If they’re affected by something that allows repeated saves, such as Hold Monster, you can time this to affect that save and keep them under the effect, effectively locking your target out of combat and turning them into a piñata.

sundering-blow|unknown.name: Sundering Blow
sundering-blow|unknown.summary: Great if you have allies who do more damage in a single hit than you do, such as a Rogue.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Never a bad choice, but less impactful for martial characters than for full casters.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(197); });

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: This offers a useful crowd control option and the ability to easily generate Heroic Inspiration. Since it forces a save, it can also extend Rage.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Inspiring Strike is great for the Barbarian. Since you have Reckless Attack, you can easily roll 4 d20’s on attack rolls every turn once you have Extra Attack, giving you plenty of opportunities to crit. However, Reassert Honor won’t do much for you because you have Reckless Attack.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Grab proficiency in Insight and hand out Inspiration to the party.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Barbarians rely on small numbers of attacks with big weapons, so Savage Attacker is a decent damage boost.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Barbarians don’t have the ability scores to support a lot of skills, and the ones that you can handle will be buffed by Rage enough that you probably don’t need more proficiencies.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: Not useful. The push+damage option is neat, but redundant with Brutal Strikes once you hit level 9, or you could just use a weapon with the Push mastery.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Great on a class that routinely draws attacks made with Advantage. Rage’s damage resistance will make this even more impactful.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: An easy choice on any melee build. If you have an easy source of Heroic Inspiration, such as someone in the party with Musician, this is a huge asset for your whole party.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: You won’t get much value out of this since it’s mostly spellcasting, but you may be able to get some utility options to use outside of combat and you can elect False Life for the leveled spell. But if you just want more hp, Tough is a much better choice.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(198); });

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: A good fit for Barbarians looking to protect their allies even if you don’t use the spellcasting.

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: A decent choice for many martial characters. A climb speed is the next best thing to a fly speed. The ability to stand up quickly makes falling or being knocked prone less of a problem. The ability to jump with less of a running start may let you easily jump over difficult terrain and other obstacles which otherwise might slow your movement in combat.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: The bonus damage doesn’t scale, but that’s not why you’re here. The push effect will stack with the Push mastery and with the push option from Brutal Strikes. Combining the three lets you push enemies a total of 35 feet away, putting most creatures outside of their ability to get back into melee without dashing. Add Crusher and you can get that up to 40 feet. The word “away” also doesn’t specify that it needs to be “directly away”, so you can launch enemies into the air, too, but that’s arguably an abuse case. I don’t recommend doing that unless your DM is totally okay with it. WotC clearly knows that this is an issue because several other push effects use the phrase “directly away”, but they omitted “directly” from a few usages in the 2024 rules.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: An excellent source of additional healing and of Temporary Hit Points. THP on a Barbarian are fantastic because Rage can stretch their effectiveness, and better efficiency from Short Rest healing helps make up for how much damage Barbarians typically absorb. I’ve used Chef on a Barbarian in a long campaign, and it was absolutely amazing.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: A simple and easy way to control enemies’ positions in combat, especially when combined with the Push mastery.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: Only usable with a Finesse weapon, which severely limits your options, but for a class that thrives in melee this can do a lot to improve your durability. Advantage on attacks is a bit more than +3 on average, so once your Proficiency Bonus hits +4 you’re more than offsetting the drawback of Reckless attack, at least against melee attacks. For barbarians using two-weapon fighting or a whip, this is worth considering.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: You have Rage for exactly these damage types.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Two-weapon fighting is absolutely viable for the Barbarian, and your Rage damage bonus provides a helpful flat bonus on the additional attacks which can make up for not applying your ability modifier to the damage. The Bonus Action attack from the Enhanced Dual Wielding feature appears to be separate from the one granted by the Light weapon property, so if you’re using two Light weapons and one has the Nick mastery, you may be able to attack with your second weapon both during your Attack action and as a Bonus Action, allowing you to make 3 total attacks (4 with Extra Attack) in a turn. We’re still waiting to see if the rules will be clarified for this. However, there are some issues: The Bonus Action attack conflicts with the Bonus Action to activate Rage, and building around Great Weapon Master will still deal more damage.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: Not as good as you would hope. The Bonus Action to spend a Hit Point Die notably does not add your Constitution modifier, which makes it an expensive and frustrating way to burn through your Hit Point Dice very quickly with minimal impact. Unless your party has some other deep, inexpensive healing resource, you need those dice for Short Rests to refill your massive pool of hit points. Take Chef instead.

grappler|phb.name: Grappler
grappler|phb.summary: An interesting alternative to using Reckless Attack. If you also make an Unarmed Strike to knock your target prone, you can hold them prone and keep their speed at 0 to prevent them from standing. This gives you Advantage on your melee attacks and gives them Disadvantage, which is safer (though slower) than using Reckless Attack. However, remember that Brutal Strike still requires you to use Reckless Attack and negates all Advantage on the attack, so this may fall out of favor once you get Brutal Strike at level 9.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Simple, easy, and reliable. A must have for any Barbarian using two-handed weapons, though it’s fine to wait until level 8 when you have Extra Attack and your Proficiency Bonus is higher than the +2 you have at level 4.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: Heavy armor disables many of your class features.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: The Guarded Mind feature gives you an easy solution to the Barbarian’s biggest weakness in combat. Concentration Breaker is only situationally useful, but Guarded Mind will come into play constantly.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Improve your Constitution and/or Dexterity and use Unarmored Defense.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: Expertise in Perception could be nice, but Rage already makes it a Strength check and gives you Advantage on Strength checks, so you already have a way to boost Perception if you need one. Of course, that doesn’t help when you’re not Raging, which is likely when you need Perception most.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: Too situational, and you’re already really good at Strength saves.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: An easy damage boost if you’re using piercing weapons like pikes.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: Pole Strike will fight for space with the Bonus Action to activate Rage, but many Barbarians don’t use their Bonus Action in combat once they’re raging. The Reactive Strike feature is a reliable and easy boost to your damage output, and makes you even better as your party’s Defender.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: Encourage Ally is a great pool of Temporary Hit Points, and the fact that it can be based on your Strength score is excellent. Last Stand may feel redundant with Reckless Attack, but it will allow you to stop using Reckless Attack when your health is low so you don’t need to make that high-risk gamble.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Choosing Dexterity will make your Dextersity saves very reliable when you also consider Danger Sense. Resilient (Wisdom) is nice, but I recommend Mage Slayer instead since it’s a guarantee.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: Not a good feat. You don’t get enough rituals, and they can only be level 1.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: An excellent choice for any melee character.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Tempting if you’re building around throwing weapons, but there’s little reason to do so.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: Shield Bash is an easy way to knock enemies Prone without using a Toppling weapon. If you combine this with Tavern Brawler, you can make an Unarmed Strike, Grapple, then knock your target Prone all with a single attack. Interpose Shield combines very nicely with Danger Sense, frequently allowing to avoid damage from area damage effects like fireballs and breath weapons.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: The Barbarian has very few good skill options, and their best options will all be enhanced by Rage enough that you probably don’t need Expertise.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Combine the Hamstring feature with a weapon with the Slow mastery, and you can give one creature a 20-foot speed penalty. Add Brutal Strike, and you can make that a 35-foot speed penalty. That puts most enemies at 0. Even if it doesn’t, you have a huge mobility advantage. Use a reach weapon, and you can hit enemies from outside of their reach, then take a few steps to get too far away for them to chase you without spending their Action to Dash. Unfortunately, the only slashing weapon with Slow is the Whip, so your options for this combo are limited and it means giving up a bigger damage die.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: More speed is nice, but hit-and-run tactics aren’t common for the Barbarian, and, if you want to do that, there are better options. Of course, you might want to intentionally trigger Opportunity Attacks in order to benefit your allies, which is occasionally useful. If you do so, try to trigger Reckless Attack after you’re done so that you don’t negate the Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: While Barbarians can’t abuse the grapple mechanics quite as well as they could in the 2014 rules, Barbarians are still good grapplers, and using chains/manacles/rope to bind a creature is absurdly powerful considering how easy it is. Binding a creature in chains requires a Strength (Athletics) check, which should be effortless while you’re raging, and the increased DC to escape will keep enemies Restrained.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: You already get two, and it’s unlikely that you need more. If you need more, you’re using two-weapon fighting with two different weapons and also want mastery in a different weapon for fighting at range.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: Even though this doesn’t provide an increase to an Ability Score that the Barbarian needs to increase, it’s an amazing feat for the Barbarian. If you’re running Reckless Attack, you’re going to be hit with attacks, which means that Zhentarim Tactics will reliably get you extra attacks essentially every turn.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is pretty great.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Power From Pain is a decent damage boost for the Barbarian since it’s so easy to become Bloodied.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: If you picked up Bloodlust, this is a tempting combo, allowing you to heal for 12 + Con PB times per Long Rest. But this still isn’t worth taking unless you’re going to benefit from the extra Temporary Hit Points on regular basis.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Brutal Strike negates any Advantage on your attack, making it less reliable than your regular attacks. This removes that problem.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Rage will give you resistance to weapon damage types, but by this level many enemies attacks will deal multiple damage types with their attacks. This provides a lot of extra durability once you’re Bloodied, which will keep you fighting. Once you’re Bloodied, look for sources of Temporary Hit Points to stretch your hp as far as possible.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: The teleportation is excellent, but the ability score increases are hard choices for the Barbarian.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character. Even if you’re a bear totem barbarian, you’re not resistant to force, psychic, necrotic, or radiant damage. This won’t help against force damage, but it can cover two of the other three at a time.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: Good on any character, but the ability score increases are hard for the Barbarian.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: More durability is always nice. If you’re a Zealot or have another way to repeatedly heal yourself in small amounts like the Durable feat or Boon of Recovery, the additional healing whenever you regain hit points is a nice bonus.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: Easy and simple. With two attacks and Reckless Attack you’re rolling four d20’s to attack. Even if you only ever get one Epic Boon, you could have 25 Strength at level 20, and adding 25 damage to a hit is a hefty bonus. If you want to fish for this damage bonus, give two-weapon fighting a look so that you’re making more attack rolls in a turn.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Extended reach is great, but you likely already have a use for your Bonus Action by this level.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is helpful insurance, but the pool of healing won’t get you very far.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: You could use this for a utility of some kind, but there aren’t many utility spells which you’ll want every Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list (neither care about your stats).

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Generally an easy go-to option, but the Barbarian doesn’t have the ability scores to back up most skills, and the ones that you’re good at are covered by Rage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: More speed is great, but the Dexterity increase is only appealing if you’re going for Unarmored Defense and you’ve already maxed out Constitution.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Free invisibility is amazing on any character, but this gets absolutely crazy on Warrior of Shadow, allowing you to cast Darkness and get more benefits than you would from Superior Defense.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: The healing is disappointing, but two damage resistances is nice.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Probably your only option for handling invisible enemies, but the ability scores are hard. If you’ve made it this far, your party is covering for you or you’ve found a creative solution.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: You can get the crucial Strength increase, but that’s the only appeal here.

chondathan-freeboter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freeboter
chondathan-freeboter|frhof.summary: Excellent for a Barbarian looking to be useful outside of combat. The Ability Scores are good, the skills are decent, and you get Skilled. Use Skilled to get proficiency in Thieves’ Tools and you could be a passable Scout.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Perfect Ability Scores, but the feat and skills are horrible.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: The feat will work to extend Rage because it forces a save, but everything else about this is a bad fit.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: A good option for front-line martials. The ability scores are great, and Tough is an easy go-to feat if you don’t want more complexity, but you won’t get much use out of the skills.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: An easy choice, this gets you Strength and Constiution increases, Tough, and two decent skills for the Barbarian.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and perception is a great skill. Alert isn’t crucial for most martial characters, but remember that you can trade initiative with a willing ally to help an allied spellcaster act early.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: You can get a Strength increase and Lucky, but everything else is a bit fit.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Perfect Ability Scores and a good feat, but terrible skills.

knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.name: Knight of the Gauntlet
knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.summary: Workable Ability Scores, but Tyro of the Gauntlet isn’t great, and the skills are terribe.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: Almost good, but nothing here is quite a good fit. You can still get a Strength increase, the Lords’ Alliance Agent feat is decent, and you get one passable skill.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: Strength and Skilled are fine, but that’s all that you get, and that’s not enough.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Good Ability Scores, Purple Dragon Rook works for the Barbarian, and you get one passable skill.

rashemi-wanderer|frhof.name: Rashemi Wanderer
rashemi-wanderer|frhof.summary: Good Ability Scores, Tough, and decent skills for the Barbarian.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores and one good skill, but Tavern Brawler is minimally useful for the Barbarian, especially once you get Brutal Strikes at level 9.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: Good ability scores for the Barbarian, and Savage Attacker is good feat for the weapons that Barbarians typically use, especially since you’ll never get more than two attacks, but Athletics is borderline useless in the 2024 rules, and Intimidation won’t help you much since you’re probably going to dump Charisma.

vampire-devotee|aboh.name: Vampire Devotee
vampire-devotee|aboh.summary: Good Ability Scores and Vampire’s Plaything is decent, but the skills are bad.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Bad Ability Scores, bad feat, only one good skill.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: You can get a Strength increase, Zhentarim Ruffian is decent, and you get one good skill. On its own, this Background is fine, but Zhentarim Tactics is absolutely amazing, so you might take this just to easily qualify for Zhentarim Tactics.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: Good Ability Scores, but the skills are bad you’ll get very little value out of Aberrant Dragonmark since it’s mostly spellcasting.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: If you want a Dragonmark on a Barbarian, this is it. Perfect Ability Scores, good skills, and the feat gives you +1d4 to the skills and a great Reaction option to protect your allies. Even if you never cast Shield even once, it’s pretty good.

house-kundarak-heir|efota.name: House Kundarak Heir
house-kundarak-heir|efota.summary: Good Ability Scores, but nothing else here works easily for the Barbarian.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances to damage types which are frequently used to bypass resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing damage, and a once per day transformation that offers flight or options to handle crowds, both of which are challenges for most Barbarians. The Bonus Action cost to activate Celestial Revelation does conflict with Rage, but waiting until turn 2 to have both effects running should be fine since it’s only once per day. Healing Hands is a nice splash of healing, but you’ll likely only use it to rescue dying allies since the healing won’t make a dent in the Barbarian’s massive pool of hit points.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: A damage resistance, likely to a common damage type like poison or fire, and a decent way to handle crowds of small enemies. The 2024 Barbarian’s Rage can be extended by forcing enemies to make a saving throw, in part specifically to support Dragonborn Barbarians using their breath. You also get Darkvision and flight once per day.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and even more hit points. Tremorsense is only situationally useful, but it may also be your only way to handle hidden or invisible enemies, making it a useful tool for the Barbarian.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision, an extra skill, and Fey Ancestry are all great for the Barbarian. Things get difficult when we look at innate spellcasting since many of the options are combat spells that rely on Concentration. Wood Elf may be viable here, however, since Druidcraft has no combat application, Longstrider doesn’t require Concentration, and Pass Without Trace isn’t helpful for Barbarians in combat. Altogether, the Wood Elf offers some interesting utility, though not being able to recast the innate spells does make them less useful than they are for spellcasting classes.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great. The Barbarian’s biggest weakness is their mental saves, and Gnomish Cunning does a lot to help. However, Advantage when you have a low or even negative ability modifier may not get you very far at high levels.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: The Giant Ancestry options provide some very exciting effects, especially when you combine the on-hit effects with Weapon Mastery and eventually with Brutal Strikes. Personally, I like Hill’s Tumble and Stone’s Endurance for melee martial builds, but nearly all of the options are worth consideration. Large Form and and Powerful Build are both neat, but they won’t be as impactful as Giant Ancestry.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Brave and Lucky are both nice, but not enough on their own. Halfling Nimbleness is neat, but rarely impactful since you can already move through allies’ spaces and if you need to get past an enemy it should involve hurting them. Naturally Stealthy isn’t helpful for the front-line martial characters.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Advantage on two mental saves and resistance to Psychic damage. Mental saves are one of the Barbarian’s biggest weaknesses, but rolling with Advantage may not be enough to save you if your modifier is still -1.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Darkvision, Fey Ancestry, a Cantrip, a skill or tool, and the ability to negate the Unconscious condition once per Long Rest. This isn’t as easy to pick as the Human, and the Cantrip may see very little use, but the versatility is nice and the ability to change both the Cantrip and the proficiency may be helpful.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is an excellent option for the Barbarian, allowing them to move between targets more easily in combat and padding their hit points even further. Remember that while you’re raging your damage resistances will also protect your Temporary Hit Points, doubling their effectiveness against bludgeoning/piercing/slashing damage. Relentless Endurance provides a safety net in case things go badly for you. Darkvision is great, too.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Lots of good choices here. Beasthide makes you more durable, longtooth gives you more damage output, and Wildhunt can negate the drawback of Reckless Attack. You’ll have some difficulty getting both Shifting and Rage going at the same time since both require your Bonus Action, but otherwise it’s great.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting that you won’t be able to use effectively. The Dragonborn is directly comparable and a much better fit for the Barbarian.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: +1 AC, some resistances and immunities, and no need to sleep. A great formula for a simple, durable barbarian. Be sure to pick up proficiency in Perception to capitalize on the fact that you don’t need sleep so that you can remain alert and watch over your party during long rests.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

animal-handling|wis.name: Animal Handling
animal-handling|wis.summary: (Wis): Not really helpful for the function of the Barbarian.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(196); });

athletics|str.name: Athletics
athletics|str.summary: (Str): The only Strength-based skill, and it’s borderline useless. The one appealing use is binding creatures in chains, which is appealing for Strength-based builds since chains/manacles/rope are so incredibly overpowered in the 2024 rules.

intimidation|cha.name: Intimidation
intimidation|cha.summary: (Cha): Useful while raging, and likely your only viable social skill.

nature|int.name: Nature
nature|int.summary: (Int): Intelligence is a dump stat for Barbarians, but if no one in the party has access to Nature, it’s not an awful choice.

perception|wis.name: Perception
perception|wis.summary: (Wis): One of the most important skills in the game. At least two people in the party should have it, but more is always better.

survival|wis.name: Survival
survival|wis.summary: (Wis): Adventuring tends to involve a lot of wandering around in untamed wilderness, so Survival can be very helpful to your party. However, actual Survival checks are exceptionally rare.

battle-axe-maul|function.name: Battle Axe / Maul
battle-axe-maul|function.summary: Topple is fine, but it’s only appealing in melee if you have other melee allies. If you want Advantage, you already have Reckless Attack.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(600); });

glaive-greatsword|unknown.name: Glaive / Greatsword
glaive-greatsword|unknown.summary: The Graze mastery is good insurance for characters with a chance to miss, but you’re going to maximize Strength and then use Reckless Attack, so missing will be rare until Brutal Strike comes online, and Graze doesn’t help with Brutal Strike.

greataxe-halberd|unknown.name: Greataxe / Halberd
greataxe-halberd|unknown.summary: Cleave is probably your only option for handling crowds. The additional attack will apply your Rage damage bonus, but it may be difficult to use reliably since the second target needs to be adjacent to the first.

longsword-war-pick|unknown.name: Longsword / War Pick
longsword-war-pick|unknown.summary: The Sap mastery offsets the penalty for Reckless Attack, adding to your durability without cutting into your damage output.

pike-warhammer|unknown.name: Pike / Warhammer
pike-warhammer|unknown.summary: Push becomes very appealing once you get Brutal Strike and can launch enemies 25 feet away in one hit.

rapier-shortsword|unknown.name: Rapier / Shortsword
rapier-shortsword|unknown.summary: Vex isn’t helpful when you have Reckless Attack.

scimitar|unknown.name: Scimitar
scimitar|unknown.summary: Crucial if you plan to use two-weapon fighting. Only your secondary weapons needs to have Nick, so strongly consider pairing a scimitar with a different light weapon.

trident|unknown.name: Trident
trident|unknown.summary: Your go-to ranged option. With the Thrown property and the Topple mastery, you can throw these at flying enemies to knock them prone, causing most flying enemies to fall.

whip|unknown.name: Whip
whip|unknown.summary: The only weapon with Reach and with the Slow mastery.

hide|unknown.name: Hide
hide|unknown.summary: Unarmored Defense will almost certainly match Hide’s maximum of 14 AC. Skip this and save your gold for half plate.

breastplate|stealth.name: Breastplate
breastplate|stealth.summary: Trade 1 AC to not get Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

half-plate|unknown.name: Half plate
half-plate|unknown.summary: will provide more AC than your Unarmored Defense until your total modifiers in Dexterity and Constitution add up to +7. Expect to spend most of your career in half plate unless you need to be stealthy.

fighter|unknown.name: Fighter
fighter|unknown.summary: Additional Weapon Mastery options and a Fighting Style feat. Not essential, but helpful. If you’re looking at two-weapon fighting, this is more useful than if you’re fighting with a single weapon.

monk|unknown.name: Monk
monk|unknown.summary: Unarmored Defense abilities don’t stack. You use the calculation that gives you the highest AC, and your Wisdom should not exceed your Constitution. That said, if you’re fighting unarmored, you can still use Martial Arts even while raging, making it a tempting choice if your subclass doesn’t lean heavily on your Bonus Action.

frenzy|reckless-attack.name: Frenzy
frenzy|reckless-attack.summary: While Raging, the first hit you land on your turn while using Reckless Attack does extra damage equal to Xd6 where X is your Rage Damage, so 2d6 when you get this feature and scaling to 4d6 at level 16. Like an angriest Sneak Attack, it’s just extra d6s of damage once per your turn while doing something you were going to do anyway (Reckless Attack). It’s straightforward and effective

mindless-rage|unknown.name: Mindless Rage
mindless-rage|unknown.summary: This makes you immune to two ways to take you out of combat without wearing down your huge pile of hit points.

retaliation|unknown.name: Retaliation
retaliation|unknown.summary: Absolutely fantastic. We can also can grapple or shove the target as our Retaliation since you’re able to make an Unarmed Strike.

intimidating-presence|unknown.name: Intimidating Presence
intimidating-presence|unknown.summary: Excellent crowd control, giving you a way to debuff big groups of enemies while you focus on them one at a time. The usage limitation is tight, and the cost to recharge it is high, so save this for encounters with multiple enemies. Burning this on single targets is an absolute waste unless you’re trying to burn through Legendary Resistances.

animal-speaker|unknown.name: Animal Speaker
animal-speaker|unknown.summary: Speak with Animals is exactly as useful as your DM decides that it will be. Beasts are abundant in most environments on the material plane, but they might not be willing or able to tell you anything useful.

bear|unknown.name: Bear
bear|unknown.summary: Damage resistance to most damage types in the game. Force, Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant are commonly used to overcome damage resistances, and resistance to them is rare. If you can keep enemies focused on you, this will reduce a lot of damage over the course of your career. Despite its general effectiveness, Bear won’t be useful in every fight. Reserve it for when you’re facing enemies that can deal non-weapon damage types, like dragons or spellcasters.

eagle|unknown.name: Eagle
eagle|unknown.summary: This is a ton of additional mobility, but unless you build and play to benefit from that mobility, it will provide very little value. The easiest option is to use this to quickly reach high-priority enemies, but in many fights that’s not difficult. Your best bet is to use the mobility in combination with grappling the Push Weapon Mastery to force enemies into dangerous positions, such as in a tight group, so that allied spellcasters can hit them with area damage. In a party with multiple Blasters, this is very powerful.

wolf|unknown.name: Wolf
wolf|unknown.summary: Excellent in a party that relies heavily on attacks, and the larger your party is, the better this gets. Parties with Fighters, Monks, Warlocks, or spellcasters that like to summon creatures will all get a ton of value from this. Because this is consistently useful if even one other person in your party relies on attack rolls, this is the default when you go into combat. If you don’t know for certain that Bear or Eagle will provide value, Wolf is usually a safe bet.

owl|unknown.name: Owl
owl|unknown.summary: Darkvision is available from a huge number of Species, including up to 120 feet of Darkvision. This is only useful if you are a Species without Darkvision, if you can’t find a magic item to solve the problem, and if you can’t convince an allied spellcaster to cast Darkvision on you.

panther|unknown.name: Panther
panther|unknown.summary: The next best thing to a fly speed. If you don’t know for certain that you need Owl or Salmon, default to Panther.

salmon|unknown.name: Salmon
salmon|unknown.summary: Only situationally useful. Most games never require swimming.

nature-speaker|unknown.name: Nature Speaker
nature-speaker|unknown.summary: Only situationally useful. Unless you’re constantly exploring new, unmapped areas, you might never use this. If you’re in a hexcrawl, this might be fantastic.

falcon|eagle.name: Falcon
falcon|eagle.summary: Flight is extremely important at high levels, and flying without a spell or a magic item means that you can continue to fight in melee against flying enemies. If you don’t have any better ideas, combine this with Rage of the Wilds (Eagle), grapple an enemy or two, then fly them up into the air as high as possible before you drop them.

lion|unknown.name: Lion
lion|unknown.summary: Excellent, provided that you can prevent enemies from moving away from you. Consider the Sentinel feat or grappling.

ram|unknown.name: Ram
ram|unknown.summary: This is good, but you can use the Topple mastery to knock creatures prone.

vitality-surge|unknown.name: Vitality Surge
vitality-surge|unknown.summary: A nice pad of Temporary Hit Points. This will go an unusually long way when combined with the damage resistance from Rage, but you should only expect the THP to absorb 1 or 2 attacks per Rage, especially at low levels.

life-giving-force|unknown.name: Life-Giving Force
life-giving-force|unknown.summary: A huge amount of Temporary Hit Points, but you can’t use them on yourself, you may not be able to apply them consistently in combat, and they expire when your Rage ends. Fortunately, Rage has a 10-minute duration, so you and your party can stand around for a few turns feeling generally angry while you pass out THP. Since you apply this at the start of your turn while Raging, you won’t be able to use this until the turn after you Rage. Combat typically lasts 3 turns, so, if you Rage on turn 1, you might get to apply the THP twice in an encounter, and the points may not last long enough to have an effect. Allies need to be within 10 feet of you for you to target them, so encourage them to end their turns nearby. You can use Branches of the Tree to teleport them to you if necessary, but that occurs at the beginning of their turn, so they may be able to walk to you without eating your Reaction. This amount of temporary hp is typically expensive and requires feats like Inspiring Leader or upcasting spells like False Life. With the durability provided by this, you can protect relatively frail allies like horses and familiars which otherwise become a liability early in the game since their hp doesn’t scale. You might even try mounted combat.

branches-of-the-tree|function.name: Branches of the Tree
branches-of-the-tree|function.summary: The obvious use here is to pull enemies adjacent to you and reduce their speed to 0, usually forcing them to spend their turn there. This can usually put your allies out of harm’s way, and if your target resorts to ranged attacks, they’ll make them at Disadvantage since they’re in your reach. You can also use this to help allies. Creatures can choose to willingly fail saving throws, and reducing the target’s speed to 0 is optional, so you can teleport allies out of dangerous positions, then let them spend the rest of their turn doing whatever they like. If you can fly, there’s nothing stopping you from using Branches of the Tree while airborn. This is dangerous for non-flying enemies because you can hit them with easy falling damage, but the ability to reduce flying enemies’ speed to 0 means that you can force them to fall, too, giving you an easy counter to enemies which might otherwise be difficult to hold in place. Once enemies have fallen, you’ve reduced their speed to 0, which prevents them from standing for the rest of the turn.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

battering-roots|unknown.name: Battering Roots
battering-roots|unknown.summary: A World Tree Barbarian with a Reach weapon like a glaive can attack out to 20 feet, allowing you to reach enemies over a huge area. Adding the Push and Topple masteries also diversifies your tactical options quite a bit. If you’re using a Push or Topple weapon, now’s the time to switch. Note that you only get the extra mastery options with Heavy/Versatile weapons, so you may still want to throw tridents to deal with enemies more than 20 feet away. Remember that the extended reach only applies on your own turn. It does not allow you to make Opportunity Attacks at crazy distances unless you somehow cause a creature to move during your own turn.

travel-along-the-tree|unknown.name: Travel Along the Tree
travel-along-the-tree|unknown.summary: 60 feet is a wonderful amount of teleportation. Combined with Battering Roots and just plain walking, almost no enemy is out of reach. You may even be able to teleport into the air to grapple flying enemies. Remember that you can use this as part of the Bonus Action to activate Rage. The group teleportation option won’t be consistently useful, but using it to teleport into combat and ambush your enemies can be very effective. You need to be able to see the target location, and the range isn’t fantastic, but seeing through a keyhole, a crack underneath a door, or through a window all qualify.

divine-fury|you-can-t-use-it-outside-of-.name: Divine Fury
divine-fury|you-can-t-use-it-outside-of-.source:
you can’t use
		it outside of your own turn
divine-fury|you-can-t-use-it-outside-of-.summary: A large and consistent damage boost. You only get to use this once one each of your turns (you can’t use it outside of your own turn), so, if you’re using Reckless Attack, you likely don’t need to scramble for additional attack attempts to guarantee that you’ll deal this damage reliably. Resistance to Necrotic and Radiant damage is rare, and resistance to both is almost non-existent.

warrior-of-the-gods|unknown.name: Warrior of the Gods
warrior-of-the-gods|unknown.summary: A small amount of additional durability. There is no reason to split this up over multiple uses, so reserve it for when you’re in a bad situation and heal yourself as much as possible all at once.

fanatical-focus|unknown.name: Fanatical Focus
fanatical-focus|unknown.summary: Excellent for save-or-suck effects, and, since it works once per Rage, you get to use it numerous times in a single day. Rerolls are fantastic, but often put you in the position of rerolling a save with a poor modifier that you’re still going to fail. Adding your Rage damage bonus means that your chances to succeed on the reroll are a bit better. Unfortunately, save DC’s scale faster than the Rage damage bonus, so this won’t make it significantly easier to pass saves targeting your worst saving throw modifiers.

zealous-presence|unknown.name: Zealous Presence
zealous-presence|unknown.summary: Advantage on all attacks and saves for a round can be impactful, but it only lasts for one round, it does’t affect you, and you only get to use it once per day unless you spend a Rage to use it again.” This gets more useful the larger your party is, so encourage your allies to summon creatures, use pets, etc. If your allies happen to also need to make saves, we can consider that a bonus as the main purpose of this ability is the Advantage on attack rolls. It’s difficult to time abilities like this to protect allies from effects which call for saving throws. Despite how potentially powerful this is, it has a ton of problems. If you want to grant allies Advantage on attacks, you can knock enemies prone with unarmed strikes or a Topple weapon, or you can restrain them with a net. Neither of those options have daily resource limits. Providing Advantage on saves is much harder, but it’s also much less likely to take effect than the Advantage on attacks. On top of that, this doesn’t affect you. You’re using this purely to buff your allies. Is a replaceable 1-round buff really as impactful as 10 minutes of Rage? Probably not.

rage-of-the-gods|function.name: Rage of the Gods
rage-of-the-gods|function.summary: This lasts for 1 minute once per day, and you must choose to use it when you Rage, so you can’t walk around with Rage running to save yourself a Bonus Action like other Barbarians can. If you already have Rage running, you can let it expire the turn before, then Rage again to activate this. If you’re reading a physical book, note that two of the bullets wrap to the next column above the subclass art and can be easy to miss in the text. Tyler has done this repeatedly. : Flight is always excellent, though 1 minute per day doesn’t remove your need to throw weapons to handle flying enemies in most encounters.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); }); : Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant damage are relatively rare, but they’re also typically used to get around resistances to Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing damage. Between the basic resistances from Rage and this, you’re very well protected. : Good insurance for when things go badly. Remember that you’re a creature within 30 feet of yourself, so you can use this on yourself.

flight|function.name: Flight
flight|function.summary: is always excellent, though 1 minute per day doesn’t remove your need to throw weapons to handle flying enemies in most encounters.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

resistance|unknown.name: Resistance
resistance|unknown.summary: Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant damage are relatively rare, but they’re also typically used to get around resistances to Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing damage. Between the basic resistances from Rage and this, you’re very well protected.

revivification|unknown.name: Revivification
revivification|unknown.summary: Good insurance for when things go badly. Remember that you’re a creature within 30 feet of yourself, so you can use this on yourself.

cheat-death|function.name: Cheat Death
cheat-death|function.summary: Avoid dropping to 0 hp up to 6 times per day. Do not sacrifice more than one item at a time.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(187); });

magical-guidance|unknown.name: Magical Guidance
magical-guidance|unknown.summary: Even more Flash of Genius. At this point you can likely use it on every save in a typical day.

child-of-the-sun|lfl.name: Child of the Sun
child-of-the-sun|lfl.summary: Faerie Fire is already on your spell list. If you really like Faerie Fire enough to take this, play a Cartographer.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Tinker’s Magic makes this pointless, and it was already a bad feat.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: You don’t have the Wisdom to make the save DC reliable.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Reassert Honor may be good, but you won’t crit often enough to make Inspiring Strike appealing.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: A great way to get some extra spellcaster, especially from other classes. Druid or Cleric to get Guidance, Healing Word, and an offensive cantrip like Word of Radiance can be very impactful.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Rallying Cry is great, but the skills aren’t good fits. Go for Musician instead.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Mathematically, this won’t significantly improve your damage, but it’s helpful if you tend to roll poorly.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Hex can be a useful damage boost for Artificers who rely on weapons. The retaliatory damage is useful if you’re built for melee.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: An easy way to expand your skill options, but you probably only need this in a small party.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: A little bit of defense against magic, plus an offensive use for your Bonus Action. It’s decent, but the Artificer has a ton of Bonus Action options already. Most Artificer subclasses lean on your Bonus Action, plus the Homunculus Servant spell lets you get a combat pet that you command as a Bonus Action. This feat isn’t bad, it’s just hard to fit it alongside the Artificer’s existing options.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: You have no reason to use Unarmed Strikes.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: Heroic Inspiration is really good. If your party has ways to consistently generate Heroic Inspiration, this can be very impactful.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: A little bit of extra spellcasting, and you can turn a Hit Point Die into Temporary Hit Points or damage. The spellcasting comes from the Sorcerer, and you already share most of the Sorcerer’s spells, so it’s best to use this for a reliable level 1 spell like Absorb Elements or Shield which you’re nearly certain to use in combat. Aberrant Fortitude might rescue a failed Constitution save, but you only get to use it once per Long Rest, so don’t take Aberrant Dragonmark just for that. The spellcasting is the draw here. If you just want the spellcasting, compare this to Magic Initiate. Magic Initiate is much more flexible, and gets you a second Cantrip, so you’re trading the second Cantrip for Aberrant Fortitude (+1d4 on a failed Con save) and Aberrant Surge (roll a Hit Point Die to deal damage or gain Temp HP). If you don’t need the second Cantrip, and/or if you want Greater Aberrant Mark, Aberrant Dragonmark is a good choice.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: Access to some very useful Divination spells, most of which aren’t on the Artificer’s spell list. Detect Magic and See Invisibility are both staples in any adventuring party, and you get both prepared for free, plus free castings of each. The spell list gets you access to great spells like Clairvoyance and Arcane Eye, though many of the spells on the spell list are bad. The situational options are helpful to have available since the Artificer can change their prepared spells daily.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: The skills and spells aren’t great for the Artificer. They’re not unusable, but they’re not going to make your build significantly better.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: The ability to deal with Beasts and low-Intelligence Monstrosities may be useful at low levels, but will diminish in effectiveness between levels 5 and 10. The spell list is overly focused on Beasts, but does include some great options like Command and Find Familiar.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: This significantly expands your healing spell options, but you don’t strictly need it to cover your party’s needs. Artificers already get Cure Wounds and Lesser Restoration, but getting them prepared or free is helpful, and access to Healing Word and Prayer of Healing are both excellent.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: A lot of the spells are great, but they’re also already on the Artificer’s spell list. If you’re going to use these spells a lot, consider Potent Dragonmark to save yourself some prepared spells.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: Thematically, this is a perfect fit for the Artificer. But the spell list overlaps significantly with the Artificer’s spell list, so this doesn’t add much to what you can already do. If you plan to take Potent Dragonmark, this may be worthwhile for the additional prepared spells, but be certain that you’re going to use enough spells from the spell list to justify two feats.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Misty Step for free, plus a ton of other great spells like Pass Without Trace and Find Steed. The skills are awful, and the higher-level spells are only situationally useful, but the low-level spells are good enough that this will always feel impactful.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: The skills are bad, and most of the spells are bad. You get a few useful utilities like Comprehend Languages and Tongues, but you’ll skip over so many of the spells that it’s difficult to justify this.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Good skills, Shield prepared for free, and access to great options like Compelled Duel and Death Ward. Many of the best spells accessible through Mark of the Sentinel are already on the Artificer’s spell list, but taking Potent Dragonmark will get you all of those spells prepared so that you can use your normal pool of prepared spells for other things. This is a fantastic choice for any melee Artificer build.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: An easy choice for Infiltrator Armorer builds who are leaning into stealth, but the spell list is great in general, providing access to illusions and stealth options which generally aren’t available to the Artificer.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: The spells aren’t great, but it does get you a permanent damage resistance, and a couple of the spells like Feather Fall and Conjure Minor Elementals are great.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Other than Armor of Agathys, the spells provided by Mark of Warding are all extremely situational utilities that are only likely to see use if you have a permanent base to defend.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: Bad Ability Scores, and the other features are too limited to justify this.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: If you want an easy source of Temporary Hit Points, play an Artillerist.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Artificers have several options to replicate items which grant Blindsight, allowing you and your allies to function (mostly) normally in the area of Fog Cloud, while your enemies are slowed and effectively blind.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Repeating Shot will let you ignore the Loading property, and you have much better uses for your Bonus Action than another attack with a hand crossbwo.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: Bad ability scores, and too few Artificers rely on Bludgeoning damage to justify this.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: If you’re worried about incoming weapon damage types, stack your AC higher and cast Shield.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: You have better uses for your Bonus Action than weapon attacks.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Choosing Acid or Fire may be helpful for Alchemists.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: Without an Intelligence increase, this is already a hard choice. You’re unlike to Disengage often enough for that to matter, so you’re only here for Flustering Strike, which isn’t usable enough to justify the feat on its own.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Misty step is fantastic on any character, and the Artificer gets alarmingly few Divination spell options. Fey Touched provides some easy access to some great spells like Bless and Compelled Duel. Back-row artificers will find that Bless is a powerful buff at any level, while front-row Artificers will find that Compelled Duel makes them an exceptionally effective Defender.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Artillerists and Battle Smiths can technically use weapons which would qualify for Great Weapon Master, but Artillerists should be using True Strike, and Battle Smiths will frequently cut into their own attacks to give their Steel Defender a second attack.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: The +1 AC compared to medium armor is not worth needing to get to 15 Strength to avoid the speed penalty.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: Only the Armorer gets proficiency in heavy armor. By the time you’ve hit 20 Intelligence and can justify this, you’re probably stacking AC bonuses, so the odds of you getting hit shrink, which makes this less impactful.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: If you want to provide Temporary Hit Points, play an Artillerist. This might be useful for melee builds (so not Artillerist), but go for Tough instead and get THP from spells.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Easy to fit on an Intelligence-based character like the Artificer, but the usefulness of this feat depends heavily on how much your DM can make the Study Action matter in combat.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational. This is only really useful in a campaign that heavily features vampires or that spends a lot of time in the Underdark.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Bad prerequisite and bad Ability Scores for the Artificer.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Bad Ability Scores, and the features are only situationally useful.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: Useful if you can use this to get Expertise, but using Search as a Bonus Action is only useful if your DM frequently uses hiding or invisible enemies in combat.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: Bad prerequisite and bad Ability Scores for the Artificer.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Few Artificers rely on weapon damage types, but this might be useful if you’re relying heavily on a firearm.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: Potentially useful for the Alchemist when combined with their level 5 damage boost, but there just aren’t enough spellst that deal Poison damage for this to be consistently useful. If your allies get a lot of use out of the brewed poison, this might be worth the feat, but wait until you have a lot of gold to spend on materials.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: The only Artificer that could reasonably use a polearm is the Battle Smith, and your Bonus Action is dedicated to your Steel Defender, so you lose most of Polearm Master’s value.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: Bad prerequisite and bad Ability Scores for the Artificer.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Never a bad idea. Proficiency in either Dexterity or Wisdom saves could be very useful. But remember that you can also replicate items which provide save bonuses and that you have Flash of Genius. Be careful about over-investing in saves when those resources could go elsewhere.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: Not a good feat. You don’t get enough rituals, and they can only be level 1.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: This is great for melee Battle Smiths and potentially for Defender/Juggernaut Armorers if you have other allies that like to fight in melee. However, it doesn’t have an Intelligence increase, so you may prefer to save this until you hit 20 Intelligence unless you’re certain that you’ll get enough value to justify the setback.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: This is a good feat, but there are few spell options that appeal to the Artificer.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Artillerists, Infiltrator Armorers, and ranged Battle Smiths may find this helpful. Other Artificers will get more value from Spell Sniper. In any case, Wand of the Warmage may be sufficient.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: Too dependent on Strength. Unfortunately, attacking with Intelligence doesn’t change the save DC for the Shield Bash.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: You’re not likely to rely on slashing damage, but a Battle Smith might get some use here. Unfortunately,

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: Bad Ability Scores. If you want mobility, use spells or magic items.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: A nice boost to your Cantrips, but not totally necessary. Use True Strike with a crossbow.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: The Artificer has very few spell options which deal Radiant damage. True Strike is your best bet, and this isn’t good enough to take for once Cantrip.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: Artificers are not built for grappling.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: An easy addition to the Artificer. You won’t need Telekinetic Shove every round, so it won’t constantly compete for space with your other Bonus Action options.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: An easy way to expand your spellcasting similar to Fey Touched and Shadow Touched, but you get to pick the level 1 spells from two schools instead of just one.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: An easy choice on any Artificer, but especially useful on melee builds. Even with proficiency in Constitution saves, Advantage is still a huge benefit when you’re concnetrating on something important.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: Good for melee builds, provided that you’re not stacking AC bonuses. If your AC is high, you’ll get less value from Retaliate.

greater-aberrant-mark|efota.name: Greater Aberrant Mark
greater-aberrant-mark|efota.summary: A dramatic improvement over Abberant Dragonmark. This is a great choice for melee builds.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(193); });

greater-mark-of-detection|efota.name: Greater Mark of Detection
greater-mark-of-detection|efota.summary: If you need your allies to see invisible foes, cast Faerie Fire.

greater-mark-of-finding|efota.name: Greater Mark of Finding
greater-mark-of-finding|efota.summary: The improvements to Hunter’s Mark are too situational, and almost no Artificers will benefit from them.

greater-mark-of-handling|efota.name: Greater Mark of Handling
greater-mark-of-handling|efota.summary: Artificers aren’t built for mounted combat, but Mark of Handling lets you cast Find Steed, which is enough to change that. An Armorer Artificer might work very well as a mounted combtant, but other Artificers won’t get much benefit here.

greater-mark-of-healing|efota.name: Greater Mark of Healing
greater-mark-of-healing|efota.summary: The extra healing is neat, but casting level 1 Cure Wounds a few extra times will quickly be too little healing to justify in combat, and outside combat you have options like Prayer of Healing. The rerolls on Cure Wounds dice are nice, but increase the average healing very little.

greater-mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Greater Mark of Hospitality
greater-mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: The temporary hit points are cool, but Inspiring Leader is a much better option for this. Of course, Inspiring Leader requires either Wisdom or Charisma, and you might not have enough of either to qualify.

greater-mark-of-making|efota.name: Greater Mark of Making
greater-mark-of-making|efota.summary: Terrible. Potent Dragonmark gets you a scaling spell slot which will match the improved free casting of Magic Weapon starting at level 5, then outpace it as you gain levels.

greater-mark-of-passage|efota.name: Greater Mark of Passage
greater-mark-of-passage|efota.summary: The improvement to Misty Step is great, but it’s probably not good enough to be once per day. There’s a similar spell called Scatter which does this, but it’s a level 6 spell. Even so, I’m not convinced that this worth the feat.

greater-mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Greater Mark of Scribing
greater-mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: This is interesting, but sharing a level 1 Ritual spell is not good enough for a feat. The Telepathy is also interesting, but you should look for Rary’s Telepathic Bond or a species with Telepathy if you want Telepathy within the party.

greater-mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Greater Mark of Sentinel
greater-mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Improved Sentinel is great. If you’re built to be effective with weapons and can tank hits for your allies, this could be great. Battle Smiths and Armorers are obvious choices here.

greater-mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Greater Mark of Shadow
greater-mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Terrible. Potent Dragonmark gets you a scaling spell slot which will match the improved free casting of Magic Weapon starting at level 5, then outpace it as you gain levels.

greater-mark-of-storm|efota.name: Greater Mark of Storm
greater-mark-of-storm|efota.summary: 1 minute of flight per day is not worth a feat.

greater-mark-of-warding|efota.name: Greater Mark of Warding
greater-mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Improved Warding is fantastic, but not so effective that it justifies Mark of Warding unless it’s already a good fit for your build.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: If you take a Dragonmark feat, Potent Dragonmark can dramatically increases its effectiveness. Of course, this assumes that the dragonmark’s spells are useful enough to justify this.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is great, especially since high level creatures frequently deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: The benefits are minor and inconsistent.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: Artificers don’t have built-in options for generating Temporary Hit Points other than spells, so there isn’t a ton of value here. Boon of the Bright Sun offers a great option, but look at other Epic Boons first.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Useful for weapon-focus Artificers like the Armorer.

boon-of-communication|frhof.name: Boon of Communication
boon-of-communication|frhof.summary: Leave this to someone with good Charisma.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Appealing on melee builds. Even with stacked AC, you still have d8 hit dice, so resisting damage makes you considerably more resilient.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Without built-in options to Shapeshift, there’s very little value here.

boon-of-fortune-s-favor|frhof.name: Boon of Fortune’s Favor
boon-of-fortune-s-favor|frhof.summary: Excellent on literally anyone. Remember that you also have Flash of Genious, so you may be able to turn a near miss into a success rather than gambling on a reroll, but rerolling may also put you in range to use Flash of Genious.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: Artificers don’t rely heavily enough on B/P/S damage to justify this.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but the Artificer doesn’t have greay sources fo poison damage other than Cantrips.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Misty Escape.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Tempting, but you only get to use it once since the Artificer’s highest-level spell slot is level 5.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: I would only consider this in a small party with poor sill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: Great for melee builds, but ranged builds shouldn’t need this often enough to justify selecting it.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: Awful. The odds of rollig to retain a spell slot are too small to justify this.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: Without built-in options to make creatures Frightened, the Artificer will get little value here.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Two damage resistances that turn into immunities when you’re Bloodied. Disadvantage on saves against your Lighting/Thunder spells is neat, but Artificers have very few of them, so you’re mostly here for the resistances.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Great on anyone, but especially useful on Infiltrator Armorers since they’re already well-suited to stealth.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: The damage resistances are night, but the healing it paltry. Consider Boon of Energy Resistance first.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Permanent Truesight is great, but remember that you can replicate a Gem of True Seeing.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: You get the crucial Intelligence increase, and Magic Initiate (Cleric) offers access to great options like Guidance and Healing Word. Guide provides similar benefits with better Ability Score Increases.

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: Fantastic for Infiltrator Armorer builds. Dexterity, Intelligence, Skilled, and one good skill give you enough to cover essentials skill for a Scout so that you can easily fill in for a Rogue in the party.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: I want so badly for this to work, but Crafter is an awful feat.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: The Ability Scores and the feat work great, but the skills are wasted on the Artificer.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: No Intelligence increase. Archaologist or Scribe will also get you skilled, but the Ability options work better for the Artificer.

chondathan-freeboter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freeboter
chondathan-freeboter|frhof.summary: No Intelligence increase. Archaologist or Scribe will also get you skilled, but the Ability options work better for the Artificer.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: Perfect ability scores, decent skills, and an easy go-to feat. Proficiency in Thieves’ Tools is redundant, unfortunately. This is an easy go-to choice if you don’t know what to pick on any Artificer build.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Bad Ability Scores, and you don’t need Healer.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: The Ablity Scores are great for the Artificer, but the feat relies on Wisdom, and the skills aren’t great, so this is a hard choice.

emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Caretaker
emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.summary: Good Ablity Scores, but the feat is terrible and the skills aren’t great.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: No Intelligence increase and terrible skills.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: No Intelligence increase and middling skills. A melee build will benefit a lot from Tough, and increase both Constitution and Wisdom are great defensively, but lacking an Intelligenc increase is really hard on the Artificer.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: Basically the same as Farmer, but slightly different Ability Scores and skills.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: If you want Magic Initiate (Wizard), take Sage.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Not terrible, but you can get better Ability Score Increases and still get the Alert feat from Criminal.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: Perfect Ability Scores, and Magic Initate can get you great options like Guidance and Healing Word. The sklls are decent, too.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: The Ability Scores ae fine, but Harper Agent will be borderline useless.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Bad Ability Scores, bad skills, and you don’t need Healer.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: You can get an Intelligence increase, Lucky is always nice, and you get Investigation. Unfortunately, a lot of this background is wasted on the Artificer.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: Good Ability Scores, Alert is an easy feat choice, and the skills are decent. Proficiency in Thieves’ Tools is redundant, but this is still a great choice that will work on any Artificer build.

knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.name: Knight of the Gauntlet
knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.summary: The feat isn’t great, and the skills are attrocious. You can get an Intelligence increase, but that is not enough to carry everything else.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: Bad feat, middling skills. You do get an Intelligence increase, though.

lorwyn-expert|lfl.name: Lorwyn Expert
lorwyn-expert|lfl.summary: Bad Ability Scores, bad feat, bad skills.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
