inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A massive amount of temporary hit points.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Only situationally useful. I would only consider this in a campaign that takes place in the Underdark or in a game with vampires as common enemies.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: The Bonus Action buff is neat, but not enough without a Wisdom increase.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Clerics are already proficient in two mental saves, and they’re really good at Wisdom saves, which is the important one, so the benefits here are minimal.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: This is only helpful if your DM likes to use stealthy enemies and/or likes to include traps in combat encounters.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: Strength saves are not common enough to justify this.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: You should not be using weapons enough to justify using this.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: Clerics don’t have good options for dealing Poison damage.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: Clerics should not be taking the Attack action enough to make this useful.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: This is what your spellcasting is for.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: high Constitution saves are crucial for maintaining Concentration. War Caster may be better if you’re building for the front lines so that you can use Reactive Spell, but, if you only care about Concentration, Resilient is better.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: There are some great level 1 Ritual spells like Comprehend Languages and Find Familiar, but the fact that this only lets you get level 1 spells significantly limits its usefulness. Getting rituals from outside of your own spell list is nice, but unless there are specific Rituals that you want, this isn’t worth a feat.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Even if you’re built to fight in close quarters, War Caster is a better choice.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells are always nice, and Invisibility is a staple spell, but Shadow Magic’s options for 1st-level spells simply aren’t as good as those available via Fey Touched.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Clerics don’t make enough attack rolls to justify this.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: Clerics shouldn’t take the Attack action often enough to make this useful.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: There are some great Wisdom-based skills that might be worth Expertise.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: You should not be using weapons enough to justify using this.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: Potentially helpful for reaching allies quickly, or for running Spirit Guardians through crowds of enemies.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Very few cleric spells involve ranged spell attacks.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: There is no spellcaster better suited to use this feat than the Cleric. Note that the damage only applies to one damage roll of the spell, so you get the best results from instantaneaous spells like Guiding Bolt, Flame Strike (by the gods, we found a use for it! Not a good one, but it’s there!), and Sunburst.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: An easy choice on any spellcaster. Telekinetic Shove will compete for your Bonus Action with options like Healing Word and Spiritual Weapon, but you won’t be able to use it effectively every turn, so it’s not really an issue. Remember that creatures can willingly fail saving throws, allowing you to use this on allies in order to move them out of dangerous positions, break grapples, or otherwise help them.

telepathic|phb.name: Telepathic
telepathic|phb.summary: Very cool, but usually talking works fine.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Charm Person is not good enough to justify a feat, and Clerics don’t rely enough on attacks to capitalize on attacking charmed enemies.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Access to some great spells from other spell lists. Most Clerics have almost no Illusion options, and there are many great Enchantment spells on other spells lists which will remain useful for your whole career.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Great for Clerics built for the front lines. If you only care about Concentration, Resilient (Constitution) provides a bigger bonus, but War Caster can improve your mental ability scores, so it’s often easier to fit into a build. The text of the Opportunity Attack rules allow you to make an Opportunity Attack whenever a creature leaves your reach. War Caster’s Reactive Spell feature allows you to replace that attack with a single-target spell. This is intended to be used on enemies, but RAW this also allows you to cast buffs or healing spells on your allies when they leave your reach.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: You should not be using weapons enough to justify using this unless you’re going for War Domain, and even then it’s not a fantastic choice. Take a level of Fighter.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: Cleric’s attacks aren’t powerful enough that the Opportunity Attack feels impactful. Expertise is great, especially since you can change it, but that’s not enough on its own.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to Radiant damage is great, but you’re not going to get much out of the attack stuff.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Clerics don’t make enough attacks to justify this even if you’re a War Cleric.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: The Temporary Hit Points benefit could be useful. Clerics have a lot of options for THP, so you could get a lot of mileage here, but you might not be casting them often enough to make it worthwhile.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Nice for War Domain, but otherwise skip it.

boon-of-communication|frhof.name: Boon of Communication
boon-of-communication|frhof.summary: Clerics are not built to be a Face.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: You’re probably your party’s primarily healer, and not dying makes it a lot easier to be a healer.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: Basically free Misty Step every time that you cast a spell as an Action. Unfortunately, Bonus Action and Reaction spells don’t qualify. According to the Rules Glossary: “When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.” Outside of combat, you can still use this to get around obstacles. Cast a harmless spell like Thaumaturgy and you can teleport without making a mess.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Clerics have many of the best options for dealing Radiant damage, so this is an easy boost. Unfortunately, it only works once per day.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: 2d4 averages to 5. Adding +5/-5 to a saving throw can rescue you or an ally, or it can cause an enemy to fail a save. On a d20 scale, 5 means that there’s a 25% chance on any given roll that this will have an impact. Granted, it is still a dice roll, so the smaller the gap, the safer this is to use. On a full caster where save-or-suck spells are such a huge part of your arsenal, this is devastatingly effective. The fact that you can use it once per encounter is amazing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Clerics don’t have other built-in shapechanging options, so it’s hard to get consistent value out of this.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: You will benefit more from Resilient (Constitution).

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: You should not be using weapons enough to justify this.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: You won’t use the Attack part often, but Dodge as a Bonus Action can be very useful for spellcasters since most big spells are an Action.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance is a great save-or-suck spell, and it’s not on the Cleric’s spell list.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: Take Boon of Dimensional Travel instead.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: This gives you a 25% chance to retain your spell slot when casting spells of up to level 4. You get 4 level 1 spell slots and 3 of each of levels 2, 3, and 4. On average, you get 1 extra level 1 spell slot, and slightly less than 1 for levels 2, 3, and 4. This is fine, but definitely don’t make it your first boon.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: Charisma is a dump stat for Clerics, which makes this hard to choose.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: The damage resistance/immunity is nice, but Clerics don’t have many spells which rely on Lightning or Thunder damage.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Be invisible at all times outside of combat. Take advantage of invisibility at the start of combat, then look for ways to become invisible as frequently as possible. Even if you’re not making attack rolls (and you almost certainly aren’t doing so often), the defensive benefits of invisibility are massive. However, remember that a lot of things are an Action, so it’s very easy to break this invisibility. Notable examples that people easily overlook include Hide, Search, and Study.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: You’re only here for the damage resistance. The healing is negligible on a class that can cast Heal.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: You have magic options to handle invisible enemies.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Better skills than Sage, but Sage’s ability scores are better, and you already get Cleric spellcasting.

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: A potential fit for Trickery Clerics. The additionals proficiencies from Skilled, plus good ability scores make a great basis for a high-Dexterity build. Unfortunately, the built-in skills aren’t a great fit. Chondathan Freebooter is a better option if you want Skilled.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Bad ability scores, and Charisma-based skills are hard for most Clerics.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Maybe a good choice for Trickery Clerics, but lacking a Wisdom increase is hard to justify. Chondathan Freebooter is a better option if you want Skilled.

chondathan-freebooter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freebooter
chondathan-freebooter|frhof.summary: An easy choice for Trickery Clerics. Grab increases in Dexterity and Wisdom, then use Skilled to cover whatever proficiencies you need to cover for a Rogue. You already get Sleight of Hand, which is fantastic.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: Maybe a good choice for Trickery Clerics, but lacking a Wisdom increase is hard to justify.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, but you don’t need Healer, and the skills are bad.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Cult of the Dragon Initiatiate is a great feat for the Cleric, but the ability scores and skills only work well for a Trickery Cleric, and you can’t get a Wisdom increase.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: Musician is great, but it’s not enough.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: Excellent ability scores for the Cleric, and more hit points never hurt, but the skills aren’t great.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: No Wisdom increase, but otherwise a passable option for a melee build.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Comparable to Sage. Good ability scores, workable skills, and Magic Initiate (Wizard).

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Excellent for front-line builds intending to use weapons.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: Excellent for melee clerics. You can increase Constitution and Wisdom and grab Shillelagh from the Druid’s spell list. The skills aren’t fantastic unless you’re going for Trickery Domain to use Stealth, but the other benefits may be enough to make up for it.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Decent ability scores, but the skills are middling, and there’s little reason for Healer when you can cast Healing Word.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. If you want Lucky, look elsewhere.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. If you want Alert, look elsewhere.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. If you want Alert, look elsewhere.

knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.name: Knight of the Gauntlet
knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.summary: Bad feat, bad skills, mediocre ability scores.

lorwyn-expert|lfl.name: Lorwyn Expert
lorwyn-expert|lfl.summary: Good ability scores, you can get Faerie Fire, and the skills are passable. Magic Initiate will typically be more impactful than Child of the Sun, so consider Guide or Moonwell Pilgrim instead.

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, one decent skill, and Magic Initiate (Druid)

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: No Wisdom increase, but otherwise good.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: No Wisdom increase and both skills are based on dump stats for the Cleric.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Decent ability scores, one good skill, and Purple Dragon Rook is a great feat.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Great ability scores, decent skills despite being Intelligence-based, and Magic Initiate (Wizard). You might enjoy some of the Wizard’s spells like True Strike and Find Familiar or Shield.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores for a melee build, plus one good skill, but you’re absolutely not going to use Tavern Brawler.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: A good choice for Trickery Domain. Be sure to pick up proficiency in Thieves’ Tools with Skilled.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: No Wisdom increase, and most Clerics will rarely benefit from Savage Attacker since Clerics do so little with weapons.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: The appeal here is getting Hex, which the Cleric doesn’t have a great way to use.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: No Wisdom increase, and most Clerics will rarely benefit from Savage Attacker since Clerics do so little with weapons.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: You already have tons of options for radiant damage, and this doesn’t offer a Wisdom increase.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Decent, but Vampire Hunter isn’t a good feat.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: A good choice for Trickery Domain.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores aren’t a good fit. You’ll get more value out of a background which gives you Magic Initiate.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(187); });

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills for everyone except a Trickery Cleric, but Trickery Clerics should go for Mark of Shadow. The feat doesn’t offer anything new.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: Perfect ability scores, especially for a War Cleric, two Wisdom-based skills and a bonus to them from the feat, plus the feat gets you some great level 1 spells.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: Workable ability scores, decent skills, and a good feat.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are good, but the skills are middling and the feat is functionally useless.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: The feat is good, but not enough on its own.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: An easy choice for the Trickery Cleric.

house-sivis-heir|efota.name: House Sivis Heir
house-sivis-heir|efota.summary: Very little value here, but at least you get a Wisdom increase.

house-tharashk-heir|efota.name: House Tharashk Heir
house-tharashk-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores and skills, but the feat is bad.

house-vadalis-heir|efota.name: House Vadalis Heir
house-vadalis-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores, but that’s the only good part.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. You’re mostly here for the transformation, which could be appealing for melee builds. You can do more with spells, but there’s nothing stopping you from using Celestial Revelation and Spirit Guardians at the same time.

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: Clerics generally can’t afford to be good at Charisma, but Shapechanger’s persistant Advantage on Charisma checks paired with two additional Face skills could offset relatively poor Charisma.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and once per day flight are great, but you will likely never use the breath weapon beyond very low levels.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense is neat, but you have spells to handle invisible or hidden enemies. The durability is great for melee builds, but less appealing for ranged builds.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great, plus you can get access to some spells from outside of the Cleric’s spell list. The Drow’s Faerie Fire gives you a great offensive support option, the High Elf’s cantrip can get you a great offensive cantrips from the Wizard’s spell list, and the Wood Elf’s access to Pass Without Trace simplifies stealth for the whole party.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options. Paired with good Wisdom and proficiency in Wisdom saves, failing those saves will be exceptionally rare.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage offers some great options. Cloud Jaunt offers teleportation, which normally isn’t an option for the Cleric. Stone’s Endurance offers some excellent damage mitigation. Other options mostly offer damage, which will only be useful if you’re building to use weapons, and very few clerics can do that effectively. Large Form is neat, but probably only useful to make Spirit Guardians 5 feet wider.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Lucky is the only part of the Halfling’s traits which will be consistently useful. Brave is great, but you already have fantastic Wisdom saves. Halfling Nimbleness is rarely useful; if you need to heal at range you have Healing Word, and if you get dragged into melee, something has volunteered to be hit with Spirit Guardians. Naturally Stealthy is functionally useless in combat without Cunning Action.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Dual Mind makes the Kalashtar comparable to the Gnome, but you trade Advantage on Intelligense saves for Resistance to Psychic damage.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Very versatile. The additional Cantrip may remove the need for Magic Initiate if you wanted to grab Cantrips from another class, and the additional proficiency will give you more options without dipping into your limited spell slots.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is an excellent option for getting out of dangerous positions quickly without a spell, and the Temporary Hit Points are great. If you’re running Spirit Guardians, Adrenaline Rush might help you hit more targets, too. If that doesn’t keep you alive, Relentless Endurance provides some insurance, which is great since you’re probably your party’s healer.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Beasthide and Swiftstride could be very helpful when you’re running Spirit Guardians.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting almost entirely from outside of the Cleric’s spell list. The spell choices aren’t crazy, but there are some consistently useful options here.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and you learn Ray of Frost. Not terrible, but not especially exciting. The other spells you get are terrible.

history|int.name: History
history|int.summary: (Int): A useful knowledge skill, but skip it if anyone else in the party takes it.

insight|wis.name: Insight
insight|wis.summary: (Wis): Helpful for a Face, and you have the Wisdom to back it up. Since many Faces tend to have low Wisdom, it’s a very good idea for you to pick this up even if you’re not your party’s Face.

medicine|wis.name: Medicine
medicine|wis.summary: (Wis): This skill is useless. Medicine is best done magically.

persuasion|cha.name: Persuasion
persuasion|cha.summary: (Cha): Crucial for a Face, but you can skip it if someone in the party has more Charisma than you.

religion|int.name: Religion
religion|int.summary: (Int): The Cleric’s best Knowledge skill, and important to the theme of the class. Thaumaturge Clerics also get to add their Wisdom modifier to Intelligence (Religion) checks, making this an easy choice.

crossbow-light|unknown.name: Crossbow, Light
crossbow-light|unknown.summary: This may do more damage than your Cantrips at low levels because weapons add your ability bonus to damage. If you have good Dexterity, consider a crossbow until your cantrips scale at 5th level.

javelin|unknown.name: Javelin
javelin|unknown.summary: Same logic as the Light Crossbow, but Strength-based.

mace|unknown.name: Mace
mace|unknown.summary: The iconic Cleric weapon. It’s not great, but it gets the job done. Carry one for when you need to wade into melee.

leather|function.name: Leather
leather|function.summary: If you have 18 Dexterity, this will match Scale Mail. Otherwise Scale Mail is strictly better starting armor.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(195); });

chain-mail|unknown.name: Chain Mail
chain-mail|unknown.summary: Starting armor for Clerics who get heavy armor proficiency from their domain.

half-plate|unknown.name: Half plate
half-plate|unknown.summary: Most Clerics will max out at Half plate.

shield|unknown.name: Shield
shield|unknown.summary: You can put your holy symbol on your shield, so there is almost no reason not to have one.

full-plate|unknown.name: Full Plate
full-plate|unknown.summary: Clerics with proficiency in heavy armor should absolutely upgrade to Full Plate as soon as they can afford it.

artificer|unknown.name: Artificer
artificer|unknown.summary: Starting at level 1 as an Artificer gets you proficiency in Constitution saves without slowing your spell slot progression, but the multiclassing ability score requirements are hard for the Cleric.

barbarian|unknown.name: Barbarian
barbarian|unknown.summary: Rage and Reckless Attack won’t be particularly useful since Clerics don’t get Extra Attack, and Unarmored Defense requires you to have too many high ability scores.

druid|unknown.name: Druid
druid|unknown.summary: The Cleric and the Druid share Wisdom-based spellcasting, so a few levels to get low-level class features and some low-level spell options like Shillelagh and Faerie Fire can be very effective. However, Magic Initiate will typically suffice if you just want spellcasting.

fighter|protector.name: Fighter
fighter|protector.summary: Starting with 1 level in Fighter gets you Constitution saves, heavy armor, shields, martial weapons, Fighting Style, Weapon Mastery, and Second Wind. All of that makes you immediately better than Divine Order (Protector). Two levels gets you Action Surge, but you can’t use Action Surge to cast spells, so it’s not especially appealing.

monk|unknown.name: Monk
monk|unknown.summary: The Monk’s Unarmored Defense works well for Clerics since they need so much Wisdom. 14 Dexterity and 20 Wisdom with Unarmored Defense will match Half plate, but remember that Unarmored Defense doesn’t work with shields, so you’ll need 18 Dexterity to match the AC of a normal Cleric with a shield. Martial Arts is a great way to use your Bonus Action offensively without cutting into your spells.

ranger|unknown.name: Ranger
ranger|unknown.summary: Whatever you want from the Ranger, you can get it from the Druid, the Fighter, or the Rogue.

rogue|unknown.name: Rogue
rogue|unknown.summary: One level for Expertise or two for Cunning Action can be very powerful on a Trickery Domain Cleric.

sorcerer|unknown.name: Sorcerer
sorcerer|unknown.summary: Two levels for Font of Magic can be very powerful, but the multiclassing ability score requirements are hard for the Cleric

wizard|unknown.name: Wizard
wizard|unknown.summary: Clerics and Wizards have access to some of the best spells in the game, but the multiclassing ability score requirements are hard for the Cleric.

life-domain-spells|unknown.name: Life Domain Spells
life-domain-spells|unknown.summary: The low-level options are absolutely fantastic, and many of the Life Domain Spells are essentially required for a Cleric to take. Unfortunately, the high-level options are less useful. : Bless is nearly a win condition at low levels where adding 1d4 to a roll can exceed your proficiency bonus, and it remains a staple buff at basically any level so long as you don’t need your Concentration for something else. Cure Wounds is a fine healing spell, but in combat you want to rely on Healing Word and spend your Action on offense. : Aid is a fantastic buff for the entire party that can also be used in place of Mass Healing Word to rescue multiple dying alllies. Lesser Restoration is nice to have handy, but much of the time the effects which it removes can wait until you can rest and prepare spells to fix them. : Mass Healing Word is very expensive for very little healing, so hopefully you’ll never need to use it when you can cast Aid and you have Channel Divinity: Preserve Life. Revivify is the “Cleric Tax”, so getting it for free is really nice. : Aura of Life is only situationally useful, but it’s great against undead enemies. Death Ward is a fantastic defensive buff with a long duration. : Greater Restoration should be an option of last resort since the material component is expensive, but every party needs it eventually. Mass Cure is redundant with Preserve Life.

level-1-spells|unknown.name: Level 1 Spells
level-1-spells|unknown.summary: Guiding Bolt is a fantastic spell, providing both excellent damage and Advantage on your party’s next attack. It remains a good use of a low level spell slot through your whole career, especially with Guided Strike to rescue a failed attack roll. Shield of Faith will remain useful at every level. +2 AC is big in 5e, and 10 minutes is a fantastic duration for a spell slot. However, it requires Concentration, which means that you can’t combine it with other great low-level buffs like Bless.

level-2-spells|unknown.name: level 2 spells
level-2-spells|unknown.summary: Magic Weapon is essential if you lack permanent magical weapons, but for allies that rely heavily on weapons, the +1 attack/damage bonus is also a huge boost to their damage output. If you’re expecting to face several encounters in the 1-hour duration, Spiritual Weapon is a staple Cleric option, and a great way to convert your Bonus Action into damage output while leaving your Action free for non-Concentration spells like Guiding Bolt. However, it competes for space with War Priest both conceptually and within the action economy.

level-3-spells|unknown.name: level 3 spells
level-3-spells|unknown.summary: Crusader’s Mantle is Divine Favor for the whole party. The damage per attack is still small, but if you have someone using Two-Weapon Fighting, allies with Extra Attack, or just a large party, the value adds up quickly. But it generally can’t compete with Spirit Guardians, which you also get. Spirit Guardians is among the most efficient damage options in the game, and many clerics prepare it every day.

level-4-spells|unknown.name: level 4 spells
level-4-spells|unknown.summary: Fire Shield is a great defensive buff if you’re on the front lines, especially if you’re not wearing heavy armor and a shield. Freedom of movement is situationally useful.

level-5-spells|unknown.name: level 5 spells
level-5-spells|unknown.summary: Hold Monster is a fantastic save-or-suck spell which you can immediately follow with an attack from War Priest for a guaranteed critical hit. Steel Wind Strike is simple, direct damage. Since you can use Guided Strike without an action for your own attacks, you can use it with multiple missed attacks within a single turn. Note that the damage is fixed regardless of your weapon, so you can wave a dart and still deal 6d10 damage to each of your targets if you don’t routinely wield a weapon.

disciple-of-life|unknown.name: Disciple of Life
disciple-of-life|unknown.summary: This isn’t a ton of healing all at once, but it will be especially useful with Healing Word, which is a good combination because it uses a Bonus Action, but normally doesn’t heal for a particularly large amount. Over the course of your career, the total amount of additional healing will be significant, so I encourage you to keep a running score if for no other reason than to remind your party members how badly they need you to survive.

channel-divinity-preserve-life|unknown.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
channel-divinity-preserve-life|unknown.summary: Fantastic when you’re looking at a possible TPK. Since you’re healing so much, most characters of your level will go from 0 to half hit points, unless you’re looking at someone like a Barbarian with d12 hit dice and 20 Constitution or if you’re splitting the points between multiple allies. Even so, the scaling is excellent. As you gain additional uses of Channel Divinity this will quickly become your go-to option for large amounts of hit point recovery while in combat.

blessed-healer|unknown.name: Blessed Healer
blessed-healer|unknown.summary: There is now almost never a reason to cast a healing spell on yourself instead of helping your allies. However, casting a healing spell to restore hit points should not happen frequently during combat, so this may not trigger as frequently as you would like.

supreme-healing|unknown.name: Supreme Healing
supreme-healing|unknown.summary: As you add more and more dice, your rolls will skew toward the statistical average, meaning that each d8 from Cure Wounds is effectively 4.5 points of healing. Maximizing the die improves this to 8 points of healing, almost doubling the effects of your healing spells and thereby making your spell slots spent on healing much more efficient, allowing you to reserve high-level spell slots for more interesting things. If you need healing in a fight, most characters should cast Heal or Mass Heal, neither of which involve dice. But with Supreme Healing, Cure Wounds heals more per spell slot level than Heal does, making it a viable source of healing in combat.

blessings-of-knowledge|unknown.name: Blessings of Knowledge
blessings-of-knowledge|unknown.summary: Proficiency and Expertise in two knowledge skills. Your Intelligence likely isn’t great, but Expertise can easyly make up for that without making your scramble to fit high Intelligence into your build.

knowledge-domain-spells|unknown.name: Knowledge Domain Spells
knowledge-domain-spells|unknown.summary: Knowledge Domain gets 3 spells per spell level instead of the usual 2, which is exciting. Almost none of the spells are combat options, though you do get Command, Banishment, and Synaptic Static. The Divination spells on the list are especially useful thanks to Mind Magic. : Command and two utilities which you’ll cast either as Rituals or using Mind Magic. : Very situational utilities. : Three situaitonally useful utilities. : Pretend Confusion isn’t here and you still get two absolute amazing spells: one fantastic scouting option and one powerful offensive option. : Synpatic Static is an amazing offensive option. Legend Lore and Scrying are only situationally useful and expensive to cast, but Mind Magic allows you to bring them out at a moment’s notice without paying for the expensive material components, so they’re considerably more accessible.

mind-magic|unknown.name: Mind Magic
mind-magic|unknown.summary: This is an amazing utility. The ability to cast Tongues, Arcane Eye, and Scrying without a spell slot or spell components makes it much easier to use those spells on a day where you need to save spell slots for combat. Scrying is especially useful because it normally has a 10-minute casting time and requires a focus worth 1,000gp, but Mind Magic lets you cast it as an Action. Legend Lore also has a 10-minute casting time and consumes a material component worth 250+ gp, so Mind Magic is a great way to constantly as your DM for plot information.

unfettered-mind|unknown.name: Unfettered Mind
unfettered-mind|unknown.summary: Telepathy is neat, but proficiency in Intelligence saves is the real benefit here. Intelligence saves aren’t common, but proficiency in an extra save is always welcome in a game where you typically only get two.

divine-foreknowledge|unknown.name: Divine Foreknowledge
divine-foreknowledge|unknown.summary: This is basically the spell Foresight but with a 1-hour duration. This is easily worth a level 6 spell slot to recharge. If possible, keep this running in every fight that’s a meaningful threat.

light-domain-spells|function.name: Light Domain Spells
light-domain-spells|function.summary: A fantastic set of offensive spells which close the gap between Clerics and Wizards. : Faerie Fire is a great way to handle invisible creatures, but it’s also helpful support option for allies that rely on attacks because it’s an easy source of Advantage against multiple targets. Burning Hands is a great low-level AOE damage spell, but resist the urge to burn all of your spell slots casting it or you won’t have any slots to heal with. At high levels, Faerie Fire remains incredibly potent, but Burning Hands will be obsolete after a few levels.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); }); : Scorching Ray is a great single-target option, especially if you have Bless or Faerie Fire running to boost the attack rolls. See Invisibility gives you an even better way to handle invisibile enemies than Faerie Fire. : Daylight is only situationally useful, but Fireball is the sledgehammer of offensive spells: sometimes you just need to hit your problems until they fall down. In terms of instantaneous area damage, there isn’t another spell that can compete with Fireball until 9th-level spells introduce stuff like Meteor Swarm. : Arcane Eye is my absolute favorite scouting option. Wall of Fire is among the best area control spells in the game. : Flame Strike is considerably less important since you get Fireball, but it’s only 2d6 damage behind Fireball, and avoiding common Fire damage resistances with half of the damage can make the spell more reliable against some enemies. Scrying is only situationally useful so it’s frustrating to have it prepared every day.

level-1-spells|function.name: Level 1 Spells
level-1-spells|function.summary: Faerie Fire is a great way to handle invisible creatures, but it’s also helpful support option for allies that rely on attacks because it’s an easy source of Advantage against multiple targets. Burning Hands is a great low-level AOE damage spell, but resist the urge to burn all of your spell slots casting it or you won’t have any slots to heal with. At high levels, Faerie Fire remains incredibly potent, but Burning Hands will be obsolete after a few levels.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

radiance-of-the-dawn|unknown.name: Radiance of the Dawn
radiance-of-the-dawn|unknown.summary: The damage isn’t great beyond low levels. Magical darkness can really cause problems, and a guaranteed way to remove it is very convenient, but you can also negate magical darkness with the spell Daylight, which you get prepared for free once you hit level 5. So there’s a small level window where this might be impactful, but once you get through low levels you’ll frequently get better results from the Harness Divine Power Optional Class Feature if your DM allows it.

warding-flair|meaning-that-they-roll-a-s.name: Warding Flair
warding-flair|meaning-that-they-roll-a-s.source:
meaning
		that they roll a second die and choose the lower of the two results, not
		that they need to dump whatever they’ve already rolled
warding-flair|meaning-that-they-roll-a-s.summary: You won’t get a ton of uses, so save this for enemies which can do a lot of damage on a single attack. This needs to be activated “before an attack hits or misses”, which is frustratingly vague, but I assume it means “before the result of the attack is determined”. So your DM could roll, ask “Does a 25 hit?” knowing full well that it does, and you could scream “Warding Flare!” before the DM says “you are hit” and the DM would then roll with Disadvantage (meaning that they roll a second die and choose the lower of the two results, not that they need to dump whatever they’ve already rolled). Of course, your DM might read that differently and take my portrayal of that interaction poorly, so check with your DM before you assume how this works. Tragically, Jeremy Crawford’s only response on the subject doesn’t actually clarify the answer.

improved-flare|like-a-wizard.name: Improved Flare
improved-flare|like-a-wizard.summary: Fantastic if you have allies who are squishier than you (like a Wizard) or if you need to buy time until you can heal someone.

corona-of-light|unknown.name: Corona of Light
corona-of-light|unknown.summary: If you’re anything like me, you want to make a joke about light beer whenever you see this ability. But, unlike light beer, this is fun. It’s essentially an overdrive button for your Fire and Radiant damage spells, which is especially nice with Light Domain Spells and with Cleric staples like Spirit Guardians. However, it’s an Action to activate, which can make it hard to use in combat. Start this before jumping into combat if possible.

blessing-of-the-trickster|unknown.name: Blessing of the Trickster
blessing-of-the-trickster|unknown.summary: Perpetual Advantage without Concentration. Fantastic and reliable.

invoke-duplicity|function.name: Invoke Duplicity
invoke-duplicity|function.summary: This can be difficult to use effectively, but once you get your head around it, it’s very potent. The best use case is to put the illusion somewhere visible while you’re hidden nearby and use the illusion as the origin point of your short-range spells. Options like Word of Radiance are much safer when you can walk your illusion into a crowd of enemies to cast it, and, since the illusion isn’t a creature, it’s not worried about things like Opportunity Attacks, area control effects, or even enemy creatures blocking spaces. You can use the illusion to get yourself Advantage in melee, but I’m nervous to recommend capitalizing on that as a go-to tactic. Weapon attacks aren’t a great option for Clerics. Easy access to Advantage may make weapons viable compared to cantrips, especially with Divine Strike, but don’t let that compel you to build around melee. This notably applies to all attacks, so you can deliver spells like Inflict Wounds and Spiritual Weapon with Advantage.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); }); If you’re happy using your illusory double as a distraction and as a courier for your spells, you can totally ignore the Advantage part of Invoke Duplicity and you’ll still do just fine. The wording of the ability allows you to place the illusion and move it around in the air. This may be helpful for targeting spells with less concerns about cover, or for targeting flying enemies. Strangely, Invoke Duplicity doesn’t offer details on how to handle interaction with the illusory double. What happens if the illusion is attacked? Can creatures disbelieve it, and if they do so, how do they then perceive the illusion? If creatures are aware that the double is an illusion, do you still get Advantage on attacks when you and your double are adjacent to a creature? Jeremy Crawford has confirmed that the duplicate is immune to damage and that weapons pass right through itezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });, but that’s the only useful rules answer that I’ve found on the subject.

trickery-domain-spells|unknown.name: Trickery Domain Spells
trickery-domain-spells|unknown.summary: Lots of really fun options, many of which aren’t normally available to Clerics, and many of which can make your entire party stealthy. : Disguise Self and Charm Person can diffuse quite a few social situations. Charm Person can’t completely replace a real Face, but it gets pretty close. : Two of the best stealth spells in the game. : Hypnotic Pattern can shut down entire encounters with one spell. Nondetection is only situationally useful, but it does protect stealthy characters like the Trickery Cleric from magical detection. : Confusion sucks, but teleportation is great. : Modify Memory is very situational, but Dominate Person is a great way to turn a powerful humanoid enemy into a fun pet for up to a minute.

level-7-spells|unknown.name: Level 7 Spells
level-7-spells|unknown.summary: Confusion sucks, but teleportation is great.

level-9-spells|unknown.name: Level 9 Spells
level-9-spells|unknown.summary: Modify Memory is very situational, but Dominate Person is a great way to turn a powerful humanoid enemy into a fun pet for up to a minute.

trickster-s-transposition|unknown.name: Trickster’s Transposition
trickster-s-transposition|unknown.summary: Teleportation like this can be very powerful, allowing you to move around easily in combat and to get around obstacles outside of combat by flying your duplicate to wherever you want to go, then switching places with it.

shared-distraction|unknown.name: Shared Distraction
shared-distraction|unknown.summary: You no longer need to be in melee with the target to benefit, and now your allies also benefit. Providing easy Advantage on attacks for your entire party is a huge benefit even if you’re not taking advantage of it.

healing-illusion|unknown.name: Healing Illusion
healing-illusion|unknown.summary: Not a lot of healing, but potentially a good way to rescue a dying ally without spending a Spell Slot. You may be able to use this on yourself when you fall unconscious since the illusion ends when you become Incapacitated.

guided-strike|unknown.name: Guided Strike
guided-strike|unknown.summary: +10 is a huge bonus, almost certainly turning a missed attack into a hit. Channel Divinity uses scale from 2 at low levels to 4 at high levels, but that’s likely not enough to use Channel Divinity every time someone misses an attack. Reserve this for high-value attacks like powerful spells and Sneak Attack.

war-domain-spells|unknown.name: War Domain Spells
war-domain-spells|unknown.summary: War Domain’s spells strike a balance between direct, offensive options and defensive options, most of which have a decidedly martial feel. : Guiding Bolt is a fantastic spell, providing both excellent damage and Advantage on your party’s next attack. It remains a good use of a low level spell slot through your whole career, especially with Guided Strike to rescue a failed attack roll. Shield of Faith will remain useful at every level. +2 AC is big in 5e, and 10 minutes is a fantastic duration for a spell slot. However, it requires Concentration, which means that you can’t combine it with other great low-level buffs like Bless. : Magic Weapon is essential if you lack permanent magical weapons, but for allies that rely heavily on weapons, the +1 attack/damage bonus is also a huge boost to their damage output. If you’re expecting to face several encounters in the 1-hour duration, Spiritual Weapon is a staple Cleric option, and a great way to convert your Bonus Action into damage output while leaving your Action free for non-Concentration spells like Guiding Bolt. However, it competes for space with War Priest both conceptually and within the action economy. : Crusader’s Mantle is Divine Favor for the whole party. The damage per attack is still small, but if you have someone using Two-Weapon Fighting, allies with Extra Attack, or just a large party, the value adds up quickly. But it generally can’t compete with Spirit Guardians, which you also get. Spirit Guardians is among the most efficient damage options in the game, and many clerics prepare it every day. : Fire Shield is a great defensive buff if you’re on the front lines, especially if you’re not wearing heavy armor and a shield. Freedom of movement is situationally useful. : Hold Monster is a fantastic save-or-suck spell which you can immediately follow with an attack from War Priest for a guaranteed critical hit. Steel Wind Strike is simple, direct damage. Since you can use Guided Strike without an action for your own attacks, you can use it with multiple missed attacks within a single turn. Note that the damage is fixed regardless of your weapon, so you can wave a dart and still deal 6d10 damage to each of your targets if you don’t routinely wield a weapon.

war-priest|function.name: War Priest
war-priest|function.summary: A convenient use for your Bonus Action, allowing you to turn any spare Bonus Action into an attack. Once you hit 20 Wisdom, you might find yourself unable to use all of your War Priest uses in a given adventuring day, provided that your party remembers to take Short Rests. The biggest difficulty here is that you need to invest in either Strength or Dexterity to make these attacks effective, which is difficult for the cleric. Shillelagh helps, but it also competes for your Bonus Action. Your best bet is to use Guided Strike when you miss, but that does add another limited resource to the equation whenever you want to attack. There’s also a great deal of competition within the subclass for your Bonus Action, and nearly every use of your Bonus Action is more appealing than War Priest. Fortunately, these options start to come online right as you start getting ability score increases and decide that it’s time to leave your Strength or Dexterity at 16 in order to focus on Wisdom.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });

war-god-s-blessing|unknown.name: War God’s Blessing
war-god-s-blessing|unknown.summary: Casting Shield of Faith without Concentration is a significant buff at any point in your career, and since Channel Divinity recharges on a Short Rest, you can afford to use it frequently. Spiritual Weapon as a Bonus Action is similarly fantastic, and will be a much more reliable use for your Bonus Action than building yourself to use War Priest, but the damage may feel unappealing at high levels since it won’t scale.

avatar-of-battle|unknown.name: Avatar of Battle
avatar-of-battle|unknown.summary: Permanent resistance to the three most common damage types in the game.

guidance|phb.name: Guidance
guidance|phb.summary: As long as you’re not concentrating on something with a long duration between fights, you should be constantly throwing this on your allies. Your Rogue should have Guidance for every skill check they make while searching, sneaking, handling traps, etc.

light|phb.name: Light
light|phb.summary: Disposable magic light is fantastic, but if you don’t have room for the cantrip you’ll do fine with torches.

mending|phb.name: Mending
mending|phb.summary: Too situational. Short of Rust Monsters and a few oozes, nearly nothing in 5e deals damage to your equipment. If you’re playing Spelljammer this is essential, but otherwise you can skip it.

resistance|phb.name: Resistance
resistance|phb.summary: The amount of damage prevented is small and doesn’t scale, so committing Concentration to this is hard to justify beyond very low levels. This could be useful against low-CR elementals which you’ll face at levels 1 and 2, but 1d4 damage per turn just isn’t enough beyond that.

sacred-flame|phb.name: Sacred Flame
sacred-flame|phb.summary: Probably the best source of radiant damage in the game. It’s a reliable way to kill zombies, and since it requires a saving throw rather than an attack, you can use it against adjacent enemies without issue. The ability to ignore cover is nice on a spell which calls for a Dexterity save, but you could also switch to a different spell like Toll the Dead if cover becomes an issue.

spare-the-dying|unknown.name: Spare the Dying
spare-the-dying|unknown.summary: The only benefit to Spare the Dying is that it has 15-foot range, and that’s so little range that it’s hardly worth considering. Buy a Healer’s Kit and walk the 15 feet if you need to stabilize an ally as an Action.

thaumaturgy|phb.name: Thaumaturgy
thaumaturgy|phb.summary: Thematically fun, but not especially useful. See our Practical Guide to Prestidigitation and Similar Cantrips for more.

toll-the-dead|phb.name: Toll the Dead
toll-the-dead|phb.summary: 60 ft. range, the damage is measured in d12’s, and since it’s Necrotic damage, almost nothing will resist it.

word-of-radiance|xgte.name: Word of Radiance
word-of-radiance|xgte.summary: A great way to handle crowds of multiple enemies. See our article on Melee Cantrips vs. Extra Attack for a breakdown of the math comparing melee Cantrips to normal martial attacks.

bane|phb.name: Bane
bane|phb.summary: While the debuff is good, Bane is often difficult to justify. Against crowds, enemies will die too quickly to justify debuffing them. Against bigger enemies, it makes more sense to hit them with something more debilitating. However, Bane isn’t without merit. Since it targets Charisma saves, many enemies that are resistant to more common Constitution or Wisdom saves still have poor Charisma saves. It’s also especially useful against enemies with Legendary Resistance because it puts the DM into a no-win situation: do they burn a Legendary Resistance one a level 1 spell, or do they accept the debuff which will make them more vulnerable for the rest of the fight?

bless|phb.name: Bless
bless|phb.summary: At low levels Bless can decide if you win or lose a fight, but even at very high levels adding 1d4 to attack rolls can dramatically improve your party’s damage output. This gets better as your party gains the ability to make more numerous attacks, so if you have fighters, warlocks, or characters who use two-weapon fighting, Crossbow Expert, or Polearm Master, this will get a ton of mileage. If you’re not concentrating on anything else, Bless is a great go-to option in nearly any case.

command|phb.name: Command
command|phb.summary: Enough effects to be useful in many situations, but it’s a single-target spell and the effects only last one turn, so at low levels it’s hard to justify. Consider picking this up a few levels into your career once you have the ability to upcast it to affect multiple targets. The best uses of Command typically require support from your allies. Approach and Flee are great if you have melee allies who can make Opportunity Attacks when the target moves. Drop is great if someone in your party can quickly pick up the dropped item, preventing weapon-using enemies from arming themselves again. Grovel can cause flying enemies to fall. Halt simply trades actions, but robbing your target of a turn is certainly impactful. At high levels, spending an Action and a level 1 spell slot to prevent a powerful foe from acting can easily win a fight.

create-or-destroy-water|eepc-xgte.name: Create or Destroy Water
create-or-destroy-water|eepc-xgte.summary: The ability to magically create water has many uses. Few of them are combat-related, but this neatly solves a major component of any survival scenario.

cure-wounds|phb.name: Cure Wounds
cure-wounds|phb.summary: Significantly more healing than Healing Word, but the action economy is worse in exchange. Save this for when you need a lot of hit points in a hurry. Ideally, you’ll heal an ally from 0 hp (or at least close to it) to full or nearly full hp. As a rule, healing in combat is a bad choice unless someone is unconscious or you can heal them enough to keep them conscious for multiple turns. If you heal an ally and they immediately take damage roughly equal to what you healed, you have spent an Action and a spell slot to negate an Action from an enemy that likely won’t need to track spell slots for more than a few rounds. If all that you’re doing is offsetting damage, you’re in an attrition fight. Players always lose attrition fights, even when they win the fight.

detect-evil-and-good|phb.name: Detect Evil and Good
detect-evil-and-good|phb.summary: Situationally useful, and you can use it to find invisible enemies or detect enemies through thin walls.

detect-magic|phb.name: Detect Magic
detect-magic|phb.summary: Essential. If you’re not concentrating on anything else, it’s often a good idea to cast this as a ritual and walk around with it.

detect-poison-and-disease|phb.name: Detect Poison and Disease
detect-poison-and-disease|phb.summary: Very situational, and unless you can also cast Protection From Poison there’s little you can do about it anyway. Fortunately, you can cast this as a ritual.

guiding-bolt|phb.name: Guiding Bolt
guiding-bolt|phb.summary: Great single-target damage for a 1st-level spell, and even though the Advantage only applies for one attack it’s easy to have an ally follow your Guiding Bolt with another spell or with a high-powered attack like a Sneak Attack.

healing-word|phb.name: Healing Word
healing-word|phb.summary: More important than Cure Wounds, especially at low levels. As a bonus action you can heal an unconscious ally enough to get them back into the fight, and you still have your action for Cantrips.

inflict-wounds|phb.name: Inflict Wounds
inflict-wounds|phb.summary: Bad damage on a Constitution save at melee range.

protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.name: Protection from Evil and Good
protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.summary: A great defensive option at any level, but Sanctuary will be more effective in melee and Sanctuary doesn’t care about creature type.

purify-food-and-drink|phb.name: Purify Food and Drink
purify-food-and-drink|phb.summary: Cast this as a ritual and you’ll never need to worry about spoiled food again. One of many reasons that Dungeons and Dragons makes a terrible wilderness survival game.

sanctuary|phb.name: Sanctuary
sanctuary|phb.summary: Potentially forcing enemies to give up an attack is great, and this doesn’t prevent the target from contributing via class features, the Help action, summoned creatures, pets, etc, though preventing spellcasting means that your target can’t spend the rest of the fight casting buffs and support spells. Sanctuary also has a Bonus Action casting time, so you can attack or cast a Cantrip in the same turn before casting Sanctuary on yourself. It doesn’t even require Concentration, so for the puny cost of a few level 1 spell slots, you could throw this on everyone in your party over the course of several turns (don’t actually do this; no one will be able to attack). Since Sanctuary allows the attacker to retarget their attack, Sanctuary isn’t as effective against ranged attacks as it is against melee attacks, but that shouldn’t deter you.

shield-of-faith|phb.name: Shield of Faith
shield-of-faith|phb.summary: +2 AC is a significant boost, and the Bonus Action casting time means that you can easily wait to cast this until you get into combat. The spell lasts 10 minutes and it’s only level 1, so Shield of Faith remains an excellent buff on any character at any level. However, it requires Concentration, so in many cases Sanctuary will be more effective unless you’re running directly from one encounter to another and can benefit from Shield of Faith’s relatively long duration.

wardaway|frhof.name: Wardaway
wardaway|frhof.summary: A weaker version of Tasha’s Mind Whip, Wardaway makes some huge trades to fit into a level 1 spell. The damage is obviously much worse, but that’s not why you’re here. The target still gets to move and act in the same turn, but halving their speed is still impactful. The biggest limitation is that Wardaway uses a Constitution save instead of a much more reliable Intelligence save. At low levels where enemies have very few saving throw proficiencies, Wardaway may be decently reliable. But enemies at low levels also rarely have Bonus Actions, so they’re likely to fail the save and barely notice the spell’s effect.

aid|phb.name: Aid
aid|phb.summary: With an 8-hour duration and three targets, this is a staple buff that’s worth casting literally every day. Keep in mind that this actually increases the targets’ hit point maximum, so temporary hit points can be added, too. Aid’s casting time allows it to be used in combat, which is unusual but offers an interesting option. With three targets and a 30-foot range, you can cast it to both buff and heal your allies during combat. Targets’ current hit points and hit point maximum both increase, so allies at 0 hit points are healed in addition to having their hit point maximum raised, thereby allowing Aid to serve a similar function to Mass Healing Word.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); }); However, since spells don’t stack with themselves, it’s hard to repeat this trick. You’ll need to cast Aid again using higher-level spell slots, which can get expensive quickly, so Mass Healing Word is probably better if Aid is already running and if Mass Healing Word is an option for your party.

augury|phb.name: Augury
augury|phb.summary: This is my absolute favorite divination spell because it allows players to politely ask their DM for hints. Castable as a ritual with a reusable material component, if you have time you can cast this repeatedly to question all sorts of decisions.

blindness-deafness|phb.name: Blindness/Deafness
blindness-deafness|phb.summary: Blindness is crippling, especially for enemies who fight at range like archers and spellcasters. It’s also helpful against melee enemies, but Constitution saves tend to be high, so it’s often best to use this on enemies which are more physically frail. Deafness is a mild annoyance.

borrowed-knowledge|scoc.name: Borrowed Knowledge
borrowed-knowledge|scoc.summary: A great way to cover skill proficiencies that your party doesn’t have, Borrowed Knowledge lasts an hour and doesn’t require Concentration, so you can combine it with Enhance Ability to become instantly excellent at any skill. Enhance Ability is more broadly useful because you can cast it on other allies to support them when their best skills come into play, but when there’s a gap in your party’s skillset, you can use this to come to the rescue.

calm-emotions|phb.name: Calm Emotions
calm-emotions|phb.summary: Two situational but frequently useful effects. First, you can use this to temporarily suppress effects which charm or frighten your allies. Both effects are common, and many enemies can apply them to your whole party. Charm effects often include mind control effects, and suppressing them for a minute on a willing ally can easily buy you enough time to deal with whatever is trying to mind control your friends. Fear effects are often area effects, such as a dragon’s Frightful Presence, so suppressing them for a minute can bring whichever portions of your party failed their saves back into the fray. Second, you can use this to make enemies not be hostile toward you and your allies for one minute. That will at least pause most encounters for the spell’s duration, which is enough time to either heal and buff the party or escape. I wouldn’t try to negotiate a truce in one minute, especially since the targets can go right back to hostile the moment that the spell ends. Note that this effect intentionally uses the “Hostile/Indifferent/Friendly” disposition scale described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide.

continual-flame|phb.name: Continual Flame
continual-flame|phb.summary: Having reliable, constant light is really nice. Cast this on a shield, a necklace, a weapon, or maybe a whole bunch of different things to guarantee that you always have adequate light without casting light or lighting a torch.

deryan-s-helpful-homunculi|frhof.name: Deryan’s Helpful Homunculi
deryan-s-helpful-homunculi|frhof.summary: Since you can cast this as a Ritual, you’re effectively turning gold into short-lived assistance while crafting an item. This is only useful if you’re leaning into the 2024 rules’ extremely lackluster crafting system, and even then it’s only useful if you’re in a hurry but also have a ton of extra money lying around.

enhance-ability|phb.name: Enhance Ability
enhance-ability|phb.summary: Fantastic and versatile. Using this to buff Charisma for your party’s Face will make any social situation go a lot better.

find-traps|unknown.name: Find Traps
find-traps|unknown.summary: Too expensive and too imprecise. Invest in Investigation.

gentle-repose|phb.name: Gentle Repose
gentle-repose|phb.summary: Very situational, but it solves some interesting problems. Normally you can cremate a body to prevent it from becoming undead, but cremating a body takes an alarmingly large amount of fuel which you probably don’t have laying about. You can mutilate the body, but that’s gross and in many campaign settings the gods view that sort of thing as evil. So if you need to maintain a body until you can give it a real burial, this is your best bet. Fortunately, you can cast it as a ritual and you can typically wait until the next day so that you can prepare this as needed. Gentle Repose also pauses the timer on effects which raise the dead. While this is specifically called out as working with Raise Dead, it works with anything that raises creatures from the dead. That includes Revivify. So if you keep this prepared, you can haul your allies around until you can cast 3rd-level spells and until you can scrape together enough diamond dust to raise them. Remember that while spells don’t stack, their durations can overlap so if you cast Gentle Repose early to avoid gaps in spell duration you can keep bodies preserved indefinitely.

hold-person|phb.name: Hold Person
hold-person|phb.summary: On/off button for Humanoids. Humanoids are a tiny portion of DnD’s roster of enemies, so this spell is situational by design. Even some creatures which have historically been common Humanoid antagonists like Hoblins and Sahuagin have changed creature type in the 2024 rules, though there are more NPC stat blocks than in the 2014 rules, which might keep Humanoids a relevant threat in some campaigns. In encounters with multiple foes, you can up-cast Hold Person to paralyze multiple targets, so this can still handle groups of enemies when AOE damage spells aren’t a good idea for whatever reason. Paralysis is a serious status condition, granting Advantage on attacks against the targets and guaranteeing Critical Hits for attacks made within 5 feet of the target. Send anyone with a weapon into melee to finish off the targets before they manage to succeed on a follow-up save to remove the condition. However, remember that targets get an additional save at the end of each round, so you can’t predict how long this will stay in effect. If you up-cast this to affect multiple targets, you may reach a point where so few of them are still paralyzed that maintaining Concentration may not be worthwhile.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

lesser-restoration|phb.name: Lesser Restoration
lesser-restoration|phb.summary: Situational, but a situation that comes up often.

locate-object|phb.name: Locate Object
locate-object|phb.summary: Too situational, and too easy to counter. Anyone with any knowledge of magic that’s trying to hide something will wrap it in lead.

prayer-of-healing|phb.name: Prayer of Healing
prayer-of-healing|phb.summary: A Short Rest plus some extra healing for 5 targets. Useful if you’re pressed for time or if your party goes through hit points quickly and needs more healing than Hit Point Dice can provide.

protection-from-poison|phb.name: Protection From Poison
protection-from-poison|phb.summary: Situational, but poison is common across the full CR range, so this is a fantastic defensive option at any level. The 1-hour duration means that you can get a lot of mileage out of a single spell slot even if you cast it ahead of time.

searing-orb|drops.name: Searing Orb
searing-orb|drops.summary: The damage is dismal, but you’re here for the debuff. Unfortunately, Con saves ten to be high, so many enemies will be able to reliably pass the save. If you manage to catch a crowd of enemies (probably 3 or more), it may be worth the gamble.

silence|phb.name: Silence
silence|phb.summary: Verbal components are extremely common in spells, including many that spellcasters frequently use to escape dangerous situations. If you can trap an enemy spellcaster in place (such as by having an ally grapple them) and drop Silence around them, you’ll significantly limit their options. In the 2024 rules, spellcasting enemies will have combat actions that aren’t actually spells and which will ignore Silence, but you’ll still limit some of their best options.

spiritual-weapon|phb.name: Spiritual Weapon
spiritual-weapon|phb.summary: Basically a summon spell without the advantage of a body to draw attacks, and the 1-minute duration and constant need to use your Bonus Action mean that it quickly becomes obsolete once real summon spells come online for other spellcasters when they get level 3 spells.

warding-bond|phb.name: Warding Bond
warding-bond|phb.summary: A dangerous, but interesting way to protect an ally. Generally you’ll find preventing them from taking damage with spells like Sanctuary will be more effective.

zone-of-truth|phb.name: Zone of Truth
zone-of-truth|phb.summary: Situational and much less reliable than you would hope. Creatures are aware that they’re under the effect, and they can choose to “be evasive”, which means that they could give you true but useless answers or simply not answer. Creatures other than the caster also don’t know who passed or failed the save, so unless they already trust you other creatures might not believe you when you tell them that a creature is telling the truth. If a creature is willing to talk, they can prove that they are saying what they believe to be true, and you can know whether or not they believe it to be true. But if the creature is incorrect, if you’re lying to other creatures (which they might believe that you are), or if any other number of other things go wrong, this spell simply fails to meet its intended purpose. In short, this helps honest creatures prove to you that they are being honest. Nothing else. If you want to get answers from an unwilling or unhelpful subject, cast Detect Thoughts.

animate-dead|phb.name: Animate Dead
animate-dead|phb.summary: Undead are excellent replacements for living creatures in many ways. An undead guard never gets tired while keeping watch. An undead horse never tires of marching. An undead porter won’t complain about their back hurting from hauling your treasure. Sure, desecrating the bodies of the dead is “icky” or “evil” depending on who you ask, but you likely can’t pay NPCs to work 24/7 in highly dangerous conditions far from home, so sometimes you need to compromise ethics in favor of effectiveness.

astral-flood|drops.name: Astral Flood
astral-flood|drops.summary: Decent area damage with good secondary effects. Compare to Fireball’s 8d6 (avg. 28) damage, Astral Flood’s 4d10 (avg. 22) isn’t significantly worse, and the scaling is only slightly worse than Fireball’s. But the rider effects are the big selling point here. The Cold dmaage option imposes Disadvantage on a d20 test, which includes saving throws. If you have other allies with powerful save-or-suck spells, this can prime a whole group of enemies to be quickly incapacitated with spells like Sleep or Hypnotic Pattern. The only drawback is the 30-foot cone, and even that isn’t that bad.

aura-of-vitality|phb.name: Aura of Vitality
aura-of-vitality|phb.summary: Never use this in combat, but 20d6 healing for a level 3 spell is very efficient. That’s an average of 70 hit points, which matches Heal.

beacon-of-hope|phb.name: Beacon of Hope
beacon-of-hope|phb.summary: Thematically, this is a really cool spell. Mechanically, it’s very hard to use. The best way to use this would be when a fight is going poorly so you throw up Beacon of Hope and start casting Mass Cure Wounds or Mass Healing Word to get your party back into the fight. But In those cases you typically just want your party above 0 hit points, and the difference of a few hit points on average won’t matter much. Also, you can’t cast two leveled spells in the same turn anyway, so that ideal scenario is explicitly against the rules. Instead, use the time you would spend casting this to cast literally anything else so you can end the fight faster instead of burning precious resources trying to feed hit points into an insatiable blender.

bestow-curse|phb.name: Bestow Curse
bestow-curse|phb.summary: The effects are versatile enough that you can easily bring this into play in a variety of situations, and the scaling mechanism works well enough that this remains a viable option for higher-level spell slots. Use the third option against big tanky enemies with poor Wisdom, or use the first option against enemies that like to grapple. If you’re ever uncertain, use the third option. Robbing a creature of their turn on a failed saving throw is debilitating, and can take creatures almost completely out of a fight.

clairvoyance|phb.name: Clairvoyance
clairvoyance|phb.summary: With a 1-mile range and the ability to place the sensor in a place you can’t see, this is a fantastic way to safely scout dangerous places. If you have enough time to sit around and cast the spell repeatedly you can scout whole structures from the outside by gradually learning about more interior locations through previous castings.

create-food-and-water|phb.name: Create Food and Water
create-food-and-water|phb.summary: Rations are cheap, but it’s good that you can prepare this if you somehow find yourself somewhere without food for extended periods. This also lets you create 30 gallons of water, which is enough for a nice bath but not enough to fill a 5-foot cube.

daylight|phb.name: Daylight
daylight|phb.summary: A Continual Flame, Light, or even a torch is typically sufficient, but sometimes you need to light up larger areas like dark battlefields or massive caverns. This also dispels magical darkness of 3rd level or lower, which is great if you’re fighting enemies like drow which can produce magical darkness. Tragically, you can’t cast Daylight at a higher level to dispel magical darkness of higher levels.

dispel-magic|phb.name: Dispel Magic
dispel-magic|phb.summary: Every party needs someone who can cast Dispel Magic. It’s simply too important to forgo.

fast-friends|ai.name: Fast Friends
fast-friends|ai.summary: A fantastic non-lethal option for handling single targets, but it has some limitations. The target needs to be able to understand you, so you likely need to share a language. The spell requires Concentration, so you don’t want to maintain this during combat if you can avoid it. And of course, you don’t want to try casting this during combat. If you can isolate a single enemy outside of combat, you may be able to ply them for information or send them on errands which will save you trouble later. Tragically, the spell only lasts an hour so the effects end just as you’re getting really attached to your new best friend, and the targets know that you charmed them. You may be able to cast this repeatedly or you may be able to negotiate the situation peacefully even after the spell ends, but many people don’t take kindly to being charmed. You can also compare this to Suggestion. In the 2024 rules, Suggestion is unrestricted to the point that I use the 2014 version in my own game, but Suggestion doesn’t let you change the commands part-way through the spell. 2024 Suggestion is a better spell than Fast Friends, but Fast Friends is still decent.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

glyph-of-warding|phb.name: Glyph of Warding
glyph-of-warding|phb.summary: Depending on how your DM handles it, this is either a situationally useful defensive measure or a reality-bending way to break the game from the comfort of your own home. See our Practical Guide to Glyph of Warding.

incite-greed|ai.name: Incite Greed
incite-greed|ai.summary: This is a gamble. If targets fail their saves you can draw them into melee range with you and keep them there for up to a minute. You then need to find a way to capitalize on their position. You could walk your full speed away (affected targets can do nothing but move toward you, so they can’t take Reactions to perform an Opportunity Attack), drop Concentration, then hit them with a Fireball.

laerel-s-silver-lance|frhof.name: Laerel’s Silver Lance
laerel-s-silver-lance|frhof.summary: The damage type is fantastic, the Prone effect is great, very few area damage spells target Strength saves, and you can omit targets to avoid hitting friends. There’s definitely a niche here, but 3d10 (avg. 16.5) is very low compared to other level 3 spells. Lightning Bolt is 8d6 (avg. 28), and upcasting Laerel’s Silver Lance actually widens that gap. Preparing this and buying the 250 gp spell component feels like too much investment for the extremely narrow case where you can justify using this over other damage spells. But the Cleric spell list has very few direct damage spells, so this may be more useful than it is for other classes which can cast it.

life-transference|xgte.name: Life Transference
life-transference|xgte.summary: With the buffs to Cure Wounds, this is totally obsolete.

magic-circle|phb.name: Magic Circle
