magic-circle|phb.summary: With a 1-minute casting time, you can’t use this in combat unless you have time to prepare and your enemies are coming to you. Even then, using this in combat isn’t reliable protection because it doesn’t mitigate the effects of spells and abilities which don’t require attack rolls like breath weapons or fireballs. The best use case is generally to invert the effects and use a spell to summon a creature so that you can bargain with it without risk of the creature escaping. Even then, the 1-hour duration may not be enough to guarantee your safety. If you want similar effects in combat, Protection From Evil and Good will do the trick.

mass-healing-word|phb.name: Mass Healing Word
mass-healing-word|phb.summary: You never want to need this. It heals exactly as much as standard Healing Word at a much higher cost, but the ability to heal multiple targets means that you can bring multiple allies back into the fight and you still have your Action that turn. Also, the upcasting is terrible.

motivational-speech|ai.name: Motivational Speech
motivational-speech|ai.summary: This makes the Inspiring Leader somewhat obsolete. Inspiring Leader will provide considerably more temporary hit points, but this doesn’t require a feat and takes one tenth the time.

protection-from-energy|phb.name: Protection From Energy
protection-from-energy|phb.summary: An important, staple defensive option, but it’s single-target and requires Concentration so you can’t afford to keep it running constantly.

remove-curse|phb.name: Remove Curse
remove-curse|phb.summary: Situational, but irreplaceable. Fortunately, you can usually wait a day to prepare this.

revivify|phb.name: Revivify
revivify|phb.summary: (Optional): Everyone who is capable of casting this should keep it handy. It’s simply too good to forgo.

spirit-guardians|phb.name: Spirit Guardians
spirit-guardians|phb.summary: Among the Cleric’s most defining options, Spirit Guardians can win encounters and is rife with abuse cases. The tactics to multiply damage output from Spirit Guardians were defining in the 2014 DnD rules, and in the 2024 rules, they’re now a defining tactic for the character optimization meta as a whole. In an enclosed space, Spirit Guardians makes you the center of an extremely dangerous sphere. With a 15-foot radius, a Medium character can cover a sphere 35 ft. in diameter, easily filling many rooms, and even in larger area, this is still a big area to control. Reducing enemies’ speeds by half further complicates things for them, and if you can create difficult terrain in the area, they’re basically out of luck. Even if you do nothing but cast this spell, walk around, and Dodge on your turn, you can often dominate encounters. The 10-minute duration is long enough that you could easily carry this through multiple fights, and you still get to use your full turn to do more stuff. Spirit Guardians’ damage can trigger once per turn, not once per round, so you can reapply the damage by moving yourself and/or your enemies. The damage triggers when the Emanation enters a target’s space (such as when you cast the spell or walk the AOE onto your enemies), when a target enters the AOE (such as when they move toward you or when your allies knock them into the AOE with a Push weapon), and when a target end their turn in the area. To trigger the damage as often as possible, encourage your allies to collect speed debuffs and forced movement effects. You may also let an ally grapple you and drag you around the battlefield, bringing the damage to your enemies without introducing additional points of failure from your ally attacking or forcing saving throws.

spirit-shroud|tcoe.name: Spirit Shroud
spirit-shroud|tcoe.summary: Clerics never get Extra Attack, and you don’t have options like Scorching Rays to trigger this multiple times per turn unless you’re a Light Domain Cleric. Spirit Guardians is a much more effective use of a spell slot.

tongues|phb.name: Tongues
tongues|phb.summary: The second this spell becomes available to your party, all of their language proficiencies feel silly. The 1-hour duration is long enough to get through all but the lengthiest social situations, and if you’re in a situation where you need to re-cast Tongues you’re not likely to need your spell slots for much else (except Enhanced Ability (Eagle’s Splendor)).

water-walk|phb.name: Water Walk
water-walk|phb.summary: Usually flight is a better option than walking across a liquid, but at least you can cast this as a Ritual.

aura-of-life|phb.name: Aura of Life
aura-of-life|phb.summary: Generally only useful if you know that you’re facing the types of undead which reduce your hit point maximum (there are several). The healing is numerically very efficient for the spell slot: 100 hit points to as many living creatures as you can fit into the 30-foot radius for the spell’s 10-minute duration. However, it only affects creatures at 0 hit points, so you’re never going to actually get that amount of healing unless you’re sprinting across an endless field of dying creatures. The more likely case is that you’ll use this while your allies repeatedly get knocked back to 0 hit points so that they can repeatedly stand back up at 1 hp and keep fighting.

aura-of-purity|phb.name: Aura of Purity
aura-of-purity|phb.summary: Technically situational, but the defenses are broad enough that you can cover a wide variety of situations. In most encounters it’s unlikely that you’ll be hit with more than one or two negative status conditions, but Aura of Purity provides broad enough protection that you’ll be able to counter many of the most common conditions with the same spell.

banishment|phb.name: Banishment
banishment|phb.summary: Among the most powerful save-or-suck spells in the game for several reasons. First, it’s a Charisma saving throw and very few creatures are good at those. Second, many powerful enemies like fiends are extraplanar, so you can easily remove them with a single spell (though many of them can cast Plane Shift to come right back, so watch out for that). Finally, casting the spell at a higher level allows you to target additional creatures so you can remove big parts of an encounter for up to a minute, deal with anything that passes the initial round of banishment, then prep yourself for everything else to drop back in while your party stands around with readied actions.

control-water|phb.name: Control Water
control-water|phb.summary: All of the effects are situational, and there are some weird edge cases like using the Flood option on a puddle or a full bucket where it’s unclear what happens when the water overflows its container.

death-ward|phb.name: Death Ward
death-ward|phb.summary: With an 8-hour duration, this is a great insurance policy. It’s great to throw this on death-prone characters like your party’s Defender, but if you expect to face a high-level spellcast you should also consider putting this on your less-durable allies like wizards to protect them from things like Power Word Kill.

divination|phb.name: Divination
divination|phb.summary: Much more precise than Augury, and it works much further into the future. The 25gp component cost won’t hurt much at this level, but it’s enough to deter you from using this every time you have a question.

doomtide|function.name: Doomtide
doomtide|function.summary: The damage isn’t high, but it’s a good damage type and the save debuff is excellent. Magical darkness will force most enemies to exit the AOE on their turn so that you can force them back into it to trigger the effect again. But, unlike most ongoing area damage spells, the sphere moves away from you gradually, which can make it difficult to keep the spell in the area where you’re fighting. There’s also no word on what happens when the sphere hits cover, so it might run right through walls. : This is something to be done by an NPC, not by a player. A permanent ball of nonsense rolling slowly away from you forever is not something that a player needs. The spell doesn’t end when it moves out of range, but you can drop it up to a mile away and watch it terrorize innocent civilians. Also, how weird is that material component? A string of black pearls from another plane, but somehow it doesn’t have a gp cost. The sphere notably keeps going forever. As explained in the rules for spell ranges, “If a spell has movable effects, they aren’t restricted by its range unless the spell’s description says otherwise.” You could, in theory, shoot this into space and it would float along like an angry little cloud forever.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });

freedom-of-movement|phb.name: Freedom of Movement
freedom-of-movement|phb.summary: Situational, but a great way to handle being grappled if you have poor Strength and if you’re not proficient in either Athletics or Acrobatics.

guardian-of-faith|phb.name: Guardian of Faith
guardian-of-faith|phb.summary: Only useful because of the 8-hour duration. The cap of 60 damage means that it’s going to make 3 to 6 attacks (more if enemies have Evasion or Damage Resistance), which isn’t enough to justify this in combat. Instead, throw it up to protect yourself while your party is resting or as a trap that you’re going to drive your enemies into. Guardian of Faith is arguably a decent area control spell, and it doesn’t require Concentration like similar spells. But Guardian of Faith’s limited damage and absolute lack of scaling makes it hard to justify the spell slot. Your best bet is to line up several Guardian of Faith spells in a row and drag enemies through them in succession. But that’s a very expensive way to replicate Spike Growth just so that you can avoid Concentration.

locate-creature|phb.name: Locate Creature
locate-creature|phb.summary: More effective than mundane tracking, but the 1,000-foot range can be a problem if the target is actively fleeing from you. If you’re going to use this, be sure that you’re moving faster than your target.

sticks-to-snakes|drops.name: Sticks to Snakes
sticks-to-snakes|drops.summary: This is effectively a summoning spell which summons 4 CR 1/8 creatures. By the time you can cast this, that’s utterly useless. The best-case scenario is using this on wooden items that enemies are carrying. You can’t use it on magic items, so you can’t use it on the enemy wizard’s magic staff, but you can use it on mundane enemy weapons like spears. Most enemies use nonmagical weapons even if their attacks are magic, so this could be occasionally useful through the whole level range. But that depends on your enemies’ weapon selection, which is difficult to predict, so this is only situationally useful.

stone-shape|phb.name: Stone Shape
stone-shape|phb.summary: Stone is an incredibly common material in dungeons, castles, and other structures, so the ability to reshape it is immensely powerful. Using this to pass through walls or seal doors are obvious options, but a clever player can do a lot of damage by sabotaging structures or altering natural stone terrain. Typically you can’t use this in combat, but you could shape a 5 ft. cube directly above an enemy so that it falls on them. Tragically, the 5e rules don’t specify how much damage is dealt by falling objects or a DC to avoid them, so the effect comes down to what your DM does with the improvised damage table in the DMG.

circle-of-power|phb.name: Circle of Power
circle-of-power|phb.summary: Great protection against enemy spellcasters, but it’s entirely passive and only matters if your enemies rely primarily on spells, so it’s situational by design.

commune|phb.name: Commune
commune|phb.summary: A yes-or-no answer is enough to get a great deal of information if you ask your questions well. But you need to ask all three questions before the spell’s 1-minute duration expires, so your DM could (and probably should) set a real-world timer. If the DM needs time to think of the answers, pause the timer. Unlike Divination, this doesn’t consume the material component so if you can spare the prepared spell, you should consider casting this once every evening before you rest to see what you can learn.

contagion|phb.name: Contagion
contagion|phb.summary: Sage Advice made significant changes to how this spell works, so if you have a physical copy of the Player’s Handbook make sure you go download the latest version of the Sage Advice and Errata documents. If you hit the target with a melee spell attack, they’re poisoned for a minimum of 3 turns. Poisoned is an extremely effective debuff, though many creatures are resistant or immune to it. Even so, the Poisoned effect may be more significant than the disease. The target must fail a total of three saving throws to apply your chosen disease, and considering a typical combat lasts 3-5 rounds many enemies won’t live long enough for that to happen. Consider the Poisoned effect to be the primary effect of the spell, and think of the disease as a neat novelty which might come up if you don’t manage to kill the target fast enough.

dawn|phb.name: Dawn
dawn|phb.summary: This is a mediocre area denial option. You can spend a Bonus Action to move it, which is really nice, but Constitution saves tend to be high, and the damage isn’t spectacular. Compare this to casting Spirit Guardians as a level 5 spell: 5d8 damage (avg. 22.5) compared to 4d10 (avg. 22), but Spirit Guardians won’t hurt you or your allies, and if you need to move the effects, you can walk and spend your Bonus Action doing something like casting a Cantrip. Dawn’s single saving grace is that it specifically says “this light is sunlight”, which means that it hurts vampires and some other monsters very badly. If you can grapple a vampire to hold it in the radius of Dawn, you can kill them pretty easily.

dispel-evil-and-good|phb.name: Dispel Evil and Good
dispel-evil-and-good|phb.summary: In most cases, Protection from Evil and Good will do the trick, but Dispel Evil and Good has two additional effects. You can prematurely end the spell to end a charm/frighten/possession effect, or to attempt to banish creatures from other planes. They do still get a saving throw, and if the creatures are native to the plane they’re on, nothing happens. It’s very important to note that the banishment effect isn’t limited by the spell’s duration: creatures banished this way are sent to another plane and must return by normal means. However, since the banishment effect doesn’t affect creatures on their home plane, the banishment may not be as appealing as spells like Banishment which can affect creatures native to your current plane.

flame-strike|phb.name: Flame Strike
flame-strike|phb.summary: Only as much damage as Fireball cast a spell level lower than whatever spell slot you use for Flame Strike. The big appeal is that there are two damage types, so creatures which are immune or resistant to one generally won’t be resistant or immune to both. But if you’re casting a 5th-level spell intending to only get partial damage, you’re wasting a 5th-level spell slot. If you want radiant damage, 5th-level Spirit guardians will deal 5d8 radiant damage (avg. 22.5) compared to 10d6 (avg. 25) from Flame Strike, and Spirit Guardians last 10 minutes and you can walk around with it. If you want fire damage, most Clerics are out of luck, but if you just need a ranged AOE, Dawn or Insect Plague will be more effective in almost every case.

geas|phb.name: Geas
geas|phb.summary: This spell is situational by design. It has a 1-minute casting time and Verbal components, so you’re not going to break this out in combat or while sneaking around in a dungeon. You’re going to restrain the subject, and stand around chanting for a full minute and hope that they fail the save. Once that’s done, you need to give them a suitable command (read the spell description). Generally you’ll want it to be something that benefits you, but will also take the target most of the duration to keep them from becoming a problem for you. Also remember that the base effect of the Charmed condition makes it easier for you to talk the creature into doing things with Charisma checks, so a Geased creature may be a useful ally for the duration of the effect even if the original order isn’t directly related to what you want them to do. Increasing the spell level extends the duration, but weirdly the damage doesn’t increase. 5d10 is a nice pile of damage, but it doesn’t scale with spell level and at some point the target will get smart enough to wake up, trigger the 5d10 damage, take a short rest, then go about their business. If the damage scaled this would be less of a problem, but damage is so easily repaired in 5e outside of combat that without further penalties Geas is more a tax on hit dice than the magical shackles it’s intended to be. If you want a homebrew fix, add a level of fatigue each day that the target is out of compliance, or make the damage impossible to heal until they go a day without taking it. Neither of those is a perfect solution, but they’re miles better than an average of 27.5 damage.

greater-restoration|phb.name: Greater Restoration
greater-restoration|phb.summary: If you don’t have a Cleric in the party, you need this.

hallow|phb.name: Hallow
hallow|phb.summary: Situational by design. This isn’t a spell that you just carry around. With a 24-hour casting time, this is a spell that you plan out well in advance, get comfortable for, and probably eat a hefty meal beforehand because you don’t want to stop for food or water until it’s done. The effects are powerful and versatile, and since they’re permanent until dispelled this spell can easily outlive you. Unfortunately, the spell is still susceptible to Dispel Magic, and watching some jerk repeatedly cast Dispel Magic as a 3rd-level spell until they pass the DC 19 ability check for your 9th-level Hallow feels really bad after you spent so much time and money to cast it.

holy-weapon|xgte.name: Holy Weapon
holy-weapon|xgte.summary: 1-hour duration and cast as a bonus action. The intent is that you’ll cast this and attack in the same turn, but Clerics never get Extra Attack (War Clerics get an extra attack as a bonus action a few times per day, but that isn’t enough to keep you busy for an hour) so that’s a horrible use of this spell. Put this on someone making a whole bunch of attacks with one weapon. A fighter is ideal, but someone using Polearm Master or Crossbow Expert will suffice. You want as many attacks as you can get as quickly as you can get them to maximize the total damage dealt. When the duration runs short, or when you need to concentrate on something else, end the spell early and blind every enemy in the radius.

insect-plague|phb.name: Insect Plague
insect-plague|phb.summary: An improvement over Dawn in some ways, but some of the same challenges. Creatures can still move out of the area to avoid the ongoing damage, but with a 20-foot radius of difficult terrain that’s slightly harder to accomplish than in the area of Dawn, but not by enough that Insect Plague is actually better.

legend-lore|phb.name: Legend Lore
legend-lore|phb.summary: Situational, but potentially very useful. “Famous” is a bit subjective, but there’s easy room to argue that someone gaining notoriety in some fashion is famous enough to qualify. The spell calls out that you could learn “secret lore that has never been widely known,” which presents some interesting opportunities. You might be able to learn things like the identities of secretive, unknown enemies. The more you know already, the more detailed the information becomes, so repeated castings might lead to you learning a ton of useful information. But the rules text also gives the DM a way to disguise information with “figurative language or poetry.” So your DM might give you some absolute nonsense in order to disguise relevant plot details. My advice: If the DM enjoys that, lean into it. If they’re doing it to keep you from spoiling the plot, let them keep their secrets for now.

mass-cure-wounds|phb.name: Mass Cure Wounds
mass-cure-wounds|phb.summary: You shouldn’t need this. It doesn’t do enough healing to justify the spell slot, so the best use case is to cast it when you have more than one ally at 0 hit points. If you reach that point, things have gone very seriously wrong. Healing Word is a much more efficient way to get people conscious, and considering how little healing you’re getting out of Mass Cure Wounds your allies will probably go down again anyway if anything looks at them funny.

planar-binding|phb.name: Planar Binding
planar-binding|phb.summary: At the level you get this, 1,000gp is a steep price to pay for a spell that lasts 24 hours. Save this for higher levels when you can cast something like Gate to summon a powerful creature and bind it to your service for a long time. If you can somehow get two 9th-level spells, you could summon a Balor or something equally powerful for a year and a day, then command it to conquer a continent for you or something. Most creatures won’t be happy about this form of servitude, of course, so be sure to plan for their sudden yet inevitable betrayal. For more help, see my Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

raise-dead|phb.name: Raise Dead
raise-dead|phb.summary: Don’t bother preparing this unless someone is already dead. If your ally dies, they’ll still be dead the next day when you prepare Raise Dead.

scrying|phb.name: Scrying
scrying|phb.summary: Spy on the campaign’s antagonists at every opportunity. The material component is expensive, but it’s reusable so you can buy a fancy mirror once then spend the rest of your character’s career spying on people from afar. The target gets a saving throw to resist, but doesn’t know that they’re being targeted by the spell. The sensor works the same way that Clairvoyance does (uses your normal senses, invisible luminous orb, etc.), so generally creatures will never know that they’re being spied on unless they can see through invisibility. While the text of the spell isn’t clear, I believe that the Connections use whichever has the biggest effect rather than stacking, so you can’t use your macaroni art of the target and a lock of their hair from your closet shrine to them to give them a -12. In case it wasn’t clear already: using this spell is super creepy, and you shouldn’t go around using it for recreational purposes.

summon-celestial|phb.name: Summon Celestial
summon-celestial|phb.summary: Summon a pet fighter. Defender is a melee fighter that can grant temporary hit points. Avenger is a ranged fighter that shoots lasers from a bow. Both deal radiant damage and can fly. It’s pretty great. For more help, see my Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

blade-barrier|phb.name: Blade Barrier
blade-barrier|phb.summary: The AOE is good and the damage is good. The wall also provides 3/4 cover, which is great since Clerics almost never use spells that require ranged attacks. Casting a spell that targets creatures on the other side of the wall doesn’t care about cover unless the center of the AOE is on the wrong side for some reason. Unfortunately, there’s no spell level scaling, and aside from being difficult terrain, there’s very little preventing enemies from running through the wall, suffering the damage, and going right back to fighting as though you had just hit them with a 6d10 Fireball or something.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(183); }); Blade Barrier also doesn’t have the advantage of portability provided by Spirit Guardians, and Spirit Guardians does comparable damage (1d8 per spell level vs 1d10 per spell level). Unless you need to put up the barrier and retreat, Spirit Guardians is likely a better choice.

create-undead|phb.name: Create Undead
create-undead|phb.summary: If you just need something to ride around on or a minion to carry your treasure, use Animate Dead. If you want to have an intelligent thrall to handle complex tasks or to act as a bodyguard, use Create Undead. But remember: undead are evil and will murder you at the first opportunity, and generally DMs don’t like players dragging an undead army around behind them.

dirge|frhof.name: Dirge
dirge|frhof.summary: This is another one of those Spirit Guardians-style spells: Turn it on, walk into a room, blend your enemies. However, most of those spells have Emanations of 10 to 20 feet. Dirge has a staggering like radius of 60 feet, which will cover all by the largest combat encounters. It pays for that massive radius with a 1-minute duration (compared to 10 for similar spells) and only 3d10 damage (compared to 3d8 for level 3 Spirit Guardians). The secondary effect knocks foes prone of halves their speed, effectively eating half of their speed either way. Creatures (and remember that you can omit specific creatures from the spell’s effect) also can’t heal while in the area, which doesn’t come up often, but is a nice bonus. Unlike other Spirit Guardians-style spells, you can’t easily abuse it by using forced movement to drag enemies in and out of the AOE. Because the radius is so large, you’ll likely fill the area of any combat encounter. Where similar spells are at their best when you can apply the damage several times per round, Dirge likely can’t do that. Instead, you’re here for the speed debuff. Stack it with other speed debuffs like Ray of Frost, the Slasher feat, and the Slow Weapon Mastery, and you can effectively freeze enemies in place. Combine that with some forced movement to get enemies into a small area, and you and your allies and bring down your enemies with a few low-cost area damage effects. : Casting this as a Circle spell is brutal. Exhaustion imposes a penalty on saves which quickly turns this into a death spiral, and the inability to remove the Exhaustion by resting means that most creatures are permanently exhausted. If you can use this to hit important antagonists (the BBEG or their named lackies), it could shift the direction of an entire campaign unless those creatures have access to a spellcaster who can cast Greater Restoration and several hundred gp of diamond dust.

find-the-path|phb.name: Find the Path
find-the-path|phb.summary: This is barely useful as it is, but the next spell level brings Plane Shift, which will immediately solve long-distance travel challenges.

forbiddance|phb.name: Forbiddance
forbiddance|phb.summary: This is a strange spell, and it’s very easy to abuse in ways that the designers likely didn’t intend. Since you can cast it as a ritual, it’s basically a 1,000gp cost to buy into the spell, then it’s free to cast any time after that unless you want to make it permanent. Forbiddance is intended to create areas where you can keep creatures of a specific type out of the area, so important holy sites could keep out undead and fiends, but potentially allow celestials. But as the spell is written the area can be occupied while you cast the spell, including by creatures that you’re going to forbid. If you come upon a dungeon which you know is full of forbiddable creatures (technically you don’t need to know, but knowing ahead of time is the abuse case), you can sit down, spend 20 minutes to cast this as a ritual, and turn 40,000 square feet of dungeon into a 30-foot high area of ongoing damage for 24 hours with no save. That’s a 200x200x30 area, and 30 feet is tall enough for many two-story buildings, so you could enclose up to 80,000 square feet of floor space in sufficiently rectangular buildings. The damage is easily enough to eliminate anything that can’t get out of the AOE in a hurry, which is astoundingly hard since the damage seems to come from absolutely nowhere. If you’re a lich just hanging around in your lair minding your own business, your only recourse is to run in a random direction and hope for the best or teleport away to safety.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(184); });

harm|phb.name: Harm
harm|phb.summary: 14d6 averages to 49 damage, which is pretty good. But it’s a single-target spell with a Constitution saving throw, and Constitution saves tend to be high. By comparison, a 7th-level Spirit Guardians will deal 7d8 damage (average 31.5) to every enemy within 15 ft. of you on a save that’s usually lower than Constitution saves. If you deal damage even twice, that’s a better option than Harm, and Spirit Guardians lasts for 10 minutes. Harm’s biggest appeal is potentially reducing the target’s hit point maximum, which is good against enemies with regeneration or which can heal themselves magically.

heal|phb.name: Heal
heal|phb.summary: Among the best in-combat healing in the game, Heal restores a reliable, consistent 70 points of hp. That won’t bring a player from 0 to full hit points (except maybe wizards), but it’s enough to keep them in the fight for a while in most cases. It also removes some annoying status conditions, but not enough that it can replace Restoration.

heroes-feast|phb.name: Heroes’ Feast
heroes-feast|phb.summary: An absolutely amazing spell, the 1,000gp cost means that you need to save it for special occasions.

planar-ally|phb.name: Planar Ally
planar-ally|phb.summary: Casting this spell is expensive, difficult, and confusing, and the creature that you summon counts as a member of the party and gets a share of the experience points that your party earns. Use this as an absolute last resort, or if you know a specific extraplanar creature which might be willing to help you for free.

sunbeam|phb.name: Sunbeam
sunbeam|phb.summary: Spirit Guardians will typically be a better offensive use of a spell slot.

true-seeing|phb.name: True Seeing
true-seeing|phb.summary: You don’t always want this running, but you always want this available. For 1 hour you can see through illusions and invisibility, effectively negating them, and you can see into the Ethereal plane so that you can see creatures using options like Blink or walking around on the ethereal plane on their own like Phased Spiders. However, you can only see 120 feet away, so you’re not totally protected. Invisible creatures can maintain a safe distance while observing and even attacking you if there is sufficient space to do so.

word-of-recall|phb.name: Word of Recall
word-of-recall|phb.summary: A great way to escape to somewhere safe if adventuring is going badly for you and your party. The cap on 5 other creatures may be hard if you have a large party or if members of your party have pets.

conjure-celestial|phb.name: Conjure Celestial
conjure-celestial|phb.summary: All the damage of Spirit Guardians, but you steer the effect at range instead of standing in the middle of it, and it heals you and your allies. You can use all of the same tactics as everything else in the spirit guardians meta to repeatedly trigger the damage to your enemies and the healing to your allies. You can move this into an ally on your turn, then your ally can walk out and back in on their own turn to heal twice in a round. Like Spirit Guardians, the 10-minute duration is enough to carry this between multiple encounters, and the ability to heal your party with it means that you don’t even need to worry about stopping to rest and heal. Even without repeatedly triggering the effect, 4d12 is enough to get nearly any character from 0 to full hit points within a minute.

divine-word|phb.name: Divine Word
divine-word|phb.summary: Primarily this is written as a way to handle crowds of weak enemies, and while the spell does that well it’s actually more effective as a way to banish high-CR extraplanar enemies. Affected creatures are banished similar to Banishment, but there’s no numerical limit on the number of affected creatures and they can’t return for 24 hours without serious magic like Wish, so enemies can’t Plane Shift right back into the fight to express how little they enjoyed that time that you banished them.

etherealness|phb.name: Etherealness
etherealness|phb.summary: A profoundly effective scouting/escape option. Unless you’re fighting ethereal enemies, you’re untouchable. You can see and hear into the material plane (albeit at limited distance), allowing you to spy on other creatures in person without their knowledge. The spell lasts 8 hours, which is sufficient to do a lot of things potentially including a Long Rest.

fire-storm|phb.name: Fire Storm
fire-storm|phb.summary: Imagine a fireball that you got to cut up and shape in 10-foot cubes. That’s essentially what Fire Storm is. It’s a decent blast spell, but it doesn’t do nearly enough damage for a spell of this level.

plane-shift|phb.name: Plane Shift
plane-shift|phb.summary: Simultaneously a fantastic long-distance travel spell and a single-target save-or-suck. If you want to travel within the same plane you may need to cast this twice, so make sure that your lay-over is somewhere pleasant like Celestia or Elysium. If you use this to get rid of someone, send them somewhere really unpleasant like sending a demon to Celestia or a humanoid to the plane of fire. Unfortunately, you do need a specific tuning fork for each plane that you want to visit, so start a collection as soon as possible.

power-word-fortify|phb.name: Power Word Fortify
power-word-fortify|phb.summary: A huge amount of Temporary Hit Points. There’s no specified duration, so these THP last until your next Long Rest, making it easy to cast this before walking into a dangerous situation.

regenerate|phb.name: Regenerate
regenerate|phb.summary: Limb removal is exceptionally rare in DnD 5e, typically the subject of specific traps or house rules written by players who enjoy the thought of their characters losing limbs every time a sword comes out. Still, any amount of regeneration means that a character never stays Dying, and with a 1-hour duration this heals an impressive 600 hit points on top of the initial hit point restoration.

resurrection|phb.name: Resurrection
resurrection|phb.summary: Situational by design, and intentionally very expensive. You don’t want to need this spell, but sometimes things don’t work out as planned.

symbol|phb.name: Symbol
symbol|phb.summary: While many of the effects are wonderful, the inability to move the symbol and the high casting cost are prohibitive.

temple-of-the-gods|phb.name: Temple of the Gods
temple-of-the-gods|phb.summary: Very situational. The 1-hour casting time makes this rarely useful except for specific story points (celebrate a holy day, conduct a ceremony like a wedding, provide sanctuary against an attack that you know is coming), so you should be able to prepare and cast this well ahead of time. You can’t make this permanent, but you could technically recast the spell every day to keep it in existence if you were planning to retire in a permanent base and didn’t need a level 7 spell slot every day.

antimagic-field|phb.name: Antimagic Field
antimagic-field|phb.summary: Situational by design, but incredibly powerful. Even with such a small radius, removing magic from the game totally shifts the balance of the game. The biggest problem is that you are primarily a spellcaster, so you are turning off your biggest set of tools to use this. The best-case scenario is to use this when you are outmatched magically, but your allies can still fight without magic and defeat whatever you’re facing.

control-weather|phb.name: Control Weather
control-weather|phb.summary: Very situational, and kind of a pain for the DM. Go to your setting’s arctic equivalent, and raise the temperature to “Unbearable Heat” for 8 hours. That certainly won’t cause horrifying and potentially irreparable ecological damage that the DM will need to either totally disregard or track in some unpleasant fashion for the duration of the campaign.

earthquake|phb.name: Earthquake
earthquake|phb.summary: A powerful area control spell, but you don’t want to be within the 100 ft. radius, and because you don’t get the control the appearance of fissures you also can’t risk placing it with enemies near the edges. You also don’t want to risk using it inside or in an area where a nearby structure will fall on you. So you need to center the effect on your targets as much as possible, you need to be at a safe distance from the center point, and you may need some extra space to avoid falling structures. If you can manage those parameters and still manage to put the spell where you want (consider flying), this can level a city with an Action. Concentrating on the spell doesn’t do anything except maintain the difficult terrain, which means that you get almost all of the spell’s effects in one turn, so feel free to drop Concentration and switch to something else.

holy-aura|phb.name: Holy Aura
holy-aura|phb.summary: A great defensive buff. For one minute your party is incredibly difficult to harm. Fiends and Undead can be blinded, so Holy Aura is most useful against those enemies, but that’s such a minor part of the effect that it doesn’t matter much. Advantage on all saves and Disadvantage on all incoming attacks is a massive defense in any situation.

holy-star-of-mystra|frhof.name: Holy Star of Mystra
holy-star-of-mystra|frhof.summary: Powerful, but the use case is very complicated, and even in situations where this could be useful, it might have reduced impact depending on how your DM runs enemies. Holy Star of Mystra is at its absolute best when you’re dueling with an enemy spellcaster. The ability to reflect single-target saving throw spells of level 7 and below means that enemies will be forced to use area damage spells or non-spell offensive options. Of course, in the 2024 DnD rules, most spellcaster enemies have powerful non-spell offensive options and then a handful of specific spells, so even those enemies may not be impacted by this capability. You’re most likely to benefit from the cover benefit and the Bonus Action attack. +5 to AC and Dexterity saves is significant, and covers attacks and most area damage spells which won’t be covered by the Reaction option. Even if you’re not facing enemies that will interact with the Reaction option, it’s a good defense.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(185); }); But all of this costs a level 8 spell slot (you’ll never get more than one), and it lasts one minute and requires Concentration. The benefits are only worth the spell slot if you’re going to benefit from all of them.

sunburst|phb.name: Sunburst
sunburst|phb.summary: Imagine fireball with three times the radius and it blinds the targets. The targets get a Constitution save every turn to remove the blindness so you can’t expect it to stay in effect for long, but the save is at the end of their turns so they’ll spend at least one turn blinded if they fail the initial save, and that may be enough to determine the outcome of the encounter.

astral-projection|phb.name: Astral Projection
astral-projection|phb.summary: A relatively safe way to explore the Astral Plane, but it has some complications. Avoid Githyanki at all cost; their silver swords can cut your astral cord and kill you outright. If things ever look bad for you, spend the Action to return everyone to their bodies. If any of your allies drop to 0 they’ll go back to their body unharmed, but if you don’t see it happen you may not know about it so you need to have a way for your party to contact your astral projection from wherever you hid your bodies. If you ever get forcibly returned to your body and don’t have a chance to end the spell intentionally and bring your allies back too, they can always get home by punching themselves down to 0 hit points. While you have this spell running, make sure that your party’s bodies are hidden and protected somewhere that your enemies (or curious but hungry monsters) can’t get to you, but that won’t be immediately dangerous if you return to your body with no spell slots. A comfortable, but totally sealed underground hideout is a great option that you could feasibly create using Stone Shape and some patience. Your bodies don’t need food or air while you’re under the spell’s effects, but the spell doesn’t mention water. I assume that this is an oversight, but check with your DM; you may need to solve the issue of keeping your bodies hydrated. Since you don’t need to breathe, maybe submerge everyone in a shallow pool of water fed by a Decanter of Endless Water? Or maybe get a dedicated sect of monks to tend your bodies. Since your bodies don’t age, this makes you effectively immortal while you’re exploring the Astral Plane, so this can be a good way to keep your character alive between world-threatening problems so that you can return to the world to smite the latest lich without worrying about gray hair or whatever.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(186); });

gate|phb.name: Gate
gate|phb.summary: There are several ways to use this spell, two of which were intended when the spell was designed. Travel to another plane: The simplest option, you open a door and you walk through to another plane, leaving the gate open for up to a minute for whoever else to walk through in either direction. Summon a creature: If you know the name of a creature on another plane, you can drag them (potentially against their will and without a save) to your location. This is easy to abuse by going to a plane where you know they aren’t (pocket dimensions work great for this, but there are so many planes that it’s hard to accidentally be on the same one), then forcibly summon them. You could summon your biggest antagonist after spending a bunch of time setting up traps, buffs, and readied actions, then have your party stomp them into the dirt. Or you could Gate an enemy into somewhere immediately lethal to them, such as a pit of lava or the negative energy plane. I think the intent of this function was to summon an ally to help you in a fight, but I think my idea is more useful. One-way cover: You can only enter the portal from the front, but it’s unclear what the back looks like or how it functions. It’s not described as solid, so it’s entirely possible that you can fire projectiles through it from the rear, while projectiles from the front pass into the portal. I can’t imagine that you can see through the portal, so this may be hard to do, but it may be possible. Check with your DM. Magical drain: About to drown? about to be hit by a flow of magma or falling rocks? Open a gate to literally anywhere else and let the offending substance enjoy eternity floating in limbo or anywhere else that isn’t a problem for you. The multiverse is your dumping ground.

mass-heal|phb.name: Mass Heal
mass-heal|phb.summary: 700 hit points is enough to fully heal most parties of 20th-level characters. Dropping this mid-combat is a great way to turn a fight around.

power-word-heal|phb.name: Power Word Heal
power-word-heal|phb.summary: Full healing and removing a bunch of status conditions in one spell is really nice. Mass Heal will provide more hp and can be split among the party, but Power Word Heal does handles more status conditions.

true-resurrection|phb.name: True Resurrection
true-resurrection|phb.summary: Try to use cheaper methods if possible. The 25,000gp material component is expensive, even at this level.

magician|unknown.name: Magician
magician|unknown.summary: An additional cantrip and a huge bonus to two very important skills.

warden|primal-strike.name: Warden
warden|primal-strike.summary: Medium armor is a nice upgrade to your AC, but what are you going to do with martial weapons? Druids don’t get Weapon Mastery or Extra Attack. Elemental Fury (Primal Strike) provides a modest damage boost, but, just like the Cleric’s Divine Strike, it doesn’t provide enough of a damage boost to compete with unmodified cantrips. Even worse, the Druid’s best weapon options are clubs and quarterstaves thanks to Shillelagh. Literally the only reason to take Warden is medium armor. If you’re worried about AC that much, start with a level of Cleric or Fighter to get heavy armor proficiency.

potent-spellcasting|unknown.name: Potent Spellcasting
potent-spellcasting|unknown.summary: Thorn Whip folks from an absurd distance away.

primal-strike|unknown.name: Primal Strike
primal-strike|unknown.summary: Another damage increase. It still won’t compete with cantrips for most druids.

evergreen-wild-shape|unknown.name: Evergreen Wild Shape
evergreen-wild-shape|unknown.summary: This means that Circle of the Moon and other subclass that depend on Wild Shape uses can’t walk into combat without their signature feature. For other subclasses it’s a nice convenience, but you’re probably fine without it.

nature-magician|unknown.name: Nature Magician
nature-magician|unknown.summary: By this level you get 4 uses of Wild Shape per rest. If you convert all of them, you can restore a level 8 spell slot once per day. Evergreen Wild Shape will guarantee you 1 use whenever you roll initiative, so you can cast a long-running level 8 spell outside of combat, recover the spell slot, then still use Wild Shape in combat. That’s a very powerful option even for subclasses that depend on Wild Shape uses in combat, though you may still want the ability to Wild Shape multiple times in the same encounter, so you’ll need to weigh your options before you use this.

longevity|unknown.name: Longevity
longevity|unknown.summary: Almost never impacts the game, but very cool thematically.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Great for starting big area control spells or for dropping big area damage spells before allies get in the way or enemies get into melee range. The second benefit allows you to trade initiative with a willing ally. To maximize this benefit, you want to have numerous allies in combat who roll initiative on their own. A familiar is an easy addition with Wild Companion. Between Advantage and a familiar, you effectively get to roll initiative 3 times and choose your favorite.

child-of-the-sun|lfl.name: Child of the Sun
child-of-the-sun|lfl.summary: Faerie Fire is already on the Druid’s spell list, so there’s basically no benefit here.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: An easy fear effect with a Wisdom-based DC. An easy fit for the Druid.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

healer|phb.name: Healer
healer|phb.summary: Rerolling dice on healing spells is nice, but not especially impactful. The vast majority of hit point restoration is either Healing word to rescue dying allies or hit dice during a Short Rest. Sources of healing intended to bring creatures up to a significant portion of their hit points usually use a static number rather than dice (ex: Heal).

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Most Druids don’t do enough with attack rolls to justify this, but Circle of the Moon might find some use here while using Wild Shape.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: Wizard spells to get more cantrips and access to Shield can have a huge impact.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: The ability to give your whole party Heroic Inspiration once per Long Rest is amazing. The extra skill is nice, too, but Insight is the only good choice for the Druid.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Only works with weapons, and beasts’ attacks in Wild Shape are not weapons.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Hex might be useful as a damage boost for Moon Druids, but it will become obsolete quickly.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Decent, but you can probably get all of the skills you want between your Background and your class skills unless you’re trying to fill in for a Rogue.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: Sacred Flame as a Bonus Action a few times per day many not impactful enough to justify the cost unless you’re rarely using your Bonus Action.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: The named attacks in stat blocks that you’ll use in Wild Shape are not Unarmed Strikes, so this does nothing to help Wild Shape.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Helpful for keeping your party’s healer alive. Even better for Circle of the Moon because you still use your own pool of hit points while in Wild Shape.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: Druids don’t do much with Opportunity Attacks, but the ability to give your whole party Advantage on Initiative is great on anyone. Moon Druids will get more value here since you retain your feats while using Wild Shape.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: Very similar to Magic Initiate if you could select Sorcerer, but you trade one Cantrip for a buff to Con saves and the THP/damage thing. To maximize the value of Aberrant Surge, you want to select a level 1 spell which you’ll cast frequently in combat, so pick a staple option like Absorb Elements or Shield which will remain equally effective for your whole career.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: The skills and spells are decent, but not amazing. You get both See Invisibility and Arcane Eye, which are both great and not on your spell list, but that’s not enough to make this an easy choice.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: The skills are a perfect fit, but most of these spells come from the Druid’s spell list. Hunter’s Mark may be useful for Circle of the Moon, especially sincey you can move it to a new target while in Wild Shape.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: Command and Find Familiar are both great, but Wild Companion makes Find Familiar pointless. If you want Command, take Magic Initiate or muliclass. Animal Friendship of low-Intelligence Monstrosities is neat, but not useful enough to make a difference.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: You already get all of these spells.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: Sleep is the best spell here that’s not already on the Druid’s spell list, and you can get that from Magic Initiate.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: None of these spells are especially useful for the Druid.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Access to some excellent spells including Misty Step, Find Steed, Pass Without Trace, and Phantom Steed.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: The most interesting things here will only be useful for characters good at Charisma-based skills, and that’s not you.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Good skills and excellent defensive options like Shield and Counterspell. Vigilant Guardian can also help you rescue an injured ally, but watch out for your d8 hit dice.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Illusions and stealth options mostly taken from the Sorcere and the Wizard’s spell lists. You alredy get Pass Without Trace, but Druids generally don’t get illusions or Invisibility.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Mostly mediocre, and Druids already get most of these spells. Conjure Minor Elementals is very powerful for Moon Druids or if you can get Spellfire Flare or Scorching Rays.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Mage Armor is a nice AC boost if you’re not in medium armor, but you’re probably here for Armor of Agathys. A Moon Druid can cast Armor of Agathys, then replace the THP with Wild Shape, which will probably give you a much bigger pool of Temporary Hit Points, so you can enjoy the retaliatory damage much longer.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: This would be interesting, but not especially effective, on a Moon Druid.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: Looks tempting for Circle of the Moon, but remember that Temporary Hit Points don’t stack, and you’ll get more from Wild Shape.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Cast Fog Cloud, then Wild Shape into something with Blindsight or Tremorsense. Druids can already cast Fog Cloud, of course, and the 5-foot speed debuff may not be enough to justify the feat.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Druids don’t rely on weapons enough for this to make sense.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: This will work in Wild Shape, but very few beasts deal bludgeoning damage.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: I can’t think of a good reason why a Druid would wield a qualifying weapon.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: The damage mitigation is only useful if your AC is bad and you’re taking a lot of hits. You generally shouldn’t do that. Moon Druids might get some use out of this while in Wild Shape since your AC won’t be amazing even with 20 Wisdom..

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Druids don’t get the sort of damage boost which makes two-weapon fighting worthwhile.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Druids rely heavily on elemental damage, but you don’t have any spells so important and amazing that you can’t just change damage types. Circle of Wildfire may be an exception.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: Interesting, but not an easy fit. You can’t get a Wisdom increase, which is already hard, and you need to hit with an attack to trigger the debuff. The best Druids to use this will have much better results with Cold Caster.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells and access to some 1st-level spells from outside of your spell list. Misty Step is great on any spellcaster.

grappler|phb.name: Grappler
grappler|phb.summary: Beast forms’ attacks are not unarmed strikes, so there’s no synergy with this feat.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Druids don’t use the types of weapons which qualify for this.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: You might consider Primal Order (Warrior) and then this feat, but that’s a lot of investment just to get better AC. Take a single level of Druid or start your build with a level of Fighter.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: The only Druid that can justify this is Circle of Spores, and even then it’s a hard choice because Strength is utterly useless for the Druid.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A massive amount of temporary hit points.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Only situationally useful. I would only consider this in a campaign that takes place in the Underdark or in a game with vampires as common enemies.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: The Bonus Action buff is neat, but not enough without a Wisdom increase.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Druids are already proficient in two mental saves, and they’re really good at Wisdom saves, which is the important one, so the benefits here are minimal.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: This is only helpful if your DM likes to use stealthy enemies and/or likes to include traps in combat encounters.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: Strength saves are not common enough to justify this.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Many beasts deal piercing damage, making this a useful choice for Circle of the Moon.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: A few druid spells and a few beast forms deal poison damage, but not enough to justify this.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: Works with Shillelagh, but short of Circle of Spores, there’s no reason to take this.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: This is what your spellcasting is for.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Constitution saves are crucial for Concentration. War Caster may be better if you’re building for the front lines so that you can use Reactive Spell, but if you only care about Concentration, Resilient is better.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: There are some great level 1 Ritual spells like Comprehend Languages and Find Familiar, but the fact that this only lets you get level 1 spells significantly limits its usefulness. Getting rituals from outside of your own spell list is nice, but unless there are specific Rituals that you want, this isn’t worth a feat.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Potentially useful for melee builds like Circle of the Moon.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells are always nice, and Invisibility is a staple spell, but Shadow Magic’s options for 1st-level spells simply aren’t as good as those available via Fey Touched.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Druids don’t use ranged weapons in any meaningful way. That’s what spells are for.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: You won’t have the Strength to back up Shield Bash.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: There are some great Wisdom-based skills that might be worth Expertise.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Many beasts deal slashing damage, making this a useful choice for Circle of the Moon.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: Potentially useful for reaching allies in need, but you can Wild Shape as a Bonus Action into an owl or something else

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Druids have a few interesting ranged spell attacks, but not enough to justify this. If cover is an issue, use a different spell.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: Ignoring resistance to Radiant damage could be very useful, especially for Circle of the Moon, which relies on changing damage types to Radiant to get around other resistances.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: Druids aren’t built for grappling, and your equipment transforms when you use Wild Shape, so you can’t turn into a snake and then bind enemies in chains.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: An easy choice on any spellcaster. Telekinetic Shove will compete for your Bonus Action with options like Healing Word, but you won’t be able to use it effectively every turn, so it’s not really an issue. Remember that creatures can willingly fail saving throws, allowing you to use this on allies in order to move them out of dangerous positions, break grapples, or otherwise help them.

telepathic|phb.name: Telepathic
telepathic|phb.summary: Very cool, but usually talking works fine.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Charm Person isn’t good enough to justify a feat, and most Druids only attack while in Wild Shape, which prevnets them from casting Charm Person until extremely high level.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Access to some great spells from other spell lists. Most Druids have almost no Illusion options, and there are many great Enchantment spells on other spells lists which will remain useful for your whole career.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Great for Druids built for the front lines, such as Circle of the Moon. If you only care about Concentration, Resilient (Constitution) provides a bigger bonus, but War Caster can improve your mental ability scores, so it’s often easier to fit into a build. The text of the Opportunity Attack rules allow you to make an Opportunity Attack whenever a creature leaves your reach. War Caster’s Reactive Spell feature allows you to replace that attack with a single-target spell. This is intended to be used on enemies, but RAW this also allows you to cast buffs or healing spells on your allies when they leave your reach.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: Potentially useful for Circle of the Moon since you have good enough attacks to make Opportunity Attacks scary. Expertise is also really nice.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to Radiant damage is nice, but the only subclass that would want to change weapon attack damage types (Circle of the Moon) can already do that.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(193); });

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: A nice combat buff for Wild Shape.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: The extra Temporary Hit Points benefit Wild Shape’s pool of THP, which is very useful for Circle of the Moon, but take Boon of Fluid Forms first.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: This looks useful for Circle of the Moon, but beasts don’t use weapons or unarmed strikes, so this won’t help you. Circle of Spores might benefit, but by this level your weapon attacks have fallen far behind your spell damage.

boon-of-communication|frhof.name: Boon of Communication
boon-of-communication|frhof.summary: Druids are not built to be a Face.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: You’re probably your party’s primarily healer, and not dying makes it a lot easier to be a healer.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: Basically free Misty Step every time that you cast a spell as an Action. Unfortunately, Bonus Action and Reaction spells don’t qualify. According to the Rules Glossary: “When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.” Outside of combat, you can still use this to get around obstacles. Cast a harmless spell like Prestidigitation and you can teleport without making a mess.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Druids don’t have as many instantaneous Radiant damage options as Clerics, but they do get Sunburst, and maximizing the damage on Sunburst once per day is basically what this Boon is for.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: 2d4 averages to 5. Adding +5/-5 to a saving throw can rescue you or an ally, or it can cause an enemy to fail a save. On a d20 scale, 5 means that there’s a 25% chance on any given roll that this will have an impact. Granted, it is still a dice roll, so the smaller the gap, the safer this is to use. On a full caster where save-or-suck spells are such a huge part of your arsenal, this is devastatingly effective. The fact that you can use it once per encounter is amazing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Transform into a CR 10 creature and retain your spellcasting. Also, +20 Temporary Hit Points whenever you shapechange, including with Wild Shape. Just remember that, unlike Wild Shape, you don’t retain your feats when you use the transformation feature here.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: You will benefit more from Resilient (Constitution). Circle of the Moon will get more out of this than most Druids, but it’s still not an amazing choice.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: Circle of the Moon is the only subclass where this is remotely appealing, and Circle of the Moon can make their beast form attacks deal Radiant damage.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Fantastic for Circle of the Moon and for any build that doesn’t lean heavily on its Bonus Action.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great. Druids have a lot of options for dealing Poison damage, but most of them are low level or outright bad and are likely obsolete by this point in your career. Moon Druids may be getting poison damage from their beast forms, in which case you may benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance is a great save-or-suck spell, and it’s not on the Druid’s spell list.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: This gives you a 25% chance to retain your spell slot when casting spells of up to level 4. You get 4 level 1 spell slots and 3 of each of levels 2, 3, and 4. On average, you get 1 extra level 1 spell slot, and slightly less than 1 for levels 2, 3, and 4. This is fine, but definitely don’t make it your first boon.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: Charisma is a dump stat for Druids, which makes this hard to choose.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: The damage resistance/immunity is nice, but there just aren’t many Lightning and Thunder damage spells which justify this. Conjure Minor Elementals will work, but that’s not useful for most Druids.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Be invisible at all times outside of combat. Take advantage of invisibility at the start of combat, then look for ways to become invisible as frequently as possible. Even if you’re not making attack rolls (and you almost certainly aren’t doing so often), the defensive benefits of invisibility are massive. However, remember that a lot of things are an Action, so it’s very easy to break this invisibility. Notable examples that people easily overlook include Hide, Search, and Study.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: You’re only here for the damage resistance. The healing is negligible on a class that can cast Heal.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: You have magic options to handle invisible enemies.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Better skills than Sage, but Sage’s ability scores are better.

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: A potential fit if you need more skills. The additionals proficiencies from Skilled, plus good ability scores make a great basis for a high-Dexterity build. Unfortunately, the built-in skills aren’t a great fit. Chondathan Freebooter is a better option if you want Skilled.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Bad ability scores, and Charisma-based skills are hard for most Druids.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Maybe a good choice if you need more skills, but lacking a Wisdom increase is hard to justify. Chondathan Freebooter is a better option if you want Skilled.

chondathan-freebooter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freebooter
chondathan-freebooter|frhof.summary: An easy choice if you’re trying to replace a Rogue in the party. Grab increases in Dexterity and Wisdom, then use Skilled to cover whatever proficiencies you need to cover for a Rogue. You already get Sleight of Hand, which is fantastic.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: Maybe a good choice if you’re trying to replace a Rogue, but lacking a Wisdom increase is hard to justify.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, but you don’t need Healer, and the skills are bad.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Cult of the Dragon Initiatiate is a great feat for the Druid, but the ability scores and skills are a hard fit, and you can’t get a Wisdom increase.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: Musician is great, but it’s not enough.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: Excellent ability scores for the Druid, and more hit points never hurt, but the skills aren’t great.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: No Wisdom increase, but otherwise a passable option for a melee build like Circle of the Moon.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Comparable to Sage. Good ability scores, workable skills, and Magic Initiate (Wizard).

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: The Wisdom increase, Perception, and Alert are enough to make this work.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: An easy default for the Druid. Perfect ability scores, more spellcasting, and decent skills.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Decent ability scores, but the skills are middling, and there’s little reason for Healer when you can cast Healing Word.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. If you want Lucky, look elsewhere.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. If you want Alert, look elsewhere.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. If you want Alert, look elsewhere.

knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.name: Knight of the Gauntlet
knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.summary: Bad feat, bad skills, mediocre ability scores.

lorwyn-expert|lfl.name: Lorwyn Expert
lorwyn-expert|lfl.summary: Good ability scores and the skills are passable, but you can already cast Faerie Fire.

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, one decent skill, and Magic Initiate (Druid)

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: No Wisdom increase, but otherwise good.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: No Wisdom increase and both skills are based on dump stats for the Druid.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Decent ability scores, one good skill, and Purple Dragon Rook is a great feat.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Better ability scores than Acolyte, though the Intelligence-based skills are harder for the Druid.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores for a melee build, plus one good skill, but you’re absolutely not going to use Tavern Brawler.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: Decent ability scores, and with Skilled you may fill in for a Rogue in your party. That feels like an odd choice for a scribe, but here we are.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: No Wisdom increase, and most Druids will rarely benefit from Savage Attacker since Druids do so essentially nothing with weapons. Circle of the Moon might be an exception, but lacking a Wisdom increase is still really hard.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: The appeal here is getting Hex. Hex might be useful for Circle of the Moon as a low-level damage boost while in Wild Shape, but it will become obsolete beyond low levels.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: No Wisdom increase, and most Druids will rarely benefit from Savage Attacker since Druids do so essentially nothing with weapons. Circle of the Moon might be an exception, but lacking a Wisdom increase is still really hard.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: You already have tons of options for radiant damage, and this doesn’t offer a Wisdom increase.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Decent, but Vampire Hunter isn’t a good feat.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and between the skills and Thieves’ Tools you could fill in for a Rogue in your party. Lucky is an easy feat on any character.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores aren’t a good fit. You’ll get more value out of a background which gives you Magic Initiate.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(188); });

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills, and the feat doesn’t get you anything that you need.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: Great ability scores, great skills, and a good feat. For Druids planning to be in melee, this is excellent.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: Decent ability scores and skills, but the feat isn’t great.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are good, but the skills are middling and the feat is functionally useless.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: The feat is good, but not enough on its own.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: An easy fit, especially if you want to invest in Stealth.

house-sivis-heir|efota.name: House Sivis Heir
house-sivis-heir|efota.summary: Very little value here, but at least you get a Wisdom increase.

house-tharashk-heir|efota.name: House Tharashk Heir
house-tharashk-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores and skills, but the feat is bad.

house-vadalis-heir|efota.name: House Vadalis Heir
house-vadalis-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores, but that’s the only good part.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. We don’t yet have a melee-friendly Druid that’s not relying on Wild Shape, and since species traits aren’t retained in Wild Shape, there’s very little appeal here. The transformation may still be useful for flight and for the modest damage boost, but at once per day I don’t think it’s enough to justify.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(189); });

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: Druids generally can’t afford to be good at Charisma, but Shapechanger’s persistant Advantage on Charisma checks paired with two additional Face skills could offset relatively poor Charisma.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and once per day flight are great, but you will likely never use the breath weapon beyond very low levels.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense is neat, but you have spells to handle invisible or hidden enemies. Without medium armor like the Cleric, you may find the extra durability helpful.

elf|phb.name: Elf
