starry-form|enemy-has-big-aoe-damage-or-.summary: Instead of locking you into a singular combat mode, Starry Form has an attack mode, a healing mode, and a utility/casting mode. Expect to use Starry Form in any noteworthy combat, but remember that you only get a few uses per short rest, so may need to survive without it sometimes until your Wild Shape uses per rest scale. Choosing which constellation to use is one of the most important tactical decisions that you can make in an encounter. If you’re in close quarters and need to keep your spells going, go for Dragon. If your party is short on hit points going into the encounter, or if there’s some kind of hit point attrition issue (enemy has big AOE damage, or you’re fighting in a burning building), go for Chalice. Otherwise, go for Archer and pump out damage as fast as you can. This tactical decision goes away at level 10 when you get Twinkling Constellations (In a way. Keep reading.), but, until then, this will be among the hardest and most impactful choices that you make in a fight. : 1d8+Wis radiant damage as a Bonus Action. It’s a spell attack, so the attack uses your Wisdom modifier and doesn’t benefit from things like the Sharpshooter feat. This is a great offensive option, and the fact that it doesn’t stop you from casting a level 1+ spell on the same turn is just spectacular. This is likely your go-to option in combat because it’s going to be useful in every combat on every turn at any level. The damage improves at level 10, but this would still be great even if it didn’t. : Roughly doubles the total amount healed by Healing Word, and you can target a creature not targeted by your spell so that you can heal two creatures at once. However, this also encourages healing in combat, which you should try very hard to avoid doing. The healing improves at level 10. : Druids have a lot of Concentration spells, so guaranteeing a minimum roll of 10 on those checks is really helpful. Concentration saves have a DC of 10 or half of the damage taken, so you’re protected from any single source dealing up to 20 damage before considering your Constitution modifier. Guaranteeing a minimum roll of 10 on Intelligence and Wisdom checks allows you to use this outside of combat, which is a great utility option if you have knowledge skills like Arcana or Nature. At level 10, this adds a 20-foot fly speed, allowing you to fly while keeping your Concentration on a spell.

archer|unknown.name: Archer
archer|unknown.summary: 1d8+Wis radiant damage as a Bonus Action. It’s a spell attack, so the attack uses your Wisdom modifier and doesn’t benefit from things like the Sharpshooter feat. This is a great offensive option, and the fact that it doesn’t stop you from casting a level 1+ spell on the same turn is just spectacular. This is likely your go-to option in combat because it’s going to be useful in every combat on every turn at any level. The damage improves at level 10, but this would still be great even if it didn’t.

chalice|unknown.name: Chalice
chalice|unknown.summary: Roughly doubles the total amount healed by Healing Word, and you can target a creature not targeted by your spell so that you can heal two creatures at once. However, this also encourages healing in combat, which you should try very hard to avoid doing. The healing improves at level 10.

dragon|unknown.name: Dragon
dragon|unknown.summary: Druids have a lot of Concentration spells, so guaranteeing a minimum roll of 10 on those checks is really helpful. Concentration saves have a DC of 10 or half of the damage taken, so you’re protected from any single source dealing up to 20 damage before considering your Constitution modifier. Guaranteeing a minimum roll of 10 on Intelligence and Wisdom checks allows you to use this outside of combat, which is a great utility option if you have knowledge skills like Arcana or Nature. At level 10, this adds a 20-foot fly speed, allowing you to fly while keeping your Concentration on a spell.

cosmic-omen|weal.name: Cosmic Omen
cosmic-omen|weal.summary: Tactically similar to the Bard’s Bardic Inspiration and Cuttings Words features. You won’t be able to use this as often as a Bard can use Bardic Inspiration, but up to 5 times per day is still extremely impactful, especially since you can use this as a Reaction. The Weal/Woe options are roughly equivalent, so when you roll to see which one you get you’re essentially deciding if you get to use this offensively (weal) or defensively (woe) that day.

twinkling-constellations|even-at-just-20.name: Twinkling Constellations
twinkling-constellations|even-at-just-20.summary: More damage from Archer, more healing from Chalice, and flight from Dragon (even at just 20 ft. speed) are all big improvements. The ability to change your constellation each turn without spending an action means that the difficult tactical decision which you normally make when you activate Starry Form goes away, making your life much easier. Now you get to make that decision every turn instead. Do you suffer from Analysis Paralysis? This will either make it way better or way worse. Do you have an ally down at 0 hit points? Switch to chalice and heal them. Need to maintain a Concentration spell? Turn on dragon, fly out of reach and do your thing. The rest of the time? Archer.

full-of-stars|unknown.name: Full of Stars
full-of-stars|unknown.summary: A bit late, and strange on a subclass that’s so clearly intended to fill a back-line role, but consider that the Druid has notoriously poor AC and just d8 hit points this is a fantastic improvement to your durability.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Potentially useful for utility options like Guidance and emergency healing with Healing Word, but your party hopefully has those from spellcasting classes.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(188); });

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: Great for Dexterity-based builds, especially for the Eldritch Knight. A Dexterity-based Eldritch Knight could use Skilled to replace a Rogue in the party. Dexterity-based builds which don’t want the Intelligence increase should consider other backgrounds.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: Good ability scores for an Eldritch Knight, but Persuasion is a hard skill for the Fighter, and Crafter isn’t a great feat.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: An easy choice for some Dexterity-based builds, especially Dexterity-based Banerret. You get Charisma-based skills that aren’t on the Fighter’s skill list, and Tireless Reveler is a fantastic feat.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Dexterity, Constitution, and Skilled is a great combination for Dexterity-based builds, especially if you’re filling in for a Rogue in the party.

chondathan-freebooter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freebooter
chondathan-freebooter|frhof.summary: Great if you need to add more skills. A Dexterity-based build could easily use this to cover capabilities normall handled by a Rogue.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: A good choice for Dexterity-based builds, especially if there isn’t a Rogue in the party.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Excellent ability scores, but the skills are bad and Healer is a bad feat.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: The ability scores are perfect for Dexterity-based builds, but Cult f the Dragon Initiate has a Wisdom-based DC, which makes it hard to use

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: Good ability scores for a Banneret, and the Musician feat works well in any party.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: A good option for front-line martials. The ability scores are great, and Tough is an easy go-to feat if you don’t want more complexity, but you won’t get much use out of the skills.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: An easy go-to choice. Good ability scores for Strength-based builds, Tough, and workable skills.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: For the Eldritch Knight, Sage is usually a better fit. But this can get you a Dexterity increase, which you can’t get from Sage. Unfortunately, the skills are both Charisma-based, which is a hard choice.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Good ability scores for any Strength-based Fighter, and Perception is a great skill. Alert isn’t crucial for most martial characters, but remember that you can trade initiatives with a willing ally to help an allied spellcaster act early.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: A fine choice for Dexterity-based builds, but you may struggle to use the Druid spellcasting for anything except Eldritch Knight, which may struggle without an Intelligence increase. Still, using Shillelagh with Intelligence may work out long term.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: The ability scores could work for a Dexterity-based Eldritch Knight or Banerret, but the feat is horrible.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: No Strength or Dexterity increases, and Healer is a terrible feat.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: A good choice for Strength-based Bannerets.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and a decent feat, but the skills are bad.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: This could work for an Intelligence-based Eldritch Knight, but you’ll need to get Shillelagh from your species or take a second Origin Feat to get Magic Initiate (Druid).

knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.name: Knight of the Gauntlet
knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.summary: The ability scores are fine, but Tyro of the Gauntlet is only situationally useful, and the skills are horrible.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: A good choice for Strength-based Bannerets. A Champion will get the most use out of Lords’ Alliance Agent, but the ability scores aren’t great for the Champion.

lorwyn-expert|lfl.name: Lorwyn Expert
lorwyn-expert|lfl.summary: The ability scores are good for a typical Fighter, but only the Eldritch Knight will benefit significantly from the ability to cast Faerie Fire, and you can’t get an Intelligence increase.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: This could work for an Intelligence-based Eldritch Knight, but you’ll need to get Shillelagh from your species or take a second Origin Feat to get Magic Initiate (Druid).

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: You could use this for an all-Charisma Banerret, but the skills aren’t an easy fit. Guide will be a better fit for most builds that want access to Druid spells/

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: Excellent for Dexterity-based builds and for Eldritch Knights. Lucky is an easy feat for anyone, and the Intelligence-based skills are workable.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: This could work for an Eldritch Knight build.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Decent abilty scores, and Purple Dragon Rook is great. Remember that you also get a skill from Purple Dragon Rook, so you can get workable skills even though you’re saddled with Animal Handling.

rashemi-wanderer|frhof.name: Rashemi Wanderer
rashemi-wanderer|frhof.summary: An easy go-to choice. Good ability scores for Strength-based builds, Tough, and workable skills.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Intelligence and Constitution seem appealing for the Eldritch Knight, especially with Magic Initiate (Wizard) and Intelligence-based skills, but remember that you’re still a Fighter first, so you need either Strength or Dexterity unless you can get Shillelagh and use it for an Intelligence-only build. Usually you use your Origin Feat to do that, but you might get it from your species, instead.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores for a melee build plus one good skill. Tavern Brawler isn’t a great choice, but the ability to push an enemy 5 feet while also dealing damage with an Unarmed Strike may be useful if you’re not using weapons with the Push mastery.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, especially an Eldritch Knight. The skills are pretty good, and if you don’t have another Intelligence-based character in the party, you can use Skilled to get knowledge skills like Arcana.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: Savage Attacker isn’t amazing, but this is still a decent choice for Dexterity-based builds.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: A possible choice for Dexterity-based Eldritch Knights. Shadowmoor Hexer works really well on a class built to survive in melee.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: The nominal default for the Fighter. Savage Attacker is a decent feat at low levels when you’re only making a few attacks, but will feel less impactful as you make more and more attacks in a turn. The skills aren’t great, but Intimidation might give you something useful to do in social situations.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: Potentially useful for Eldritch Knights, but you’ll want to build around Intelligence, so you’ll need to get Shillelagh from somewhere.

vampire-devotee|aboh.name: Vampire Devotee
vampire-devotee|aboh.summary: Surprisingly useful for Stength-based melee builds. The ability scores are great, and Vampire’s Plaything lets you Dash or Disengage as a Bonus Action a few times per day so that you can quickly reposition. Unfortunately, skills may be hard to use unless you’re building a Banneret.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: The feat is bad and the skills aren’t good enough to make up for it. There are other Backgrounds with the same ability score options.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, and between the skills and Thieves’ Tools you could fill in for a Rogue in your party. Lucky is an easy feat on any character.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: The ability scores aren’t perfect, but Intimidation is the go-to social skill for fighters, and Perception is good on anyone. But you’re here for Zhentarim Ruffian and eventually Zhentarim Tactics. It’s an incredibly easy build for Strength-based melee attacks which all but guarantees that you can attack as a Reaction every round.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are fine, but they don’t fit the Eldritch Knight, which is the subclass most likely to use Aberrant Dragonmark. You’ll likely get more from a Background that provides Magic Initiate.

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores and skills for a Fighter that needs Intelligence (Eldritch Knight, Psionic Warrior), but the feat isn’t a good fit.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: The feat is great for the Eldritch Knight, but the ability scores and skills don’t line up well.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: There isn’t a Fighter build that can effectively benefit from the specific combination of ability scores and spellcasting.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: This could work for a Dexterity-based Eldritch Knight build, but lack of an Intelligence increase and mediocre skills make it a hard choice.

house-kundarak-heir|efota.name: House Kundarak Heir
house-kundarak-heir|efota.summary: A decent option for Eldritch Knights, but the feat isn’t amazing.

house-lyrandar-heir|efota.name: House Lyrandar Heir
house-lyrandar-heir|efota.summary: The feat is bad, and that’s the only reason you’re here.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based Eldritch Knight and a great feat, but the skills are bad.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: Even for a Dexterity-based Eldritch Knight, there is very little value here.

house-tharashk-heir|efota.name: House Tharashk Heir
house-tharashk-heir|efota.summary: It’s hard to make this work. Your best bet is an Intelligence-base Eldritch Knight, but that means neglecting the two Wisdom-based skills.

house-thuranni-heir|efota.name: House Thuranni Heir
house-thuranni-heir|efota.summary: A decent fit for Dexterity-based Eldritch Knights.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. Celestial Revelation is very useful for the Fighter, offering both a way to handle crowds and flight, neither of which are available for most Fighters.

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: A great choice for the Banneret, but other subclasses may find little value here. Additional Face skills and perpetual Advantage on Charisma checks means that you can be a reliable Face even with middling Charisma.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: A damage resistance, likely to a common damage type like poison or fire, a decent way to handle crowds of small enemies, Darkvision, and flight once per day.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense offers a way to find hidden or invisible enemies which most Fighters can’t replicate. Altogether, a great package for melee builds.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great. The innate spellcasting is only consistently useful for the Eldritch Knight, but Blade Ward can be useful for any Fighter even if you don’t use the other spells.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision is both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options. However, Gnomish Cunning may feel obsolete once you get Indomitable at level 9.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage offers numerous excellent options. I like Cloud’s Jaunt, Hill’s Topple, and Stone’s Endurance. Large Form is great for melee builds looking to occupy more space on the battlefield.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Brave and Lucky are both nice, but not enough on their own. Halfling Nimbleness is neat, but rarely impactful since you can already move through allies’ spaces and if you need to get past an enemy it should involve hurting them. Naturally Stealthy isn’t helpful for the front-line martial characters. Lucky may be helpful since fighters make so many attacks, but I don’t think that’s enough.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: A lot of overlap with the Gnome, but you trade Advantage on Intelligence saves for resistance to Psychic damage.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Fantastically versatile, the Khoravar works for nearly any build. Eldritch Knights will enjoy easy access to a huge number of Cantrips (especially Shillelagh and True Strike),

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is great for front-line melee builds, letting you move into melee quickly and padding your hit points for when you inevitably draw a lot of attacks. Relentless Endurance provides some insurance in case things go wrong, and you can heal yourself as a Bonus Action with Second Wind on your next turn to keep from immediately dying.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Shifting is a great use of your Bonus Action, providing a helpful pool of Temporary Hit Points, plus some extra effects Beasthide and Swiftstride are the easy go-to options.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting. Only useful for the Eldritch Knight, but who will find the additional spellcasting will be very welcome.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(190); });

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and bad spellcasting. Ray of Frost is the only good spell here, and Eldritch Knights can already get that from their normal spellcasting.

athletics|str.name: Athletics
athletics|str.summary: (Str): The only Strength-based skill, and it’s borderline useless. The one appealing use is binding creatures in chains, which is appealing for Strength-based builds since chains/manacles/rope are so incredibly overpowered in the 2024 rules.

history|int.name: History
history|int.summary: (Int): History can provide a lot of useful background information. This is especially viable for Eldritch Knights.

intimidation|cha.name: Intimidation
intimidation|cha.summary: (Cha): Fighters almost universally dump Charisma, but if you want some social skills this seems like your best choice.

perception|wis.name: Perception
perception|wis.summary: (Wis): One of the most important skills in the game. At least two people in the party should have it, but more is always better.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Never a bad choice, but less impactful for martial characters than for full casters.

child-of-the-sun|lfl.name: Child of the Sun
child-of-the-sun|lfl.summary: Faerie Fire is really good, but it’s only cnsistently useful for the Eldritch Knight.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: A great feat, but there aren’t any Wisdom-based Fighter subclasses, so it’s hard to make this work.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Fighters get more attacks than nearly any other class, especially the Champion Fighter, which makes this a great choice for Fighters. Knock your enemies prone or gain Advantage some other way, and you can throw a whole bunch of d20’s.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: Druid spells to get Shillelagh for Eldritch Knight Fighters or Wizard spells to expand the Eldritch’s Knight’s existing spellcasting can both have a big impact, but there’s no appeal here for other Fighters.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: A great feat to support your party, but the skills aren’t easy choices for the Fighter.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Decent if you’re using weapons with big damage dice, but as you add more attacks per turn this becomes less impactful.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Combining the Fighter’s unusually large number of attacks with Hex can deal consistently good damage output while stretching the value of a single spell slot. The retailiatory damage also works really well, and the Fighter’s proficiency in Constitution saves makes Concentration reasonably safe. Add War Caster, and you can lean into the retaliatory damage.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Good for Dexterity-based builds and for Eldritch Knights to pick up skills which capitalize on your ability scores.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: Fighters don’t use their Bonus Action every turn by default, so Spellfire Spark can be a useful use unused action economy if you have a high mental ability score to use for the save DC.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: There is very litle to use this. Grab a weapon with the Push mastery.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Always helpful for front-line melee builds, but not essential.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: Absolutely fantastic on a melee build. Pick up Sentinel and/or Zhentarim Tactics, and you have a powerful combination that will let you attack as a Reaction nearly every round.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: The Eldritch Knight may get some value out of this even though the Wizard spell list includes almost everything on the Sorcerer’s spell list. To maximize the value of Aberrant Surge, you want to select a level 1 spell which you’ll cast frequently in combat, so pick a staple option like Absorb Elements or Shield which will remain equally effective for your whole career.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: Almost all of these spells are already on the Wizard’s spell list, and you still need to prepare them.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: The low-level spells are great for the Eldritch Knight. Hunter’s Mark is an easy fit on a class which makes more attacks than most characters.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: Eldritch Knight is the only subclass that will find this remotely valuable, and you already get most of the spells. Animal Friendship of low-Intelligence Monstrosities is neat, but not useful enough to make a difference.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: This makes you feel very similar to a Paladin.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: The spells are decent, but few are great complements to the Eldritch Knight’s capabilities. Aid is nice, but it’s not enough.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: You can already cast all of the spells here worth having.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Access to some excellent spells including Misty Step, Find Steed, Pass Without Trace, and Phantom Steed. Find Steed is especially exciting if you want a mounted combat build but don’t want to play a Paladin.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: The most interesting things here will only be useful for characters good at Charisma-based skills, and that’s not you.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: This is a great choice for the Eldritch Knight. Shield prepared for free and Vigilant Guardian are both great, and you get access to some great defensive options from the Cleric and the Paladin, such as Shield of Faith.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Nearly every spell on the spell list comes from the Wizard’s spell list. This may be tempting for the Stealth bonus and for Pass Without Trace, but I don’t think that’s enough on a class that’s not built to rely on stealth.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Largely mediocre, and almost entirely from the Wizard’s spell list.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Most of the spells are already on the Wizard’s spell list, with the exception of Armor of Agathys and Sanctuary. Armor of Agathys is interesting, but you can’t afford to upcast it enough to keep it impactful. Sanctuary is also useful, provided that your Save DC is high enough for it to matter.

actor|phb.name: Actor
actor|phb.summary: Not a great fit for the Fighter, even for a subclass like the Banerret that relies on Charisma.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(195); });

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: A decent choice for many martial characters. A climb speed is the next best thing to a fly speed. The ability to stand up quickly makes falling or being knocked prone less of a problem. The ability to jump with less of a running start may let you easily jump over difficult terrain and other obstacles which otherwise might slow your movement in combat.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: The push effect is decent, especially when combined with a Push mastery, but without other stacking sources of push distance you’ll have trouble getting past the 30-foot threshold where most creatures won’t have enough speed to immediately run back into melee. The Battle Master’s Pushing Attack is one such option.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: An excellent source of additional healing and of Temporary Hit Points. Good for any melee build.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Grab Fighting Style (Blind Fighting), and suddenly you’re the only one who can see inside your Fog Cloud. Grab a whip and the Slasher fear, and you can impose a -20 ft. speed penalty in one attack. Stacked with the speed penalty from Cloying Mists, that will nearly immobilize most enemies. It’s an incredibly easy build for the Eldritch Knight, and very few enemies can do anything about it. Of course, your allies also won’t be able to see, so it may be impolite to bring this to the table regardless of how effective it is.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: paired with Fighting Style (Archery) is a simple build for consistently good damage at range. At high levels once you’ve hit 20 Dexterity, you can use a heavy crossbow with Heavy Weapon Master for a heftu damage boost.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: A simple and easy way to control enemies’ positions in combat, especially when combined with the Push mastery.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: A consistent and effective way to boost your AC in melee if you’re using Finesse weapons like rapiers or short swords. However, giving up your Reaction prevents you from making an Opportunity Attack, and punishing enemies for moving away from you is an important part of being your party’s front line.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: Potentially useful on melee builds without a shield to mitigate incoming damage, but once per rest may not be impactful enough to make this feel worthwhile. Take Heavy Armor Master first.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Without an additional damage boost on hit, the Bonus Action attack doesn’t meaningfully improve two-weapon fighting for you. Fighting Style (Two-Weapon Fighting) and a Nick weapon are all that you need.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: Not as good as you would hope. The Bonus Action to spend a Hit Point Die notably does not add your Constitution modifier, which makes it an expensive and frustrating way to burn through your Hit Point Dice very quickly with minimal impact. Unless your party has some other deep, inexpensive healing resource, you need those dice for Short Rests to refill your massive pool of hit points. Take Chef instead.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Even the Eldritch Knight should not use a single element enough to justify this.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: Flustering Strike is really good. Putting this on a Dexterity-based build or on a Banerret with decent Charisma can make it very effective. The improvement to Disengage will rarley matter, Unfortunately.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Helpful for the Eldritch Knight. More spells and some free castings can do a lot for you.

grappler|phb.name: Grappler
grappler|phb.summary: Even if you do nothing else to make yourself good at unarmed strikes, this is a great way to hold enemies in place without heavily cutting into your damage output. You’ll want to use a one-handed weapon (Versatile weapons also work well here) to leave a hand free. If you use a weapon with the Topple mastery or if you make another unarmed strike, you can knock your target prone and keep them there, then drag them away from your allies.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Essential and reliable if you’re using two-handed melee weapons. The damage bonus notably applies to any weapon with the Heavy property, making it an option for weapons like longbows and heavy crossbows. The Strength increase is hard for Dexterity-based builds, but strongly consider this once you’ve hit 20 Dexterity.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: Fighters already get proficiency in heavy armor.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: A huge amount of damage reduction.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: You might have enough Wisdom to qualify for this. It’s a fantastic addition to any party, but definitely don’t rush to take it until you’ve hit 20 in Strength or Dexterity.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Too situational, and the ability score increase only makes sense for the Eldritch Knight.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Standard Bearer is only situationally useful, but many harmful effects are riders on top of the Charmed and Frightened conditions. Granting three allies immunity to those conditions for a full minute can make encounters against many enemies significantly easier.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Great insurance against difficult mental saves. This may feel redundant once you get Indomitable, or you might find that you’re using both reliably.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: Without a magical mount of some kind, mounted combat simply isn’t viable.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: If you’re proficient in Perception and have decent Wisdom, you may be well qualified to use Perception reliably. But even then, this is only helpful if your DM likes to use stealthy enemies and/or likes to include traps in combat encounters.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: Strength saves are not common enough to make this feel impactful.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Excellent if you prefer piercing weapons. Spectacular if you’re a Champion.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: This could work for Dexterity-based builds, but it’s not especially impactful. You’ll get more value out of something like Piercer.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: One spell slot per SHort Rest that’s as good as a full spellcaster (at least until level 11), but especially useful for the Eldritch Knight to expand your terribly limited number of prepared spells.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: An easy way to support your allies. Inspiring Leader provides considrably more Temporary Hit Points, so consider that first, but Inspiring Leader can’t be used in combat.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: More saves never hurt. Resilient (Dexterity) is easy to fit into a Dexterity-based build.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: Not even on an Eldritch Knight.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Fantastic. This provides the “stickiness” that you need to be your party’s Defender, allowing you to easily fill that role regardless of any of your other build choices.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Helpful for the Eldritch Knight, but Fey Touched offers better spells.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Helpful for ranged builds, but not essential unless your DM really enjoys using cover. Thrown weapon builds might enjoy this to offset their poor range relative to weapons like bows and muskets.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: Excellent on Strength-based sword-and-board builds. Shield Bash is great action economy. Interpose Shield will help mitigate area damage, especially once you have Indomitable and can turn a failed save into a successful one and fully negate the damage.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: Strength-based Fighters have very few good skill options, but Dexterity-based Fighters and Fighters that need high Intelligence or Charisma all have better options.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Excellent if you prefer slashing weapons. Consider a weapon with the Slow mastery so that you can stack the speed penalties.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: You’re durable enough that an occasional Opportunity Attack shouldn’t scare you, but you might want the 10-foot speed boost on a melee build.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Even the Eldritch Knight doesn’t rely enough on spell attacks to make this worthwhile.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: Strength-based fighters can be good grapplers, and Advantage on grappled enemies reduces the need for you to knock them prone to get Advantage. Instead, use Action Surge to bind them in chains/manacles/rope in the same turn that you grapple them.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: Potentially useful for the Eldritch Knight and maybe even the Banerret.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Play an Eldritch Knight or take Magic Initiate.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Helpful for the Eldritch Knight. More spells and some free castings can do a lot for you.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Fantastic on the Eldritch Knight. Grab Booming Blade since True Strike relies on your spellcasting ability modifier, which will almost certainly be worse than your Strength or Dexterity.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: You get 3 at level 1, and it scales to 6 on its own. You really don’t need more.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: An easy choice for melee builds, especially if you’re not building for high AC.

blind-fighting|phb.name: Blind Fighting
blind-fighting|phb.summary: Fantastic, but only situationally useful. Unless you have party members that like to rely on magical darkness or fog or similar effects, you’ll get more consistent benefit from other options. If it’s an option, take the Skulker feat instead.

defense|phb.name: Defense
defense|phb.summary: Consistently useful, and doesn’t discourage you from switching weapons.

dueling|phb.name: Dueling
dueling|phb.summary: Easy and consistent damage that puts you roughly on par with two-handed weapons without giving up access to a shield.

great-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Great Weapon Fighting
great-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: This raises the minimum damage for the Greatsword to 6, which feels nice but doesn’t improve your average damage roll very much. It has almost no impact on other weapons, which makes the appeal very narrow.

interception|phb.name: Interception
interception|phb.summary: Conceptually similar to Protection, but there’s some nuance in how the two styles protect your target. Protection imposes Disadvantage, so if there’s a good chance that the attack would miss, it’s the better choice. Interception reduces the damage and always works, but for big attacks it won’t negate the whole attack.

protection|phb.name: Protection
protection|phb.summary: Tempting for Defender builds, but allies need to remain adjacent to you for this to work. Being adjacent to the front line tank is generally a bad place to be unless you can do so safely without someone defending you. This also appeals to mounted combat builds because you can use it to compensate for your mount’s relative fragility, but if you’re going that route you really need the Mounted Combatant feat which lets you retarget attacks at yourself instead.

thrown-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Thrown Weapon Fighting
thrown-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: More complex than Archery, but the ability to change weapons mid-turn means that you can use multiple Weapon Mastery options in a single turn. Two-weapon fighting can work, but without an on-hit damage boost, it’s actually less damaging than Archery with a longbow or musket.

two-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
two-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: Without an on-hit damage boost on all of your attacks, two-weapon fighting can’t keep up with the damage output of two-handed weapons, especially as you add more attacks and Great Weapon Master.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to Radiant damage is nice, and the ability to change your attack damage type to Radiant can get around damage resistances to weapon damage.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Advantage on one attack per turn and a tiny damage boost. Take Boon of Combat Prowess first.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: Without a built-in way to generate Temporary Hit Points, you may lose much of the Boon’s value. The extra healing when you use Hit Point Dice is nice, but not enough on its own. To maximize the value here, take feats like Bloodlust and Chef.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Helpful, but it only affects one of your 3 or more attacks.

boon-of-communication|frhof.name: Boon of Communication
boon-of-communication|frhof.summary: Fighters are rarely a Face, but this may be useful or a Banerret or a Battle Master who has picked up maneuvers to boost their skills.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Fantastic on melee builds who tend to draw a lot of attention and take a lot of damage.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: The Eldritch Knight can combine this with War Magic to do a bunch of stuff inside of one Acton.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Fighters don’t have source of Radiant damage that will benefit from being maximized, so you lose the most exciting part of the Boon.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: More useful to support your allies’ save-or-suck spells than for anything that you’re doing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Without a built-in way to shapechange, the value here is very limited.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: Great for melee builds. Remember that the additional healing applies to Second Wind and with things like the Champion’s Heroic Rally feature.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: You don’t have a built-in way to do anything except bludgeoning/piercing/slashing damage, so this allows you to bypass troublesome damage resistances. You also have 3 or more attacks, giving you more opportunities than most characters to roll a 20 on an attack roll. If you can get Advantage, such as from knocking an enemy prone or from the Vex mastery, you can roll a big pile of d20’s in hopes of getting a 20 and adding a mountain of bonus damage.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Great for melee builds, especially if you don’t rely heavily on your Bonus Action.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance will guarantee at least one round of dancing, which is useful, but without the ability to recast the spell you’re not getting as much value as a full caster.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: You could use this for a utility of some kind, but there aren’t many utility spells which you’ll want every Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list (neither care about your stats).

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: A huge boost in mobility for Dexterity-based builds.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: Potentially useful for the Eldritch Knight, but remember that it only has a 25% chance to work.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: Immunity to fear is nice, but Fighters don’t have and easy way to make enemies Frightened, so you lost most of the value here.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Resistance/immunity to two damage types, but you can only increase a mental ability score, and there’s only one subclass with spellcasting, so this is really only useful for Eldritch Knights.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Tempting on Dexterity-based builds, but you’re probably your party’s Defender, so remember that there’s value in being a big, shiny target.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: Resistance to two damage types. The healing is negligible. Take Boon of Fortitude instead.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Probably your only option for handling invisible enemies, but the ability scores are hard. If you’ve made it this far, your party is covering for you or you’ve found a creative solution.

battleaxe|function.name: Battleaxe
battleaxe|function.summary: This is just a trident that you can’t throw and with a different damage type.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(197); });

flail|unknown.name: Flail
flail|unknown.summary: The only one-handed bludgeoning weapon with Sap. Longsword is typically a better choice unless you specifically want to take Crusher and still use the Sap mastery. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the flail’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

glaive|see-tactical-master.name: Glaive
glaive|see-tactical-master.summary: Reach and Graze. A safe option if you only care about damage output and you want something mechanically simple. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, the Graze Weapon Mastery is fantastic because you can apply Push, Sap, or Slow when you hit (see Tactical Master) and you can apply Graze when you miss, so you’re always going to get something from your attack.

greataxe|unknown.name: Greataxe
greataxe|unknown.summary: Cleave and a giant damage die. A big single damage die isn’t an advantage over other weapons, and Cleave is much easier to use with Reach.

greatsword|unknown.name: Greatsword
greatsword|unknown.summary: Great if you just want simple, reliable damage output with no complications.

halberd|unknown.name: Halberd
halberd|unknown.summary: Trade some of the greataxe’s damage for Reach. Reach makes it much easier to make the bonus Cleave attack since you can reach enemies behind your initial target.

lance|unknown.name: Lance
lance|unknown.summary: Reach and Topple. You can also use this one-handed while mounted, but Fighters don’t have an easy way to make mounted combat work. Even if you never get onto a mount, Reach and Topple is as good as any other polearm with reach.

longsword|unknown.name: Longsword
longsword|unknown.summary: An easy go-to option. Sap is fantastic, especially at low levels when enemies have few attacks. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the longsword’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

maul|unknown.name: Maul
maul|unknown.summary: Fantastic for aggressive two-handed weapon builds. Use Topple to knock your target prone, then maul them with Advantage.

pike|unknown.name: Pike
pike|unknown.summary: Reach and Push. For when you really, really don’t want anyone to come near you. Be sure to grab Polearm Master so that you can attack when enemies move into your reach and push them away from you. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the pike’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

rapier|unknown.name: Rapier
rapier|unknown.summary: The go-to option for Dexterity-based melee builds, but also great if you just want the Vex mastery on a one-handed weapon. The Vex mastery gives you Advantage, allowing you to reliably hit your target repeatedly. Once you get Studied Attacks at level 13, you’ll have Advantage on nearly every attack you make.

scimitar|unknown.name: Scimitar
scimitar|unknown.summary: The go-to secondary weapon for two-weapon fighting since it’s the Nick weapon with the largest damage die. With the Light and Nick properties, you can use this for two-weapon fighting without eating your Bonus Action. If you’re building around Slasher, pair this with a handaxe as your primary weapon.

shortsword|unknown.name: Shortsword
shortsword|unknown.summary: A go-to choice for your primary weapon when using two-weapon fighting. If you’re building around Piercer, pair this with a dagger as your secondary weapon.

trident|unknown.name: Trident
trident|unknown.summary: Absolutely essential as a thrown weapon for Strength-based builds. With the Topple mastery you can throw these to knock flying enemies prone, which causes them to fall.

warhammer|unknown.name: Warhammer
warhammer|unknown.summary: The same damage as the longsword, but with the Push mastery. Combining this with Crusher gives you a lot of power to forcibly reposition your enemies. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the warhammer’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

war-pick|unknown.name: War Pick
war-pick|unknown.summary: Longsword, but piercing damage. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the war pick’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

whip|unknown.name: Whip
whip|unknown.summary: Reach, Slow mastery, and one-handed. Grab the Slasher feat and you can apply a 20-foot speed penalty, then walk safely out of your target’s reach. The Slow mastery does become redundant at level 9 when you get Tactical Mastery, but the Whip is the only one-handed reach weapon, so it retains an interesting niche.

blowgun|unknown.name: Blowgun
blowgun|unknown.summary: There isn’t really a niche for this one in 5e.

hand-crossbow|unknown.name: Hand Crossbow
hand-crossbow|unknown.summary: Supports two-weapon fighting via Crossbow Expert. You can also use it with a sheild because the Loading property no longer requires a free hand to reload in the DnD 5.5 rules.

heavy-crossbow|muskets-aren-t-heavy.name: Heavy Crossbow
heavy-crossbow|muskets-aren-t-heavy.summary: Briefly useful at low levels because of its large damage die, but obsolete once you get Extra Attack. Crossbow Expert negates the Loading property, but if you’re going to take a feat, you should probably take Gunner and grab a pistol or a musket. If you can afford to take both Crossbow Expert and Heavy Weapon Master, the heavy crossbow is the best damage that you can get from a ranged weapon (Muskets aren’t Heavy). But upgrading from the longbow’s 1d8 to the heavy crossbow’s 1d10 isn’t worth the extra feat. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the heavy crossbow’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

longbow|unknown.name: Longbow
longbow|unknown.summary: The go-to weapon for ranged builds. The Shortbow’s Vex mastery may give you better total damage, but the Slow mastery’s crowd control can be very impactful. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the longbow’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

musket|unknown.name: Musket
musket|unknown.summary: This has the Loading property, which will present a problem as soon as you get Extra Attack, but with the Gunner feat, this is a linear upgrade from the Longbow, at least in terms of damage. Range might be an issue occasionally, but if that worries you, take Sharpshooter. If you plan to take the Heavy Weapon Master feat for the damage boost, use a Longbow or a Heavy Crossbow instead. Once you reach level 9 and get Tactical Master, consider changing weapons since the musket’s Weapon Mastery becomes redundant.

pistol|unknown.name: Pistol
pistol|unknown.summary: Good damage for a one-handed weapon, and the Vex mastery. Advantage from Vex will make your DPR with a pistol better than DPR with a musket so long as you’re repeatedly attacking the same target. You can also use it with a sheild because the Loading property no longer requires a free hand to reload in the DnD 5.5 rules. If you have enough gold, you can bring a whole bunch of loaded pistols and repeatedly draw and fire them instead of reloading. Or you could take the Gunner feat.

studded-leather|unknown.name: Studded Leather
studded-leather|unknown.summary: Dexterity-based builds should grab studded leather as soon as they hit 18 Dexterity.

chain-mail|unknown.name: Chain Mail
chain-mail|unknown.summary: Starting armor if you didn’t choose gold. Works fine until you can afford Full Plate.

full-plate|unknown.name: Full Plate
full-plate|unknown.summary: The obvious end goal for heavy armor users.

shield|unknown.name: Shield
shield|unknown.summary: +2 AC is huge in this game.

barbarian|unknown.name: Barbarian
barbarian|unknown.summary: Two levels for Rage and Reckless Attack is definitely tempting, but remember that you can get Advantage on melee attacks by knocking your target Prone with a Topple weapon or an unarmed strike.

monk|unknown.name: Monk
monk|unknown.summary: Unarmed Fighters can absolutely work, and a level of Monk for Martial Arts makes that much easier. One level of Barbarian for their version of Unarmored Defense is usually a good combination due to your likely low Wisdom.

ranger|unknown.name: Ranger
ranger|unknown.summary: Hunter’s Mark, more Weapon Masteries, and a second Fighting Style can be very helpful, especially for two-weapon fighting builds that focus on making numerous attacks.

rogue|unknown.name: Rogue
rogue|unknown.summary: Cunning Action is really good, and Expertise offers a lot of options.

warlock|unknown.name: Warlock
warlock|unknown.summary: One level for Pact of the Blade will allow you to build a Charisma-first Banneret.

wizard|unknown.name: Wizard
wizard|unknown.summary: Useful for the Eldritch Knight to expand your spellcasting.

comprehension|function.name: Comprehension
comprehension|function.summary: An excellent utility. You never get Tongues, so you’re ability to address language barriers is still limited. Fortunately, you can use this to read a language, then use Polyglot to to learn it for a day.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); });

polyglot|unknown.name: Polyglot
polyglot|unknown.summary: Do you have a language barrier? If you have 8 hours to rest, no you don’t.

well-spoken|unknown.name: Well Spoken
well-spoken|unknown.summary: Proficiency in a Face skill. Intimidation is omitted intentionally because Fighters can select it as one of their class skills. You won’t be as effective as a Charisma-based class like a Bard or a Sorcerer, but profiency and a middling Charisma modifier is enough in most cases.

group-recovery|unknown.name: Group Recovery
group-recovery|unknown.summary: This turns Second Wind into Mass Healing Word once per rest. At this level this is a great way to rescue dying allies, but it will get even better when you get Team Tactics at level 7. Limiting Group Recovery to once per Short or Long Rest is the Banneret’s biggest limitation, especially once you get Team Tactics and want to use it offensively rather than reserving Group Recovery to rescue dying allies. The result is that you get to apply your subclass exactly once per rest until you reach level 10 and get Shared Resilience.

team-tactics|unknown.name: Team Tactics
team-tactics|unknown.summary: For one round your party is borderline unstoppable. Unfortunately, this makes it hard to reserve Group Recovery for when you have dying allies.

rallying-surge|probably-attacking.name: Rallying Surge
rallying-surge|probably-attacking.summary: Not only do you get an additional Action to do whatever (probably attacking), you get to share that joy with your allies! This is especially effective if you have a Rogue in the party who can get an extra Sneak Attack out of the deal. If you can, use Group Recovery and Team Tactics first so that your allies get to make the free attack with Advantage before they spend their own turn with Advantage on everything.

shared-resilience|unknown.name: Shared Resilience
shared-resilience|unknown.summary: This is the best saving throw reroll ability in the game. A minimum of +15 on top of your ally’s saving throw modifier will dramatically improve their odds of success if not make success a guarantee. Just remember that you’re sharing your own uses of Indomitable, and you might need those so that you don’t get save-or-sucked by a random Wisdom save.

bolstered-rally|unknown.name: Bolstered Rally
bolstered-rally|unknown.summary: This will make your subclass features easier to use in fights over large areas, especially if you have allies who like to fight at long range.

unshakable-bravery|unknown.name: Unshakable Bravery
unshakable-bravery|unknown.summary: Charmed and Frightened are both common conditions, and frequently come with other nasty side effects while you’re under the effect. Immunity to them might make up for donating all of your Indomitable uses to your allies.

combat-superiority|function.name: Combat Superiority
combat-superiority|function.summary: You get four superiority dice, which means you get to use 4 maneuvers between each short/long rest. You gradually get more dice, allowing for more maneuvers at higher levels, and you gradually add more known maneuvers. You can replace known maneuvers as you level, but since there aren’t any maneuvers with prerequisites or anything, you really only need to replace maneuvers that you tried and didn’t like. Many maneuvers add your superiority die to the damage roll if you hit. Since the damage die is added to the damage roll, the additional damage is multiplied on a critical hit. This makes it especially appealing to apply a maneuver when you score a critical hit so that you get both a big pile of damage and a cool rider effect.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

student-of-war|unknown.name: Student of War
student-of-war|unknown.summary: An Artisan’s tool and another skill from the Fighter’s skill list. Artisan’s tools provide a few uses as described in the Equipment chapter of the PHB, and another skill may offer some useful options outside of combat.

know-your-enemy|fire-elementals-are-immu.name: Know Your Enemy
know-your-enemy|fire-elementals-are-immu.source: fire elementals are immune to fire, etc.
know-your-enemy|fire-elementals-are-immu.summary: Vulnerabilities are vanishingly rare in 5e, but knowing an enemy’s resistances and immunities can make life much easier against some enemies. You won’t need this in every fight because most enemies have no resistances or because their resistances are obvious (fire elementals are immune to fire, etc.). This does not specify immunity to damage, so it appears to also affect immunity to conditions. However, advantage/disadvantage on saves against specific conditions aren’t considered resistances/vulnerabilities.

improved-combat-superiority-d10|d10.name: Improved Combat Superiority (d10)
improved-combat-superiority-d10|d10.summary: These bumps only amount to an increase of 1 each, but they feel very nice. Because you’re using Superiority Dice so frequently the small bonus adds up.

relentless|unknown.name: Relentless
relentless|unknown.summary: This ensures that you always have at least one superiority die, so you can use maneuvers much more freely. The free die is once per turn, so it’s especially useful for Reactions. You can also use it outside of combat with Commanding Presence, giving yourself a perpetual +1d8 to some types of Charisma checks, making you fairly effective as a Face even with awful Charisma.

improved-combat-superiority-d12|d12.name: Improved Combat Superiority (d12)
improved-combat-superiority-d12|d12.summary: These bumps only amount to an increase of 1 each, but they feel very nice and since you’re using Superiority Dice so frequently the small bonus adds up.

ambush|phb.name: Ambush
ambush|phb.summary: (U): A bonus to Stealth can have a huge impact even though you’re likely not sneaking during combat. How effective this will be depends somewhat on your DM and how they apply the Stealth rules. If your DM asks for repeated Stealth checks in quick succession, this won’t work out. But, if you can make one check and sneak through a room or disappear into a crowd or explore a small area, this could be very helpful. This can also be used when rolling initiative which is useful if you have something like the Bugbear’s Surprise Attack.

bait-and-switch|phb.name: Bait and Switch
bait-and-switch|phb.summary: (U): Situational, but very interesting if you have frail allies who tend to get stuck in melee from time to time. Switching places with them can pull them out of melee reach, and, if they can act before your enemies, your ally could withdraw to safety, removing the need for you to boost their AC and thereby allowing you to keep that benefit for yourself without feeling selfish.

commander-s-strike|phb.name: Commander’s Strike
commander-s-strike|phb.summary: (U) If you don’t have a Rogue in your party, this is generally a poor option since you should do enough damage on your own that you should reserve your limited pool of Superiority Dice for other options. If you have a Rogue in the party, this becomes a fantastic option which you should capitalize on any time your Rogue can reliably hit the target. Sneak Attack works once per turn (not once per round), so allowing the Rogue to make an extra attack on your turn means a big pile of extra Sneak Attack damage.

commanding-presence|phb.name: Commanding Presence
commanding-presence|phb.summary: Adding a superiority die is enough to offset a poor Charisma score, allowing the Battle Master Fighter to serve as a Face without further splitting their attention on ability scores. This notably omits Charisma (Deception), so there’s mechanical incentive to be honest.

disarming-attack|phb.name: Disarming Attack
disarming-attack|phb.summary: Bonus damage and you get to force the target to drop one item if they fail a Strength save. Unfortunately, relatively few enemies use weapons, and the ones that do predominantly rely on Strength and will therefore have high Strength saves. That means that this is unreliable against most melee combatants, but can see some use against foes armed with ranged weapons or enemy casters holding some kind of focus or wand.

distracting-attack|phb.name: Distracting Attack
distracting-attack|phb.summary: Very helpful with a Rogue or some other Striker in the party, especially against enemies with high AC. However, its usefulness diminishes if you don’t have an ally who can follow your attack with a single high-damage attack to capitalize on Advantage. Sneak Attack is an obvious example, but also look for high-damage attack spells like Inflict Wounds and Chromatic Orb.

evasive-footwork|phb.name: Evasive Footwork
evasive-footwork|phb.summary: (U) Disengage as a Bonus Action and get an AC bonus until your next turn. Obviously great if you need to Disengage, but you might even use this just for the AC boost if you’re expecting to draw a lot of attacks.

feinting-attack|phb.name: Feinting Attack
feinting-attack|phb.summary: Advantage on your own attack and bonus damage. You don’t want to use this on every attack, but you can use it in conjunction with a Vex weapon to chain Advantage on your attacks, or you could use it with an Unarmed Strike to more reliably knock your target prone to get Advantage on future attacks.

goading-attack|phb.name: Goading Attack
goading-attack|phb.summary: A good taunt mechanic, but not as effective as Menacing Attack unless your target is resistant or immune to fear.

lunging-attack|phb.name: Lunging Attack
lunging-attack|phb.summary: (M) Dash as a Bonus Action and potentially a damage bonus with a melee attack. A good way to close to melee, but you don’t need to Dash frequently, so this is only situationally useful.

maneuvering-attack|phb.name: Maneuvering Attack
maneuvering-attack|phb.summary: It’s rare that this will provide a significant advantage unless you’re using the flanking variant rule or something. Movement in 5e is easy, and using something like Menacing Attack to impose Disadvantage on a potential Opportunity Attack is likely sufficient in most cases, or you can use Pushing Attack to push enemies away and get allies out of grapples.

menacing-attack|phb.name: Menacing Attack
menacing-attack|phb.summary: Frightening a target makes them considerably less effective, and, with clever positioning or the Push Weapon Mastery, you can use this to keep the target away from your allies. However, beware of creatures that are immune or resistant to fear effects.

parry|phb.name: Parry
parry|phb.summary: (U) Reducing damage is often much more effective than waiting to heal it later, but it is probably more effective to spend the same Superiority Die to defeat your attacker than it is to spend it reducing a little bit of damage. The damage reduced also doesn’t scale much since your Superiority Dice scale in size so slowly, so this may be a good option at low levels when you have relatively few hit points, but consider retraining at once you’re more confident in your durability.

precision-attack|phb.name: Precision Attack
precision-attack|phb.summary: Great against enemies with high AC, or if you absolutely need to make one attack hit, but don’t rely on it too heavily or it will eat through your Superiority Dice. Sometimes you need to accept that you missed. This is used after you make the attack roll, but you don’t want to use this every time that you miss. If you’re paying enough attention to know the target’s AC based on dice rolls, you can estimate when using this makes sense. The closer you are to hitting, the more likely this is to work. At an average bonus of 4.5 (more once your dice advanced to d10/d12) I recommend only using this if you’re within 4 points of hitting. It’s easy to compare Precision Attack to Feinting Attack since both make it easier to hit. Feinting Attack provides Advantage and a damage boost, but you need to use it before the attack. Precision Attack is nice because you can use it after your attack roll if you know that your Superiority Die could turn a near-miss into a hit, so you’re not forced to gamble a Superiority Die that you might not need to spend. Feinting Attack provides a damage bonus, which means that even if you didn’t need Advantage you still get something out of spending your die. Precision Attack doesn’t require you to spend your Bonus Action. Taking all of these considerations into account, they’re roughly equivalent. Which is better depends greatly on your build and your situation. If you use Bonus Actions heavily, definitely go for Precision Attack.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

pushing-attack|phb.name: Pushing Attack
pushing-attack|phb.summary: Using an Unarmed Strike to Shove or using a Push weapon is typically sufficient for Strength-based melee builds, but for Dexterity-based builds and for ranged builds, this can be a helpful way to break grapples or knock enemies out of position. Small creatures also aren’t penalized for their size, making this an easy and reliable way to push enemies. It’s still only situationally useful, but it’s difficult to replicate by any other means short of magic.

rally|phb.name: Rally
rally|phb.summary: This won’t be a lot of hit points, until you’ve gained a few levels, but the temporary hit points don’t have a specified expiration, so they last until they run out or the target takes a Long Rest. You can start each day by rallying your allies, then immediately take a Short Rest to get your Superiority Dice back.

riposte|phb.name: Riposte
riposte|phb.summary: (M) Spend a superiority die for an attack as a Reaction. Seems like a fantastic trade to me, especially if you’re using a big two-handed weapon and do a lot of damage per attack. Also great if you have a once per turn damage boost like Sneak Attack from levels in Rogue.

sweeping-attack|phb.name: Sweeping Attack
sweeping-attack|phb.summary: This is very little damage, and you can get much better utility from your superiority dice. If you want a similar effect, grab a Cleave weapon.

tactical-assessment|phb.name: Tactical Assessment
tactical-assessment|phb.summary: Adding a superiority die is enough to offset a poor Intelligence score, but it’s very unlikely that you took proficiency in History or Investigation.

tripping-attack|phb.name: Tripping Attack
tripping-attack|phb.summary: Knocking a target prone is great, but Strength-based builds can use a Topple weapon or an Unarmed Strike. Dexterity-based builds will struggle with those options, so Tripping Attack has some appeal there.

improved-critical|before-we-talk-about-a.name: Improved Critical
improved-critical|before-we-talk-about-a.summary: Twice as many crits (before we talk about Advantage). Not much else to say. As a nice bit of quality of life, this now works with Unarmed Strikes which it didn’t in the previous rules set.

remarkable-athlete|athletics.name: Remarkable Athlete
remarkable-athlete|athletics.summary: On the one hand, advantage on Strength (Athletics) will hardly ever matter, especially with the changes to grappling in this rules set. On the other hand, Advantage on Initiative is awesome, and the rider on crits is fun.

additional-fighting-style|unknown.name: Additional Fighting Style
additional-fighting-style|unknown.summary: The worst this will ever be is +1 AC or 10 feet of Blindsight, both of which are pretty decent on any build. Some builds may actually want two fighting styles and choose something else.

heroic-warrior|unknown.name: Heroic Warrior
heroic-warrior|unknown.summary: Free Heroic Advantage once per turn is awesome. It is a little weirdly anti-synergistic with the changes to the Heroic Advantage mechanic itself, though, because you now roll after seeing your first roll and must accept the new roll, so you can’t use it to fish for crits if you’ve already hit because you risk turning your hit into a miss. If you’re doing it right, this is mostly present to help you pass saves and do well in non-combat situations.

superior-critical|unknown.name: Superior Critical
superior-critical|unknown.summary: 50% more crits if you don’t have Advantage.

survivor|unknown.name: Survivor
survivor|unknown.summary: Between this and all of the extra sources of Temporary Hit Points in the game, a well-support Champion is nigh-immortal.

spellcasting|unknown.name: Spellcasting
spellcasting|unknown.summary: The Eldritch Knight is a 1/3 spellcaster that draws their spells from the Wizard’s spell lists. You’ll know very few spells and have very few spell slots, so you need to be absolutely certain that any given spell is worth the space. Be sure to pick up an offensive cantrip like Booming Blade which you can use alongside weapon attacks with War Magic. True Strike looks appealing on its face, but Intelligence-based attacks are a harder prospect since your Intelligence will lag behind your Strength or Dexterity. The text explicitly calls of the Eldritch Knight’s spells “Wizard Spells”, which means that Wizard features and Eldritch Knight features work well together when multiclassing.

weapon-bond|s.name: Weapon Bond
weapon-bond|s.summary: Very cool, but it rarely has any mechanical impact unless you plan to throw your weapon(s) or want to appear unarmed somewhere. Casting spells like Light or Darkness on your bonded weapon before throwing it means that you can place the spell effect at greater range and recall the weapon in order to throw it again. But this combo is both more work and less effective than most methods for abusing magical darkness. You can accomplish some odd shenanigans like bonding to oversized weapons or even siege weapons in order to freely teleport a massive object to yourself, but be cautious about how much your DM will tolerate before they have your bonded trebuchet appear in your hand and summarily crush it.

war-magic|function.name: War Magic
war-magic|function.summary: A fantastic way to use weapons and spells at the same time. Most spells will rely on your Intelligence to attack, so your best options are Booming Blade and Green-Flame Blade because they rely on weapon attacks. If Booming Blade and Green-Flame Blade aren’t available, your next best bet may be True Strike to add an on-hit damage boost to a hit with your weapon. Your Intelligence is probably going to lag behind your Strength/Dexterity, so try to get Advantage before you attack to make up for the relative loss of attack bonus. Using a Vex weapon or knocking your target prone are great options. Once you pick up Eldritch Strike, you might switch to a cantrip which calls for a saving throw like Toll the Dead. Whether Toll the Dead will deal more damage than a weapon cantrip will depend on your other build choices.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); }); Remember that this works each time that you take the Attack action. If you use Action Surge, you can use War Magic again. Unfortunately, this doesn’t work with Haste because Haste places additional limits on the additional Action which it provides.

eldritch-strike|unknown.name: Eldritch Strike
eldritch-strike|unknown.summary: Since your Intelligence probably won’t be as high as that of a real Wizard, save DCs can be a real problem. Imposing disadvantage will make your spells considerably more effective. This can enable some interesting combinations like attacking a bunch of adjacent enemies, then using War Magic to hit them with Acid Splash or Sword Burst, or shooting a bunch of enemies with a bow then hitting them with a fireball on the next turn.

arcane-charge|you-still-don-t-get-a-seco.name: Arcane Charge
arcane-charge|you-still-don-t-get-a-seco.source:
you
