arcane-charge|you-still-don-t-get-a-seco.summary: This is as much movement as using the Dash action for most characters, so, combined with Action Surge, you get to do almost as much as you could in a complete additional turn (you still don’t get a second Bonus Action).

improved-war-magic|s.name: Improved War Magic
improved-war-magic|s.summary: Level 1 and 2 spells won’t be great for damage at this level compared to an entire Action worth of attacks, but you can easily use this for buffs like Enlarge/Reduce, debuffs like Ray of Sickness, save-or-suck spells like Tasha’s Hideous Laughter, and area control options like Web. If you’re making a spell attack, I strongly recommend a Vex weapon to make up for your Intelligence likely not being at 20. If you’re relying on a saving throw, you still want to attack your target(s) first to trigger Eldritch Strike to debuff their saves. This doesn’t conflict with War Magic, so you could trade three attacks to cast a Cantrip and a level 1 or level 2 spell in one Action. Once you get to level 20 and get your 4th attack, you can make a weapon attack and still cast spells twice in a single Action. Literally no one else gets to do that. Remember that you’re still limited to casting one spell with a spell slot per turn, so even if you use Action Surge, you won’t be able to cast another level 1 or level 2 spell with Improved War Magic.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(183); });

psionic-power|function.name: Psionic Power
psionic-power|function.summary: Your pool of Psionic Energy Dice are your defining resource. You get from 4 to 12 dice over your career, and the size goes from d6 to d12 over the course of your career. That sounds like a big pool, but they mostly recharge on a Long Rest, and between Long Rests you can recharge just one die per Short Rest. If your DM adheres to the Adventuring Day rules in the DMG, that means you can recharge just two dice per day. Across a full day of adventuring, that’s a small pool to work with. You need to be cautious about spending your dice rather than burning through them in the first encounter. The initial options for spending your Psionic Energy Dice are easy ways to quickly burn through your dice for modest amounts of damage or protection. : Preventing some or all of the damage from an attack can keep you or an ally fighting, and can help allies maintain Concentration on spells. Save this for when hit points are low or when an ally’s Concentration is crucial, otherwise you risk running through your Psionic Energy dice in a hurry.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(184); }); : A modest burst of damage. The damage is a separate source from your attack (it deals damage on its own rather than adding damage to the attack), so it’s not multiplied on a critical hit. I wouldn’t consider this a go-to option until you add Telekinetic Thrust at level 7 because your pool of dice is too small and too precious to spend on something as mundane as a tiny bit of damage. However, you might make an exception in cases where the extra damage could kill the creature or cause it to lose Concentration (since it’s a separate source of damage it forces a second saving throw). : Situational. You get it once per Short Rest, which is often be enough, but you can use it again for a Psionic Energy Die if you need to. This is forced movement (even though the target is willing), so you can use it to pull allies out of melee (even if they’re grappled) without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

telekinetic-movement|even-though-the-tar.source: even though the target is willing
telekinetic-movement|even-though-the-tar.summary: Situational. You get it once per Short Rest, which is often be enough, but you can use it again for a Psionic Energy Die if you need to. This is forced movement (even though the target is willing), so you can use it to pull allies out of melee (even if they’re grappled) without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

psi-powered-leap|consider-using-action-s.name: Psi-Powered Leap
psi-powered-leap|consider-using-action-s.source:
consider using

psi-powered-leap|consider-using-action-s.summary: Even though the flight only lasts until the end of your current turn, that’s enough to get into melee with flying enemies and beat them up (consider using Action Surge to maximize the benefits) or Shove them prone to force them to fall. You can also use this to fly over pits, high walls, and other barriers. You get this once for free, but if you need it again you can recharge it with a Psionic Energy Die.

telekinetic-thrust|unknown.name: Telekinetic Thrust
telekinetic-thrust|unknown.summary: Unarmed Strikes and Topple mastery weapons are typically sufficient for Strength-based fighters who want to knock enemies prone, but this is a great counter to flying enemies for Dexterity-based builds. Flying creatures that are knocked Prone fall, which can both cause a lot of damage and bring them into melee range. While this doesn’t consume a Psionic Energy die on its own, this is an optional rider effect that you add to Psionic Strike, which does consume a die.

guarded-mind|like-you.name: Guarded Mind
guarded-mind|like-you.summary: Charm and Fear effects are common and annoying across the full level range, and can take you out of a fight. They’re especially good counters to martial characters (like you) because they tend to require Wisdom saving throws which martial characters are usually bad at. Indomitable does make this somewhat redundant, but in a long adventuring day you might prefer to dip into your Psionic Energy Dice rather than spending precious Indomitable uses. Resistance to psychic damage is nice, but only situationally useful because psychic damage is rare.

bulwark-of-force|unknown.name: Bulwark of Force
bulwark-of-force|unknown.summary: +2 AC and +2 on Dexterity saves to you and possibly the rest of your party for 1 minute, activated as a Bonus Action. This is a great buff at any level, but remember that it won’t stack with other sources of cover. You only get to use this once per day, but you can recharge it with a Psionic Energy Die, and I recommend doing so. The +2 AC to your whole party will mitigate a huge amount of damage in a typical fight. +2 on a 20-point scale is 10% of the scale, so a +2 AC bonus will negate roughly 10% of all attack damage to your party in that encounter.

telekinetic-master|unknown.name: Telekinetic Master
telekinetic-master|unknown.summary: By this level it’s entirely possible that you have raised both your Strength/Dexterity and your Intelligence to 20, so your Intelligence checks may be very good. That makes Telekinesis a useful option in combat, especially against foes with poor Strength like many spellcasters. You can use this to lift foes into the air and drop them, to move them over pits or into hazards, or just to pull them into melee range. The ability to make a weapon attack as a Bonus Action while concentrating on Telekinesis is very exciting. The obvious intent is that you use your Action to use Telekinesis, and that can be a powerful combination: lift your target into the air and shoot them, or drop them to force them to fall prone before attacking them in melee. However, you’re under no obligation to actually use Telekinesis while you’re concentrating on it. The spell has a 10-minute duration, so you can easily use it as a buff to add an attack as a Bonus Action. If you enjoy this strategy, I think you’ll agree that spending a Psionic Energy Die to recharge this ability is well worth the cost to get an additional attack with little effort.

wayfarer|phb.summary: If you plan on leaning into Advantage, this is the only Background that offers Lucky and a stat that can natively be used with weapons.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: Crafter is useful to help you buy the Plate armor you desperately want, and then largely never again. The skills, meanwhile, offer one passably interesting option and one that is almost always tied to your dump stat.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: If you’re going to be the Scout, just take Criminal. It gets you three proficiencies you want for the roll, including Thieves’ Tools, and a great starting Feat.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: One and a half good and relevant skills and a scaling bonus to initiative so you can either get your buff going before anyone else takes a turn or donate your high roll to the supremacy caster.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: With a bit of Intelligence, you can serve as your party’s Scholar. History, plus three skills from Skilled mean that you can get all of the knowledge skills. If you’re building around Dexterity, you might take a mix of Intelligence-based skills and Dexterity-based skills. However, not having Constitution as an ability may be a problem depending on your other build choices, so Scribe is likely a better choice for the same goal.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: Two decent skills for the build and more proficiencies. Criminal is a better choice if you’re planning to be your party’s Scout, but this may allow you serve as your party’s Scholar.

acid-splash|phb.name: Acid Splash
acid-splash|phb.summary: Great for handling groups of enemies, especially if you can force them into a small area with a Shove weapon. Unfortunately, you need to be built around Intelligence to use this reliably, which means Shillelagh, and Shillelagh doesn’t support any weapons with the Shove Weapon Mastery.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

blade-ward|phb.name: Blade Ward
blade-ward|phb.summary: Excellent for any melee build. -1d4 to attacks against you is a significant AC boost. It does require Concentration, so you can’t combine it with many other useful buffs, but, once you have War Magic this is an easy choice in almost any encounter.

booming-blade|scag-tcoe.name: Booming Blade
booming-blade|scag-tcoe.summary: The go-to attack cantrip for melee builds, Booming Blade is a defining tactical option for the Eldritch Knight. Combining this with the Push mastery allows you to knock enemies out of reach and leave them to take the secondary damage if they want to get back into melee with you.

chill-touch|phb.name: Chill Touch
chill-touch|phb.summary: Preventing healing is rarely impactful. See True Strike, below.

control-flames|unknown.name: Control Flames
control-flames|unknown.summary: Bad. You don’t have space for utility, and this would still be bad if you did.

create-bonfire|unknown.name: Create Bonfire
create-bonfire|unknown.summary: Decent low-budget area control. If you can grapple enemies to hold them in place or use a Push weapon to knock them into the fire, this can be easy damage.

dancing-lights|phb.name: Dancing Lights
dancing-lights|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

elementalism|phb.name: Elementalism
elementalism|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

encode-thoughts|unknown.name: Encode Thoughts
encode-thoughts|unknown.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

fire-bolt|phb.name: Fire Bolt
fire-bolt|phb.summary: Intelligence-focused builds should use True Strike with a Longbow or a thrown weapon, and other builds shouldn’t rely on spell attacks. Fire Bolt’s damage will eventually outpace True Strike, but it won’t benefit from feats that you’re using to improve your attacks with weapons.

friends|phb.name: Friends
friends|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility, though this is a tempting way to imrpove the Fighter’s meager social capabilities.

green-flame-blade|scag-tcoe.name: Green-Flame Blade
green-flame-blade|scag-tcoe.summary: Booming Blade is more useful for the Eldritch Knight’s role as a front-line tank, and you only get a total of 3 cantrips over your entire career, so it’s hard to justify taking both. The ability to damage two enemies with one attack is really enticing, but, if you need that functionality, you can either attack twice or cast Sword Burst. Note that Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything published an updated version of Green-Flame Blade.

light|phb.name: Light
light|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

lightning-lure|scag-tcoe.name: Lightning Lure
lightning-lure|scag-tcoe.summary: Despite the 15-foot range, this can be a great option for melee Eldritch Knights. Against enemies with poor Strength (like many enemy spellcasters), you can use this to drag them into melee with you and force them to teleport or Disengage in order to get away from you unharmed. If you’re flying, you may even be able to pull enemies into the air to cause a small amount of falling damage. Since it only has Verbal components, you can easily use this without juggling your weapon. The save is Strength, so you’ll only be successful with this against physically weak foes.

mage-hand|phb.name: Mage Hand
mage-hand|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

mending|phb.name: Mending
mending|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

message|phb.name: Message
message|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

mind-sliver|phb.name: Mind Sliver
mind-sliver|phb.summary: Even if you’re not building around Intelligence, Mind Sliver is fantastic. Intelligence saves are consistently the lowest save on average, so the damage and the debuff are reliable even if your save DC is mediocre. You could use this before hitting an enemy with an Unarmed Strike to grapple/shove them, or before you hit them with a Topple weapon, or you might just use it to support your allies.

minor-illusion|phb.name: Minor Illusion
minor-illusion|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

mold-earth|eepc.name: Mold Earth
mold-earth|eepc.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

poison-spray|phb.name: Poison Spray
poison-spray|phb.summary: Excellent damage, but only appealing for the big damage dice, which aren’t enough. See True Strike, below.

prestidigitation|phb.name: Prestidigitation
prestidigitation|phb.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

ray-of-frost|phb.name: Ray of Frost
ray-of-frost|phb.summary: 2024 DnD’s character options offer numerous ways to forcibly move enemies and to reduce their speed. Combining this with the Slasher feat can allow you to reduce a creature’s speed by 20 feet. If you can do this and then move out of reach, many enemies will be totally unable to get back into melee with you, effectively preventing them from fighting. I wouldn’t take this on its own, but if your party is capitalizing on forced movement and speel debuffs, it’s a good choice.

shape-water|eepc.name: Shape Water
shape-water|eepc.summary: You don’t have space for utility.

shocking-grasp|phb.name: Shocking Grasp
shocking-grasp|phb.summary: Preventing Opportunity Attacks could mean getting out of melee unimpeded, but you’re almost certainly built to endure an Opportunity Attack in a rare circumstance where you’re in melee against your will.

sword-burst|scag-tcoe.name: Sword Burst
sword-burst|scag-tcoe.summary: Eldritch Knights are typically in melee, and Sword Burst is a great way to handle crowds of multiple enemies.

thunderclap|phb.name: Thunderclap
thunderclap|phb.summary: Cast Sword Burst. It’s a better damage type on a more reliable save.

toll-the-dead|phb.name: Toll the Dead
toll-the-dead|phb.summary: Good damage, decent range, and a good damage type, but True Strike will still be a better choice in the vast majority of cases.

true-strike|phb.name: True Strike
true-strike|phb.summary: is uniquely powerful in a way that defines your other cantrip options. Because it works both in melee and at range, you can use it as a go-to attack cantrip regardless of your choice of weaponry. For an Intelligence-based build, it’s perfect. It doesn’t provide the tactical utility that Booming Blade does, but it remains equally effective both at range and in melee. If you’re building around Strength or Dexterity, True Strike is largely useless. You must use your spellcasting ability with True Strike, which means significantly worse accuracy and damage. Use Booming Blade instead.

absorb-elements|xgte.name: Absorb Elements
absorb-elements|xgte.summary: You get spellcasting later and slower than anyone else, so you have very few options for protecting yourself from non-weapon damage. This will handle that issue, but it will eat your spell slots quickly, so be sure to eliminate the source of the elemental damage as quickly as possible so that you don’t run through your spell slots too quickly. The biggest challenge for Absorb Elements is that it has Somatic components, which require a free hand. By default, this means that two-weapon fighting builds and sword-and-board builds will be unable to use this unless you’re diligent about drawing and stowing your weapon, which both makes opportunity attacks hard. Unfortunately, the only ways around this are War Caster or Subtle Spell.

alarm|phb.name: Alarm
alarm|phb.summary: Not consistently useful enough to justify. If you need this, take Ritual Caster.

burning-hands|phb.name: Burning Hands
burning-hands|phb.summary: The damage is good for a 1st-level spell if you can hit multiple foes in the AOE.

catapult|eepc.name: Catapult
catapult|eepc.summary: The damage isn’t worth the spell slot by the time you get it.

charm-person|phb.name: Charm Person
charm-person|phb.summary: Helpful in social situations, but Advantage on Charisma checks is only minimally helpful when you have 8 Charisma and no social skills.

chromatic-orb|phb.name: Chromatic Orb
chromatic-orb|phb.summary: Obsolete by the time you get it.

comprehend-languages|phb.name: Comprehend Languages
comprehend-languages|phb.summary: Only situationally useful. Consider taking Ritual Caster if you want this.

detect-magic|phb.name: Detect Magic
detect-magic|phb.summary: Essential, but hopefully someone else in the party can cast it. Consider Ritual Caster if you really need it.

disguise-self|phb.name: Disguise Self
disguise-self|phb.summary: Only situationally useful. You won’t get enough use out of this to justify having it permanently prepared.

earth-tremor|eepc-xgte.name: Earth Tremor
earth-tremor|eepc-xgte.summary: Not nearly enough damage, and being prone isn’t enough of a problem in 5e. The difficult terrain effect is the real draw. It only works on “loose earth or stone”, which may be a problematic limitation. Unfortunately, it also affects you, so be careful not to trap yourself among enemies.

expeditious-retreat|phb.name: Expeditious Retreat
expeditious-retreat|phb.summary: Nice mobility for melee builds, but Jump is a better choice so that you can also move vertically.

false-life|phb.name: False Life
false-life|phb.summary: A little bit of extra durability, but probably not worth the spell slot.

feather-fall|phb.name: Feather Fall
feather-fall|phb.summary: Essential in any party, but wait to take it until you have enough combat spells to get through the day.

find-familiar|phb.name: Find Familiar
find-familiar|phb.summary: Get an owl and have it use Flyby and Help to give you Advantage before you try to hit an enemy with Booming Blade or another spell attack.

fog-cloud|phb.name: Fog Cloud
fog-cloud|phb.summary: Decent area control. If you have Fighting Style (Blind Fighting), this can be a go-to tactic.

frost-fingers|rotf.name: Frost Fingers
frost-fingers|rotf.summary: Bad damage on a bad save.

grease|phb.name: Grease
grease|phb.summary: Decent area control, but not a big AOE. Consider using a Push weapon to repeatedly force enemies into the are to make them reattempt the saving throw.

ice-knife|phb.name: Ice Knife
ice-knife|phb.summary: Poor damage with too many points of failure.

identify|phb.name: Identify
identify|phb.summary: Only situationally useful. Consider Ritual Caster if you absolutely need this.

jim-s-magic-missile|unknown.name: Jim’s Magic Missile
jim-s-magic-missile|unknown.summary: Usually no better than Magic Missile, but very powerful oncey you have both get Spirit Shroud and Improved War Magic.

jump|phb.name: Jump
jump|phb.summary: A great boost to your mobility with a Bonus Action casting time. You can’t afford to use this in every encounter, but it’s great if you need to get past obstacles or hazards.

longstrider|phb.name: Longstrider
longstrider|phb.summary: A great buff for melee builds.

mage-armor|phb.name: Mage Armor
mage-armor|phb.summary: If you’re Dexterity-based, this is the only way to match the base AC provided by plate armor. The 8-hour duration is especially nice since you get so few spell slots to throw around.

magic-missile|phb.name: Magic Missile
magic-missile|phb.summary: Obsolete by the time you get it.

protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.name: Protection from Evil and Good
protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.summary: A fantastic defensive buff against a wide variety of enemies. Once you get Improved War Magic at level 18, it’s easy to cast this in combat.

ray-of-sickness|phb.name: Ray of Sickness
ray-of-sickness|phb.summary: Poison resistance/immunity is common. For most of your career you can’t justify spending an Action to cast this, and by the time you get Improved War Magic your other options are much more impactful.

shield|phb.name: Shield
shield|phb.summary: A fantastic defense, but you have very few spell slots, so you need to be very cautious about using it too frequently. If you’re in melee and use this a lot, consider the Defensive Duelist feat. The biggest challenge for Shield is that is has Somatic components, which require a free hand. By default, this means that two-weapon fighting builds and sword-and-board builds will be unable to use this unless you’re diligent about drawing and stowing your weapon during your turn, which may make Opportunity Attacks harder. You can get around this with options like War Caster or Ruby of the War Mage.

silent-image|phb.name: Silent Image
silent-image|phb.summary: A fantastic utility, but you probably can’t afford space for it in your limited number of prepared spells.

silvery-barbs|scoc.name: Silvery Barbs
silvery-barbs|scoc.summary: Extremely powerful, but also very complicated. See my blog post on Silvery Barbs for details on the numerous abuse cases which the spell allows. Unfortunately, it’s outside of the Eldritch Knight’s school limitations.

sleep|phb.name: Sleep
sleep|phb.summary: A good save-or-suck at any level. Incapacitated effectively robs the target of their turn, and it also breaks Concentration.

snare|xgte.name: Snare
snare|xgte.summary: Good for setting a trap, or if you’re resting somewhere dangerous with a convenient choke point like a narrow hallway. Targets are restrained for at least one round, which is hopefully enough for you to fight your way out of your bedroll and grab a weapon.

spellfire-flare|frhof.name: Spellfire Flare
spellfire-flare|frhof.summary: Potentially useful at high levels when combined with Conjure Minor Elementals and Improved War Magic.

tasha-s-caustic-brew|tcoe.name: Tasha’s Caustic Brew
tasha-s-caustic-brew|tcoe.summary: The damage is too low by the time you can cast this.

unseen-servant|phb.name: Unseen Servant
unseen-servant|phb.summary: Too situational. Consider Ritual Caster if you really want this.

wardaway|frhof.name: Wardaway
wardaway|frhof.summary: A weaker version of Tasha’s Mind Whip, Wardaway makes some huge trades to fit into a level 1 spell. The damage is obviously much worse, but that’s not why you’re here. The target still gets to move and act in the same turn, but halving their speed is still impactful. The biggest limitation is that Wardaway uses a Constitution save instead of a much more reliable Intelligence save. At low levels where enemies have very few saving throw proficiencies, Wardaway may be decently reliable. But enemies at low levels also rarely have Bonus Actions, so they’re likely to fail the save and barely notice the spell’s effect. If you are going to upcast this, cast Tasha’s Mind Whip instead.

witch-bolt|phb.name: Witch Bolt
witch-bolt|phb.summary: The secondary damage on a Bonus Action is tempting in extended fights, but casting this as an Action will rarely be worth how much damage you give up by casting this instead of attacking. When you get Improved War Magic at level 18, the Bonus Action damage is irrelevant.

aganazzar-s-scorcher|xgte.name: Aganazzar’s scorcher
aganazzar-s-scorcher|xgte.summary: I’ve never been a fan of line AOEs. It’s too difficult to line up more than two creatures at a time, so you’ll probably never hit more than two creatures unless you have a long hallway handy.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

arcane-vigor|phb.name: Arcane Vigor
arcane-vigor|phb.summary: This is what Second Wind is for.

augury|phb.name: Augury
augury|phb.summary: One of my favorite divinations, but not useful enough for an Eldritch Knight to prepare it permanently.

blindness-deafness|phb.name: Blindness/Deafness
blindness-deafness|phb.summary: A great debuff, but Con saves are hard, especially if you’re not built around Intelligence.

borrowed-knowledge|unknown.name: Borrowed Knowledge
borrowed-knowledge|unknown.summary: Combined with Tactical Knowledge, this is a great way to cover skills that your party can’t already handle.

darkness|phb.name: Darkness
darkness|phb.summary: Without the ability to see in magical darkness, Fog Cloud provides the same benefit.

darkvision|phb.name: Darkvision
darkvision|phb.summary: Great if you don’t already have Darkvision, but very expensive with your limited resources. Get Goggles of Night if you can.

dragon-s-breath|unknown.name: Dragon’s Breath
dragon-s-breath|unknown.summary: Your attacks will do more damage than spending your Action to use the breath weapon. This may be appealing if you can cast it on a familiar.

elminster-s-elusion|frhof.name: Elminster’s Elusion
elminster-s-elusion|frhof.summary: Situational by design since you only need this against spells and magic effects, which not every enemy can produce. This can help a lot with saves which are normally very dangerous for martial characters, though you’ll probably still need Indomitable for low mental saves.

enhance-ability|phb.name: Enhance Ability
enhance-ability|phb.summary: A fantastic utility outside of combat.

enlarge-reduce|phb.name: Enlarge/Reduce
enlarge-reduce|phb.summary: The increased reach and the damage boost can be useful.

flaming-sphere|phb.name: Flaming Sphere
flaming-sphere|phb.summary: You could use this as a sort of area control combined with Push and/or Slow weapons in order to hold enemies in place adjacent to the sphere to force additional damage. But by the time you can cast this, Create Bonfire will do as much damage and can be cast as part of your Attack thanks to War Magic.

hold-person|phb.name: Hold Person
hold-person|phb.summary: Only works against humanoids, who will be rare enemies by the time that you can cast this.

invisibility|phb.name: Invisibility
invisibility|phb.summary: Excellent. A Dexterity-based build may be a very effective scout if you can also cast Invisibility.

jim-s-glowing-coin|unknown.name: Jim’s Glowing Coin
jim-s-glowing-coin|unknown.summary: If you can cast this before enemies notice you, it can put your party at a huge advantage. But you can’t always expect that to be an option.

kinetic-jaunt|scoc.name: Kinetic Jaunt
kinetic-jaunt|scoc.summary: Great mobility, but not significantly more useful than Jump.

knock|phb.name: Knock
knock|phb.summary: Very useful, but your party needs to be able to handle locks long before you can cast this.

levitate|phb.name: Levitate
levitate|phb.summary: Constitution saves are hard, but lifting an enemy off the ground makes many enemies much less dangerous, often totally removing them from a fight.

magic-weapon|phb.name: Magic Weapon
magic-weapon|phb.summary: A fantastic offensive buff. It’s great at this level, and you can upcast it to increase the bonus to +2.

maximilian-s-earthen-grasp|eepc.name: Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp
maximilian-s-earthen-grasp|eepc.summary: A great way to restrain small nimble enemies and weak spellcasters, both of which are likely to look for ways to run away from you.

mirror-image|phb.name: Mirror Image
mirror-image|phb.summary: An excellent defensive buff, especially once you have Improved War Magic.

misty-step|phb.name: Misty Step
misty-step|phb.summary: Absolutely fantastic. Eventually you’ll want to trade it out once you get Arcane Charge, but that’s not until 15th level.

nystul-s-magic-aura|phb.name: Nystul’s Magic Aura
nystul-s-magic-aura|phb.summary: Only situationally useful. Masking yourself as a construct makes you immune to many dangerous spells, but enemies rarely cast those spells.

phantasmal-force|phb.name: Phantasmal Force
phantasmal-force|phb.summary: An excellent sav-eor-suck at any level, especially since it targets Intelligence saves.

pyrotechnics|eepc.name: Pyrotechnics
pyrotechnics|eepc.summary: The effects are weak and the required setup is annoying.

ray-of-enfeeblement|phb.name: Ray of Enfeeblement
ray-of-enfeeblement|phb.summary: Con saves are the least reliable save, and the creatures that suffer from this spell will also have high Constitution saves.

rope-trick|phb.name: Rope Trick
rope-trick|phb.summary: Useful, but I really hope that someone else in your party can cast this.

scorching-ray|phb.name: Scorching Ray
scorching-ray|phb.summary: Rarely a good idea, but, once you have Improved War Magic, you can combine this with Conjure Minor Elementals to deal a ton of damage very quickly.

see-invisibility|phb.name: See Invisibility
see-invisibility|phb.summary: Probably your only counter to invisible enemies unless you can get a magic item like a Lantern of Revealing. Maybe skip this if your party has other options like Faerie Fire.

shadow-blade|xgte.name: Shadow Blade
shadow-blade|xgte.summary: Compared to a rapier, the Shadow Blade adds 1d8 damage per attack, it changes to psychic damage (which is resisted by very few creatures), and it adds the Thrown property for some reason. Since it gives you Advantage to attack creatures in dim light or darkness it will offset Disadvantage for attacking creatures when it’s too dark for you to see. If you’re not built around Intelligence, this is a great boost to your damage output, and gives Strength-based and Dexterity-based builds an easy ranged option. Unfortunately, it doesn’t have Weapon Mastery because it was published under the 2014 rules.

shatter|phb.name: Shatter
shatter|phb.summary: Decent damage with a good AOE and Thunder damage. You’ll rarely use it in combat unless there is an extremely dense group of enemies.

snilloc-s-snowball-swarm|xgte.name: Snilloc’s snowball swarm
snilloc-s-snowball-swarm|xgte.summary: Shatter but with less damage and worse damage type.

spider-climb|phb.name: Spider Climb
spider-climb|phb.summary: The next best thing to flight. Very appealing for fighting at range.

spray-of-cards|bomt.name: Spray of Cards
spray-of-cards|bomt.summary: The damage is poor, but temporarily blinding a creature on a Dexterity save is potentially powerful against Strength-based enemies, who typically have awful Dexterity saves.

suggestion|phb.name: Suggestion
suggestion|phb.summary: Fantastically versatile and extremely powerful. The 2024 version of the spell is insanely abusable because of how permissive it is. RAW you can tell a creature to suffocate themselves to death. I recommend using the 2014 version of the spell to avoid Suggestion derailing your game.

tasha-s-mind-whip|tcoe.name: Tasha’s Mind Whip
tasha-s-mind-whip|tcoe.summary: Not a lot of damage, but it’s on an Intelligence save, and it severely limits your target’s action options, making this a powerful offensive option at any level.

vortex-warp|scoc.name: Vortex Warp
vortex-warp|scoc.summary: Very good, but you probably can’t afford to cast this often. It may be useful once you have Improved War Magic so that you can reposition and ally at reduced action cost.

warding-wind|xgte.name: Warding Wind
warding-wind|xgte.summary: A moving sphere of difficult terrain centered on you. This makes it easy for you to keep enemies close (especially if you use the Slow Weapon Mastery to further reduce their speed), and the 10-minute duration can get you through multiple fights.

web|phb.name: Web
web|phb.summary: Fantastic area control at any level even if your Intelligence is relatively poor.

animate-dead|phb.name: Animate Dead
animate-dead|phb.summary: You don’t have enough spell slots to keep your undead under control.

antagonize|bomt.name: Antagonize
antagonize|bomt.summary: Attacking stuff is your job. This will rarely do more damage than your own attacks.

ashardalon-s-stride|ftod.name: Ashardalon’s Stride
ashardalon-s-stride|ftod.summary: Bonus action casting time, and the damage doesn’t allow a save. This is a tempting spell for gish builds, but, by the time you can cast it, the damage is negligible. This is great for builds with better spellcasting than the Eldritch Knight, but for the Eldritch Knight you should look elsewhere.

bestow-curse|phb.name: Bestow Curse
bestow-curse|phb.summary: A powerful debuff, but against msot creatures you’ll get better results from just killing them.

blink|phb.name: Blink
blink|phb.summary: An interesting defensive option which doesn’t require Concentration, but, as a Fighter, you’re durable enough to stand up to enemy attacks. Removing yourself from the board half of the time means that you’re not there to take attacks in place of your weaker allies.

catnap|xgte.name: Catnap
catnap|xgte.summary: Only situationally useful, and you should not be the one to cast it.

clairvoyance|phb.name: Clairvoyance
clairvoyance|phb.summary: A great scouting option, but very expensive with the Eldritch Knight’s limited spellcasting.

counterspell|phb.name: Counterspell
counterspell|phb.summary: Helpful, but only situationally useful, and you almost certainly don’t have the room to prepare this on a daily basis without major sacrifices.

dispel-magic|phb.name: Dispel Magic
dispel-magic|phb.summary: If your party doesn’t have someone else who can cast Dispel Magic by the time it’s an option for you, you’re probably all dead.

enemies-abound|xgte.name: Enemies Abound
enemies-abound|xgte.summary: Astoundingly few enemies have good Intelligence saves, especially big scary melee monsters. Throw this on something tanky and horrifying that’s there to protect squishy enemies from you and your friends, and watch it freak out and kill its buddies for you. The duration is only a minute, and obviously this only works in an encounter with multiple enemies, but that doesn’t make the spell less awesome.

erupting-earth|eepc-xgte.name: Erupting Earth
erupting-earth|eepc-xgte.summary: Not enough damage to compete with Fireball, and not enough difficult terrain to justify the spell slot. If you need to slow down enemies, go stand in their way.

fast-friends|ai.name: Fast Friends
fast-friends|ai.summary: You won’t use this enough to justify one of your extremely limited preparation slots. Cast Suggestion instead.

fear|phb.name: Fear
fear|phb.summary: A great way to disable groups of opponents, but fear immunity is common.

fireball|phb.name: Fireball
fireball|phb.summary: At 8d6 damage, Fireball hitting multiple enemies will likely exceed the amount of damage you can do to a single creature until you get four attacks at 20th level.

flame-arrows|xgte.name: Flame Arrows
flame-arrows|xgte.summary: Tempting for a fighter to boost your damage output, but it’s not good enough to consume one of your few spells known that go beyond your school limitations.

fly|phb.name: Fly
fly|phb.summary: Flight is a defining tactical advantage over creatures who can’t fly, especially if those creatures don’t have effective ranged options. Even though this is beyond the Eldritch Knight’s school limitations it’s a must-have option. If you don’t have easy access to flight by other means (an allied spellcaster, an item, a flying mount, etc.), you need this.

glyph-of-warding|phb.name: Glyph of Warding
glyph-of-warding|phb.summary: Depending on how your DM handles it, this is either a situationally useful defensive measure or a reality-bending way to break the game from the comfort of your own home. See our Practical Guide to Glyph of Warding.

haste|phb.name: Haste
haste|phb.summary: An excellent buff at any level. The option to take an additional Attack action has a weird interaction with War Magic. Haste limits you to one attack, and War Magic lets you replace one attack with a cantrip when you take the Attack action on your turn. It appears that War Magic can replace the additional attack with a Cantrip.

hypnotic-pattern|phb.name: Hypnotic Pattern
hypnotic-pattern|phb.summary: Take a group of creatures out of a fight for a full minute on only one save. Targets don’t get another save, and the effect doesn’t end until the spell does or someone breaks targets out of the effect. This means that you can focus on enemies which pass the initial save, then gradually eliminate the remaining targets one at a time. This doesn’t scale with spell level, but it really doesn’t need to. A 30-foot cube is enough to hit several creatures, and so long as your Spell Save DC is decent you’ll do fine. Even if enemies spend an Action to break their allies out of the spell, you’ve spent one Action to incapacitate them and they’re spending more than that just to fix it without actually harming you or your allies.

intellect-fortress|tcoe.name: Intellect Fortress
intellect-fortress|tcoe.summary: Technically situational, but an absolutely spectacular defense against enemies which rely on spells or common effects like charm and fear effects. Unlike species traits like the Gnome’s Cunning or the Satyr and Yuan-Ti’s Magic Resistance, this applies to all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws, providing broad and effective protection against many of the most dangerous save-or-suck effects in the game. You also get resistance to Psychic damage, which is nice if you’re fighting mind flayers, aboleths, or Bards who enjoy Vicious Mockery. With a 1-hour duration, the Concentration requirement can be problematic, but it also means that you can carry this through multiple encounters at low cost, so in situations where you need this it’s not going to eat all of your spell slots.

laerel-s-silver-lance|frhof.name: Laerel’s Silver Lance
laerel-s-silver-lance|frhof.summary: The damage type is fantastic, the Prone effect is great, very few area damage spells target Strength saves, and you can omit targets to avoid hitting friends. There’s definitely a niche here, but 3d10 (avg. 16.5) is very low compared to other level 3 spells. Lightning Bolt is 8d6 (avg. 28), and upcasting Laerel’s Silver Lance actually widens that gap. Preparing this and buying the 250 gp spell component feels like too much investment for the extremely narrow case where you can justify using this over other damage spells.

leomund-s-tiny-hut|phb.name: Leomund’s Tiny Hut
leomund-s-tiny-hut|phb.summary: Perhaps an odd choice for the Eldritch Knight, but Tiny Hut is a great place to rest, and you can cast it as a ritual. If you have time to set it up it’s a great defensive position.

lightning-bolt|phb.name: Lightning Bolt
lightning-bolt|phb.summary: As much damage as fireball, but it’s much harder to hit multiple creatures with a line.

major-image|phb.name: Major Image
major-image|phb.summary: Powerful and versatile, but an Eldritch Knight likely won’t use it often enough to prepare permanently.

melf-s-minute-meteors|eepc-xgte.name: Melf’s Minute Meteors
melf-s-minute-meteors|eepc-xgte.summary: I love that you can use this to turn your bonus action into damage output, but with your poor save DC this deals too little damage to waste a 3rd-level spell slot.

nondetection|phb.name: Nondetection
nondetection|phb.summary: Only situationally useful, and you typically cast this as a precaution at the beginning of an adventuring day. You may not be able to afford to spend a spell slot on this every day.

phantom-steed|phb.name: Phantom Steed
phantom-steed|phb.summary: A wonderful utility, but you probably don’t want to prepare it permanently. Hopefully someone else in the party can cast this.

protection-from-energy|phb.name: Protection from Energy
protection-from-energy|phb.summary: An excellent defensive option, but you may be doing alright with Absorb Elements.

sleet-storm|phb.name: Sleet Storm
sleet-storm|phb.summary: Not useful enough to make it more appealing than Fireball or Hypnotic Pattern.

slow|phb.name: Slow
slow|phb.summary: A good debuff, but not good enough to compare with other level 3 options when you get so few spells.

spirit-shroud|tcoe.name: Spirit Shroud
spirit-shroud|tcoe.summary: A 1-minute combat buff which adds 1d8 damage and a 10 ft. speed reduction to each of your numerous attacks. Combined with Action Surge, you can deal a huge amount of damage very quickly. This can be very powerful on a Defender build, and it’s easy to combine with the Slow Weapon Mastery to prevent enemies from getting away from you.

stinking-cloud|phb.name: Stinking Cloud
stinking-cloud|phb.summary: While this can rob targets of their Action if they fail the save, the area is small and easy to escape.

summon-fey|phb.name: Summon Fey
summon-fey|phb.summary: Decent summons at this spell level, but no specific synergy. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-lesser-demons|xgte.name: Summon Lesser Demons
summon-lesser-demons|xgte.summary: You can’t control the demons, and they’re probably not strong enough to win an encounter on their own. The material component may also be problem since it has a 24 freshness timer. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-shadowspan|tcoe.name: Summon Shadowspan
summon-shadowspan|tcoe.summary: The Despair version’s speed debuff is great for keeping enemies in melee with you. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-undead|phb.name: Summon Undead
summon-undead|phb.summary: Several excellent combat options, and the ghostly option can fly around and do stuff for you. The Skeletal option is an effective ranged attacker, and it can easily outdamage any of your other spell options if you can fit multiple encounters into the 1-hour duration. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

sylun-s-viper|frhof.name: Syluné’s Viper
sylun-s-viper|frhof.summary: Bonus Action casting time, 1-hour duration, no Concentration. The damage is horrid, and poison immunity is obviously a problem, but the ability to make a target Incapacitated on hit means that you can lock a single target out of a fight for as long as you can reliably hit them with attacks. The Incapacitation effect doesn’t allow a save, so even Legendary Resistance won’t protect enemies from this. You also get a climb speed so that you can climb out of reach and bite enemies from safety. The spell’s biggest weakness is the Temporary Hit Points. You only get 15, and the spell ends early once you’re out of THP. You likely have good AC, but by this level any save-for-half damage effect will be enoug to cut right through the tiny pool of THP. You’ll only be able to use this safely against single targets that can’t deal damage with Lair Actions or Legendary Actions.

thunder-step|xgte.name: Thunder Step
thunder-step|xgte.summary: You can get most of the same teleportation function from Arcane Charge.

vampiric-touch|phb.name: Vampiric Touch
vampiric-touch|phb.summary: The healing is really cool, but spending your entire Action to use it is hard to justify.

wall-of-sand|eepc-xgte.name: Wall of Sand
wall-of-sand|eepc-xgte.summary: Passable area control, but Web will be more effective if the terrain supports it.

wall-of-water|eepc-xgte.name: Wall of Water
wall-of-water|eepc-xgte.summary: This makes it hard for you to to engage enemies. Wall of Sand is more useful.

arcane-eye|phb.name: Arcane Eye
arcane-eye|phb.summary: An absolutely fantastic scouting option, but not worth your only level 4 spell slot.

backlash|frhof.name: Backlash
backlash|frhof.summary: You get exactly one level 4 spell slot, you have d10 hit dice, and you have Second Wind. You shouldn’t need this enough to justify preparing it.

charm-monster|phb.name: Charm Monster
charm-monster|phb.summary: Helpful in social situations, but not consistently useful enough for you to prepare permanently.

conjure-minor-elementals|phb.name: Conjure Minor Elementals
conjure-minor-elementals|phb.summary: Excellent, but you may have better results with Spirit Shroud. Spirit Shroud fills a similar nihe, and it’s cast as a Bonus Action. Conjure Minor Elementals is cast as an Action, but has a 10-minute duration compared to Spirit Shroud’s 1-minute duration, plus Conjure Minor Elementals has a 15-foot radius compared to Spirit Shroud’s 10-foot radius, and does more damage. Pick whichever works for you.

fire-shield|phb.name: Fire Shield
fire-shield|phb.summary: One of the Fighter’s primary roles is Defender. Your job is to stand in the front and get attacked by scary monsters. Throw up Fire Shield and enjoy a bunch of extra damage output for being in the right place and doing your job. Just be sure that enemies still have a good reason to attack you instead of your allies.

greater-invisibility|phb.name: Greater Invisibility
greater-invisibility|phb.summary: Invisibility is an absolutely spectacular buff, but part of the Fighter’s primary role in the party is to draw attention away from less durable allies. If you’re invisible, you can’t do that.

ice-storm|phb.name: Ice Storm
ice-storm|phb.summary: Terrible. Bad damage, and the difficult terrain doesn’t last long enough.

mordenkainen-s-faithful-hound|phb.name: Mordenkainen’s Faithful Hound
mordenkainen-s-faithful-hound|phb.summary: Decent for defending a specific point, but not useful enough to be your only level 4 spell each day.

mordenkainen-s-private-sanctum|phb.name: Mordenkainen’s Private Sanctum
mordenkainen-s-private-sanctum|phb.summary: You get one level 4 spell slot every day. Do you really want to spend it on a place to sleep?

otiluke-s-resilient-sphere|phb.name: Otiluke’s Resilient Sphere
otiluke-s-resilient-sphere|phb.summary: Single-target save-or-suck. A good way to take a target out of a fight until you’re ready to handle them.

phantasmal-killer|phb.name: Phantasmal Killer
phantasmal-killer|phb.summary: A decent single-target debuff against martial enemies, but fear immunity is common, and the damage won’t be as impressive by this level.

polymorph|phb.name: Polymorph
polymorph|phb.summary: With an hour-long duration, this is a great use of your single 4th-level spell slot. See our Practical Guide to Polymorph for more information.

spellfire-storm|frhof.name: Spellfire Storm
spellfire-storm|frhof.summary: The damage isn’t great and Constitution saves aren’t reliable, but the AOE is decently large and this can prevent enemies from casting spells. The Con save when casting a spell is identical to Counterspell, so you’re effectively countering every spell that enemies try to cast while in the area. I would only use when facing enemy spellcasters (the damage isn’t good enough otherwise), but with enemy spellcasters on the field this can easily define an encounter. We can also compare Spellfire Storm to Moonbeam, which also creates a column of Radiant damage. Spellfire Storm deals the same damage as Moonbeam cast at the same spell level and uses the same save, but instead of bother Shapeshifters, Spellfire Storm shuts down enemy spellcasters. Spellfire Storm can’t be moved, but the considerably larger radius means that you don’t need to move it in many encounters. In close quarters, enemies may be unable to move out of the area. Of course, that also means that you can’t use forced movement to repeatedly trigger the spell’s damage like you could with area effects which don’t cover the entire battlefield. : 25,000 gp to do this is absolutely insane. This is something that should happen as a plot point, not as a player tactic. Maybe you drop this on an extraplanar gate so that your party can fight waves of demons to shut down the gate or something similarly epic and plot-defining.

spirit-of-death|bomt.name: Spirit of Death
spirit-of-death|bomt.summary: Summon Undead is arguably better, but this is still a good summon. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

stone-shape|phb.name: Stone Shape
stone-shape|phb.summary: Fantastic utility, but probably not worth your only level 4 spell slot each day.

storm-sphere|eepc-xgte.name: Storm Sphere
storm-sphere|eepc-xgte.summary: Passable area control for an extended fight, but the damage is poor, and 1 minute of this probably isn’t enough for your single level 4 spell slot. Sickening Radiance is much better.

summon-aberration|phb.name: Summon Aberration
summon-aberration|phb.summary: Three diverse and effective combat options. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-construct|phb.name: Summon Construct
summon-construct|phb.summary: Not as effective offensively as Summon Aberration, but all three summoned constructs are unusually durable for creatures summoned by similar spells. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-elemental|phb.name: Summon Elemental
summon-elemental|phb.summary: Summon Aberration is better offensively, and Summon Construct provides a more durable summon. Summon Elemental’s biggest advantage is that you can summon a creature that can fight effectively underwater, but even then it’s not a great summon. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

watery-sphere|eepc-xgte.name: Watery Sphere
watery-sphere|eepc-xgte.summary: Without a maxed out spell save DC this spell isn’t reliable enough to waste your only 4th-level spell slot.

bonus-unarmed-strike|function.name: Bonus Unarmed Strike
bonus-unarmed-strike|function.summary: Twice as many attacks as normal right from level 1, and, unlike two-weapon fighting, you get to add your ability modifier to the damage.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

martial-arts-die|unknown.name: Martial Arts Die
martial-arts-die|unknown.summary: This scales slowly, but at high levels it’s pretty great. At low levels you’ll do more damage using a quarterstaff or a spear 2-handed for the 1d8 damage die, but that won’t help your Bonus Unarmed Strike.

dexterous-attacks|unknown.name: Dexterous Attacks
dexterous-attacks|unknown.summary: Using unarmed strikes to Grapple and Shove enemies is a central tactic for the Monk. Be sure to consider the Grappler and Tavern Brawler feats, which makes Grapple/Shove even easier.

flurry-of-blows|function.name: Flurry of Blows
flurry-of-blows|function.summary: The go-to use for your Focus Points. Try to use this when you’ll get a lot of value, such as when you’ll have Advantage on your attacks.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

patient-defense|unknown.name: Patient Defense
patient-defense|unknown.summary: Add some Temporary Hit Points when you spend a Focus Point. These points don’t have a listed duration, so they last until you finish a Long Rest. Make sure that you never walk into an encounter without THP, and if you go into a Short Rest with spare FP, spend them on Patient Defense to repeatedly reroll the dice to get as much THP as possible.

step-of-the-wind|unknown.name: Step of the Wind
step-of-the-wind|unknown.summary: Bring a friend along when you spend a Focus Point with Step of the Wind. If you grapple two allies, you could drag three friends along with you at once!

flurry-of-blows|unknown.name: Flurry of Blows
flurry-of-blows|unknown.summary: 3 attacks as a Bonus Action in a damage where most martial characters are excited to get 2 attacks as an Action.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Never a bad choice, but less impactful for martial characters than for full casters.

child-of-the-sun|lfl.name: Child of the Sun
child-of-the-sun|lfl.summary: You’ll get more from Magic Initiate.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: Very powerful, and the Wisdom-based save DC works reasonably well for the Monk.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Monks make considerably more attacks than most characters, so critical hits are more likely than for most characters, which makes this worthwhile.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: Monks have enough Wisdom to make Wisdom-based spellcasting an option, but it won’t compete with your martial capabilities. You may still benefit from options like Blade Ward and Absorb Elements.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Proficiency in Insight and you can shared Heroic Inspiration with your whole party once per Long Rest.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Monks rely on small damage dice at low levels and numerous attacks at high levels, so there is never a point where this is a mathematically significant of your total damage output. It also only applies to weapons.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Hex could be a good fit for the Monk because it lasts long enough that a single casting can last through multiple fights, but without spellcasting it’s really hard to justify.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Great for picking up skills and Thieves’ Tools proficiencies so that you can easily replace a Rogue in your party.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: You can already deal damage with your Bonus Action.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: Absolutely amazing on the Monk. Consistently impactful for your whole career.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: A nice complement to the Monk’s d8 hit points, especially at low levels before your AC has scaled enough to keep you alive.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: Excellent on any melee build with a decent chance to make Opportunity Attacks.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: Without the ability to trigger Aberrant Surge repeatedly, you’ll get very little value here. Magic Initiate is a better fit.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: Almost no value here without the ability to cast spells.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: Hunter’s Mark is definitely tempting for the Monk, but once per day really isn’t enough. If you really want Hunter’s Mark, take a level of Ranger.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: Without spellcasting, this offers almost no value for the Monk. Play Warrior of Mercy.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: Without spellcasting, this offers aalmost no value for the Monk.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: If you really want Comprehend Languages, take Magic Initiate or Ritualist.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Shield once per day isn’t great, but Vigilant Guardian might be worthwhile. Just remember that using your Reaction on Vigilant Guardian means not using it on Deflect Attacks.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Useless without spellcasting. Play Warrior of Shadow.

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: A decent choice for many martial characters. A climb speed is the next best thing to a fly speed. The ability to stand up quickly makes falling or being knocked prone less of a problem. The ability to jump with less of a running start may let you easily jump over difficult terrain and other obstacles which otherwise might slow your movement in combat.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: Some useful synergy with Step of the Wind, plus the Charge Attack allows you to push enemies without needing Weapon Mastery.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: An excellent source of additional healing and of Temporary Hit Points, but you likely won’t use the treats in combat since the Monk’s Bonus Action is already heavily taxed.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Crossbows don’t count as Monk weapons. Throw darts or something.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: A simple and easy way to control enemies’ positions in combat. Of course, Empowered Strikes will cause some issues here, so this may become a frustrating option as you gain levels and damage resistances become increasingly common.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: Too much overlap with Deflect Attack.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: Deflect Attacks will be much more consistently useful.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Competes with Martial Arts. You can still use weapons with the Nick mastery to engage in two-weapon fighting, but you need to leave your Bonus Action free for the Monk’s class features.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: Not as good as you would hope. The Bonus Action to spend a Hit Point Die notably does not add your Constitution modifier, which makes it an expensive and frustrating way to burn through your Hit Point Dice very quickly with minimal impact. Unless your party has some other deep, inexpensive healing resource, you need those dice for Short Rests to refill your massive pool of hit points. Take Chef instead.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: You’re probably thinking “Warrior of the Elements.” Don’t. Just switch elements.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: Monks have two options to Disengage as a Bonus Action, so ignoring difficult terrain when you Disengage may actually be useful, but you’re here for Flustering Strike. Imposing Disadvantage on saving throws until the end of your next turn makes the target extremely vulnerable to Stunning Strike. Constitution saves are unreliable, which is the biggest challenge with Stunning Strike, but imposing Disadvantage negates that issue.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Misty Step could be very useful, but once a day likely isn’t enough to justify the feat.

grappler|phb.name: Grappler
grappler|phb.summary: Absolutely amazing on the Monk. Punch and Grab gives you the benefits of an additional unarmed strike per turn. Attack Advantage gives you an easy way to get Advantage on your attacks. Fast Wrestler lets you use your incredible speed to haul enemies far, far away from your allies. Strongly consider using Step of the Wind to run enemies away from combat and leave them there before returning to resume fighting. Leaving an enemy down a hallway or otherwise several turns of movement away from combat can dramatically shift the tide of an encounter without the possibility of failure offered by even the most powerful save-or-suck effects.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A massive amount of temporary hit points.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Extremely situational, and the impact is too small.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: The ability scores don’t work, and while the buff is great, once per day just isn’t enough.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Between high Wisdom and Disciplined Survivor, saving throws aren’t as scary for the Monk as they are for other martial characters. But at the same time, Disciplined Survivor is high enough level that you might never get to use it.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: If you’re proficient in Perception and have decent Wisdom, you may be well qualified to use Perception reliably. But even then, this is only helpful if your DM likes to use stealthy enemies and/or likes to include traps in combat encounters.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: Only situationally useful. Strength saves aren’t particularly common.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Unarmed strikes don’t deal piercing damage, and, even if your race provides that capability, Empowered Strikes will make this much less useful since you’ll want to deal Force damage to avoid increasing common damage resistances.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: The scaling spell slot can be extremely powerful with the right dragonmark feat, but you do miss some of the value since you don’t have spellcasting.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: An easy source of Advantage on attack rolls and nice way to support your allies. Consider taking Tough so that you can be Bloodied more safely. You can sidestep the Origin Feat prerequisite if you have proficiency with martial weapons. Monks only get proficiency with a subset of martial weapons, which I likely doesn’t qualify.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Disciplined Survivor will make you proficient in all saving throws.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: Not a good feat. You don’t get enough rituals, and they can only be level 1.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Fantastic for any melee build. This adds all of the Stickiness that you need to serve as your party’s Defender, but waiting to make an Opportunity Attack also conflicts with Deflect Attacks, which you desperately need to survive melee.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Invisibility is great, but without the ability to re-cast the spells, the benefits are minor.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: Monks make decent Scouts, but unlike the Ranger and the Rogue, you don’t get Expertise. This closes that gap.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Unarmed strikes don’t deal slashing damage, and, even if your race provides that capability, Empowered Strikes will make this much less useful since you’ll want to deal Force damage to avoid increasing common damage resistances.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: You have Step of the Wind for this.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: Monks are among the best characters in the game to bind creatures in chains/manacles/rope. You can use Martial Arts to attack as a Bonus Action and grapple an enemey, then use your Action to bnd that target. Combining that with the raised DC from Street Justic makes it easy to eliminate any enemy small enough for you to grapple. Even if you don’t do that, Headlock is a great way to support your allies.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: Not useful enough to compete for your Bonus Action.

telepathic|phb.name: Telepathic
telepathic|phb.summary: Only situationally useful, and it doesn’t help do Monk things.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Without other ways to maked enemies Charmed, there is very little value here.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Very little value since you don’t have spellcasting.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea, but the Monk may be an exception. Since you can’t benefit from the Fighter’s proficiencies, and most Fighting Style options aren’t appealing to the Monk, Weapon Master may be easier to fit into your build.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: An absolutely amazing feat, but the best part conflicts with Deflect Attacks.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to radiant damage is nice, but Monks can already make their attacks deal Radiant damage.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(196); });

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Advantage on an attack ocassionally and a very small damage boost each turn.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: Less useful without an easy way to give yourself Temporary Hit Points and without a way to spend Hit Point Dice in combat.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Helpful, but it only affects on your 3 or more attacks.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: This is what Empty Body is for.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: Most Monks don’t have a way to take the Magic action.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: You’re here for the once per day damage boost, and Monks don’t deal enough damage behind a single attack to make that worthwhile.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: Use this to debuff an enemy’s save when you hit them with Stunning Strike.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Monks don’t have a built-in shape-shift option, and changing form will take away all of the things that make you a good Monk.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: Even with relatively high AC and the Monk’s other defense, you’re still a melee-only class with d8 hit dice. More hp is great. For Warrior of Mercy and Warrior of the Open Hand, remember the bonus healing whenever you regain hit points.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: With 5 attacks between Extra Attack and Flurry of Blows (maybe six with two-weapon fighting shenanigans), you have a lot of opportunities to roll a 20. If you can get Advantage, such as from knocking an enemy prone, you might be rolling 12 d20s for attack rolls in a single turn.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Reach is huge for a class that is all but locked into melee attacks, and Dodge as a Bonus Action means that you don’t need to spend FP on Patient Defense.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Without a way to cast this more than once, there’s little value here.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: You don’t really need any of this unless you’re getting a ton of use out of having way too much speed.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: Awful. The odds of rollig to retain a spell slot are too small to justify this.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: Immunity to Frightened is nice, but you won’t get much use out of Intimidation, and without a built-in way to make enemies Frightened you’ll get little value from this boon.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Two damage resistances is nice, but you can’t cast spells, so you’re missing some of the benefit.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Free invisibility is amazing on any character, but this gets absolutely crazy on Warrior of Shadow, allowing you to cast Darkness and get more benefits than you would from Superior Defense.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: Two damage resistances and a little bit of healing once per rest.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Probably your only option for handling invisible enemies.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Bad ability scores, one good skill. Magic Intiate (Cleric) isn’t a great fit.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(189); });

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: Dexterity, Wisdom, and Skilled is a great combination for the Monk, especially if you’re filling in for a Rogue in the party. Unfortunately, the skills aren’t great. Charlatan and Chondathan Freebooter are easier choices.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: The Dexterity increase is not enough on its own.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: A Dexterity increase and a good feat, but the

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Dexterity, Constitution, and Skilled is a great combination for the Monk, especially if you’re filling in for a Rogue in the party. However, you don’t get proficiency in Thieves’ Tools, so you’ll need to get it from Skilled.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: A good choice if there isn’t a Rogue in the party.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: The ability scores are workable, but the feat is bad and the skills are worse.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: You can increase Dexterity and Wisdom, and you’ll need decent Wisdom so you can actually make use of Cult of the Dragon Initiate. Only one good skill, though.

emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Caretaker
emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.summary: The ability scores are workable, but the skills are bad and the feat is awful.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: Musician is great, and you can get a Charisma increase, but that’s not enough to make this easy.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: Constitution and Wisdom are decent, but you really want Dexterity. Tough is also tempting, but it’s not enough. Altogether, this is really close to a lot of things that the Monk would like, but not enough.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, one good skill, and your best choice for Magic Initiate. Grab Blade Ward, Absorb Elements, and a utlity Cantrip like Mage Hand.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Wisdom and one good skill. Alert is decnent on anyone, but that’s not enough to make this a good choice. If you want Alert, Ice Fisher may be a better fit.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: Perfect ability scores and decent skills. The spellcasting may be hard to use offensively, so stick to utility, healing, and support options. If you lean into Wisdom, you might use Shillelagh with a quarterstaff as your primary attack option.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: Dexterity, one good skill, terrible feat.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Passable ability scores, and Healer is nice on a class that can’t heal others, but the skills are poor.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, good feat, terrible skills.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: One good skill, good feat, but the ability scores are all three of the Monk’s dump stats.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: Lucky is an easy feat for anyone, but the ability scores are poor and the sills are worse. Look at Mulhorandi Tomb Raider instead.

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: You could use Magic Initiate (Druid) to get Shillelagh and build around Wisdom, but that doesn’t help your Bonus Action attacks, so it’s not a great idea.

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, and Lucky is good on anyone, but the skills are bad.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: Awful ability scores and poor skills.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Purple Dragon Rook gets you a skill proficiency, but Insight is the only good fit for the Monk, and you also get Insight from Purple Dragon Squire. The feat is good, but the background is not.

rashemi-wanderer|frhof.name: Rashemi Wanderer
rashemi-wanderer|frhof.summary: You could get a ton of extra hit points, but that’s all.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Workable ability scores, but lacking a Dexterity increase is hard. Genie Touched is an easier fit.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Excellent ability scores, one good skill, and Tavern Brawler is amazing on the Monk. Reroll your worst damage rolls and use the once per turn push to get enemies out of reach so that you don’t need to waste your Bonus Action to Disengage if you need to move away.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: A great choice if there isn’t a Rogue in the party, even beating out Criminal. With two good ability scores for the Monk, two good skills, and Skilled to pick up proficiency in things like Stealth and Thieves’ Tools, you can cover all of the proficiencies that you need to substitute for a Rogue while also getting the ability scores that we want at level 1.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: One good ability score, one good skill, mediocre feat,

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: Decent ability scores, but Savage Attack is a poor choice for the Monk, and the skills are poor.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Perfect ability scores, decent skills, terrible feat.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and between the skills and Thieves’ Tools you could fill in for a Rogue in your party. Lucky is an easy feat on any character.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: One good ability score, one good skill, and a fantastic feat.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores, and you’ll get little value from the spellcasting.

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores, and you’ll get little value from the spellcasting.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: A lot of focus on Wisdom which works for the Monk, but lack of a Dexterity increase and lack of spellcasting makes this a hard choice for the Monk.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are fine, the skills are passable, but you will get basically nothing from the feat.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: Without spellcasting, there is no point to taking this.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores and passable skills, but a bad feat. You can find better options that provide similar benefits.

house-tharashk-heir|efota.name: House Tharashk Heir
house-tharashk-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are workable and the skills are both Wisdom-based, but that’s not enough to make up for the feat.

house-thuranni-heir|efota.name: House Thuranni Heir
house-thuranni-heir|efota.summary: Workable ability scores and skills, but the feat isn’t enough to make this good.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
