aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. The transformation is very tempting, but the Monk’s Bonus Action is already heavily overtaxed and you’ll struggle to find a time to transform.

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: All about Charisma, which is not useful for the Monk.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: A damage resistance, likely to a common damage type like poison or fire, and a decent way to handle crowds of small enemies which most Monks can’t replicate. You also get Darkvision and flight once per day.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense may be hard since the Monk’s Bonus Action is so heavily taxed, but if you can’t find your enemies, you certainly can’t punch them. The durability is very welcome on the Monk.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great. The innate spellcasting may be useful, but once per day isn’t enough for some of the spells to feel impactful. You don’t need to totally avoid offensive spells like many martial characters because of the Monk’s reliance on Wisdom, but the Wood Elf is likely still your best choice. If you do go for High Elf, consider Blade Ward for your cantrip.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options. Gnomish Cunning, paired with the Monk’s high Wisdom, is enough to make up for not being proficient in Wisdom saves.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage offers numerous excellent options, but several will be redundant with the Monk’s class features. Cloud’s Jaunt is less appealing when you can Disengage for free and have crazy speed. Stone’s Endurance is nice, but partially redundant with Deflect Attack. Hill’s Topple is great since the Monk doesn’t get Weapon Mastery, though it is redundant for Warrior of the Open Hand. The on-hit damage options work fine. Large Size and Powerful Build won’t see consistent use.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Monks aren’t proficient with Wisdom saves, so Brave and the Monk’s high Wisdom will help protect you from a common status condition. Halfling Nimbleness will help you to move past and through enemy’s spaces, especially when using Patient Defense/Step of the Wind to move about. Lucky will be helpful with the Monk’s unusually high number of attacks. Naturally Stealthy is only useful outside of combat since the Monk doesn’t get Cunning Action.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Similar to the Gnome, but you trade Darkvision and Advantage on Intelligence saves for resistance to Psychic damage and telepathy.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Fantastic and versatile. Comparable to a human with Magic Initiate, but you trade most of the spellcasting for Darkvision. If you want Blade Ward, but don’t actually care about other spells, the Khoravar is a great choice.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: The temporary hit points from Adrenaline Rush are nice, but the Monk’s Bonus Action is already heavily overtaxed. Relentless Endurance is nice, but if you’re worried about taking too much damage, you can play defensively by kiting or boost your defenses with Patient Defense.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Shifting competes for your Bonus Action in a way that can be difficult for the Monk, but the buffs are pretty good. Beasthide is always an easy choice, and Swiftstride is great if you’re getting a lot of value from your high movement speed.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting. You won’t use the spellcasting consistently, and if you want a damage resistance you can get it from the Dragonborn.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and spellcasting that you won’t use.

athletics|str.name: Athletics
athletics|str.summary: (Str): Functionally useless. You can use Athletics to bind creatures in chains, but you’re better suited to using Sleight of Hand for manacles or rope.

history|int.name: History
history|int.summary: (Int): A good knowledge skill, but you don’t have the Intelligence to support it.

insight|wis.name: Insight
insight|wis.summary: (Wis): The closest thing you get to a Face skill.

religion|int.name: Religion
religion|int.summary: (Int): A good knowledge skill, but you don’t have the Intelligence to support it.

stealth|dex.name: Stealth
stealth|dex.summary: (Dex): With such a high dependence on Dexterity, Stealth is an obvious option.

dagger|unknown.name: Dagger
dagger|unknown.summary: Your go-to ranged attack option. The damage die is small, but you can replace it with your Martial Arts die, so it’s not an issue.

quarterstaff-spear|unknown.name: Quarterstaff / Spear
quarterstaff-spear|unknown.summary: When used two-handed, these provide a small damage boost compared to your unarmed strikes until you reach level 5.

barbarian|unknown.name: Barbarian
barbarian|unknown.summary: One level for the Barbarian’s version of Unarmored Defense will let you focus on Dexterity and Constitution, emphasizing your martial capabilities over features like Stunning Fist. Subclasses which rely heavily on saving throws should generally avoid this tactic, and unless you’re planning to take Constitution to 20 this isn’t necessarily better than a standard Monk.

druid|unknown.name: Druid
druid|unknown.summary: Shillelagh looks tempting, but remember that your Bonus Action attacks will still be Dexterity-based.

fighter|unknown.name: Fighter
fighter|unknown.summary: 1 level for Weapon Mastery may be worthwhile, but the Ranger has more to offer the Monk.

ranger|unknown.name: Ranger
ranger|unknown.summary: With the Monk’s high number of attacks, Hunter’s Mark looks very tempting. 1 level lets you cast Hunter’s Mark up to 4 times per day and also gets you Weapon Mastery. 2 levels will getr you Expertise and a Fighting Style.

rogue|unknown.name: Rogue
rogue|unknown.summary: One level for Expertise may be worthwhile.

hand-of-harm|or-whatever-type-your-weapo.name: Hand of Harm
hand-of-harm|or-whatever-type-your-weapo.source: or whatever type your weapon deals
hand-of-harm|or-whatever-type-your-weapo.summary: One Focus Point point to automatically deal roughly as much damage as an Unarmed Strike is more efficient than spending a Focus Point to perform a Flurry of Blows which has a chance to miss. This is also necrotic damage, which is much less-commonly resisted than bludgeoning damage (or whatever type your weapon deals). Since the damage is “extra damage” added to the attack, the extra damage die is multiplied on critical hits, much like Divine Smite or Sneak Attack, so the most effective time to use Hand of Harm is when you score a critical hit. However, this only works after you hit with an Unarmed Strike. If you’re using a weapon, there’s an incentive to fight unarmed even if your Martial Arts die would deal less damage than a weapon. Of course, Flurry of Blows and Martial Arts’ Bonus Action attack only allow Unarmed Strikes, so there’s always going to be some portion of your attacks where you can apply this.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); }); Physician’s Touch later improves Hand of Harm to add the Poisoned condition, making it an amazing way to briefly debuff enemies without a save.

hand-of-healing|function.name: Hand of Healing
hand-of-healing|function.summary: Your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier is roughly equivalent to a 1st-level Healing Word. That’s not a ton of healing all at once, but you get a ton of Focus Points per Short Rest as you gain levels, and the action economy around this is fantastic. This is also a great way to expend your remaining Focus Points whenever you reach a Short Rest. While you can use Hand of Healing as an Action, there’s almost no reason to do so in combat. Spending your Action to heal in small amounts turns combat into an attrition fight, and players always lose attrition fights. Generally you’ll use Hand of Healing during combat as part of a Flurry of Blows. When you do this, you spend the Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows, then you can decide to replace one of the Unarmed Strikes with Hand of Healing. As far as I can tell, you can make this decision at any point, so you could make one attack and see the results before deciding if you want to make another attack or heal something. Since you can move between attacks, I believe that you can also move between attacking and using Hand of Healing, so you could use Flurry of Blows to heal an ally and then run over to an enemy and attack them some more.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); }); In many ways, this is like Healing Word, and until your Focus Point pool is fairly large, that’s how you should consider Hand of Healing: a tiny amount of healing, but enough to bring a dying ally back into a fight. As you gain more levels you can afford to use this more often, and Physician’s Touch allows you to quickly remove some problematic status conditions.

implements-of-mercy|although-check-out-s.name: Implements of Mercy
implements-of-mercy|although-check-out-s.source:
although check out some of
		our
		suggestions
		to fix that
implements-of-mercy|although-check-out-s.summary: Insight and Medicine are both Wisdom-based, which makes them good skills for the Monk. Unfortunately, Medicine is borderline useless (although check out some of our suggestions to fix that), as its sole written function is made obsolete by the Healer’s Kit. Herbalism Kit does allow you to craft Antitoxins and Potions of Healing, though, which is nice.

hand-of-harm|though-spellcasters-who-don.name: Hand of Harm
hand-of-harm|though-spellcasters-who-don.source:
though spellcasters
				who don’t rely on attack rolls can largely ignore it, and it’s the single most common status immunity in the game
hand-of-harm|though-spellcasters-who-don.summary: adds the ability to make the target Poisoned with no save. Poisoned is an absolutely fantastic debuff against most enemies (though spellcasters who don’t rely on attack rolls can largely ignore it, and it’s the single most common status immunity in the game).

hand-of-healing|unknown.name: Hand of Healing
hand-of-healing|unknown.summary: adds the effect of Lesser Restoration and can also remove the Stunned condition. If this was an either/or it would be fantastic, but you get to both remove conditions and heal the target.

flurry-of-healing-and-harm|unknown.name: Flurry of Healing and Harm
flurry-of-healing-and-harm|unknown.summary: This provides a way to conserve some Focus Points a few times per day, as well as to rapidly provide a lot of healing all at once. You do still need to spend one FP to activate Flurry of Blows, but you got Heightened Focus at level 10, so Flurry of Blows is giving you three attacks instead of two. For Hand of Harm, this saves you 1 FP at the cost of one of your Flurry of Healing and Harm uses per day. You can only use Hand of Harm once per turn, so you get no additional value. It’s absolutely not worth the cost. Unlike Hand of Harm, you can use Hand of Healing as often as you like. Using Hand of Healing three times during a Flurry of Blows triples your ability to output healing. Weirdly, this also means that, rather than spending an Action to use Hand of Healing outside of combat, it’s more efficient to use Flurry of Blows and punch yourself and your party until everyone feels better. You get three times as much healing per Focus Point by doing this.

hand-of-ultimate-mercy|function.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
hand-of-ultimate-mercy|function.summary: Have a dead party member? Take a Short Rest to get your Focus Points back if you need to, then punch them back to life. You only need 5 Focus Points to use this and you get 17 per Short or Long Rest at this level. If someone goes down you likely still have a bunch to spend. The fact that this only takes an Action is great. It’s similar to Revivify, but lacks an expensive cost. You could absolutely use this in combat, and, in many cases, that’s a good idea. This doesn’t have the specific text around how mortal wounds or missing limbs are handled, but I assume it works like Raise Dead in most respects. The target notably doesn’t need to be willing to return to life, either, which raises some interesting ethical questions. The one serious limitation on this is that you can only use it once per Long Rest. But, with a 24-hour window in which it will function after the target’s death, if you need to raise 2 people, you can raise one, take a Long Rest, raise the other, and then still have a ton of time to mess around before you get anywhere near the 24-hour timer. Of course, if you have 3 dead allies, you’ll want to go find a cleric.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

darkness|function.name: Darkness
darkness|function.summary: 1 FP to cast Darkness is a pittance, and the ability to see within the effect makes it a powerful tool both offensively and defensively. Consistent Advantage on all of your attacks and Disadvantage on your enemies’ attacks against you is a massive mathematical advantage. Keeping your enemies inside the area of Darkness will have a huge impact. They’ll struggle to attack your party, and many effects can only target creatures which the creature can see, making many spells and special abilities unusable. Either Grapple enemies or take Sentinel to prevent them from moving away from you. Shadow Arts allows you to move the effect at the beginning of your turn without spending an action of any kind, but you’ll rarely need to do that. You can cast Darkness on an object, then hold it in your hand and carry it with you. Covering the object blocks Darkness, so you can stow the object if you need to reveal yourself.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

darkvision|unknown.name: Darkvision
darkvision|unknown.summary: Always useful, especially if your Species doesn’t have Darkvision already.

shadow-figments|unknown.name: Shadow Figments
shadow-figments|unknown.summary: Minor Illusion is an absolutely fantastic spell.

shadow-step|darkness.name: Shadow Step
shadow-step|darkness.summary: Teleportation is great, and Advantage is great, but Monks get by on a large number of low-damage attacks, so Advantage on one attack isn’t particularly useful. Giving up your Bonus Action also means less attacks that round. Advantage on one attack helps make up for losing your Bonus Action attacks, but you probably have Advantage from fighting in Darkness, so you want to avoid using this in any situation where regular movement would suffice. You need to teleport from darkness to darkness, so Shadow Step may be a good reason to use Shadow Arts (Darkness) to move the location of your Darkness effect in order to give yourself a destination for teleportation.

improved-shadow-step|unknown.name: Improved Shadow Step
improved-shadow-step|unknown.summary: This makes Shadow Step much easier to use at the cost of a Focus Point. You can compare this to using Flurry of Blows and giving up two of the attacks to teleport.

cloak-of-shadows|darkness.name: Cloak of Shadows
cloak-of-shadows|darkness.summary: and Shadow Arts (Darkness) compete for space. Both take an Action to turn on a powerful combat mode, and, since their benefits overlap, you’re only going to use one at a time. Being invisible means Advantage on all of your attacks and Disadvantage on attacks against you, but notably isn’t bypassed by the ability to see in magical darkness. Cloak of Shadows also lets you use Flurry of Blows for free, allowing you to go all-in on offense. In a typical 3-round combat, you’ll spend 3 FP for Cloak of Shadows and pay for the cost by making 3 flurries. Despite its obvious benefits, Cloak of Shadows doesn’t totally supplant Darkness. Darkness can still be used to blind enemies, reducing their ability to attack your allies. If you go into combat with Darkness running, you might use Shadow Arts’ ability to move the effect to repeatedly drop it onto your enemies while you rely on Cloak of Shadows to attack.

elemental-attunement|function.name: Elemental Attunement
elemental-attunement|function.summary: With no action cost and a Focus Point cost of 1, Elemental Attunement is cheap enough to use in almost every encounter. : 10 feet of additional reach puts you well outside of other creatures’ reach. It’s not entirely clear if this affects your reach for Opportunity Attacks, but I think it’s intended to do so.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); }); : Changing damage types allows you to easily avoid damage resistances. The push/pull effects let you break grapples, move enemies into dangerous positions, and position them to be hit with AOE damage. The text also says “toward or away”, but omits the word “directy”, so it appears that you can use this to move enemies off the ground to get easy falling damage.

reach|function.name: Reach
reach|function.summary: 10 feet of additional reach puts you well outside of other creatures’ reach. It’s not entirely clear if this affects your reach for Opportunity Attacks, but I think it’s intended to do so.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });

elemental-strikes|unknown.name: Elemental Strikes
elemental-strikes|unknown.summary: Changing damage types allows you to easily avoid damage resistances. The push/pull effects let you break grapples, move enemies into dangerous positions, and position them to be hit with AOE damage. The text also says “toward or away”, but omits the word “directy”, so it appears that you can use this to move enemies off the ground to get easy falling damage.

manipulate-elements|unknown.name: Manipulate Elements
manipulate-elements|unknown.summary: Elementalism is fun to play with, but has essentially no mechanical effect.

elemental-burst|unknown.name: Elemental Burst
elemental-burst|unknown.summary: Fireball radius and you can change the damage type, but less damage and shorter range. You can use Flurry of Blows with Elemental Strikes to push/pull enemies into the area, allowing you to reliably hit large numbers of enemies.

stride-of-the-elements|unknown.name: Stride of the Elements
stride-of-the-elements|unknown.summary: Fly 15 feet above your enemies, punch them with your 15-foot reach, haul them into the air, drop them for 1d6 falling damage. Use Flurry of Blows to do this 5 times per turn.

damage-resistance|unknown.name: Damage Resistance
damage-resistance|unknown.summary: Easy, adaptable damage resistance. Changing damage types multiples times mid-combat is rarely useful, but non-spellcaster enemies can rarely deal multiple types of non-weapon damage.

destructive-stride|unknown.name: Destructive Stride
destructive-stride|unknown.summary: This turns Step of the Wind into a way to race past enemies for automatic damage. The damage per target is poor, unfortunately, so this only matters if there is a large number of enemies in a small enough area to hit a bunch of them. And if that’s the case, you should be using Elemental Burst in most cases.

empowered-strikes|unknown.name: Empowered Strikes
empowered-strikes|unknown.summary: An extra 1d12 damage once per turn.

addle|function.name: Addle
addle|function.summary: If you need to get out of melee, preventing the target from taking Reactions prevents them from making an Opportunity Attack, so you can usually choose to use Flurry of Blows instead of using Step of the Wind to Disengage.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(183); });

push|unknown.name: Push
push|unknown.summary: This pushes enemies “away”, rather than “directly away”. Upward at an angle is still “away”, allowing you to launch enemies into the air to cause falling damage and knock them prone. If your first attack in a turn is from Flurry of Blows, you can use this to knock enemies prone before spending the rest of the turn attacking them with Advantage. Provided that your target has a passable chance to fail the save, Push easily outdoes Addle and Topple. Pushing an enemy out of reach and knocking them prone with falling damage means that you won’t trigger an Opportunity Attack and that your target is prone, combining the benefits of Addle and Topple. Note that this feature intentionally ignore creature size, unlike most push effects.

topple|unknown.name: Topple
topple|unknown.summary: A great way to knock high-Strength foes prone. Those same foes can reliably pass the saves to resist Push or to resist you using an Unarmed Strike to knock them prone.

wholeness-of-body|unknown.name: Wholeness of Body
wholeness-of-body|unknown.summary: Basically a pool of additional Hit Point Dice. You should absolutely not use this in combat. The healing is too minor. If you’re feeling endangered, Dodge and prevent incoming damage rather than trying to repair it while still actively taking damage.

fleet-step|unknown.name: Fleet Step
fleet-step|unknown.summary: Effectively a free Dash every turn, massively improving your mobility. Take advantage of this to forcibly reposition enemies with a combination of Open Hand Technique and grappling. Put all of your enemies into a nice, neat little ball, then high-five your party’s Blaster.

quivering-palm|unknown.name: Quivering Palm
quivering-palm|unknown.summary: 10d12 damage averages to 65. This costs 4 FP to create the vibrations, then another attack during an Attack action to trigger the damage. The target makes a Constitution save, and since Constitution saves are consistently high, we need to expect enemies to pass the save. So is this worth the Focus Points to use? For 4 FP, you can trigger Flurry of Blows twice and Stunning Blow twice. The 4 additional attacks compared to Martial Arts will deal 1d12+5 damage each. Assuming all four hit, that’s an average of 46 damage without considering the possibility of crits, falling damage from Open Hand Technique, etc. The two Stunning Fist uses might rob the target of two turns. It’s difficult to make a direct comparison between Quivering Palm and our other options. Quivering Palm can be a big damage nuke delivered very quickly, but I don’t trust Constitution saves enough to make that gamble frequently. Personally, I would rather use Stunning Fist and spend a turn punching the target while they’re unable to retaliate.

divine-sense|unknown.name: Divine Sense
divine-sense|unknown.summary: Only situationally useful, but it covers three creature types, and both Fiends and Undead are common enemies. The ability to locate nearby creatures of the affected types negates much of the benefits of stealth and invisibility, at minimum allowing you to attack the correct space. The 10-minute duration is easily enough to get through a combat encounter, but you can also use it to locate nearby enemies before you would have noticed each other by more mundane means, allowing you to engage those enemies on your own terms.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Never a bad choice, but less impactful for martial characters than for full casters.

child-of-the-sun|lfl.name: Child of the Sun
child-of-the-sun|lfl.summary: The aura that protects you and allies from Blindness will work very nicely alongside Aura of Protection. Faerie Fire is a great combat option which benefits your whole party, but your save DC may not be good enough for it to be consistently effective unless you’re building around Charisma.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: Very good, but you can’t afford the Wisdom to keep this effective.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Decent on any martial character that gets Extra Attack, but without a way to increase your chance to crit, you won’t benefit from the first half of the feat consistently. Once you pick up Aura of Protection, allies will really enjoy standing next to you, which makes it easy to capitalize on the Advantage mechanic.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: Druid spells to get Shillelagh for or Wizard spells to get options like Fire Bolt and Shield can both have a huge impact, especially for Blessed Warrior builds.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Proficiency in Persuasion, and give Heroic Inspiration to your whole party once per day. Excellent on any build if you don’t need a different Origin Feat.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Passable if you’re using weapons like greatswords or glaives, but otherwise skip it. Savage Attacker doesn’t apply to the damage from Divine Smite, unfortunately.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Hex is a more efficient use of a level 1 spell slot than Divine Smite, and the retaliatory damage can be great if you can maintain Concentration consistently. To maximize the effect, grab Armor of Agathys (either multiclass into Warlock or go Oath of Vengeance), use two-handed weapons, and take Resilient (Con) and/or War Caster. Once you have Aura of Protection, you’re set.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Great for covering all of the Face skills so that you can make room for other options, especially in a small party with poor skill coverage.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: The damage reduction is minor, but it will be impactful for a front-line character like the Paladin. Even so, you’re probably here for Sacred Flame as a Bonus Action. For a Charisma-based build, it could be a great way to use your Bonus Action on turns where you’re not using Divine Smite.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: There is very little to use this. Grab a weapon with the Push mastery.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Always helpful for front-line melee builds, but not essential, especially since you have Lay on Hands.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: Fantastic for any melee build with a reasonable change to use Opportunity Attacks. Add Sentinel and Zhentarim Tactics, and you’ll be able to make Opportunity Attacks almost every turn.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: Very similar to Magic Initiate if you could select Sorcerer, but you trade one Cantrip for a buff to Con saves and the THP/damage thing. To maximize the value of Aberrant Surge, you want to select a level 1 spell which you’ll cast frequently in combat, so pick a staple option like Absorb Elements or Shield which will remain equally effective for your whole career. The biggest problem for the Paladin is that you’ll spend most of your spell slots smiting things, which can make this less impactful.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: The skills and spells are decent, but not amazing. You get both See Invisibility and Arcane Eye, which are both great and not on your spell list, but that’s not enough to make this an easy choice.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: A few decent spells which aren’t on the Paladin’s spell list. Hunter’s Mark can be a very efficient use of a spell slot against big enemies where you won’t need to constantly retarget, but it’s definitely not as exciting as Divine Smite.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: A few decent spells, but not espeically useful for the Paladin. Find Familiar and Conjure Animals may be helpful.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: You already get everything except Healing Word.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: Some of the low-level spells are good and aren’t on the Paladin’s spell list, but nothing amazing.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: Access to Magic Weapon is extremely useful, but you may get little value from the other spells.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: You get some great spells like Misty Step, but you already get Find Steed, which is arguably the most appealing part of the feat.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: Comprehend Languages and Tongues aren’t on your spell list, and they’re very useful for a Face character.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Shield is great and Vigilant Guardian is excellent on the Paladin. Most of the spells are already on your spell list, though, so you won’t see much benefit there. If you just want Shield, Magic Initiate or Aberrant Dragonmark are better choice.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: An easy choice for Dexterity-based Paladins looking to be sneaky or otherwise tricky.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Mostly mediocre, but you do get a couple great spells including Feather Fall and Conjure Minor Elementals.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Many of the spells are already on your spell list, but you get some good options like Armor of Agathys and Glyph of Warding.

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: A decent choice for many martial characters. A climb speed is the next best thing to a fly speed. The ability to stand up quickly makes falling or being knocked prone less of a problem. The ability to jump with less of a running start may let you easily jump over difficult terrain and other obstacles which otherwise might slow your movement in combat.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: The push effect is decent, especially when combined with a Push mastery, but without other stacking sources of push distance you’ll have trouble getting past the 30-foot threshold where most creatures won’t have enough speed to immediately run back into melee.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: Normally great for front-line martial characters, but the Paladin already has a deep well of hit points thanks to Lay on Hands.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Grab Fighting Style (Blind Fighting), and suddenly you’re the only one who can see inside your Fog Cloud. Grab a whip and the Slasher fear, and you can impose a -20 ft. speed penalty in one attack. Stacked with the speed penalty from Cloying Mists, that will nearly immobilize most enemies. It’s an incredibly easy build for the Eldritch Knight, and very few enemies can do anything about it. Of course, your allies also won’t be able to see, so it may be impolite to bring this to the table regardless of how effective it is.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: A simple and easy way to control enemies’ positions in combat, especially when combined with the Push mastery.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: A consistent and effective way to boost your AC in melee if you’re using Finesse weapons like rapiers or short swords. However, giving up your Reaction prevents you from making an Opportunity Attack, and punishing enemies for moving away from you is an important part of being your party’s front line.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: This could work for a build that doesn’t use a shield, but it’s risky even with the Paladin’s deep pool of hit points and healing. Oath of Vengeance could pair this nicely with Armor of Agathys, but I can’t guarantee that it will work reliably.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Two-weapon fighting is already a difficult choice for the Paladin, and you can nearly never spare your Bonus Action to do more of it.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Most of the Paladin’s damage is radiant.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: A great way to support spellcaster allies.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells and access to some 1st-level spells from outside of your spell list. Misty Step is great on any spellcaster. The free castings are great, too, but without full spellcasting you may not be able to use the new spells enough to justify the feat.

grappler|phb.name: Grappler
grappler|phb.summary: Even if you do nothing else to make yourself good at unarmed strikes, this is a great way to hold enemies in place without heavily cutting into your damage output. You’ll want to use a one-handed weapon (Versatile weapons also work well here) to leave a hand free. If you use a weapon with the Topple mastery or if you make another unarmed strike, you can knock your target prone and keep them there, then drag them away from your allies.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Essential and reliable if you’re using two-handed melee weapons.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: A huge amount of damage reduction.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A huge amount of Temporary Hit Points.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Too situational for a feat that doesn’t give you a useful ability score increase.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational to justify unless you’re in a Underdark campaign or a campaign where vampires feature heavily.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: The Standard Bearer feature is cool, but you have Aura of Protection to protect your allies from those effects.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Your mental saves are already great thanks to proficiency in Wisdom saves and Aura of Protection.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: Thanks to Find Steed, the Paladin is well suited to mounted combat.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: Too situational, and the ability scores don’t work for the Paladin.

order-s-resilience|frhof.name: Order’s Resilience
order-s-resilience|frhof.summary: This is only situationally useful. You have Aura of Protection, and Strength saves are rare.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Great if you want to focus exclusively on damage.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: Without another built-in way to consistently deal poison damage, there is too little benefit here to justify.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: Normally a great choice for a Defender, but since Pole Strike competes for your Bonus Action with Divine Smite, you’re giving up a lot of Polearm Master’s power.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: The Temporary Hit Ponts feature is a great support option, and Advantage on attacks while Bloodied is an easy way to get consistent Advantage. Use Lay on Hands to keep your hp just below half. Note that you can bypass the requirement for Purple Dragon Squire because you have proficiency in martial weapons.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: You never get Rituals above level 1, so there’s very little appeal here.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Fantastic on a Defender build. You can’t smite on an Opportunity Attack, but it’s still an additional attack.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Invisibility can be very useful, especially for Dexterity-based builds who want to be sneaky. The level 1 spell options aren’t as good as those available from Fey Touched, but Invisibility may be worth the difference.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Paladins are not built to use ranged weapons.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: A must have if you’re using a shield. Shield Bash is an easy way to get Advantage, and Interpose Shield coupled with Aura of Protection gives you a decent chance to negate area damage.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: Easy to fit into any build. Expertise in Persuasion can be very useful, and you can increase whatever ability score you want.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Simple and reliable. Combine this with a weapon with the Slow mastery and you can impose a -20 speed penalty, making it very difficult for enemies to escape you.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Even Charisma-based Paladin builds will find almost no value here.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: Turn your Hit Point Dice into additional damage on spells like Divine Smite, and ignore resistance to Radiant damage.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: Grappling isn’t a great tactic for the Paladin, but it’s a possibility.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: Potentially useful for Blessed Warrior builds since you’re unlikely to use Divine Smite often.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Without an easy way to make enemies Charmed, there’s almost no benefit here.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: The Paladin’s spell list is small, and this can get you some great new spells.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Advantage on Concentration is great, but Reactive Spell offers you very few options since the Paladin’s spells are rarely qualifying offensive options. Unfortunately, this won’t let you smite as a Reaction.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: An easy way to trigger Opportunity Attacks and Expertise in one skill.

archery|phb.name: Archery
archery|phb.summary: Paladins are largely locked into melee thanks to Divine Smite.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(193); });

blind-fighting|phb.name: Blind Fighting
blind-fighting|phb.summary: Fantastic, but only situationally useful. Unless you have party members that like to rely on magical darkness or fog or similar effects, you’ll get more consistent benefit from other options. If it’s an option, take the Skulker feat instead.

defense|phb.name: Defense
defense|phb.summary: Consistently useful, and doesn’t discourage you from switching weapons.

dueling|phb.name: Dueling
dueling|phb.summary: Consistently effecive, and you don’t need to give up use of a shield.

great-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Great Weapon Fighting
great-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: This raises the minimum damage for the Greatsword to 6, which feels nice but doesn’t improve your average damage roll very much. It has almost no impact on other weapons, which makes the appeal very narrow. Unfortunately, it does not affect the additional damage Divine Smite.

interception|phb.name: Interception
interception|phb.summary: Conceptually similar to Protection, but there’s some nuance in how the two styles protect your target. Protection imposes Disadvantage, so if there’s a good chance that the attack would miss, it’s the better choice. Interception reduces the damage and always works, but for big attacks it won’t negate the whole attack.

protection|phb.name: Protection
protection|phb.summary: Tempting for Defender builds, but allies need to remain adjacent to you for this to work. Being adjacent to the front line tank is generally a bad place to be unless you can do so safely without someone defending you. This also appeals to mounted combat builds because you can use it to compensate for your mount’s relative fragility, but if you’re going that route you really need the Mounted Combatant feat which lets you retarget attacks at yourself instead.

thrown-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Thrown Weapon Fighting
thrown-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: Paladins are largely locked into melee thanks to Divine Smite.

two-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
two-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: Much of the Paladin’s damage output comes from Divine Smite, and because Divine Smite can only work once per turn, two-weapon fighting isn’t a good option for the Paladin.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is great, especially since high level creatures frequently deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage. You can also change your weapon’s damage type to Radiant in the rare case your target is resistant to whatever weapon you’re using.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Fine, but occasonal Advantage and a minor damage boost won’t have a huge impact.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: You have some options to get Temporary Hit Points from spells, but you’re probably not concentrating on Heroism at this level.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Excellent for a front-line melee character like the Paladin.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Remember: the automatic max Radiant damage is only once per rest. If you’re going to use it, use it on a crit.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: More useful to support your allies’ save-or-suck spells than for anything that you’re doing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Without built-in shapechange options like Polymorph, this is much less useful.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: More hit points are great, but by this level you have so many points from Lay on Hands that 40 more hp feels tiny. You can use the bonus healing with Lay on Hands, allowing you to spend a Bonus Action to as little as 1 hit point, then also heal your Constitution modifier. If your Bonus Action somehow hasn’t been used on a turn, it’s a cheap way to recover hit points/.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: Helpful, but Paladins don’t make enough attacks to make the damage boost meaningful, and you can get past damage resistances using Divine Smite’s Radiant damage.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Increasing your reach with melee attacks makes it easy to hit enemies from outside of their reach. Dodge as a Bonus Action is useful on turns where you don’t smite.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Without a built-in way to deal a lo

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance will guarantee at least one round of dancing, which is useful, but without the ability to recast the spell you’re not getting as much value as a full caster.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: You could use this for a utility of some kind, but there aren’t many utility spells which you’ll want every Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list (neither care about your stats).

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: A huge boost in mobility for Dexterity-based builds.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: Potentially useful, but remember that it only has a 25% chance to work.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: You’re already immune to Frightened, but the abilty to use Wrathful Smite and force enemies to flee is pretty great.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Resistance/immunity to two damage types is nice. The Disadvantage mechanic won’t matter often, but it applies to Destructive Wave and Thunderous Smite.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Tempting on Dexterity-based builds, but you’re probably your party’s Defender, so remember that there’s value in being a big, shiny target.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Probably your only option for handling invisible enemies. If you’ve made it this far, your party is covering for you or you’ve found a creative solution.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Tempting for Blessed Warrior builds, but lacking a Constitution increase is hard.

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: Decent for Dexterity-based builds, especially if you’re in a small party and need more skills.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: You can get increases to Strength and Dexterity, and you get one Charisma-based skill, but Crafter isn’t a great feat. Altogether it meets the absolute bare minimum of functional.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Good ability scores for Dexterity-based or Charisma-based builds, great feat, fantastic skills

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Perfect ability scores for a Dexterity-based build or a Blessed Warrior build, and an easy way to cover all of the Face skills that you need while leaving space for other skill proficiencies.

chondathan-freebooter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freebooter
chondathan-freebooter|frhof.summary: One good ability score and good skills for a Dexterity-based build, but Charlatan is a much easier choice.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: A good choice for Dexterity-based builds, especially if there isn’t a Rogue in the party.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, but Healer does almost nothing for the Paladin.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, and Dragonscarred will let you increase Constitution or Charisma, so it’s workable. Unfortunately, Cult of the Dragon Initiate’s fear effect is Wisdom-based, so it doesn’t all line up perfectly.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: The ability scores are good and the Musician feat is welcome in any party, but it’s hard to waste two skill proficiencies on borderline useless skills.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: A good option for front-line martials. The ability scores are great, and Tough is an easy go-to feat if you don’t want more complexity, but you won’t get much use out of the skills.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: Perfect ability scores, good feat, good skills. An easy default choice.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for Dexterity-based builds and good skills. Magic Initiate could offer some great options. You could try a Charisma-based build based on True Strike, but missing Extra Attack will hurt your damage output considerably.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: One good ability score, one good skill, and Alert.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: Passable for a Dexterity-based build, but not a great option for Charisma-based Shillelagh builds because you don’t get a Charisma increase.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, but the feat is awful.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Okay for a Blessed Warrior build, but the skills are middling, and Healer isn’t appealing when you have Lay on Hands.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, one good feat, and Lucky. An easy go-to choice. For Strength-based builds, this is your best option to get Lucky.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and Alert, but the skills are terrible.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: This works for a Charisma-based build, but the ability scores don’t line up well with the skill and tool proficiencies.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, a good feat for martial characters like the Paladin, and good skills for a Face.

lorwyn-expert|lfl.name: Lorwyn Expert
lorwyn-expert|lfl.summary: Good ability scores, decent feat, awful skills. If you want Faerie Fire, consider Magic Initiate instead.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: Good ability scores for Blessed Warrior builds, Lucky is an easy feat choice on any character, and one good skill.

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: Great for a Charisma-based Blessed Warrior Build. You can complement your Cleric Cantrips with Druid Cantrips. Unfortunately, one skill is Intelligence-based, and the other is Performance, so you’re not getting much value from either.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and you can get all of the Face skills that you need. The only wasted bit is History.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, good feat, one mediocre skill.

rashemi-wanderer|frhof.name: Rashemi Wanderer
rashemi-wanderer|frhof.summary: Perfect ability scores, an easy go-to feat, and good skills. This is an easy go-to option if you don’t need a different Origin Feat.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: No Charisma increase, so this doesn’t even work for Blessed Warrior.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores, but that’s really all that you get. Tavern Brawler isn’t a great choice, but the ability to push an enemy 5 feet while also dealing damage with an Unarmed Strike may be useful if you’re not using weapons with the Push mastery.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: Passable for a Dexterity-based build, especially in a small party that needs more skill coverage.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for Dexterity-based or Charisma-based builds, and the skill and tool proficiencies are good if you have decent Dexterity. Savage Attacker is fine.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: Good for Charisma-based builds, especially with a Warlock dip for Pact of the Blade and Armor of Agathys.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: Good ability scores, Savage Attacker is decent since you’ll never have more than 2 attacks, and one Face skill.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and feat for a Charisma-based build, but the skills are a bad fit.

vampire-devotee|aboh.name: Vampire Devotee
vampire-devotee|aboh.summary: Perfect ability scores, and Vampire’s Plaything lets you Dash or Disengage as a Bonus Action a few times per day. Strength-based builds will only benefit from one of the skills, and Dexterity-based builds don’t get a Dexterity increase, so Charisma-based builds are the best fit here, but you can still do okay with a Strength-based build.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, but the skills are a bad fit, and the feat is bad.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, and between the skills and Thieves’ Tools you could fill in for a Rogue in your party. Lucky is an easy feat on any character.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, good skills, excellent feat, and it sets you up for an easy and effective melee build based on Strength or Charisma.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: Perfect ability scores, a great feat, and one good skill.

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Workable ability scores, and access to Magic Weapon, which isn’t on the Paladin’s spell list. The skills aren’t great unless you’re building around Dexterity.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: Not awful, but the skills are both Wisdom-based and there’s no Chairsma increase, which is hard for the Paladin compared to similar options.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores work for a Dexterity-based build, but the feat isn’t great.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: Nothing here is good enough to justify taking this background. Take anything that gets you Magic Initiate (Cleric) instead.

house-kundarak-heir|efota.name: House Kundarak Heir
house-kundarak-heir|efota.summary: Very close to being good. The ability scores are mostly a good fit, but the whole background depends too much on Intelligence, which is a dump stat for the Paladin.

house-lyrandar-heir|efota.name: House Lyrandar Heir
house-lyrandar-heir|efota.summary: Decent ability scores and a decent feat, but the skills are bad.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: Workable ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, but the skills are bad and the feat isn’t amazing.

house-sivis-heir|efota.name: House Sivis Heir
house-sivis-heir|efota.summary: Workable for a Charisma-based build, but the Skills are Intelligence and Wisdom-based, which is hard.

house-tharashk-heir|efota.name: House Tharashk Heir
house-tharashk-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills, and the feat isn’t enough to make up for it.

house-thuranni-heir|efota.name: House Thuranni Heir
house-thuranni-heir|efota.summary: Good for Dexterity-based or Charisma-based builds.

house-vadalis-heir|efota.name: House Vadalis Heir
house-vadalis-heir|efota.summary: You could make a Charisma-based build work with this, but there’s very little reason to do so.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. An absolutely iconic species/class pairing, though not much better for the Paladin than for any other martial class. Paladins can already heal, deal radiant damage, handle crowds, and eventually fly via Find Steed.

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: Nothing here contributes to your capabilities in combat, but it will make you an excellent Face.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: A damage resistance, likely to a common damage type like poison or fire, a decent way to handle crowds of small enemies, Darkvision, and flight once per day. Paladins have a few spell options for handling crowds, and can eventually fly via Find Steed, but those options don’t come online until high levels.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense may be your only way to locate invisible enemies. Altogether, a great package for a durable Paladin.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great, plus you can get access to some spells from outside of the Paladins’s spell list. For a Blessed Warrior build, the innate spellcasting is a nice complement. The High Elf’s access to a Wizard cantrip means that you might forgo offensive Cleric cantrips in favor of options like Guidance. Dexterity-based builds might enjoy Wood Elf for access to Pass Without Trace.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options. Gnomish Cunning and Aura of Protection make your mental saves incredibly strong.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage offers numerous excellent options. I like Cloud’s Jaunt, Hill’s Topple, and Stone’s Endurance. Large Form is great for melee builds looking to occupy more space on the battlefield.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Lucky is nice, but that’s basically all that the Halfling has to offer for the Palaidn. Brave becomes obsolete at level 10 when you get Aura of Courage. Halfling Nimbeless is neat, but rarely impactful since you can already move through allies’ spaces and if you need to get past an enemy it should involve hurting them. Naturally Stealthy isn’t helpful for the front-line martial characters.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Very similar to the Gnome, but you give up some good things to get resistance to Psychic damage. Gnome is nearly always a better choice.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Roughly comparable to a human with Magic Initiate, but you trade most of the spellcasting for Darkvision and the ability to change the Cantrip. Still a great option for many builds. If you’re doing a Charisma-based build that relies on Shillelagh, this is an easy go-to choice.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is great for front-line melee builds, letting you move into melee quickly and padding your hit points for when you inevitably draw a lot of attacks. Relentless Endurance provides some insurance in case things go wrong, and you can heal yourself as a Bonus Action with Lay on Hands on your next turn to keep from immediately dying.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Darkvision, proficiency in Intimidation, and a good combat buff from Shifting. Beasthide and Longtooth are both great for most Paladins. Since you’re probably not using your Bonus Action every turn, it’s easy to fit Shifting into the Paladin’s normal tactics.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting. Possibly a good choice for Blessed Warrior builds, but otherwise you won’t use the spellcasting reliably.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and spellcasting that you won’t use.

athletics|str.name: Athletics
athletics|str.summary: (Str): The only Strength-based skill, and it’s borderline useless. The one appealing use is binding creatures in chains, which is appealing for Strength-based builds since chains/manacles/rope are so incredibly overpowered in the 2024 rules.

insight|wis.name: Insight
insight|wis.summary: (Wis): Helpful for a Face, but you may not have enough Wisdom to back it up.

medicine|wis.name: Medicine
medicine|wis.summary: (Wis): This skill is useless. Medicine is best done magically.

religion|int.name: Religion
religion|int.summary: (Int): One of the most important knowledge skills, but you probably dumped Intelligence.

battleaxe|unknown.name: Battleaxe
battleaxe|unknown.summary: This is just a trident that you can’t throw.

club-quarterstaff|druid.name: Club / Quarterstaff
club-quarterstaff|druid.summary: If you take Magic Initiate (Druid) and make the spellcasting Charisma-based, you can use Shillelagh to turn a club or quarterstaff into an effective weapon for a Charisma-based build.

flail|unknown.name: Flail
flail|unknown.summary: The only one-handed bludgeoning weapon with Sap. Longsword is typically a better choice unless you specifically want to take Crusher and still use the Sap mastery.

glaive|unknown.name: Glaive
glaive|unknown.summary: Reach and Graze. A safe option if you only care about damage output and you want something mechanically simple.

greataxe|unknown.name: Greataxe
greataxe|unknown.summary: Cleave and a giant damage die. A big single damage die isn’t an advantage over other weapons.

halberd|unknown.name: Halberd
halberd|unknown.summary: Trade some of the greataxe’s damage for Reach. Reach makes it much easier to make the bonus Cleave attack since you can reach enemies behind your initial target.

lance|unknown.name: Lance
lance|unknown.summary: Reach and Topple. You can also use this one-handed while mounted, which gets much easier when you can cast Find Steed.

longsword|unknown.name: Longsword
longsword|unknown.summary: An easy go-to option. Sap is fantastic, especially at low levels when enemies have few attacks.

maul|unknown.name: Maul
maul|unknown.summary: Fantastic for aggressive two-handed weapon builds. Use Topple to knock your target prone, then maul them with Advantage.

pike|unknown.name: Pike
pike|unknown.summary: Reach and Push. For when you really, really don’t want anyone to come near you. Be sure to grab Polearm Master so that you can attack when enemies move into your reach and push them away from you.

rapier|unknown.name: Rapier
rapier|unknown.summary: The go-to option for Dexterity-based builds, but also great for Strength-based sword-and-bord builds. The Vex mastery gives you Advantage on your next attack against the same target, allowing you to reliably hit your target repeatedly.

trident|unknown.name: Trident
trident|unknown.summary: Absolutely essential as a thrown weapon for Strength-based builds. With the Topple mastery you can throw these to knock flying enemies prone, which causes them to fall.

warhammer|unknown.name: Warhammer
warhammer|unknown.summary: The same damage as the longsword, but with the Push mastery. Combining this with Crusher gives you a lot of power to forcibly reposition your enemies, but you don’t need that much forced movement unless your party is build to capitalize on forced movement with things like Spike Growth or area control spells.

whip|unknown.name: Whip
whip|unknown.summary: Reach, Slow mastery, and one-handed. Grab the Slasher feat and you can apply a 20-foot speed penalty, then walk safely out of your target’s reach.

studded-leather|unknown.name: Studded Leather
studded-leather|unknown.summary: Dexterity-based builds should grab studded leather as soon as they hit 18 Dexterity.

chain-mail|unknown.name: Chain Mail
chain-mail|unknown.summary: Starting armor if you didn’t choose gold. Works fine until you can afford Full Plate.

full-plate|unknown.name: Full Plate
full-plate|unknown.summary: The obvious end goal for heavy armor users.

shield|unknown.name: Shield
shield|unknown.summary: +2 AC is huge in this game.

barbarian|function.name: Barbarian
barbarian|function.summary: As much as I would love to put Reckless Attack on a Paladin, the Barbarian’s class features often don’t function in heavy armor and going for light or medium armor means that your Paladin suddenly needs four high ability scores, which is simply unattainable in DnD 5e.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(196); });

bard|unknown.name: Bard
bard|unknown.summary: As much as the Bard and the Paladin’s ability scores overlap, the Bard offers very little to the Paladin without taking 3 or more Bard levels, and I don’t recommend doing that until you’ve at least picked up Aura of Protection at level 6.

fighter|unknown.name: Fighter
fighter|unknown.summary: More Weapon Mastery slots and an additional Fighting Style. I’m not sure that that’s worth a level. If you do go this route, consider starting with a level of Fighter to get proficiency in Constitution saving throws.

ranger|unknown.name: Ranger
ranger|unknown.summary: Similar to the Fighter, you can get more Weapon Mastery Slots and an additional Fighting Style, but you also don’t slow your spell slot progression. Two levels gets you Expertise, which might be helpful for important Face skills.

rogue|unknown.name: Rogue
rogue|unknown.summary: One level for Expertise is fine, but you won’t get much value beyond that. Cunning Action is great, but the Paladin depends on their Bonus Action for smiting.

sorcerer|unknown.name: Sorcerer
sorcerer|unknown.summary: If you want more spell slots to fuel your smites, Sorcerer is a good choice. It will advance your spellcasting twice as fast as Paladin levels, and a single level gets you more Charisma-based Cantrips than Blessed Warrior does, plus powerful level 1 spells like Shield. Two levels gets you Font of Magic, which can let you melt your higher-level spell slots into more numerous level 1 spell slots so that you can smite more frequently.

warlock|unknown.name: Warlock
warlock|unknown.summary: Pact Magic and Pact of the Blade are tempting, but there’s some nuance to consider. Pact Magic spell slots can be used for Divine Smite, and since they recharge on a Short Rest, they provide a more steady supply for Divine Smite than your normal spellcasting progression. But at the same time, putting those levels into Paladin or Sorcerer will get you more and higher-level spell slots, which is more impactful unless you’re also benefiting from other Warlock features. Pact of the Blade lets you use Charisma for attack and damage with your pact weapon, but feats which make you better with weapons grant increases to Strength or Dexterity. Focusing on Charisma reduces the Paladin’s MAD issues, but at the cost of making your best feat options unappealing.

oath-of-devotion-spells|especially-since.name: Oath of Devotion Spells
oath-of-devotion-spells|especially-since.source:
especially since you have Lay
				on Hands, which Beacon of Hope doesn’t affect
oath-of-devotion-spells|especially-since.summary: A few gems, but much of the list is only situationally useful. : Two excellent defensive buffs which will be useful throughout your career. : Aid is a nice buff, but Zone of Truth is only situationally useful. : I would almost almost never use Beacon of Hope in combat (especially since you have Lay on Hands, which Beacon of Hope doesn’t affect) unless you need the Advantage portion of the spell. Paladins don’t have enough spell slots to spend them on Dispel Magic unless your party is truly desperate. : Freedom of Movement is situational but very powerful. Guardian of Faith is passable area control, but it’s a spell that you cast for the 8-hour duration, not for the pitiful amount of damage. : Commune is a very powerful divination if you’re clever enough to ask useful questions. Flame Strike gives Paladins a much-needed option for handling crowds of weak enemies, especially those which aren’t affected by Turn Whatever. However, at this level Flame Strike’s damage will be underwhelming and unless you’re built around Blessed Warrior your spell save DC will probably be too low to make Flame Strike Reliable.

level-1-spells|unknown.name: Level 1 Spells
level-1-spells|unknown.summary: Bane is unreliable and rarely worth the spell slot, especially with your Charisma lagging behind full spellcasters. Hunter’s Mark is a nice damage boost against a single high-priority target, but its usefulness is limited by the Paladin’s low number of attacks per round. It can still yield considerably more damage than spending the same spell slot on Divine Smite, but only if you can maintain Concentration.

level-2-spells|unknown.name: Level 2 Spells
level-2-spells|unknown.summary: Paralysis is an off-switch for an enemy, but since your spell DC is low compared to a full spellcaster, Hold Person is unreliable. Misty Step is a great way to get around the battlefield, especially since it’s a Bonus Action to cast.

level-3-spells|especially-since-you-have.name: Level 3 Spells
level-3-spells|especially-since-you-have.source:
especially since you have Lay
				on Hands, which Beacon of Hope doesn’t affect
level-3-spells|especially-since-you-have.summary: I would almost almost never use Beacon of Hope in combat (especially since you have Lay on Hands, which Beacon of Hope doesn’t affect) unless you need the Advantage portion of the spell. Paladins don’t have enough spell slots to spend them on Dispel Magic unless your party is truly desperate.

level-4-spells|unknown.name: Level 4 Spells
level-4-spells|unknown.summary: Both situational options, and the appeal of Dimension Door is reduced because you already have Misty Step, and you don’t have the Spell Save DC to make Banishment reliable offensively.

level-5-spells|unknown.name: Level 5 Spells
level-5-spells|unknown.summary: Hold Monster makes Hold Person redundant, but your Spell Save DC may still be behind full spellcasters even at this high level. Scrying is very situational, and your full caster allies have had it for a very long time by this level.

sacred-weapon|6-8-encounters-2-short-res.name: Sacred Weapon
sacred-weapon|6-8-encounters-2-short-res.summary: Adding your Charisma as an additional attack bonus on top of Strength or Dexterity means that your attacks are exceptionally accurate. Changing your weapon damage to Radiant allows you to easily bypass damage resistances. With two uses of Channel Divinity per Short or Long Rest and a 10-minute duration for Sacred Weapon, you can afford to use Sacred Weapon in nearly every encounter. If your party typically follows the Adventuring Day advice in the Dungeon Master’s Guide (6-8 encounters, 2 Short Rests), you may need to fit multiple encounters into the 10-minute duration until you get 3 uses of Channel Divinity at level 11. The additional attack bonus offsets leaving your Strength/Dexterity low in order to focus on your Charisma, allowing you to focus on Charisma first without relying on Blessed Warrior. This may be worthwhile to support Aura of Protection and to make your spellcasting more effective, but it does come at the cost of effectiveness offensively.

aura-of-devotion|unknown.name: Aura of Devotion
aura-of-devotion|unknown.summary: Situational by design, but Charm effects are common and frequently dangerous. Many effects will charm a target and apply other nasty effects while the targets is charmed. Aura of Devotion blocks those effects.

smite-of-protection|unknown.name: Smite of Protection
smite-of-protection|unknown.summary: +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saves for your whole party for one round. A nice buff, but it encourages you to smite every turn and burn through all of your spell slots in a hurry.

holy-nymbus|unknown.name: Holy Nymbus
holy-nymbus|unknown.summary: Activated as a Bonus Action and lasts 10 minutes. This is only usable once per day, but you can recharge it at the cost of 1 of your 2 level 5 spell slots. : Only Situationally useful since it affects so few creature types. : At this level your Proficiency Bonus is +6, and you might have 20 Charisma. 11 automatic damage is good, especially in a crowded fight. : Very rarely matters. Some creatures like drow and vampires are affected by sunlight, but they’re a vanishingly small portion of the creatures in the game.

holy-ward|unknown.name: Holy Ward
holy-ward|unknown.summary: Only Situationally useful since it affects so few creature types.

radiant-damage|unknown.name: Radiant Damage
radiant-damage|unknown.summary: At this level your Proficiency Bonus is +6, and you might have 20 Charisma. 11 automatic damage is good, especially in a crowded fight.

sunlight|unknown.name: Sunlight
sunlight|unknown.summary: Very rarely matters. Some creatures like drow and vampires are affected by sunlight, but they’re a vanishingly small portion of the creatures in the game.

inspiring-smite|unknown.name: Inspiring Smite
inspiring-smite|unknown.summary: A decent number of Temporary Hit Points. While you’ll usually hoard them for yourself, the ability to share them with allies offers a fantastic tactical option. Keep in mind that you need to use Divine Smite before you can activate this, so be sure to keep a spell slot ready so that you can smite something and trigger Inspiring Smite. The Temporary Hit Points don’t have a specified expiration, so they last until creatures take a Long Rest. If you’re able to maintain your own pad of THP, you can gradually build up THP on each of your allies throughout an adventuring day.

oath-of-glory-spells|unknown.name: Oath of Glory Spells
oath-of-glory-spells|unknown.summary: A good mix of combat buffs and non-combat utilities, as well as a handful of damage options. : Guiding Bolt is hard because paladins generally can’t invest enough in Charisma to be good at spell attacks. You likely won’t cast it often, but it is still a decent ranged attack spell if you’re out of melee range. Heroism is a great defensive option. At the early levels where the fear immunity is helpful, your Charisma will be too low for good temp HP, and the high levels where the temp HP isn’t relevant, you’re immune to fear. : Enhance Ability is just an all-around great spell outside of combat, though your most likely use case in combat is for Strength, and you can use Peerless Athlete for that, so save Enhance Ability for outside of combat when you need things like Advantage on Charisma checks in social situations. Magic Weapon is great if you don’t have a permanent magic weapon, but it requires Concentration so generally you’ll want to cast something else unless you absolutely need this. : Two fantastic buffs, but both require Concentration. : We’re unlikely to have the Charisma to make Compulsion reliable, and the effect is not that useful. Compelling targets to run away in a direction and using our Concentration just makes fights take longer than they need to. Freedom of Movement is great, but only situationally useful. Fortunately, it doesn’t require Concentration, and you can share it with your steed. : Legend Lore is a great way to get plot information, but you won’t use it consistently. Yolande’s Regal Presence is very similar to Spirit Guardians, but trades much of the damage to knock creatures prone. Use it to attack prone enemies.

level-3-spells|unknown.name: Level 3 Spells
level-3-spells|unknown.summary: Haste and Protection From Energy are two of the most important buffs in the game.

peerless-athlete|unknown.name: Peerless Athlete
peerless-athlete|unknown.summary: Extremely situational. Athletics and Acrobatics are borderline useless. You might get some use out of longer jump distances if you’re able to jump over difficult terrain.

aura-of-alacrity|unknown.name: Aura of Alacrity
aura-of-alacrity|unknown.summary: A nice improvement to your party’s mobility.

glorious-defense|unknown.name: Glorious Defense
glorious-defense|unknown.summary: This is a fantastic defensive ability, combining the AC bonus of the spell Shield with a free counterattack. Be sure to grab a throwable weapon or a weapon with Reach to enjoy the effect to its fullest.

living-legend|unless-you-re-using-two-we.name: Living Legend
living-legend|unless-you-re-using-two-we.summary: Two fantastic combat buffs, plus Advantage on Charisma checks for some reason. Activated as a Bonus Action and lasts 10 minutes. This is only usable once per day, but you can recharge it at the cost of 1 of your 2 level 5 spell slots. : Don’t be tempted to use this for Charisma checks in social situations. You can cast Enhance Ability for that. : With Aura of Protection you have a decent chance to pass any save.
