Adding a reroll every round is fantastic. : Paladins only get two attacks (unless you’re using two-weapon fighting), so this makes it very likely that all of your attacks will hit.

charismatic|unknown.name: Charismatic
charismatic|unknown.summary: Don’t be tempted to use this for Charisma checks in social situations. You can cast Enhance Ability for that.

saving-throw-reroll|unknown.name: Saving Throw Reroll
saving-throw-reroll|unknown.summary: With Aura of Protection you have a decent chance to pass any save. Adding a reroll every round is fantastic.

unerring-strike|unless-you-re-using-two-.name: Unerring Strike
unerring-strike|unless-you-re-using-two-.summary: Paladins only get two attacks (unless you’re using two-weapon fighting), so this makes it very likely that all of your attacks will hit.

oath-of-noble-genies-spells|function.name: Oath of Noble Genies Spells

Conjure Minor Elementals is very efficient damage, though you may get more value out of Summon Elemental since the 1-hour duration is more likely to last through multiple encounters, and you don’t have a built-in way to make a huge number of attacks which would make Conjure Minor Elementals the massive problem that it is for many spellcasters. : Banishing Smite is normally a decent way to remove a weakened enemy from a fight, but you have Dao’s Crush to handle important single enemies. Do not cast Contact Other Plane unless you’re about to take a Long Rest.

level-1-spells|function.name: Level 1 Spells
level-1-spells|function.summary: Thunderous Smite is the only spell in the batch that you’re likely to use.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

elemental-smite|or-have-an-ally-do-it.name: Elemental Smite
elemental-smite|or-have-an-ally-do-it.source: or have an ally do it
elemental-smite|or-have-an-ally-do-it.summary: This is absurdly good. Adding a rider effect to Divine Smite makes it dramatically more impactful, and several of the effects are excellent. : This is insanely powerful. Perfect when you need to eliminate a single high-priority target. The target doesn’t get a save to become Grappled and Restrained, and instead must spend their Action to attempt an ability check to end the condition. Even if your target does so, they’ve spent an Action to undo something which you can immediately apply again on your next turn. Even creatures with Legendary Resistance can’t do anything about this. This effect is so much better than the other options that I dropped their ratings because this is so much more powerful that I can’t justify giving them the same rating. You can further abuse this by binding your target in chains/manacles/rope on your next turn (or have an ally do it). Then. even if they end the grapple, they’re still Restrained. Enemies that rely primarily on attacks are immediately trivialized. The rules around the grapple mechanics here are extremely unclear. The Grappling rules state that a grapple ends “if the distance between the Grappled target and the grappler exceeds the grapple’s range.” What is the grapple’s range here? Because you can use Divine Smite if you throw a melee weapon. Does that mean that the grapple stays in place until the target exceeds the maximum throw range of the weapon that you use for the smite? If you use a weapon without the Thrown property, do you use the weapon’s reach, or do you use the maximum thrown range if you use that weapon as an improvised thrown weapon? Even if this only worked on targets within 5 feet and it ended if you moved more than 5 feet away from your target, this would still be insanely powerful.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); }); : A great way to move from one target to another or to escape a dangerous position. The temporary damage resistance is great if you need to dive into a crowd of enemies or if you’re low on hit points. : A little bit of extra damage. It’s decent at level 3, but it doesn’t scale at all, so it’ll feel pointless after a few levels. : Excellent crown control. This can break grapples, force your enemies and your allies away from each other, and then knock enemies prone so that you and your allies get Advantage on melee attacks against them. If you have alies who will act before your next enemy, it may be helpful to push your allies away even though you knock them prone in some cases. Note that you get Thunderous Smite as a subclass spell. If you’re using this to affect one creature, use Thunderous Smite instead and save yourself a use of Channel Divinity.

djinni-s-escape|unknown.name: Djinni’s Escape
djinni-s-escape|unknown.summary: A great way to move from one target to another or to escape a dangerous position. The temporary damage resistance is great if you need to dive into a crowd of enemies or if you’re low on hit points.

efreeti-s-fury|unknown.name: Efreeti’s Fury
efreeti-s-fury|unknown.summary: A little bit of extra damage. It’s decent at level 3, but it doesn’t scale at all, so it’ll feel pointless after a few levels.

marid-s-surge|unknown.name: Marid’s Surge
marid-s-surge|unknown.summary: Excellent crown control. This can break grapples, force your enemies and your allies away from each other, and then knock enemies prone so that you and your allies get Advantage on melee attacks against them. If you have alies who will act before your next enemy, it may be helpful to push your allies away even though you knock them prone in some cases. Note that you get Thunderous Smite as a subclass spell. If you’re using this to affect one creature, use Thunderous Smite instead and save yourself a use of Channel Divinity.

genie-s-splendor|unlike-the-monk.name: Genie’s Splendor
genie-s-splendor|unlike-the-monk.summary: 10 + Dex + Cha AC while unarmored. This is likely the best version of Unarmored Defense in the game since it works with a shield (unlike the Monk) and uses two ability scores that you can build your character around (unlike the Barbarian). You also get another skill proficiency, which is nice.

aura-of-elemental-shielding|unknown.name: Aura of Elemental Shielding
aura-of-elemental-shielding|unknown.summary: Damage resistance which you can change every round and share with nearby allies. Between this and the save bonus from Aura of Protection, you can your allies are very well protected against area elemental damage.

elemental-rebuke|unknown.name: Elemental Rebuke
elemental-rebuke|unknown.summary: Great for when you’re crit or otherwise take a big hit from a single attack. Even without the retaliatory damage this would be pretty great.

noble-scion|unknown.name: Noble Scion
noble-scion|unknown.summary: Primarily defensive, but still very powerful. : Fast Flight with Hover. Always amazing. : Absolutely fantastic. You likely want to reserve this for saving throws, but the ability to guarantee success on one save each round is a massive defensive benefit for your whole party.

flight|unknown.name: Flight
flight|unknown.summary: For most Paladins, this will double your speed. With a 10-minute duration, you have enough time and mobility to chase enemies.

minor-wish|unknown.name: Minor Wish
minor-wish|unknown.summary: Absolutely fantastic. You likely want to reserve this for saving throws, but the ability to guarantee success on one save each round is a massive defensive benefit for your whole party.

nature-s-wrath|unknown.name: Nature’s Wrath
nature-s-wrath|unknown.summary: An AOE restrain effect that you can use multiple times per Short or Long Rest. This is absolutely fantastic at any level. Unfortunately, many creatures have high Strength save, but that’s not universal.

oath-of-the-ancients-spells|not-a-save.name: Oath of the Ancients Spells
oath-of-the-ancients-spells|not-a-save.summary: About half of the options on the list are bad, but you generally get one viable option from each pair of spells. : Speak With Animals is only useful as your DM decides it will be. Ensnaring Strike is a great option for a bunch of reasons, and works very similarly to a smite. Use it to ensnare a target, then let them bleed out a bit while you’re off dealing with more pressing issues. Note that after the initial save it’s a Strength Check (not a Save), so even creatures proficient in Strength Saves will have trouble escaping. Even better, the damage scales linearly with spell level, so it remains an excellent go-to use for a spell slot for your whole career. : Moonbeam is difficult to use unless you can restrain a creature inside its effect long enough to justify the spell slot (Grapple them, for instance), and, even then, it’s better left to full spellcasters. Misty Step is a fantastic option and solves a lot of mobility issues, including pits, chasms, difficult terrain, walls of fire, and other nasty materials, enemies, etc. Misty Step to the BBEG and wave your sword in their face. : Plant Growth is weirdly effective area control, and Protection From Energy is a fantastic and very important defensive option. : Ice Storm is a frustrating combination of not enough damage and too little area control. Stone Skin is an extremely good buff, but the 100gp component cost can add up quickly so you don’t want to cast it constantly. : Commune With Nature is a useful divination, especially in unfamiliar areas, but Tree Stride is extremely situational and totally useless if you’re not in a forest or jungle.

level-1-spells|not-a-save.name: Level 1 Spells
level-1-spells|not-a-save.summary: Speak With Animals is only useful as your DM decides it will be. Ensnaring Strike is a great option for a bunch of reasons, and works very similarly to a smite. Use it to ensnare a target, then let them bleed out a bit while you’re off dealing with more pressing issues. Note that after the initial save it’s a Strength Check (not a Save), so even creatures proficient in Strength Saves will have trouble escaping. Even better, the damage scales linearly with spell level, so it remains an excellent go-to use for a spell slot for your whole career.

level-2-spells|grapple-them-for-instance.name: Level 2 Spells
level-2-spells|grapple-them-for-instance.summary: Moonbeam is difficult to use unless you can restrain a creature inside its effect long enough to justify the spell slot (Grapple them, for instance), and, even then, it’s better left to full spellcasters. Misty Step is a fantastic option and solves a lot of mobility issues, including pits, chasms, difficult terrain, walls of fire, and other nasty materials, enemies, etc. Misty Step to the BBEG and wave your sword in their face.

aura-of-warding|unknown.name: Aura of Warding
aura-of-warding|unknown.summary: These damage types are rare, but they’re also frequently used to bypass damage resistances to common damage types, and resistance to them is rare. Sharing resistance with your whole party can be great protection against enemies like Aberrations, Celestials, and Undead.

undying-sentinel|unknown.name: Undying Sentinel
undying-sentinel|unknown.summary: Good insurance in case things go badly. If you hit this, use Lay on Hands to heal yourself as much as you can manage.

elder-champion|unknown.name: Elder Champion
elder-champion|unknown.summary: Activated as a Bonus Action and lasts just 1 minute. This is only usable once per day, but you can recharge it at the cost of 1 of your 2 level 5 spell slots. : Paladins don’t have a ton of offensive spellcasting, but you might bring some to capitalize on this. This also works with Channel Divinity, so Abjure Enemies and Wrath of Nature will both benefit. : You already have a ton of durability. Healing 10 hp isn’t much, but it does feel good. In a typical 3-round combat, you can expect most of this healing to apply after the fight ends. : Fantastically powerful even with the Paladin’s limited spellcasting. Combined with the Diminish Defiance feature, your spells are very effective.

diminish-defiance|unknown.name: Diminish Defiance
diminish-defiance|unknown.summary: Paladins don’t have a ton of offensive spellcasting, but you might bring some to capitalize on this. This also works with Channel Divinity, so Abjure Enemies and Wrath of Nature will both benefit.

regeneration|unknown.name: Regeneration
regeneration|unknown.summary: You already have a ton of durability. Healing 10 hp isn’t much, but it does feel good. In a typical 3-round combat, you can expect most of this healing to apply after the fight ends.

swift-spells|unknown.name: Swift Spells
swift-spells|unknown.summary: Fantastically powerful even with the Paladin’s limited spellcasting. Combined with the Diminish Defiance feature, your spells are very effective.

oath-of-vengeance-spells|unknown.name: Oath of Vengeance Spells
oath-of-vengeance-spells|unknown.summary: Most of the spells are good on their own, but depend on a high Spell Save DC that you almost certainly don’t have. But there are a few good buffs and Misty Step, so there are some gems here. : Bane is unreliable and rarely worth the spell slot, especially with your Charisma lagging behind full spellcasters. Hunter’s Mark is a nice damage boost against a single high-priority target, but its usefulness is limited by the Paladin’s low number of attacks per round. It can still yield considerably more damage than spending the same spell slot on Divine Smite, but only if you can maintain Concentration. : Paralysis is an off-switch for an enemy, but since your spell DC is low compared to a full spellcaster, Hold Person is unreliable. Misty Step is a great way to get around the battlefield, especially since it’s a Bonus Action to cast. : Haste and Protection From Energy are two of the most important buffs in the game. : Both situational options, and the appeal of Dimension Door is reduced because you already have Misty Step, and you don’t have the Spell Save DC to make Banishment reliable offensively. : Hold Monster makes Hold Person redundant, but your Spell Save DC may still be behind full spellcasters even at this high level. Scrying is very situational, and your full caster allies have had it for a very long time by this level.

vow-of-enmity|unknown.name: Vow of Enmity
vow-of-enmity|unknown.summary: Easy Advantage, provided that you don’t need to switch targets. You’ll want to focus on eliminating one target at a time and quickly move through your enemies. With two uses of Channel Divinity per Short or Long Rest and a 1-minute duration for Vow of Enmity, you can afford to use Sacred Weapon in most encounters, but, depending on how your party paces an adventuring day, you may need to save it for more difficult encounters. Advantage is fairly easy to get in the 2024 DnD 5e rules, but options like Shove and Topple weapons typically require setup before you get Advantage. Vow of Enmity lets you get right to work, and you don’t need to worry about your target standing or anything else.

relentless-avenger|unknown.name: Relentless Avenger
relentless-avenger|unknown.summary: The best part of the Sentinel feat.

soul-of-vengeance|unknown.name: Soul of Vengeance
soul-of-vengeance|unknown.summary: A fantastic way to get an extra attack each round. You probably don’t even need a reach weapon to keep your target in reach because you’re hitting with Opportunity Attacks reliably thanks to Advantage, and then you’re holding them in place with Relentless Avenger. It’s basically an even better version of the Sentinel feat.

avenging-angel|unknown.name: Avenging Angel
avenging-angel|unknown.summary: Activated as a Bonus Action and lasts 10 minutes. This is only usable once per day, but you can recharge it at the cost of 1 of your 2 level 5 spell slots. : For most Paladins, this will double your speed. With a 10-minute duration, you have enough time and mobility to chase enemies. : Frightened is already a major debuff. Granting Advantage on attacks to hit the targets is just mean. The Frightened effects and early if the target takes damage, but Grapple and Shove notably don’t deal damage, so you have some great options to make enemies’ lives even worse before you resort to actually damaging them.

frightful-aura|unknown.name: Frightful Aura
frightful-aura|unknown.summary: Frightened is already a major debuff. Granting Advantage on attacks to hit the targets is just mean. The Frightened effects and early if the target takes damage, but Grapple and Shove notably don’t deal damage, so you have some great options to make enemies’ lives even worse before you resort to actually damaging them.

guidance|phb.name: Guidance
guidance|phb.summary: Really good, but you likely can’t make room for it since you only get two Cantrips.

resistance|phb.name: Resistance
resistance|phb.summary: The amount of damage prevented is small and doesn’t scale, so committing Concentration to this is hard to justify beyond very low levels. This could be useful against low-CR elementals which you’ll face at levels 1 and 2, but 1d4 damage per turn just isn’t enough beyond that.

sacred-flame|phb.name: Sacred Flame
sacred-flame|phb.summary: Not as much damage as Toll the Dead, and unless you plan to fight a lot of undead, and you’ll use both in the same situations, so you can only justify having one of the two. Pick the one with better damage.

spare-the-dying|unknown.name: Spare the Dying
spare-the-dying|unknown.summary: 1 point of Lay on Hands takes a Bonus Action and will get your target back into a fight.

thaumaturgy|phb.name: Thaumaturgy
thaumaturgy|phb.summary: Thematically fun, but not especially useful. See our Practical Guide to Prestidigitation and Similar Cantrips for more.

toll-the-dead|phb.name: Toll the Dead
toll-the-dead|phb.summary: 60 ft. range, the damage is measured in d12’s, and since it’s Necrotic damage, almost nothing will resist it.

word-of-radiance|xgte.name: Word of Radiance
word-of-radiance|xgte.summary: A great way to handle crowds of multiple enemies. Grab full plate and a shield and walk into a crowd of enemies. See our article on Melee Cantrips vs. Extra Attack for a breakdown of the math comparing melee cantrip spells to normal martial attacks.

bless|phb.name: Bless
bless|phb.summary: If you don’t have something else on which to use your Concentration, use Bless. +1d4 to attack rolls and saves is huge in 5e.

command|phb.name: Command
command|phb.summary: Useful, but only effective if you’re building around Charisma.

compelled-duel|phb.name: Compelled Duel
compelled-duel|phb.summary: Forcing a foe into single combat with you is extremely helpful. You are likely your party’s Defender, and while much of the time that only requires you to stand in the right place, sometimes you will need to actively force enemies to attack you instead of your allies.

cure-wounds|phb.name: Cure Wounds
cure-wounds|phb.summary: Use lay on hands. You don’t get enough spell slots to spend them on healing.

detect-evil-and-good|phb.name: Detect Evil and Good
detect-evil-and-good|phb.summary: Situationally useful, and you can use it to find invisible enemies or detect enemies through thin walls.

detect-magic|phb.name: Detect Magic
detect-magic|phb.summary: Someone in the party needs this, and ideally it should be someone with the ability to cast rituals.

detect-poison-and-disease|phb.name: Detect Poison and Disease
detect-poison-and-disease|phb.summary: Very situational, and unless you can also cast Protection From Poison there’s little you can do about it anyway. Fortunately, this can be cast as a ritual, but you can’t do that so leave it to someone who can.

divine-favor|phb.name: Divine Favor
divine-favor|phb.summary: 1d4 damage on hit, Bonus Action casting time, no Concnetration. While it’s certianly not as exciting as Divine Smite, four hits with this running deals as much damage as level 1 Divine Smite, and Divine Favor lasts for a full minute. If you’re expecting a long fight, if you’re using two weapons (or Polearm Master), or if you have Extra Attack, this is likely a more efficient use of a level 1 spell slot.

divine-smite|phb.name: Divine Smite
divine-smite|phb.summary: The damage is good and the scaling is good, but this doesn’t get you anything except damage. It’s a perfectly fine spell, and it’s a great baseline to measure other Paladin spells against.

heroism|phb.name: Heroism
heroism|phb.summary: A truly fantastic buff for a level 1 spell, but you’re going likely be the one who needs this most since Paladins are typically the party’s Defender, and Concentration will make the spell difficult to rely upon. Shield of Faith is better damage mitigation and has a Bonus Action casting time, so it’s nearly always a better choice.

protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.name: Protection from Evil and Good
protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.summary: A fantastic defensive buff, and even though it requires Concentration it will be reliable between Disadvantage on attacks against you and your high AC while stomping around in heavy armor.

purify-food-and-drink|phb.name: Purify Food and Drink
purify-food-and-drink|phb.summary: One of many reasons that Dungeons and Dragons makes a terrible wilderness survival game. Leave this for someone who can cast rituals if possible.

searing-smite|phb.name: Searing Smite
searing-smite|phb.summary: You are guaranteed 2d6 fire damage, and you get more if your target fails their save. You get 1d6 per spell level immediately, then another 1d6 per spell level at the start of each of the target’s turns for up to a minute. The scaling is also better than Divine Smite, adding a total of 2d6 per spell level compared to Divine Smite’s 1d8 per spell level. Of course, there are still problems here. Constitution saves are typically high, so enemies are unlikely to fail the save, so you can only count on the initial two instances of damage. Even if you’re building around Charisma, you can only count on that initial damage, and anything beyond the target’s next turn is a pleasant surprise. Fire resistance and immunity are common, so the damage type is also worse than Divine Smite. Finally, there is some value in Divine Smite immediately dealing damage compared to waiting for the target’s turn, especially if the damage reduces the target to 0.

shield-of-faith|phb.name: Shield of Faith
shield-of-faith|phb.summary: Not very exciting, and it takes Concentration, but a paladin with full plate, a shield, Defense fighting style, and Shield of Faith has an AC of 23, which will keep you very safe for a very long time.

thunderous-smite|phb.name: Thunderous Smite
thunderous-smite|phb.summary: You only lose 2 damage on average compared to Divine Smite, and pushing enemies away and knocking them Prone is easily worth the lost damage if your party is going to capitalize on the target being Prone before they can stand again. If you combine this with the Push Weapon Mastery, you can knock enemies a total of 10 feet away. A creature with 30 ft. speed would then spend half to stand, walk 15 feet, and still be 5 feet too far away from you, meaning that they may be unable to attack you that turn.

wardaway|frhof.name: Wardaway
wardaway|frhof.summary: A weaker version of Tasha’s Mind Whip, Wardaway makes some huge trades to fit into a level 1 spell. The damage is obviously much worse, but that’s not why you’re here. The target still gets to move and act in the same turn, but halving their speed is still impactful. The biggest limitation is that Wardaway uses a Constitution save instead of a much more reliable Intelligence save. At low levels where enemies have very few saving throw proficiencies, Wardaway may be decently reliable. But enemies at low levels also rarely have Bonus Actions, so they’re likely to fail the save and barely notice the spell’s effect.

wrathful-smite|phb.name: Wrathful Smite
wrathful-smite|phb.summary: You trade a considerable amount of Divine Smite’s damage for an excellent debuff. Frightened enemies can’t willingly move closer to the source of their fear, so you can use the Push Weapon Mastery to push enemies out of reach and leave them unable to get back into melee until the condition ends.

aid|phb.name: Aid
aid|phb.summary: Not essential, but a good way to pad your party’s hit points throughout the day. Just be careful; if the spell ends while you’re below 5 hit points you’ll fall to 0 and fall unconscious. Aid’s casting time allows it to be used in combat, which is unusual but offers an interesting option. With three targets and a 30-foot range, you can cast it to both buff and heal your allies during combat. Targets current hit points and hit point maximum both increase, so allies at 0 hit points are healed in addition to having their hit point maximum raised, thereby allowing Aid to serve a similar function to Mass Healing Word. However, since spells don’t stack with themselves, it’s hard to repeat this trick. You’ll need to cast Aid again using higher-level spell slots, which can get expensive quickly, so Mass Healing Word is probably better if Aid is already running and if Mass Healing Word is an option for your party.

find-steed|phb.name: Find Steed
find-steed|phb.summary: gives you a magical mount and addresses some my many problems with 5e’s mounted combat rules. Among the steed’s many benefits, its hit points scale with spell level, so it gets more durable as enemies’ attacks get more dangerous. This means that you can actually expect the steed to survive more than a single hit.

gentle-repose|phb.name: Gentle Repose
gentle-repose|phb.summary: Very situational, but it solves some interesting problems. Normally you can cremate a body to prevent it from becoming undead, but cremating a body takes an alarmingly large amount of fuel which you probably don’t have laying about. You can mutilate the body, but that’s gross and in many campaign settings the gods view that sort of thing as evil. So if you need to maintain a body until you can give it a real burial, this is your best bet. Gentle Repose also pauses the timer on effects which raise the dead. While this is specifically called out as working with Raise Dead, it works with anything that raises creatures from the dead. That includes Revivify. So if you keep this prepared, you can haul your allies around until you can cast 3rd-level spells and until you can scrape together enough diamond dust to raise them. Remember that while spells don’t stack, their durations can overlap so if you cast Gentle Repose early to avoid gaps in spell duration you can keep bodies preserved indefinitely.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

lesser-restoration|phb.name: Lesser Restoration
lesser-restoration|phb.summary: Situational, but a situation that comes up often. If you don’t have a cleric in the party you may be the only one with access to this spell, so you’ll want to take it at some point.

locate-object|phb.name: Locate Object
locate-object|phb.summary: Too situational, and too easy to counter. Anyone with any knowledge of magic that’s trying to hide something will wrap it in lead.

magic-weapon|phb.name: Magic Weapon
magic-weapon|phb.summary: If your game uses magic items, you may never need this. If it doesn’t, this is essential. A bonus to your attacks makes your damage output multiplicatively more reliable. With a 1-hour duration and no Concentration, one casting provides a lot of value from one of your few spell slots.

prayer-of-healing|phb.name: Prayer of Healing
prayer-of-healing|phb.summary: A Short Rest plus some extra healing for 5 targets. Useful if you’re pressed for time or if your party goes through hit points quickly and needs more healing than Hit Point Dice can provide.

protection-from-poison|phb.name: Protection From Poison
protection-from-poison|phb.summary: Situational, but poison is common across the full CR range, so this is a fantastic defensive option at any level. The 1-hour duration means that you can get a lot of mileage out of a single spell slot even if you cast it ahead of time.

shining-smite|phb.name: Shining Smite
shining-smite|phb.summary: Only situationally useful, but very important if your party doesn’t have another counter to hidden or invisible enemies. The DnD 5.5 stealth rules use the Invisible condition for hidden creatures, so this outright prevents stealth. Against creautre sthat use actual invisibility, you can cast this after you hit them and then you’re good as long as you can maintain Concentration.

warding-bond|phb.name: Warding Bond
warding-bond|phb.summary: Few characters are so well-suited to use this spell as the Paladin. With d10 hit dice and Lay on Hands you have a huge well of hit points, and using this provides a great deal of protection to comparably fragile allies. This also doesn’t require Concentration, so you can combine it with options like Heroism to further mitigate damage.

zone-of-truth|phb.name: Zone of Truth
zone-of-truth|phb.summary: Situational and much less reliable than you would hope. Creatures are aware that they’re under the effect, and they can choose to “be evasive”, which means that they could give you true but useless answers or simply not answer. Creatures other than the caster also don’t know who passed or failed the save, so unless they already trust you other creatures might not believe you when you tell them that a creature is telling the truth. If a creature is willing to talk, they can prove that they are saying what they believe to be true, and you can know whether or not they believe it to be true. But if the creature is incorrect, if you’re lying to other creatures (which they might believe that you are), or if any other number of other things go wrong, this spell simply fails to meet its intended purpose. In short, this helps honest creatures prove to you that they are being honest. Nothing else. If you want to get answers from an unwilling or unhelpful subject, cast Detect Thoughts.

aura-of-vitality|phb.name: Aura of Vitality
aura-of-vitality|phb.summary: Never use this in combat, but 20d6 healing for a level 3 spell is very efficient. That’s an average of 70 hit points, which matches Heal.

blinding-smite|phb.name: Blinding Smite
blinding-smite|phb.summary: Compared to Divine Smite, you lose 1d8 damage to potentially Blind the target. That’s a really good trade even if the blindness only lasts for one round. Constitution saves are high, but you’re gambling 1d8 damage to blind a creature likely for an entire encounter with no way to recover, so it’s worth the gamble.

create-food-and-water|phb.name: Create Food and Water
create-food-and-water|phb.summary: Rations are cheap, but it’s good that you can prepare this if you somehow find yourself somewhere without food for extended periods. This also lets you create 30 gallons of water, which is enough for a nice bath but not enough to fill a 5-foot cube.

crusader-s-mantle|phb.name: Crusader’s Mantle
crusader-s-mantle|phb.summary: Divine Favor, but for yourself and all of your allies within 30 ft. It gets better in larger parties, especially if you have allies who make lots of attacks, such as by using two weapons, Polearm Master, Action Surge, or Flurry of Blows. 1d4 damage ism’t a lot, so your party really needs to make a lot of attacks to justify this.

daylight|phb.name: Daylight
daylight|phb.summary: A Continual Flame, Light, or even a torch is typically sufficient, but sometimes you need to light up larger areas like dark battlefields or massive caverns. This also dispels magical darkness of 3rd level or lower, which is great if you’re fighting enemies like drow which can produce magical darkness. Tragically, you can’t cast Daylight at a higher level to dispel magical darkness of higher levels.

dispel-magic|phb.name: Dispel Magic
dispel-magic|phb.summary: Useful, but you get this so much later that your party should have access to this from a full spellcaster.

elemental-weapon|phb.name: Elemental Weapon
elemental-weapon|phb.summary: Not significantly better than Magic Weapon, a spell level higher, and it takes Concentration. Unfortunately, you can’t use both. Instead, you can cast Magic Weapon and Divine Favor to get the same attack bonus and the same amount of additional damage.

remove-curse|phb.name: Remove Curse
remove-curse|phb.summary: Situational, but irreplaceable. Fortunately, you can usually wait a day to prepare this.

revivify|phb.name: Revivify
revivify|phb.summary: Too good to forgo. Everyone who can get this should take it.

spirit-shroud|tcoe.name: Spirit Shroud
spirit-shroud|tcoe.summary: With a 1-minute duration and a Bonus Action casting time, this is a linear upgrade from Divine Favor. You upgrade from 1d4 to 1d8 damage, and you can impose a -10 speed penalty on nearby enemies. Stack that with a Slow weapon and potentially the Slasher feat, and you can potentially drop an enemy’s speed to 0. We can also do a basic damage comparison with Divine Smite. A level 3 Divine Smite deals 4d8 damage. Combat is expected to take roughly 3 rounds, and you have Extra Attack by this level. If you hit with 4 of your 6 attacks in those three rounds, Spirit Shroud will do the same amount of damage. Divine Smite will still be more impressive on crits, but Spirit Shroud is more consistent and is much more useful beyond just damage.

aura-of-life|phb.name: Aura of Life
aura-of-life|phb.summary: Only useful if you know that you’re facing the types of undead which reduce your hit point maximum (there are several).ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

aura-of-purity|phb.name: Aura of Purity
aura-of-purity|phb.summary: Technically situational, but the defenses are broad enough that you can cover a wide variety of situations. In most encounters it’s unlikely that you’ll be hit with more than one or two negative status conditions, but Aura of Purity provides broad enough protection that you’ll be able to counter many of the most common conditions with the same spell.

banishment|phb.name: Banishment
banishment|phb.summary: A great way to remove an enemy from a fight. Many creatures have poor Charisma saves well into high levels, so even a Paladin with middling Charisma may be able to use this reliably. It’s tempting to drop this once you can cast Banishing Smite. Don’t.

death-ward|phb.name: Death Ward
death-ward|phb.summary: This will absolutely save your life, and with an 8 hour duration you can cast it at the beginning of the day before you go do anything dangerous.

find-greater-steed|xgte.name: Find Greater Steed
find-greater-steed|xgte.summary: A curious leftover from the 2014 rules, Find Greater Steed is still allowed since it hasn’t been reprinted. The allowed creatures include options with fly speeds, but the DnD 5.5 version of Find Steed will give you a much more durable steed since its hit points will scale.

locate-creature|phb.name: Locate Creature
locate-creature|phb.summary: More effective than mundane tracking, but the 1,000-foot range can be a problem if the target is actively fleeing from you. If you’re going to use this, be sure that you’re moving faster than your target.

staggering-smite|phb.name: Staggering Smite
staggering-smite|phb.summary: You trade much of Divine Smite’s damage for a 1-round save-or-suck. Stunned will break Concentration, and the target can’t do anything on their turn except move. You might follow this by shoving and/or grappling your target while they have Disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity saves.

banishing-smite|phb.name: Banishing Smite
banishing-smite|phb.summary: Roughly the same damage as a level 5 Divine Smite, plus the added banishment effect. Unfortunately, the banishment effect isn’t great. The target needs to be below 50 hp after the spell’s damage is applied, and then the target still gets a Charisma save. The only advantage compared to Banishment is that Banishing Smite has a Bonus Action casting time.

circle-of-power|phb.name: Circle of Power
circle-of-power|phb.summary: Technically situational, but spellcasting enemies are common at such high level.

destructive-smite-destructive-wave|phb.name: Destructive Smite / Destructive Wave
destructive-smite-destructive-wave|phb.summary: This is a decent AOE for a class that otherwise struggles to handle groups of foes since Paladins don’t get any other area damage spells. 10d6 damage is a big pile, and the damage types are very rarely resisted. Unfortunately, it’s on a Con save, so you need to expect that enemies will pass the save.

dispel-evil-and-good|phb.name: Dispel Evil and Good
dispel-evil-and-good|phb.summary: In most cases, Protection from Evil and Good will do the trick, but Dispel Evil and Good has two additional effects. You can prematurely end the spell to end a charm/frighten/possession effect, or to attempt to banish creatures from other planes. They do still get a saving throw, and if the creatures are native to the plane they’re on, nothing happens. It’s very important to note that the banishment effect isn’t limited by the spell’s duration: creatures banished this way are sent to another plane and must return by normal means. However, since the banishment effect doesn’t affect creatures on their home plane, the banishment is usually not as appealing as the spell Banishment, which can affect creatures native to your current plane. The one advantage is that you don’t need to maintain Concentration for the spell’s 1-minute duration for your target to remain on their home plane.

geas|phb.name: Geas
geas|phb.summary: This spell is situational by design. It has a 1-minute casting time and Verbal components, so you’re not going to break this out in combat or while sneaking around in a dungeon. You’re going to restrain the subject, and stand around chanting for a full minute and hope that they fail the save. Once that’s done, you need to give them a suitable command (read the spell description). Generally you’ll want it to be something that benefits you, but will also take the target most of the duration to keep them from becoming a problem for you. Also remember that the base effect of the Charmed condition makes it easier for you to talk the creature into doing things with Charisma checks, so a Geased creature may be a useful ally for the duration of the effect even if the original order isn’t directly related to what you want them to do. Increasing the spell level extends the duration, but weirdly the damage doesn’t increase. 5d10 is a nice pile of damage, but it doesn’t scale with spell level and at some point the target will get smart enough to wake up, trigger the 5d10 damage, take a short rest, then go about their business. If the damage scaled this would be less of a problem, but damage is so easily repaired in 5e outside of combat that without further penalties Geas is more a tax on hit dice than the magical shackles it’s intended to be. If you want a homebrew fix, add a level of fatigue each day that the target is out of compliance, or make the damage impossible to heal until they go a day without taking it. Neither of those is a perfect solution, but they’re miles better than an average of 27.5 damage.

greater-restoration|phb.name: Greater Restoration
greater-restoration|phb.summary: If you don’t have a Cleric in the party, you need this.

holy-weapon|xgte.name: Holy Weapon
holy-weapon|xgte.summary: An excellent damage boost. +2d8 radiant damage on hit means that you’re doing as much damage as you would do by burning a low-level spell slot to use Holy Smite. Your weapon becomes a magic weapon so you can bypass many creatures’ damage reduction. You get all of this for an hour with Concentration, and you can cast it as a Bonus Action. You can also dismiss the spell for a cool burst of damage, but that’s probably not going to see a lot of use unless the duration happens to run out while you’re fighting. The most direct comparison is to level 5 Spirit Shroud. Spirit Shroud will add the same amount of extra damage plus the slow effect on nearby enemies, but Spirit Shroud only lasts 1 minute. On a class that gets exactly one level 5 spell slot, you really want to get a lot of mileage out of it, so Holy Weapon’s 1-hour duration is much more appealing.

raise-dead|phb.name: Raise Dead
raise-dead|phb.summary: Essential, but by this level you should have access to Raise Dead already from other spellcasters in the party.

summon-celestial|tcoe.name: Summon Celestial
summon-celestial|tcoe.summary: (Optional): The Paladin’s best level 5 spell in combat. While your summon won’t be as effective as that of full caster, it’s still very good. Two attacks that do as much damage as the damage boost from Holy Weapon, plus a powerful rider effect and another body on the field to block space and make Opportunity Attacks. Unfortunately, the summon’s attack bonus uses your spell attack modifier. Unless you have 20 Charisma (which you might by this level even if you’re not doing a Charisma-focused build), the summon’s relatively unreliable attacks may be a problem depending on exactly what your spell attack modifier is. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spellsezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: The ability scores only work for Wisdom-based builds, and even then it’s not great. The skills are fine, but not amazing, and you there aren’t many applicable Cleric spells that complement the Ranger’s capabilities which won’t compete for space with Hunter’s Mark.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(187); });

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: Great if you want more skills, but Scribe has better fixed skills for the Ranger.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: You can get the crucial Dexterity increase, but that’s the only appeal here.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Workable ability scores and a great feat, but the skills are a bad fit for the Ranger.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Dexterity, Constitution, and Skilled is a great combination for the Ranger, especially if you’re filling in for a Rogue in the party. However, you don’t get proficiency in Thieves’ Tools.

chondathan-freebooter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freebooter
chondathan-freebooter|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, one good skill, and Skilled. Not quite as good as Scribe, but close.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for a Wisdom-based build, but Healer does very little for you and the skills are base.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for a Dexterity-based build, and Dragonscarred will let you increase Constitution or Charisma, so it’s workable. You may have enough Wisdom to make Cult of the Dragon Initiate’s fear effect work for you.

emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Caretaker
emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.summary: Terrible feat despite being thematically very cool for the Ranger.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: One good ability score and the Musician feat is really good, but the skills are horrible.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: Since Strength-based Ranger builds don’t really work, this is best for Druidic Warrior builds. The skills are fine for the Ranger, and Tough is always an easy choice if you don’t want more complexity.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and one good skill. Magic Initiate could offer some great options. You could try a Wisdom-based build based on True Strike, but missing Extra Attack will hurt your damage output considerably.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Fine for Strength-based Ranger builds, but Strength-based Ranger builds are bad.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: The default for Rangers. Perfect ability scores, good skills, and Druid spellcasting without giving up your Fighting Style. If you want a Wisdom-based build, Guide is a great way to get Shillelagh.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores and one good skill, but the feat is awful.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Okay for a Druidic Warrior build, but the skills are middling. The Ranger’s ability to magically heal is very limited, so Healer may be worthwhile if your party is short on healing options.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores and Lucky, but the skills are bad. If you want Lucky, Wayfarer is a much better choice.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and Alert, but the skills are terrible.

knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.name: Knight of the Gauntlet
knight-of-the-gauntlet|frhof.summary: Mediocre ability scores, bad feat, horrible skills.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, and the skills are only good if you’re a Fey Wanderer trying to be a Face.

lorwyn-expert|lfl.name: Lorwyn Expert
lorwyn-expert|lfl.summary: Workable ability scores for a Wisdom-based build and one good skill. It’s fine, but it’s basically just a worse version of Guide for the Ranger.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: Bad ability scores, bad skills. Get Lucky somewhere else.

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and Lucky, but the skills are a hard choice for the Ranger.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: The abiity scores and skills are bad. You can get Skilled from other choices.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, one good skill, great feat. Not good enough to make up for the rest, though.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: A tempting option for Druidic Warrior builds, but the skills are difficult on the Ranger.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores for a melee build plus one good skill. Tavern Brawler isn’t a great choice, but the ability to push an enemy 5 feet while also dealing damage with an Unarmed Strike may be useful if you’re not using weapons with the Push mastery.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: Good ability scores, good skills, and Skilled can close the proficiency gap between the Ranger and the Rogue.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores, decent skills, and a passable feat.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: The Dexterity increase is the best thing here, and that’s not enough.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: Good ability scores, Savage Attacker is decent since you’ll never have more than 2 attacks, but the skills are bad.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, one good skill, bad feat.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores, the skills and Thieves’ Tools are perfect for a stealthy Ranger replacing a Rogue in the party.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: Mediocre ability scores, one good skill, great feat for melee builds. If you want Zhentarim Tactics, try to get it from somewhere else.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores aren’t a good fit. You’ll get more value out of a background which gives you Magic Initiate.

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Fine ability scores and decent skills, but little value from the feat.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: Excellent for a Wisdom-based build. Grab Shillelagh and you’re in good shape.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are good and the skills are okay, but the feat isn’t great.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: Great ability scores, one good skill, but very little value from the feat.

house-kundarak-heir|efota.name: House Kundarak Heir
house-kundarak-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores, bad skills, and the feat isn’t nearly enough to make up for it.

house-lyrandar-heir|efota.name: House Lyrandar Heir
house-lyrandar-heir|efota.summary: Mediocre ability scores, only one good skill, and the feat isn’t enough to make up for it.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: Decent ability scores and a good feat, but bad skills.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: Excellent ability scores, one good skill, and a good feat. Persuasion usually isn’t a good skill for the Ranger, but Fey Wanderer’s bonus on Charisma checks makes them a good Face, so that’s an easy combination.

house-tharashk-heir|efota.name: House Tharashk Heir
house-tharashk-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores and skills work for a Wisdom-based build, but the feat isn’t helpful.

house-thuranni-heir|efota.name: House Thuranni Heir
house-thuranni-heir|efota.summary: Decent ability scores, one good skill, great feat. House Phiarlan is better.

house-vadalis-heir|efota.name: House Vadalis Heir
house-vadalis-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores for a Wisdom-based build, but the skills are bad and you already get most of the spells.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. While the Ranger does sometimes need their Bonus Action free for Hunter’s Mark, that’s not so frequently that it makes Celestial Revelation hard to use. It’s a great combat buff, granting flight for ranged builds or a way to handle crowds for melee builds.

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: You are not a Face, and this won’t solve that issue. Fey Wanderer is a notable exception.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: A damage resistance, likely to a common damage type like poison or fire, a decent way to handle crowds of small enemies, Darkvision, and flight once per day. Excellent for melee builds.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense may be your only way to locate invisible enemies. Great for melee builds, but likely wasted on ranged builds.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great, plus you can get access to some spells from outside of the Ranger’s spell list. The Drow’s Faerie Fire gives you a great offensive support option, and the High Elf’s cantrip can get you a great offensive cantrips from the Wizard’s spell list. The Wood Elf makes sense thematically, but you can already get both Longstrider and Pass Without Trace, though getting two more spells prepared for free isn’t a bad thing. This is all even more useful for Druidic Warrior builds since the High Elf’s cantrip gives you more room to select non-damage cantrips like Guidance.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage offers numerous excellent options. I like Cloud’s Jaunt, Hill’s Topple, and Stone’s Endurance. Rangers typically don’t have the durability to use Large Form and turn themselves into a target, but Giant Heritage may be enough on its own.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Brave will be very helpful with the Ranger’s moderately high Wisdom. Lucky is always decent, though not hugely impactful. Halfling Nimbleness and Naturally Stealthy won’t be consistently useful.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Very similar to the Gnome, but you give up some good things to get resistance to Psychic damage. Gnome is nearly always a better choice.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Roughly comparable to a human with Magic Initiate, but you trade most of the spellcasting for Darkvision and the ability to change the Cantrip.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush provides a taste of the Rogue’s mobility which rangers can’t typically match, and the Temporary Hit Points are always great. Relentless Endurance provides some insurance, especially on melee builds which typically draw more attacks.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Darkvision, an extra skill, and a good combat buff from Shifting. The Ranger’s Bonus Action can often be over-taxed by Hunter’s Mark and the class’s stubborn dependency on it, but you may be able to use Shifting when you’re facing enemies tough enough enemies that they’ll survive more than one round.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting. Possibly a good choice for Druidic Warrior builds, but otherwise you won’t use the spellcasting reliably.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(189); });

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and spellcasting that you won’t use.

animal-handling|wis.name: Animal Handling
animal-handling|wis.summary: (Wis): Even for a Beast Master Ranger this is still worthless.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(191); });

athletics|str.name: Athletics
athletics|str.summary: (Str): Functionally useless. You can use Athletics to bind creatures in chains, but you’re better suited to using Sleight of Hand for manacles or rope.

insight|wis.name: Insight
insight|wis.summary: (Wis): Rangers need a bit of Wisdom, so pick this up to back up your party’s Face.

investigation|int.name: Investigation
investigation|int.summary: (Int): Very useful, especially if you’re serving as your party’s Scout, but Intelligence isn’t a great ability for Rangers, so you might leave this to other folks in the party.

nature|int.name: Nature
nature|int.summary: (Int): Your only knowledge skill. It’s a good skill, but Intelligence is hard for Rangers.

perception|wis.name: Perception
perception|wis.summary: (Wis): With high Wisdom there is no reason not to take this.

stealth|dex.name: Stealth
stealth|dex.summary: (Dex): Rangers don’t strictly need to be stealthy, but with high Dexterity it certainly doesn’t hurt.

survival|wis.name: Survival
survival|wis.summary: (Wis): Very situational, but if anyone was going to take this it should be a Ranger.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Never a bad choice, but less impactful for martial characters than for full casters.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(192); });

child-of-the-sun|lfl.name: Child of the Sun
child-of-the-sun|lfl.summary: Faerie Fire is really good, but it competes with Hunter’s Mark for Concentration, and the Ranger depends too much on Hunter’s Mark for that to be an easy choice. Even if you do want this, go for Magic Initiate (Druid) instead.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: Excellent, espeically for a Wisdom-based build.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

healer|phb.name: Healer
healer|phb.summary: Terrible. You can cast Cure Wounds, but you shouldn’t do that often enough to make this impactful.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Decent on any martial character that gets Extra Attack, but without a way to increase your chance to crit, you won’t benefit from the first half of the feat consistently.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: Druid spells might remove the need for Druidic Warrior, or you can get more cantrips (either from the Druid or elsewhere) so that you feel closer to a full spellcaster.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Proficiency in Insight, and give Heroic Inspiration to your whole party once per day. Excellent on any build if you don’t need a different Origin Feat.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Rangers rarely use weapons with big damage dice, so this won’t have a significant impact. If you somehow make muskets effective, this might be worthwhile.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Hex is a great damage buff, but it competes for spae with Hunter’s Mark, which you get for free several times per day.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Great for picking up skills and Thieves’ Tools proficiencies so that you can easily replace a Rogue in your party.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: Rangers lean too heavily on their Bonus Action to make this an easy choice.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: There is very little reason to use this. Grab a weapon with the Push mastery.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Always helpful for front-line melee builds, but not essential.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: The Opportunity Attack feature is great for melee builds, and giving your whole party Advantage on Initiative is great on anyone. Strongly consider adding Zhentarim Tactics, too, so that you can make Opportunity Attacks more often.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: Very similar to Magic Initiate if you could select Sorcerer, but you trade one Cantrip for a buff to Con saves and the THP/damage thing. To maximize the value of Aberrant Surge, you want to select a level 1 spell which you’ll cast frequently in combat, so pick a staple option like Absorb Elements or Shield which will remain equally effective for your whole career.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(193); });

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: The skills and spells are decent, but not amazing. You get both See Invisibility and Arcane Eye, which are both great and not on your spell list, but that’s not enough to make this an easy choice.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: Very few spells that you don’t already get.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: You’re most likely to use Find Familiar, but that’s not enough to justify this over Magic Initiate. Animal Friendship of low-Intelligence Monstrosities is neat, but not useful enough to make a difference.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: You already get everything except Healing Word.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: Some of the low-level spells are good and aren’t on the Paladin’s spell list, but nothing amazing.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: Rangers already get Magic Weapon, and you’ll get very little value from the other spells.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Access to some excellent spells including Misty Step, Find Steed, Pass Without Trace, and Phantom Steed.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: The most interesting things here will only be useful for characters good at Charisma-based skills, and that’s not you.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Shield is great. Vigilant Guardian might see use, but you have d8 hit dice, so don’t get too carried away. The leveled spells mostly come from the Cleric and the Paladin, and they’re great spells, but might be hard for you to use consistently without cutting into Hunter’s Mark. Beast Master Rangers might find useful options here for keeping their companion alive, but remember that you can spend a single spell slot to replace them, so spending spells on things like Warding Bond is wasteful.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: A great addition to a sneaky Ranger since Rangers generally don’t get access to illusions.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Mostly mediocre, but you do get a couple great spells including Feather Fall and Conjure Minor Elementals.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Mage Armor and Armor of Agathys could be great additions for melee builds.

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: A decent choice for many martial characters. A climb speed is the next best thing to a fly speed. The ability to stand up quickly makes falling or being knocked prone less of a problem. The ability to jump with less of a running start may let you easily jump over difficult terrain and other obstacles which otherwise might slow your movement in combat.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: The push effect is decent, especially when combined with a Push mastery, but without other stacking sources of push distance you’ll have trouble getting past the 30-foot threshold where most creatures won’t have enough speed to immediately run back into melee.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: An excellent source of additional healing and of Temporary Hit Points. Good for any melee build.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Grab Fighting Style (Blind Fighting), and suddenly you’re the only one who can see inside your Fog Cloud. Grab a whip and the Slasher fear, and you can impose a -20 ft. speed penalty in one attack. Stacked with the speed penalty from Cloying Mists, that will nearly immobilize most enemies. It’s an incredibly easy build for the Eldritch Knight, and very few enemies can do anything about it. Of course, your allies also won’t be able to see, so it may be impolite to bring this to the table regardless of how effective it is.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Normally a good choice for ranged weapon builds, but the importance of Hunter’s Mark can make it difficult to use two hand crossbows to take advantage of the Bonus Action attack. You may be better served by using two-weapon fighting to throw daggers.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: A simple and easy way to control enemies’ positions in combat, especially when combined with the Push mastery. Unfortunately, there are no Finesse weapons that deal bludgeoning damage, so very few Rangers can actually use this. Druidic Warrior builds using Shillelagh are your best bet.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: A consistent and effective way to boost your AC in melee if you’re using Finesse weapons like rapiers or short swords, which most melee Rangers will. Boosting your AC by this much may prevent you from getting hit, which will do a lot to protect your Concentration on Hunter’s Mark.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: With d8 hit dice, you don’t have the hit points to back this up.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: An additional attack while two-weapon fighting can be a big damage boost, but your Bonus Action may be overtaxed by subclass features and by Hunter’s Mark, so this isn’t always a good idea even for two-weapon fighting builds.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: Not as good as you would hope. The Bonus Action to spend a Hit Point Die notably does not add your Constitution modifier, which makes it an expensive and frustrating way to burn through your Hit Point Dice very quickly with minimal impact. Unless your party has some other deep, inexpensive healing resource, you need those dice for Short Rests to refill your massive pool of hit points. Take Chef instead.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: The Ranger gets too few spells that will benefit from this, and most of them are terrible.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: A great way to support spellcaster allies, but most Rangers won’t benefit a lot on their own since most of the subclass rely on attacks instead of saves.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Misty Step is excellent, and the additional spells per day can be very helpful.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Strength-based Rangers don’t work well, so qualifying weapons are a bad idea

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: Heavy armor is the missing piece to make Strength-based Rangers work, but if you’re running around with 8 Dexterity you’re probably not going to survive to level 4 in order to take this. Start with a level of Fighter instead.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A big pile of durability for your whole party. Best on Druidic Warrior builds.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Too situational for a feat that doesn’t give you a useful ability score increase.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational to justify unless you’re in a Underdark campaign or a campaign where vampires feature heavily.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, and Standard Bearer is only situationally useful.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Great insurance against difficult mental saves.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: There aren’t rules for the Beast Master to ride their companion, and regular mounts are too frail to last long.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: Useful if your GM likes to use sneaky creatures.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: The vast majority of the Ranger’s best weapons deal piercing damage.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: Without another built-in way to consistently deal poison damage, there is too little benefit here to justify.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: Reactive Strike is a great way to get additional attacks and apply Hunter’s Mark damage, but it’s only viable for Druidic Warrior builds using Shillelagh since Strength-based builds don’t work well for the Ranger. The Bonus Action attack is also very powerful, but competes in the action economy with applying Hunter’s Mark.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: The Temporary Hit Ponts feature is a great support option, and Advantage on attacks while Bloodied is an easy way to get consistent Advantage. Note that you can bypass the requirement for Purple Dragon Squire because you have proficiency in martial weapons.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Proficiency in Constitution saves really helps with Concentration, not to mention how common Constitution saves are. Concentrating on Hunter’s Mark is crucial for the Ranger, and it’s especially difficult for melee builds. Druidic Warrior builds may prefer War Caster since you can increase your Wisdom when you take the feat. Relentless Hunter makes this less important once you reach level 13, but a lot of campaigns never get that far.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: Not a good feat. You don’t get enough rituals, and they can only be level 1.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Absolutely fantastic on the Beast Master since you’ll routinely have an ally fighting right alongside you.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Invisibility is great on the Ranger, but the level 1 spell options aren’t as good as Fey Touched.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Helpful for ranged builds, but not essential unless your DM really enjoys using cover. Thrown weapon builds might enjoy this to offset their poor range relative to weapons like bows and muskets.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: Rangers don’t have the Strength to make this work.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: A good way to close the skill gap with the Rogue.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Hard to justify without Cunning Action.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: The ability for melee builds to move in and out of melee with relative safety makes hit-and-run tactics much more viable, making it much easier to maintain Concentration on Hunter’s Mark since you’re not standing around in melee waiting to be attacked.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Maybe for Druidic Warrior since Produce Flame, Starry Wisp, and Thorn Whip are likely your go-to ranged attack options.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: Without a consistent way to deal Radiant damage, there’s very little value here.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: Rangers are not great grappling since Strength-based Ranger builds struggle so much, and without an easy way to grapple and also bind your target in one turn, the rest of the feat isn’t consistently useful.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: Potentially useful for Druidic Warrior builds, provided that your Bonus Action isn’t being monopolized by your class and by Hunter’s Mark.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Without an easy way to make enemies Charmed, there’s almost no benefit here.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: The Ranger’s spell list is small, and this can get you some great new spells.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Great for Druidic Warrior builds, but most Rangers will get more out of Resilient (Constitution).

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: You already get Weapon Mastery. If you need more, strongly consider a 1-level dip into Fighter.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: An easy way to trigger Opportunity Attacks and Expertise in one skill.

blind-fighting|phb.name: Blind Fighting
blind-fighting|phb.summary: Fantastic, but only situationally useful. Unless you have party members that like to rely on magical darkness or fog or similar effects, you’ll get more consistent benefit from other options. If it’s an option, take the Skulker feat instead.

defense|phb.name: Defense
defense|phb.summary: Consistently useful, and doesn’t discourage you from switching weapons.

dueling|phb.name: Dueling
dueling|phb.summary: 2 damage closes the damage gap between a longsword and a two-handed weapon like a greataxe or greatsword (4.5->6.5 vs. 6.5/7), so you can have the damage of a two-handed weapon with the AC of sword-and-board. Note that this works while using a shield.

great-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Great Weapon Fighting
great-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: This raises the minimum damage for the Greatsword to 6, which feels nice but doesn’t improve your average damage roll very much. It has almost no impact on other weapons, which makes the appeal very narrow. It does appear to let you reroll the damage die from Hunter’s Mark because it’s “Extra Damage”, but that’s still not enough to make a greatsword a good choice for the Ranger.

interception|phb.name: Interception
interception|phb.summary: Conceptually similar to Protection, but there’s some nuance in how the two styles protect your target. Protection imposes Disadvantage, so if there’s a good chance that the attack would miss, it’s the better choice. Interception reduces the damage and always works, but for big attacks it won’t negate the whole attack.

protection|phb.name: Protection
protection|phb.summary: Tempting for Defender builds and pet builds (Beast Master and Drakewarden), but allies need to remain adjacent to you for this to work. Being adjacent to the front line tank is generally a bad place to be unless you can do so safely without someone defending you. This also appeals to mounted combat builds because you can use it to compensate for your mount’s relative fragility, but if you’re going that route you really need the Mounted Combatant feat which lets you retarget attacks at yourself instead.

thrown-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Thrown Weapon Fighting
thrown-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: With the ability to use two-weapon fighting and throw Nick weapons, the math behind three attacks gets complicated. If you use a handaxe as your primary weapon and either a dagger or a light hammer as your secondary weapon for the Nick mastery, the Advantage from your handaxe’s Vex mastery can push the DPR just slightly past that of a musket making two attacks. Later adding Dual Wielder, Fighting Style (Archery), and Fighting Style (Two-Weapon Fighting) can add additional boosts to your damage output.

two-weapon-fighting|phb.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
two-weapon-fighting|phb.summary: Two-weapon fighting is a major damage boost for melee builds thanks to Hunter’s Mark.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is great, especially since high level creatures frequently deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage. You can also change your weapon’s damage type to Radiant in the rare case your target is resistant to whatever weapon you’re using.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Fine, but occasonal Advantage and a minor damage boost won’t have a huge impact.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: Without a built-in way to give yourself Temporary Hit Points, this is useless.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Great if you’re built to fight in melee where you’re going to draw a lot of attacks.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: You don’t have a big burst of Radiant damage which justifies this.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: More useful to support your allies’ save-or-suck spells than for anything that you’re doing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Without built-in shapechange options like Polymorph, this is much less useful.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: You will benefit more from Resilient (Constitution).

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: Fantastic for two-weapon fighting builds since you’ll be making up to 4 attacks. Archery builds might get less value, but it’s still a fine option.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Increasing your reach with melee attacks makes it easy to hit enemies from outside of their reach. Dodge as a Bonus Action is useful on turns where you don’t need to retarget Hunter’s Mark.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance will guarantee at least one round of dancing, which is useful, but without the ability to recast the spell you’re not getting as much value as a full caster.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: You could use this for a utility of some kind, but there aren’t many utility spells which you’ll want every Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list (neither care about your stats).

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: Potentially useful, but remember that it only has a 25% chance to work.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
