athlete|phb.summary: A decent choice for many martial characters. A climb speed is the next best thing to a fly speed. The ability to stand up quickly makes falling or being knocked prone less of a problem. The ability to jump with less of a running start may let you easily jump over difficult terrain and other obstacles which otherwise might slow your movement in combat.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: Combining Cunning Action (Dash) and the push effect can allow you to rush into melee, knock your target back, then retreat to a safe distance.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: This won’t contribute anything meaningful to what you do as a Rogue, but passing out snacks for THP always feels nice.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Without a way to see through the fog, Fog Cloud only functions as a way to block line of sight. The 5-foot speed penalty isn’t enough on its own.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Not worth the feat. Use Steady Aim to attack with Advantage so that you still roll 2 d20’s to hit while also qualifying for Sneak Attack.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: Basically every weapon that the Rogue can use for Sneak Attack deals Piercing damage. There are a few exceptions like the Sling, but there’s little reason to use them and Crusher’s ability scores don’t offer a Dexterity increase.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: Too much overlap with Uncanny Dodge.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Grab a weapon with Nick, and you can roll at least two d20s to attack, which dramatically improves the reliability of Sneak Attack. The possible third attack as a Bonus Action doesn’t help significantly, especially since you can use Steady Aim if you need Advantage.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: This is bad and it conflicts with your Bonus Action class feature.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Even the Arcane Trickster won’t rely on the sorts of spells that this benefits.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: Once you get Cunning Strike you can combine this easily with several of the effects, but the most likely beneficiary is casters in your party.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Helpful for the Arcane Trickster. More spells and some free castings can do a lot for you. But Misty Step may not be especially useful since you have Cunning Action.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: You can Sneak Attack with qualifying ranged weapons like the Musket, but the ability score increase is useless and you’re only going to get the damage bonus once per round.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: You should not be in heavy armor.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: If you have the ability scores to qualify for this, it’s a massive amount of temporary hit points. But it can’t improve Dexterity, so you probably want to wait to take this.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Even for the Arcane Trickster, this is hard to justify.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational to justify unless you’re in a Underdark campaign or a campaign where vampires feature heavily.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, and Standard Bearer is only situationally useful.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Great insurance against difficult mental saves, but you can also protect yourself by hiding so that you can’t be targeted. At high levels, Slippery Mind makes this much less appealing. You may want this to help break Concentration, but the Rogue’s single-hit damage scales considerably faster than saving throw modifiers, so you should be able to consistently break Concentration by delivering a Sneak Attack.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: Competes with your crucial class features too much to justify.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Nearly all the Rogue’s preferred weapons deal Piercing damage. Note that the reroll can be any of the attack’s damage dice, so you’re free to reroll a Sneak Attack damage die.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: Since Rogues depend on making big single hits, poisoning a weapon before you go into combat is less of a hassle than it is for classes that rely on numerous attacks. Even so, the damage doesn’t scale with level, so it will be less impactful at high level. Assassin Rogues will get considerably more value here thanks to Envenom Weapons.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: You should not be using a polearm to attack stuff.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing. Most subclasses will miss much of the value, but this is great for the Arcane Trickster to expand their tiny number of prepared spells.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: Handing out THP is great, but this feat will provide very little value in combat compared to Cunning Action.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Never a bad choice, but it’s hard to say which ability score to use this on until you’re high enough level that you have 20 Dexterity and every feat that you could want.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: Not even on an Arcane Trickster.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Potentially an easy way to get Sneak Attack outside of your own turn.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: You’re almost certainly going to learn Invisibility.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Helpful for ranged builds, but not essential.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: You don’t get proficiency with shields.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: More skills are always nice, especially once you have Reliable Talent.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: This feat was made for the Rogue. It’s absolutely essential if you’re planning to fight at range.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Rogues get very few slashing weapons that also qualify for Sneak Attack, but this can work with whips.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Even the Arcane Trickster can’t rely on spell attacks since they can’t apply Sneak Attack.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: Without a consistent way to deal Radiant damage, there’s very little value here. If you add True Strike to your tactics, this could be a good way to get some extra damage.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: The Thief Rogue can, in theory, grapple an enemy as an Attack Action, then use Fast Hands to bind the same creature in chains/rope/manacles. But Rogues typically don’t have the Strength to support this tactic.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Without an easy way to make enemies Charmed, there’s almost no benefit here.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Potentially useful for the Arcane Trickster. The majority of the qualifying spells are aleady on the Wizard’s spell list, but extra spellcasting is great since you get so few spell slots.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: You already get enough Weapon Mastery slots.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: An easy way to trigger Opportunity Attacks and Expertise in one skill.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is great, especially since high level creatures frequently deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage. You can also change your weapon’s damage type to Radiant in the rare case your target is resistant to whatever weapon you’re using.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: The Rogue is perhaps the single best character to use this boon since you generally rely on making single attacks. It’s still not great, unfortunately. Boon of Combat Prowess will yield more consistent results.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: Without a built-in way to give yourself Temporary Hit Points, this is useless.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Functionally removes your ability to miss unless you’re making Opportunity Attacks. If you’ve been using two-weapon fighting in order to get a second chance to deliver Sneak Attack, you can safely stop doing that and look at weapons with better Weapon Mastery options.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Great if you’re built to fight in melee where you’re going to draw a lot of attacks. Note that Uncanny Dodge halves damage from an attack rather than granting Resistance, so it will stack, quarting incoming damage from that attack.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: If you can get an attack cantrip like Booming Blade or True Strike, this is fantastic.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: You don’t have a big burst of Radiant damage which justifies this.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: More useful to support your allies’ save-or-suck spells than for anything that you’re doing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: Without built-in shapechange options like Polymorph, this is much less useful.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: You don’t attack frequently enough for the damage boost to be meaningful. Bypassing resistances is nice, but if you have a magic weapon, it’s almost a non-issue.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Increasing your reach with melee attacks makes it easy to hit enemies from outside of their reach, and Dodge as a Bonus Action is likely just as useful as Cunning Action.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, and Cunning Strike lets you trade 1d6 damage for 2d6 poison damage which you can then reroll to get better damage

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance will guarantee at least one round of dancing, which is useful, but without the ability to recast the spell you’re not getting as much value as a full caster.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: You could use this for a utility of some kind, but there aren’t many utility spells which you’ll want every Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list (neither care about your stats).

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Stunningly powerful when combined with Reliable Talent.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: The speed is nice, but you can already Disengage as a Bonus Action.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: Potentially useful for the Arcane Trickster, but remember that it only has a 25% chance to work.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: Without a built-in way to make enemies Frightened, there’s very little value here. Scion of the Three has a Cunning Action option that works great here, and Arcane Trickster can use spells, but other subclass should look elsewhere.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Resistance/immunity to two damage types. The Disadvantage mechanic won’t help you, even if you’re an Arcane Trickster.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Excellent on a stealthy character like the Rogue. However, remember that a lot of things are an Action, so it’s very easy to break this invisibility. Notable examples that people easily overlook include Hide, Search, and Study.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: Resistance to two damage types. The healing is negligible. Take Boon of Fortitude instead.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Probably your only option for handling invisible enemies. If you’ve made it this far, your party is covering for you or you’ve found a creative solution.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: You could us this and build around True Strike to use a mental ability score for your attacks, but you’ll need to get True Strike from somewhere else, such as your species. If you sort that out, you could use Magic Initiate (Cleric) to get a powerful level 1 Cleric spell like Bless or Healing Word. But you’ll likely have better results playing a Human so that you can take Magic Initiate with your extra feat, then pick up a different Background.

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: Good if your party needs more skill coverage. Basically identical to Scribe, but with different fixed skills.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: Good ability scores for an Arcane Trickster, and the skills are decent, but Crafter isn’t a great feat.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, great feat, fantastic skills if you’re going to be your party’s Face.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Absolutely fantastic for the Rogue, especially in a small party where you have gaps in skill proficiencies or for a rogue planning to play their party’s Face.

chondathan-freebooter|frhof.name: Chondathan Freebooter
chondathan-freebooter|frhof.summary: Good, but hard to justify compared to Archaeologist or Scribe, which offer better ability scores.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, bad feat, bad skills.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Close to workable, but the Background and the feats stubbornly refuse to pick one mental ability score to emphasize, so it’s really hard to make everything here work on a single character.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: The ability scores are good and the Musician feat is welcome in any party, but it’s hard to waste two skill proficiencies on borderline useless skills.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: God ability scores and skills. If you want access to Booming Blade or True Strike, but aren’t building an Arcane Trickster, this is a great way to get it. If you’re building an Arcane Trickster, look at Sage instead.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Bad ability scores. If you want Alert, go for Inquisitive.

guide|phb.name: Guide
guide|phb.summary: Great ability scores, decent skills, and you can get some good utility options from Magic Initiate (Druid). I frequently advocate for Shillelagh, but you can’t Sneak Attack with it, so it’s not a good choice for the Arcane Trickster.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and one good skill, but the feat is awful.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Not good enough to justify the lack of a Dexterity increase.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores. The skills are fine and Lucky is good, but you have several better options to get Lucky. Look at Warfarer instead.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and Alert, but the skills are terrible.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: This can work for an Intelligence-based Arcane Trickster build. Alert offsets your relatively poor Dexterity for initiative rolls, and you get decent proficiencies.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: You could use this for an Intelligence-based Arcane Trickster build, but there’s really no reason to do so.

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: Good ability scores for any Rogue with decent Intelligence.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: This could work for an Intelligence-based Arcane Trickster build, but Scribe has better skills.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Intelligence and Constitution work fine for the Arcane Trickster, especially with Magic Initiate and Intelligence-based skills, but remember that you’re still a Rogue first, so you really want Dexterity. You can build around Intelligence and use True Strike for your attacks, but that won’t fix your AC and it won’t support your crucial Dexterity-based skills.

sailor|phb.name: Sailor
sailor|phb.summary: Decent ability scores, plus one good skill, but you’re absolutely not going to use Tavern Brawler.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: An easy go-to option, especially in a small party that needs more skill coverage. Good ability scores, good skills, and Skilled gives you even more options.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: Savage Attacker isn’t great, but the ability scores and skills are good.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: Workable ability scores, only one good skill, bad feat.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: Good ability scores, but Savage Attacker is wasted on the Rogue, and the skills aren’t great.

vampire-survivor|aboh.name: Vampire Survivor
vampire-survivor|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, decent skills, bad feat,

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores, good skills, and Lucky are all great, but the tool proficiency is redundant since Rogues already get proficiency in Thieve’s Tools. If you’re fine not getting another tool, this is a great choice.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and skills for a Rogue that plans to invest in Charisma. Zhentarim Ruffian is amazing, but it does require you to be in melee to get the full benefit.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores aren’t a good fit. You’ll get more value out of a background which gives you Magic Initiate.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(188); });

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: A perfect fit for the Arcane Trickster.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores and skills are fine, but the feat is a bad fit.

house-lyrandar-heir|efota.name: House Lyrandar Heir
house-lyrandar-heir|efota.summary: The only thing good here is the Dexterity increase.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: Excellent ability scores and a good feat for the Arcane Tricksters, but the skills are bad.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: A decent fit for the Arcane Trickster, but with no Intelligence increase and with a Charisma-based skill, it’s easy to make yourself MAD by accident. House Thuranni is an easier choice.

house-thuranni-heir|efota.name: House Thuranni Heir
house-thuranni-heir|efota.summary: A decent fit for the Arcane Trickster.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. Celestial Revelation is neat, but Heavenly Wings is the only option that will be reliably easy for you to use. Flight once per day and the modest damage bonus are fine, but amazing.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(189); });

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: Two extra skills, perpetual Advantage on Charisma checks, and built-in disguises. Excellent if you’re planning to be your party’s Face.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and once per day flight are great, but you will likely never use the breath weapon beyond very low levels.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. Tremorsense may be your only way to locate invisible enemies. Definitely tempting, but the durability is wasted on the Rogue, and Tremorsense isn’t enough on its own.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great. The innate spellcasting is neat, but only consistently useful for the Arcane Trickster.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage offers some interesting options, they’re all either redundant or unimpressive alongside the Rogue’s existing features. Cloud Jaunt is great, but in most situations it’s redundant with Cunning Action. The on-hit damage options are interesting, but they’ll feel minor compared to Sneak Attack and Precise Strike. Stone’s Endurance is good, but with Evasion and Uncanny Dodge you already have a lot of damage mitigation. Large Form and Powerful Build won’t see use on a Rogue.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: The Halfling is tailor made for the Rogue. Brave covers one of the Rogue’s weakest defenses. Halfling Nimbleness lets you move through enemies’ spaces, allowing you to get past enemies easily when paired with Cunning Action (Disengage). Lucky won’t trigger very often since rogues make so few d20 rolls compared to other martials, but it’s nice insurance. Naturally Stealthy lets you hide behind most of your allies, which is especially useful in environments with few hiding places.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Very similar to the Gnome, but you give up some good things to get resistance to Psychic damage. Gnome is nearly always a better choice.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Roughly comparable to a human with Magic Initiate, but you trade most of the spellcasting for Darkvision and the ability to change the Cantrip. If you just want one Cantrip like True Strike or Booming Blade, Khoravar may be a better choice than Human.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: The temporary hit points from Adrenaline Rush are nice, but with Cunning Action is much less appealing. Relentless Endurance is nice, but if you’re worried about taking too much damage you can hide and rely on sniping.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill. Rogues lean heavily on their Bonus Action, so it will probably be hard to make Shifting useful.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and some innate spellcasting. Only useful for the Arcane Trickster, and even then most of the spells aren’t great choices compared to Sneak Attack.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and spellcasting that you won’t use.

athletics|str.name: Athletics
athletics|str.summary: (Str): Functionally useless. You can use Athletics to bind creatures in chains, but you’re better suited to using Sleight of Hand for manacles or rope.

investigation|int.name: Investigation
investigation|int.summary: (Int): Very helpful, but not as important as Perception.

perception|wis.name: Perception
perception|wis.summary: (Wis): Perception is by far the most important skill in the game, and it’s important enough that several characters in the party should have it even if you’re really good at it.

sleight-of-hand|dex.name: Sleight of Hand
sleight-of-hand|dex.summary: (Dex): Now used to pick locks. If you’re proficient in both Sleight of Hand and Thieves’ Tools, you’ll use the higher of your two modifiers and roll with Advantage.

stealth|dex.name: Stealth
stealth|dex.summary: (Dex): A Rogue without Stealth is a very strange Rogue.

dagger|unknown.name: Dagger
dagger|unknown.summary: Finesse, Light, Thrown, and Nick mastery. Pair with a shortsword and take Piercer.

hand-crossbow|unknown.name: Hand Crossbow
hand-crossbow|unknown.summary: You can use hand crossbows for two-weapon fighting, but there’s very little reason to do so when you could use a hand crossbow and a dagger without eating your bonus action. You need your Bonus Action for Cunning Action.

light-crossbow|unknown.name: Light Crossbow
light-crossbow|unknown.summary: Your best long-range option. If hiding and sniping works for you, this is your weapon of choice.

scimitar|unknown.name: Scimitar
scimitar|unknown.summary: The go-to secondary weapon for two-weapon fighting since it has the largest damage die of any weapon with the Nick property, but if you’re taking Piercer you’ll want to use a dagger instead.

rapier|unknown.name: Rapier
rapier|unknown.summary: A larger damage die than the shortsword, but the ability to make a second attack with a dagger if your first attack misses will easily make up the miniscule difference in damage output.

shortbow|unknown.name: Shortbow
shortbow|unknown.summary: Perfectly fine, but if you can make sniping work, the light crossbow is much better.

shortsword|unknown.name: Shortsword
shortsword|unknown.summary: Finesse, Light, Vex mastery, and works with piercer. Pair with a dagger.

studded-leather|unknown.name: Studded Leather
studded-leather|unknown.summary: You’re going to live in this.

artificer|function.name: Artificer
artificer|function.summary: The Artificer is an interesting option for many rogues. The Artificer’s cantrips include melee cantrips like Booming Blade, and their spellcasting includes a combination of buffs and healing options which can add a lot of utility. Two levels gets you access to Infusions, including powerful options like Enhanced Defense and replicate Magic Item so that you can get Goggles of Night if your race doesn’t have Darkvision. Three levels gets you a subclass, and the Armorer subclass’s Infiltrator Armor offers perpetual advantage on Stealth checks as well as a powerful ranged attack option which you can choose to use with Dexterity and which works with Sneak Attack since it’s a weapon attack. If magic items like a Cloak of Elvenkind are available in your game this is less appealing, but in games where that’s not an option the Artificer is very tempting.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(197); });

barbarian|unknown.name: Barbarian
barbarian|unknown.summary: Unarmored Defense can be an AC boost for the Rogue compared to light armor. Reckless Attack can provide Advantage on attacks without eating your Bonus Action, but it only works with Strength-based attacks, which is a horrible idea for the Rogue.

bard|unknown.name: Bard
bard|unknown.summary: Two levels for more Expertise and a splash of spellcasting.

fighter|depending-on-your-dexterity-modi.name: Fighter
fighter|depending-on-your-dexterity-modi.summary: Fighting Style goes a very long way for the Rogue if you go for Archery, but Two-Weapon Fighting is a trap. Adding 3-5 damage (depending on your Dexterity modifier) really won’t matter compared to your Sneak Attack damage, so stick to Rogue for Two-Weapon Fighting builds. Swashbuckler Rogues might consider the Fencing style and pick up a shield (and possibly even medium armor) so that they can make good use of Panache. The +2 damage outpaces the 1.75 average Sneak Attack damage you get per Rogue level, so a single level won’t cut into your damage output.

monk|unknown.name: Monk
monk|unknown.summary: The Bonus Action attacks can’t apply Sneak Attack, and Unarmored Defense based on Wisdom won’t be any better than studded leather. Monk’s Focus is redundant with Cunning Action. 3 levels for Way of Shadow is a decent option, but that’s a lot of investment to be sneaky in combat when you’re already built to be sneaky in combat.

ranger|unknown.name: Ranger
ranger|unknown.summary: 1 level gets you a Fighting Style and access to Hunter’s Mark, which makes Two-Weapon Fighting slightly more impactful. 3 levels for Gloom Stalker can make your life much easier in many campaigns.

warlock|unknown.name: Warlock
warlock|unknown.summary: You can’t deliver Sneak Attack with Eldritch Blast, and the Warlock’s low-level Invocations aren’t especially useful for the Rogue. If you want spellcasting, Wizard is usually an easier choice.

wizard|and-therefore-sneak-attack.name: Wizard
wizard|and-therefore-sneak-attack.summary: One level gets you some spellcasting, including ritual casting and access to great options like Booming Blade, True Strike, and Find Familiar. Since you have more spell options than Magic Initiate provides, pick up Find Familiar and have your familiar use the Help action to grant you Advantage (and therefore Sneak Attack) on your attacks.

spellcasting|unknown.name: Spellcasting
spellcasting|unknown.summary: The Arcane Trickster’s defining feature. When selecting spells, remember that Sneak Attack requires weapon attacks with Finesse weapons or ranged weapons, so you can’t apply it to spell attacks. Instead, you’ll generally rely on spells like Booming Blade, Shadow Blade, and True Strike.

mage-hand-legerdemain|unknown.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
mage-hand-legerdemain|unknown.summary: Controlling the hand as a Bonus Action means that you can pick locks and pick pockets while you’re doing other things like fighting or casting other spells, and, since the hand is invisible, you can send it off to do those things unnoticed while you and your allies are busy hiding, fighting, carousing, or whatever else you do with your day.

magical-ambush|function.name: Magical Ambush
magical-ambush|function.summary: Since your spell DC likely won’t be as good as that of a dedicated spellcaster, this does a lot to improve the reliability of your offensive spells. I’m still nervous to recommend spells which require saving throws as a go-to option for the Arcane Trickster, but mathematically it makes sense. Disadvantage works out to slightly more than a -3 penalty, so, if your Intelligence is 14 or higher, your spells can be roughly as reliable as those of a Wizard with 20 Intelligence. Magical Ambush requires the Invisible condition, but it does not require you to be actually invisible. When you take the Hide action successfully, you gain the Invisible condition. This means that you can use Cunning Action to Hide, then immediately hit an enemy with Magical Ambush. Remember that this only works on saves made on the same turn that you cast the spell. Repeated saves like those against Hold Person won’t benefit, and neither will spells which don’t call for a save until the beginning of the target’s turn like Web.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); });

versatile-trickster|unknown.name: Versatile Trickster
versatile-trickster|unknown.summary: This won’t benefit you directly, but your other melee allies can benefit a great deal.

spell-thief|unknown.name: Spell Thief
spell-thief|unknown.summary: The obvious use is to steal spells from enemy spellcasters, but, in a game when you might go several levels without seeing a spellcaster, a better option may be to “steal” spells from your party’s other spellcasters. This can be especially helpful if your party has non-Wizard spellcasters.

initiative|unknown.name: Initiative
initiative|unknown.summary: Couple with the Rogue’s high Dexterity, you’ll consistently act early in the initiative order, which is crucial for enabling Surprising Strikes.

surprising-strikes|unknown.name: Surprising Strikes
surprising-strikes|unknown.summary: Not a ton of damage at first, but it’s easily accessible and the scaling keeps this relevant throughout your career. Unfortunately, a poor dice roll means that your signature feature could not function. Note that this applies during the first full round of combat, so if you can manage a second Sneak Attack in that time, you can apply this a second time, too. This may be very difficult, but if you have a Battle Master in the party who also rolled well on initiative, you might get to deal a big pile of damage.

masterful-mimicry|unknown.name: Masterful Mimicry
masterful-mimicry|unknown.summary: Neat, but only situationally useful. This will depend heavily on your own creativity and on your DM’s willingness to play along.

roving-aim|unknown.name: Roving Aim
roving-aim|unknown.summary: This makes Advantage even easier, ensuring that you’ll be able to use Sneak Attack every time.

envenom-weapons|poison.name: Envenom Weapons
envenom-weapons|poison.summary: Cunning Strike (Poison) is great despite targeting Constitution saves. This outright negates the damage cost to use it, making it even better. The bonus damage from this ignores Resistance to Poison damage, but, unfortunately, it doesn’t do anything about Advantage on saves against poison. Creatures with Resistance to Poison damage almost always have Advantage on saves against poison.

death-strike|unknown.name: Death Strike
death-strike|unknown.summary: The damage will be excellent when this works, but targeting a Constitution save makes this unreliable. To lean into this, pile as many damage sources as you can into this attack. Basic Poison, buffs, Booming Blade, Piercer, whatever you can get. Make it hurt. Don’t forget that Surprising Strikes applies, too. While this may be unreliable due to the save, there’s also no limit on its use, so you can use this in every encounter. However, it suffers from the same issue as Assassinate: If you won’t beat an enemy on initiative, it won’t work at all.

bloodthirst|unknown.name: Bloodthirst
bloodthirst|unknown.summary: This provides an easy way to get an extra Sneak Attack by attacking outside of your turn. Do not use this when you were the one to make a creature to Bloodied, and you’ll get essentially no benefit from doing so. You only get this a few times per day, and you need to make it count.

bane|unknown.name: Bane
bane|unknown.summary: The damage resistance is only situationally useful, but the Cantrip is fantastic.

bhaal|unknown.name: Bhaal
bhaal|unknown.summary: Resistance to an extremely common damage type and a Cantrip which will boost your defenses.

myrkul|unknown.name: Myrkul
myrkul|unknown.summary: The damage resistance is only situationally useful, and you have absolutely no reason to use the cantrip.

terrify|unknown.name: Terrify
terrify|unknown.summary: A fantastic debuff for hardly any cost. Getting Advantage on your future attacks against the target will significantly improve your damage output. This may be effective enough that you don’t need to use Vex weapons.

aura-of-malevolence|unknown.name: Aura of Malevolence
aura-of-malevolence|unknown.summary: This feels very cool, but the actual damage delt is pitiful.

cutthroat|unknown.name: Cutthroat
cutthroat|unknown.summary: Finally some sustainability. We should have gotten this feature a lot sooner, but better late than never, I suppose.

murderous-intent|unknown.name: Murderous Intent
murderous-intent|unknown.summary: This is great insurance if you tend to roll poorly, but it raises the average on a d6 from 3.5 to 4, so it’s not a huge damage boost.

psionic-power|function.name: Psionic Power
psionic-power|function.summary: The most important part of the subclass. Your pool of Psionic Energy Dice are your defining resource. The die size goes from d6 to d12 over the course of your career, and you get more every few levels. It looks like a big pool, but they mostly recharge on a Long Rest, and between long rests you can recharge just one die per Short Rest. If your DM adheres to the Adventuring Day rules described in the DMG, that means you can recharge just two dice per day. Across a full day of adventuring that’s a small pool to work with and you need to be cautious about spending your dice rather than burning through them in the first encounter. The Soulknife’s Psionic Energy Dice are much easier to retain than the Psi Warrior’s because they often aren’t expended if you fail a roll, but you’ll still need to be prudent about when something is worth a die.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); }); : This feature is all about being the best skill monkey. If you fail a check you can roll a die even if the chances are incredibly slim that it will make a difference. There’s no waste if you still don’t make it. nearly every other feature like this in the game requires you to gamble the resource on the possibility of success. That said, there is the incredibly nebulous definition of “success” with regards to certain skills. If you’re making an Investigation check and you don’t find anything because there was nothing to find, did you succeed or did you fail? This is a conversation to have with your group and deciding the answer is beyond the scope of this article, but I have a suggestion for how to run it: because you choose to roll the Psi-die after you see what you rolled and the results of the initial d20 roll, my suggestion is that the Psi-die is only considered spent if the results are tangibly different after rolling it. This way “you still find nothing” doesn’t consume the die. : What if your party always had walkie-talkies? Maybe you’re scouting ahead, maybe your Wizard wants to tell you where the fireball is going to be before they cast it. Rary’s Telepathic Bond is a 5th-level spell, and you’re replicating its effects (mostly) at level 3. Rary’s Telepathic Bond also notably has a 1-hour duration, and you get 1d6 hours (up to 1d12 hours at 17th level). You’re limited to adding 2 allies when you get this (you’re in the group for free), but the number increases with your Proficiency Bonus. Don’t forget: you get this once per day for free, so there’s little reason to not use it.

psi-bolstered-knack|unknown.name: Psi-Bolstered Knack
psi-bolstered-knack|unknown.summary: This feature is all about being the best skill monkey. If you fail a check you can roll a die even if the chances are incredibly slim that it will make a difference. There’s no waste if you still don’t make it. nearly every other feature like this in the game requires you to gamble the resource on the possibility of success. That said, there is the incredibly nebulous definition of “success” with regards to certain skills. If you’re making an Investigation check and you don’t find anything because there was nothing to find, did you succeed or did you fail? This is a conversation to have with your group and deciding the answer is beyond the scope of this article, but I have a suggestion for how to run it: because you choose to roll the Psi-die after you see what you rolled and the results of the initial d20 roll, my suggestion is that the Psi-die is only considered spent if the results are tangibly different after rolling it. This way “you still find nothing” doesn’t consume the die.

psychic-whispers|mostly.name: Psychic Whispers
psychic-whispers|mostly.summary: What if your party always had walkie-talkies? Maybe you’re scouting ahead, maybe your Wizard wants to tell you where the fireball is going to be before they cast it. Rary’s Telepathic Bond is a 5th-level spell, and you’re replicating its effects (mostly) at level 3. Rary’s Telepathic Bond also notably has a 1-hour duration, and you get 1d6 hours (up to 1d12 hours at 17th level). You’re limited to adding 2 allies when you get this (you’re in the group for free), but the number increases with your Proficiency Bonus. Don’t forget: you get this once per day for free, so there’s little reason to not use it.

psychic-blades|unintelligent-creatures-e.name: Psychic Blades
psychic-blades|unintelligent-creatures-e.summary: This is your primary combat option. You can attack with the blades equally well in melee and at range, and, with a range of 60 feet, your range is much greater than that of a Rogue using daggers, making this one of the best options available if you want to be a ranged rogue. The fact that this deals psychic damage is great, too, since it’s so rarely resisted and easily bypasses common resistances to non-magical weapon damage. Oh, and it’s a d6 damage die instead of the dagger’s d4. The Bonus Action attack option is nice, but the comparison to regular two-weapon fighting is a little messy. If you’re using a Nick weapon like a dagger, you can use two-weapon fighting without spending your Bonus Action, leaving it free for Steady Aim or Cunning Action. Psychic Blades’ Bonus Action attack consumes your Bonus Action, but it also applies your ability modifier to damage. You can’t use Psychic Blades with two-weapon fighting because the blades lack the Light property. However, this feature does have some drawbacks. The blades only manifest when you take the Attack action or make an Opportunity Attack, which means that you can’t easily benefit from allies using things like a Battle Master Fighter using Commander’s Strike or Order Domain Clerics’ Voice of Authority feature. Remember that Sneak Attack is once per turn, not per round, so you’re giving up a substantial piece of Rogue optimization. The blades also don’t gain attack bonuses like a magic weapon, and you’re locked into a damage type that some things (unintelligent creatures, especially) have unmitigatable resistance or even immunity to. Carry some daggers, even if they’re only as backup weapons. You can mitigate the off-turn attack limitations somewhat by drawing and stowing a dagger before or after attacking on alternate turns, but that trades your Free Item Interaction every turn for the ability to make meaningful attacks as a Reaction every other turn at most. That’s a hard trade, not to mention how annoying it is. You could also get Fighting Style (Thrown Weapon) which will allow you to draw a dagger as part of the making the Opportunity Attack, but that may not be worth the cost to do so unless you’re really leaning into the ability to Sneak Attack with your Reaction.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

homing-strikes|maybe-you-don-t-want-to-a.name: Homing Strikes
homing-strikes|maybe-you-don-t-want-to-a.source:
maybe you don’t want to attack with both of your
				Psychic Blades every turn; Cunning Action also exists
homing-strikes|maybe-you-don-t-want-to-a.summary: Use this on the last attack of your turn (maybe you don’t want to attack with both of your Psychic Blades every turn; Cunning Action also exists), provided that you can deal Sneak Attack with that attack. If you miss the attack roll, you can try to turn a near miss into a hit. If you still miss, this costs you nothing. If you do hit, you’re trading your Psionic Energy Die for a Sneak Attack. That’s a very good trade a lot of the time. Even so, you don’t want to use this constantly because it will deplete your psionic dice pool too quickly. Use it when you need it to land that crucial blow.

psychic-teleportation|unknown.name: Psychic Teleportation
psychic-teleportation|unknown.summary: A Bonus Action short-ranged teleport. Even moving the minimum of 10 feet is enough to get you out of grapples and many area control effects, as well as through many tight openings like arrow slits. However, if you need to cross a large gap you’ll find that the unpredictable range is frustrating. Fortunately, you choose whether or not you want to teleport after you roll the die, so you never need to worry about accidentally teleporting yourself above a pit of acid or something, but you’re committing to spend the die before you roll it. Look for other options if you’re not likely to get as far as you need to go.

psychic-veil|unknown.name: Psychic Veil
psychic-veil|unknown.summary: Invisibility for a full hour, and you get it once per day for free. An hour is a long time, and you can do a lot of things without breaking Invisibility, including things like disarming traps and taking the Help action to help allies in combat. Combined with Psychic Whispers and Expertise, you’re an amazing Scout. You can spend a Psionic Energy Die to recharge Psychic Veil, but that’s an easy way to spend your dice very quickly when mundane Stealth checks will often suffice. Save this for when you actually need it.

rend-mind|unknown.name: Rend Mind
rend-mind|unknown.summary: Note quite as good as Hold Monster, but about as close as you can get without casting it. Stunned takes the target out of the fight and makes it very easy to kill them. Since the DC is Dexterity-based your DC will match that of spellcasters, and the one-minute duration is nice. You get this once per day for free, but spending a quarter of your Psionic Energy Dice to recharge it is very costly, so you need to save this for powerful single foes rather than using this in every encounter. If your target may have Legendary Resistances, hit them with Cunning Strike effects to cut through them before attempting Rend Mind.

sleight-of-hand|function.name: Sleight of Hand
sleight-of-hand|function.summary: Fast Hands: : You will rarely need to disarm traps or pick locks in combat. : Check the text of the Utilize action in the Rules Glossary. “When an object requires an action for its use, you take the Utilize action.” This covers caltrops, healer’s kits, dousing a space in oil, binding a creature in manacles, and many other uses. This is fantastically versatile. This also lets you take the Magic action as a Bonus Action in order to use a magic item. Most magic items with an activated ability require you to take the Magic action to use it, so this allows you to use scrolls, wands, and many other items as a Bonus Action. Using a scroll of True Strike, Green-Flame Blade, or Booming Blade is especially powerful here. Since they allow you to make a weapon attack, you can deal Sneak Attack using your Bonus Action, thereby leaving your Action free. You can then use your Action to Ready an attack outside of your own turn, allowing you to deal Sneak Attack twice in a single round.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });

sleight-of-hand|unknown.name: Sleight of Hand
sleight-of-hand|unknown.summary: You will rarely need to disarm traps or pick locks in combat.

use-an-object|function.name: Use an Object
use-an-object|function.summary: Check the text of the Utilize action in the Rules Glossary. “When an object requires an action for its use, you take the Utilize action.” This covers caltrops, healer’s kits, dousing a space in oil, binding a creature in manacles, and many other uses. Most magic items with an activated ability require you to take the Magic action to use it, so this allows you to use scrolls, wands, and many other items as a Bonus Action. Using a scroll of True Strike, Green-Flame Blade, or Booming Blade is especially powerful here. Since they allow you to make a weapon attack, you can deal Sneak Attack using your Bonus Action, thereby leaving your Action free. You can then use your Action to Ready an attack outside of your own turn, allowing you to deal Sneak Attack twice in a single round.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });

climber|unknown.name: Climber
climber|unknown.summary: The next best thing to a fly speed.

jumper|unknown.name: Jumper
jumper|unknown.summary: Jumping isn’t always useful in a game with magical flight, but the ability to jump long distances can be helpful for getting past obstacles like pits and difficult terrain.

stealth-attack|unknown.name: Stealth Attack
stealth-attack|unknown.summary: What if your Sneak Attack was also a Stealth Attack? Yeah, the name isn’t fantastic. But the effect allows you to move out of cover, attack, then return to cover without needing to hide again. This allows you to snipe without constantly spending your Bonus Action to Hide again, allowing you to Dash in order to move much greater distances, to use your Bonus Action with Fast Hands, or to do whatever else you like. Keep in mind that Cunning Strike only triggers if your Sneak Attack hits. If you miss, you’re exposed and you’ll need to Hide again.

attunement|unknown.name: Attunement
attunement|unknown.summary: By this level, Attunement has almost certainly become a limitation. Adding a 4th attunement items gives you a lot of extra power. You’re not an Artificer, but 4 is still good.

charges|unknown.name: Charges
charges|unknown.summary: A 1 in 6 chance to matter is not a lot, but if you’re collecting items that run on charges, this can extend their usefulness a bit. Getting lucky with a Ring of Wishes would feel really nice.

scrolls|unknown.name: Scrolls
scrolls|unknown.summary: Spell scrolls offer a ton of potentially utility. Do not use them offensively. Also, you need to make an Arcana check, so I hope you got proficiency in Arcana somehow since you will need to make an Arcana check to use the scroll.

thief-s-reflexes|unknown.name: Thief’s Reflexes
thief-s-reflexes|unknown.summary: Two entire turns is crazy. You can Sneak Attack twice and use Fast Hands to activate two scrolls, possibly all before enemies get a chance to act if your initiative roll was really good.

acid-splash|phb.name: Acid Splash
acid-splash|phb.summary: Rogues are at their best when they’re focused on dealing big damage to single targets. Acid Splash won’t help you with that. It’s tempting to add area damage to your options, but the gap in how much damage Acid Splash does compared to Sneak Attack is massive, especially when you consider other things like Cunning Strike and Weapon Mastery.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

blade-ward|phb.name: Blade Ward
blade-ward|phb.summary: Excellent for any melee build, but not worth the Action to cast it in combat. If you can cast this before walking into a fight, it’s fantastic.

booming-blade|scag-tcoe.name: Booming Blade
booming-blade|scag-tcoe.summary: Attack, then use Cunning Action to Disengage. Instant hit-and-run tactics, and enemies take extra damage if they chase you.

create-bonfire|eepc-xgte.name: Create Bonfire
create-bonfire|eepc-xgte.summary: The damage isn’t as good as a Sneak Attack, but rogues don’t have a lot of spells which require Concentration so if you can set this up before combat or on a turn when you can’t deliver a Sneak Attack it could provide some useful area control.

dancing-lights|phb.name: Dancing Lights
dancing-lights|phb.summary: An amusing distraction, but you can usually accomplish the same thing using Mage Hand and a candle or torch.

encode-thoughts|unknown.name: Encode Thoughts
encode-thoughts|unknown.summary: Too situational. It’s a neat idea for a thieves’ guild to use this, but you just can’t afford space for it.

friends|phb.name: Friends
friends|phb.summary: Despite being built around Intelligence, you might make room for Charisma-based skills. An easy way to quickly charm a creature can be very helpful, though watch our for the 1-minute duration and the consequences when it ends.

frostbite|xgte.name: Frostbite
frostbite|xgte.summary: Maybe useful once you get Magical Ambush, but it’s a stretch.

green-flame-blade|scag-tcoe.name: Green-Flame Blade
green-flame-blade|scag-tcoe.summary: Allows you to attack two enemies at once, which rogues are generally bad at doing. But you can’t guarantee that enemies will be positioned for the secondary damage, so this is inherently situational.

gust|eepc.name: Gust
gust|eepc.summary: The push effect is too weak to justify. This could be useful if it didn’t have Verbal components because you could use it to create distractions while sneaking, but you still need to break stealth to cast it.

infestation|xgte.name: Infestation
infestation|xgte.summary: Not useful enough to use instead of attacking.

lightning-lure|scag-tcoe.name: Lightning Lure
lightning-lure|scag-tcoe.summary: Not useful enough to use instead of attacking

message|phb.name: Message
message|phb.summary: Conceptually great for a Rogue, but it’s only situationally useful.

mind-sliver|phb.name: Mind Sliver
mind-sliver|phb.summary: An amazing cantrip, but it won’t deliver Sneak Attack.

prestidigitation|phb.name: Prestidigitation
prestidigitation|phb.summary: Versatile and fantastic, a creative rogue can do a lot between this and Minor Illusion. For suggestions on how to use Prestidigitation to its fullest, see our Practical Guide to Prestidigitation.

sword-burst|scag-tcoe.name: Sword Burst
sword-burst|scag-tcoe.summary: Run into a crowd, Sword Burst, Cunning Action (Disengage).

toll-the-dead|phb.name: Toll the Dead
toll-the-dead|phb.summary: Fine damage, but it won’t deliver Sneak Attack.

true-strike|phb.name: True Strike
true-strike|phb.summary: The go-to attack option for ranged builds, True Strike allows you to build around Intelligence and attack both in melee and at range equally well. Booming Blade may have more tactical impact and potentially better damage, but it only works in melee.

absorb-elements|xgte.name: Absorb Elements
absorb-elements|xgte.summary: Very powerful, but Rogues get both Uncanny Dodge and Evasion, so this isn’t as useful for you as for other characters.

alarm|phb.name: Alarm
alarm|phb.summary: Not useful enough to prepare permanently.

charm-person|phb.name: Charm Person
charm-person|phb.summary: A great option for handling social situations, especially once you have Magical Ambush.

comprehend-languages|phb.name: Comprehend Languages
comprehend-languages|phb.summary: Not useful enough to prepare permanently.

detect-magic|phb.name: Detect Magic
detect-magic|phb.summary: Essential in any party, but hopefully someone else can cast it.

disguise-self|phb.name: Disguise Self
disguise-self|phb.summary: Situationally useful. If your game involves a lot of social situations and intrigure, this may be very useful.

distort-value|ai.name: Distort Value
distort-value|ai.summary: Too situational, though it does feel very thematic for the Rogue.

earth-tremor|eepc-xgte.name: Earth Tremor
earth-tremor|eepc-xgte.summary: Not a good fit for the Rogue.

feather-fall|phb.name: Feather Fall
feather-fall|phb.summary: Every party should have it, but hopefully someone else can cast it.

find-familiar|phb.name: Find Familiar
find-familiar|phb.summary: Familiars are extremely useful, and you can cast this as a ritual. An owl can move into melee range, then Dash away using its Flyby ability to avoid provoking Opportunity Attacks. This allows you to easily target foes for Sneak Attack with very little effort on top of the other fantastic benefits of having a familiar. I just wish that the owl wasn’t so significantly better than every other option so that there was a good reason to consider other types of familiars

fog-cloud|phb.name: Fog Cloud
fog-cloud|phb.summary: Useful for covering your escape, and Darkvision can’t see through it.

grease|phb.name: Grease
grease|phb.summary: Potentially useful for knocking enemies prone before you rush into melee to attack.

identify|phb.name: Identify
identify|phb.summary: Leave this to a full spellcaster if anyone bothers to use it at all. Cursed items are rare, the rules for identifying magic items are generous.

jump|phb.name: Jump
jump|phb.summary: A huge improvement to mobility for a melee build, but wait to take this until you have a few spell slots to throw around.

longstrider|phb.name: Longstrider
longstrider|phb.summary: An easy mobility boost with a long duration.

mage-armor|phb.name: Mage Armor
mage-armor|phb.summary: This will raise your maximum AC by 1 compared to Studded Leather. That’s a great benefit if you don’t expect to find magic armor in your game.

magic-missile|phb.name: Magic Missile
magic-missile|phb.summary: Reliable damage, but not enough of it.

protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.name: Protection from Evil and Good
protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.summary: A good defensive buff against a large number of creatures, but not consistently useful enough for you to prepare permanently since you’re not your party’s Defender.

shield|phb.name: Shield
shield|phb.summary: In most cases, this is redundant with Uncanny Dodge. However, Shield boosts your AC until your next turn, potentially negating multiple attacks. In situations where you’re being targeted with numerous attacks, Shield will be considerably more protective than Uncanny Dodge. Still, in those situations ideally you have a tanky ally like a fighter to draw attention, or you’re using other spells like Blur or Mirror Image to protect yourself.

silent-image|phb.name: Silent Image
silent-image|phb.summary: While not nearly as powerful as Major Image, if you just want an object or a visual effect, Silent Image does the job just as well. Throw up a fake wall, door, or portcullis to slow pursuers. Create a piece of furniture like a box or a chest, then hide inside it and stab people when they try to open it like a pointy jack in the box. Illusions are limited more by your creativity (and your DM’s willingness to play along) than by the spell’s text.

silvery-barbs|scoc.name: Silvery Barbs
silvery-barbs|scoc.summary: Extremely powerful, but also very complicated. See my blog post on Silvery Barbs for details on the numerous abuse cases which the spell allows.

sleep|phb.name: Sleep
sleep|phb.summary: A powerful save-or-suck spell at any level. Once you have Magical Ambush, you can incapacitate one or more creatures turn 1 and potentially remove them from the fight entirely.

spellfire-flare|frhof.name: Spellfire Flare
spellfire-flare|frhof.summary: Spell attacks will not help you.

snare|xgte.name: Snare
snare|xgte.summary: Not useful enough to prepare permanently.

thunderwave|phb.name: Thunderwave
thunderwave|phb.summary: If you need to get away from enemies, Cunning Action (Disengage).

unseen-servant|phb.name: Unseen Servant
unseen-servant|phb.summary: A nice utility, but not consistently useful enough to prepare permanently.

wardaway|frhof.name: Wardaway
wardaway|frhof.summary: A weaker version of Tasha’s Mind Whip, Wardaway makes some huge trades to fit into a level 1 spell. The damage is obviously much worse, but that’s not why you’re here. The target still gets to move an act in the same turn, but halving their speed is still impactful. The biggest limitation is that Wardaway uses a Constitution save instead of a much more reliable Intelligence save. At low levels where enemies have very few saving throw proficiencies, Wardaway may be decently reliable. But enemies at low levels also rarely have Bonus Actions, so they’re likely to fail the save and barely notice the spell’s effect. If you are going to upcast this, cast Tasha’s Mind Whip instead.

arcane-vigor|phb.name: Arcane Vigor
arcane-vigor|phb.summary: Your only option for self healing, but healing in combat is rarely a good idea, and this is very expensive.

augury|phb.name: Augury
augury|phb.summary: As much as I love this spell, it’s not useful enough to prepare permanently.

blindness-deafness|phb.name: Blindness/Deafness
blindness-deafness|phb.summary: Constitution saves are unreliable, but Magical Ambush will mitigate that significantly, making this a powerful debuff.

blur|phb.name: Blur
blur|phb.summary: A fantastic defensive buff, especially if you’re fighting in melee where you’re going to be targeted by a lot of attacks.

borrowed-knowledge|unknown.name: Borrowed Knowledge
borrowed-knowledge|unknown.summary: A great way to pretend to be good at a skill for a little. It appears to work with Reliable Talent, so with this spell running you may be more reliable at any skill than anyone else in the party.

cloud-of-daggers|phb.name: Cloud of Daggers
cloud-of-daggers|phb.summary: Without a way to force enemies into the AOE, this will see very little use.

continual-flame|phb.name: Continual Flame
continual-flame|phb.summary: Not useful enough to prepare permanently.

darkness|phb.name: Darkness
darkness|phb.summary: Without the ability to see in magical darkness, this is no more useful than Fog

darkvision|phb.name: Darkvision
darkvision|phb.summary: is crucial for a class that benefits so much from fighting in the dark, so if you don’t have this from your race or from an ally, you should strongly consider it.

dragon-s-breath|unknown.name: Dragon’s Breath
dragon-s-breath|unknown.summary: Your attacks will do more damage than spending your Action to use the breath weapon. This may be appealing if you can cast it on a familiar.

dust-devil|eepc.name: Dust Devil
dust-devil|eepc.summary: Too situational. If you desperately need a push effect, get Gust of Wind.

earthbind|unknown.name: Earthbind
earthbind|unknown.summary: Use Cunning Action to hide, then Sneak Attack with a ranged weapon. Snipe your enemies out of the sky if they’re dumb enough to be a flying target.

elminster-s-elusion|frhof.name: Elminster’s Elusion
elminster-s-elusion|frhof.summary: Situational by design since you only need this against spells and magic effects, which not every enemy can produce. You already have Evasion to cover Dexterity saves, but your other saves are weak by comparison, so Advantage on those saves may be very helpful. It’s often easier to hide so that you can’t be targeted, though that isn’t always an option.

enhance-ability|phb.name: Enhance Ability
enhance-ability|phb.summary: Fantastically useful in situations where you or an ally are making a lot of ability checks at once, such as in social situations.

gift-of-gab|ai.name: Gift of Gab
gift-of-gab|ai.summary: Are you playing a silver-tongued rogue, but in real life you’re barely able to string two syllables together? Here’s your solution. But be warned: while the spell doesn’t allow a saving throw, it only fixes the past 6 seconds.

hold-person|phb.name: Hold Person
hold-person|phb.summary: You get this far too late, and the number of humanoid enemies was reduced significantly in the 2024 rules as many historically humanoid creatures changed creature type.

jim-s-glowing-coin|unknown.name: Jim’s Glowing Coin
jim-s-glowing-coin|unknown.summary: If you can cast this before enemies notice you, it can put your party at a huge advantage. But you can’t always expect that to be an option.

kinetic-jaunt|scoc.name: Kinetic Jaunt
kinetic-jaunt|scoc.summary: This is what Cunning Action is for.

knock|phb.name: Knock
knock|phb.summary: You get proficiency in Thieves’ Tools, you have good Dexterity, and you might also have proficiency or Expertise in Sleight of Hand, which means that you’re really good at picking locks. Bringing a spell that invalidates those capabilities feels silly.

levitate|phb.name: Levitate
levitate|phb.summary: Constitution saves are hard, but lifting an enemy off the ground makes many enemies much less dangerous, often totally removing them from a fight. They only get an initial save, which you can make much more reliable with Magical Ambush, so you may be able to use this to great effect.

locate-object|phb.name: Locate Object
locate-object|phb.summary: Too situational to prepare peraenantly, though it does feel very useful on a Rogue who might do a lot of sneaking and stealing.

magic-mouth|phb.name: Magic Mouth
magic-mouth|phb.summary: Find a way to cast Thaumaturgy to raise your voice’s volume, then cast this spell on a piece of paper and scream into it for as long as you are physically capable. Set the trigger to “when the paper is unfolded”. Leave the paper for someone to find, or use mage hand to open it at a distance. Instant distraction. The material component is inexpensive by the time you can cast this, and the duration is “until dispelled”, so you can carry about a big stack of pre-cast Magic Mouth spells for all sorts of shenanigans. Still, this it too situational to prepare permanently.

magic-weapon|phb.name: Magic Weapon
magic-weapon|phb.summary: A fantastic offensive buff, but you’re only making one attack per weapon, so you won’t get nearly as much use out of this as other characters would.

maximilian-s-earthen-grasp|eepc.name: Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp
maximilian-s-earthen-grasp|eepc.summary: Restraining an enemy makes them easy to Sneak Attack, but this isn’t worth the Action cost when you could Cunning Action (Hide) and Sneak Attack on the same turn.

mirror-image|phb.name: Mirror Image
mirror-image|phb.summary: As effective as Blur (at least until you take a couple hits), and it doesn’t require Concentration.

misty-step|phb.name: Misty Step
misty-step|phb.summary: Fantastic short-range teleportation with only Verbal components, so you can use it to easily escape grapples and restraints.

nystul-s-magic-aura|phb.name: Nystul’s Magic Aura
nystul-s-magic-aura|phb.summary: Only situationally useful. Masking yourself as a construct makes you immune to many dangerous spells, but enemies rarely cast those spells.

phantasmal-force|phb.name: Phantasmal Force
phantasmal-force|phb.summary: An excellent save-or-suck at any level, especially since it targets Intelligence saves. Combined with Magical Ambush, this is almost unstoppable.

pyrotechnics|eepc.name: Pyrotechnics
pyrotechnics|eepc.summary: The effects are weak and the required setup is annoying.

ray-of-enfeeblement|phb.name: Ray of Enfeeblement
ray-of-enfeeblement|phb.summary: Con saves are the least reliable save, and the creatures that suffer from this spell will also have high Constitution saves.

rope-trick|phb.name: Rope Trick
rope-trick|phb.summary: Useful, but I really hope that someone else in your party can cast this.

see-invisibility|phb.name: See Invisibility
see-invisibility|phb.summary: Probably your only counter to invisible enemies unless you can get a magic item like a Lantern of Revealing. Maybe skip this if your party has other options like Faerie Fire.

shadow-blade|xgte.name: Shadow Blade
shadow-blade|xgte.summary: Compared to a rapier, the Shadow Blade adds 1d8 damage per attack, it changes to psychic damage (which is resisted by very few creatures), and it adds the Thrown property for some reason. Since it gives you Advantage to attack creatures in dim light or darkness, it will offset Disadvantage for attacking creatures when it’s too dark for you to see. This is a great boost to your damage output. Unfortunately, it doesn’t have Weapon Mastery because it was published under the 2014 rules. You can upcast the spell to increase the damage dice, but you really don’t need to. Guaranteed Advantage while attacking a target in dim light or darkness means that you can easily apply Sneak Attack, and compared to your pile of sneak attack dice the extra d8 isn’t worth your extremely limited higher-level spell slots. Unfortunately, attack cantrips including Booming Blade and True Strike both require you to use a weapon with a monetary value, which means that you can’t use them with Shadow Blade.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

shatter|phb.name: Shatter
shatter|phb.summary: The damage isn’t good enough to justify the Action cost.

snilloc-s-snowball-swarm|xgte.name: Snilloc’s snowball swarm
snilloc-s-snowball-swarm|xgte.summary: Shatter. but with less damage and worse damage type.

spider-climb|phb.name: Spider Climb
spider-climb|phb.summary: The next best thing to flight. Very appealing for fighting at range and for bypassing many terrain obstacles.

spray-of-cards|bomt.name: Spray of Cards
spray-of-cards|bomt.summary: The damage is poor, but temporarily blinding a creature on a Dexterity save is potentially powerful against Strength-based enemies, who typically have awful Dexterity saves.

suggestion|phb.name: Suggestion
suggestion|phb.summary: Fantastically versatile and extremely powerful. The fact that you can use this with Magical Ambush feels very silly. Jump out of a barrel and shout “go take the day off” and watch your target load up their belongings and go home for the day. The 2024 version of the spell is insanely abusable because of how permissive it is. RAW you can tell a creature to suffocate themselves to death. I recommend using the 2014 version of the spell to avoid Suggestion derailing your game.

tasha-s-mind-whip|tcoe.name: Tasha’s Mind Whip
tasha-s-mind-whip|tcoe.summary: Not a lot of damage, but it’s on an Intelligence save, and it severely limits your target’s action options, making this a powerful offensive option at any level.

vortex-warp|scoc.name: Vortex Warp
vortex-warp|scoc.summary: Very good, but it doesn’t affect you, so this is best left to full spellcasters.

warding-wind|xgte.name: Warding Wind
warding-wind|xgte.summary: A moving sphere of difficult terrain centered on you. This can make it difficult for enemies to get into melee with you, which can make hit-and-run tactics very simple. But you may be better served by using Cunning Action to move in and out of range of your enemies’ movement.

web|phb.name: Web
web|phb.summary: Fantastic area control at any level even if your Intelligence is relatively poor.

animate-dead|phb.name: Animate Dead
animate-dead|phb.summary: You don’t have enough spell slots to keep your undead under control.

antagonize|bomt.name: Antagonize
antagonize|bomt.summary: Attacking stuff is your job. This should never do more damage than your own attacks.

ashardalon-s-stride|ftod.name: Ashardalon’s Stride
ashardalon-s-stride|ftod.summary: You have Cunning Action if you need to move around without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

bestow-curse|phb.name: Bestow Curse
bestow-curse|phb.summary: A powerful debuff, but against most creatures you’ll get better results from just killing them.

blink|phb.name: Blink
blink|phb.summary: An interesting defensive option which doesn’t require Concentration, but you can easily make yourself untargetable with Cunning Action (Hide) in many situations.

catnap|xgte.name: Catnap
catnap|xgte.summary: Only situationally useful, and you should not be the one to cast it.

clairvoyance|phb.name: Clairvoyance
clairvoyance|phb.summary: A great scouting option, but Rogues are built for scouting and you get very few spell slots.

conjure-constructs|frhof.name: Conjure Constructs
conjure-constructs|frhof.summary: The damage and the Action economy are terrible, but you might use this between encounters to provide Temporary Hit Points to your whole party. That’s a very expensive way to get a few THP for a subclass that gets one level 4 spell slot.

counterspell|phb.name: Counterspell
counterspell|phb.summary: Helpful, but only situationally useful, and you almost certainly don’t have the room to prepare this on a daily basis without major sacrifices.

dispel-magic|phb.name: Dispel Magic
dispel-magic|phb.summary: If your party doesn’t have someone else who can cast Dispel Magic by the time it’s an option for you, you’re probably all dead.

enemies-abound|xgte.name: Enemies Abound
enemies-abound|xgte.summary: Astoundingly few enemies have good Intelligence saves, especially big scary melee monsters. Throw this on something tanky and horrifying that’s there to protect squishy enemies from you and your friends, and watch it freak out and kill its buddies for you. The duration is only a minute, and obviously this only works in an encounter with multiple enemies, but that doesn’t make the spell less awesome.

erupting-earth|eepc-xgte.name: Erupting Earth
erupting-earth|eepc-xgte.summary: Not enough damage to compete with Fireball, and not enough difficult terrain to justify the spell slot.

fast-friends|ai.name: Fast Friends
fast-friends|ai.summary: You won’t use this enough to justify one of your extremely limited preparation slots. Cast Suggestion instead.

fear|phb.name: Fear
fear|phb.summary: A great way to disable groups of opponents, but fear immunity is common. Somewhere an Arcane Trickster has made a habit of using Magical Ambush to leap from cover, shout “Boo!”, and cause entire encounters to drop their weapons and flee.

fireball|phb.name: Fireball
fireball|phb.summary: Rogues are very good at killing big, singular enemies, but they’re bad at handling crowds of weak enemies. Fireball neatly fills that gap. Even if you’re surrounded, you’re proficient in Dexterity saves and have Evasion. Drop a Fireball at you’re feet, and you’ll probably come out in better shape than your enemies will.

flame-arrows|xgte.name: Flame Arrows
flame-arrows|xgte.summary: Bad. A total of 12d6 damage is not enough for a level 3 spell slot, and that’s assuming that you manage to make 12 qualifying attacks in the 1-hour duration and hit with them. A Rogue is arguably the most likely to make this work, but it’s just not enough damage.

fly|phb.name: Fly
fly|phb.summary: It’s hard to overstate how powerful flight is.

gaseous-form|phb.name: Gaseous Form
gaseous-form|phb.summary: If anyone were to use this to great effect, it would be a Rogue. But it’s still only situationally useful, so it’s hard to justify preparing it permanently.

glyph-of-warding|phb.name: Glyph of Warding
glyph-of-warding|phb.summary: Depending on how your DM handles it, this is either a situationally useful defensive measure or a reality-bending way to break the game from the comfort of your own home. See our Practical Guide to Glyph of Warding.

haste|phb.name: Haste
haste|phb.summary: Used as intended, Haste is a decent short-term buff that will give you either some extra movement or an additional chance to hit if your one attack per turn misses. In most cases, you can get the same benefits from your Bonus Action by using Cunning Action for movement or Two-Weapon Fighting for an additional attack. But Haste also has an abuse case which you can use to reliably get a Sneak Attack outside of your turn. On your own turn, use the bonus Action from Haste to attack. If you miss, you’ve still taken the Attack action on your turn, so you still qualify for two-weapon fighting if you need another attack (and provided that you meet the other requirements). Then spend your normal Action to take the Ready action. Use a sufficiently broad condition like “anyone other than me moves or acts”, and choose to attack as your response to the condition. Then when someone else tries to do something you can attack using your Reaction, potentially dealing another Sneak Attack (remember that Sneak Attack is once per turn, not once per round).

hypnotic-pattern|phb.name: Hypnotic Pattern
hypnotic-pattern|phb.summary: Use Magical Ambush, save-or-suck the entire encounter, then quickly eliminate enemies one at a time. Barring resistance/immunity to Charmed, you’re basically unstoppable.

intellect-fortress|tcoe.name: Intellect Fortress
intellect-fortress|tcoe.summary: Technically situational, but an absolutely spectacular defense against enemies which rely on spells or common effects like charm and fear effects. Unlike species traits like the Gnome’s Cunning or the Satyr and Yuan-Ti’s Magic Resistance, this applies to all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws, providing broad and effective protection against many of the most dangerous save-or-suck effects in the game. You also get resistance to Psychic damage, which is nice if you’re fighting mind flayers, aboleths, or Bards who enjoy Vicious Mockery. With a 1-hour duration, the Concentration requirement can be problematic, but it also means that you can carry this through multiple encounters at low cost, so in situations where you need this it’s not going to eat all of your spell slots.

laerel-s-silver-lance|frhof.name: Laerel’s Silver Lance
laerel-s-silver-lance|frhof.summary: The damage type is fantastic, the Prone effect is great, very few area damage spells target Strength saves, and you can omit targets to avoid hitting friends. There’s definitely a niche here, but 3d10 (avg. 16.5) is very low compared to other level 3 spells. Lightning Bolt is 8d6 (avg. 28), and upcasting Laerel’s Silver Lance actually widens that gap. Preparing this and buying the 250 gp spell component feels like too much investment for the extremely narrow case where you can justify using this over other damage spells.

leomund-s-tiny-hut|phb.name: Leomund’s Tiny Hut
leomund-s-tiny-hut|phb.summary: Tiny Hut is a great place to rest, and you can cast it as a ritual. Leave it to a full caster if you can.

lightning-bolt|phb.name: Lightning Bolt
lightning-bolt|phb.summary: Line AOEs are really hard. Use Fireball.

major-image|phb.name: Major Image
major-image|phb.summary: Fantastically versatile, and creatures don’t make a saving throw. Instead, they need to know to touch the illusion or make an Intelligence (Investigation) check, or they need to physically interact with the illusion.
