Even then, you can buy yourself a great deal of time while the target tries to figure out your illusion.

nondetection|phb.name: Nondetection
nondetection|phb.summary: Good, but not totally essential. Divination spells include things like See Invisibility, so if you or your party relies on invisibility of any kind this protects from several magical countermeasures to both stealth and invisibility. However, most enemies aren’t spellcasters and won’t have access to those divination options, so you can’t justify casting this every day. The spell also has an expensive material component specifically to deter you from casting this all the time. Still, with an 8-hour duration, if you need this spell it’s going to do exactly what you need it to do.

phantom-steed|phb.name: Phantom Steed
phantom-steed|phb.summary: By the time you can cast this, your allies can likely produce much better ways to travel long distances.

protection-from-energy|phb.name: Protection from Energy
protection-from-energy|phb.summary: You have Evasion and you can cast Absorb Elements. You won’t get enough out of this to justify preparing it permanently.

sleet-storm|phb.name: Sleet Storm
sleet-storm|phb.summary: Not useful enough to make it more appealing than Fireball or Hypnotic Pattern.

slow|phb.name: Slow
slow|phb.summary: A good debuff, but it won’t help you do Rogue things.

spirit-shroud|tcoe.name: Spirit Shroud
spirit-shroud|tcoe.summary: With only one or two attacks per turn, this isn’t worth the spell slot.

stinking-cloud|phb.name: Stinking Cloud
stinking-cloud|phb.summary: While this can rob targets of their Action if they fail the save, the area is small and easy to escape.

summon-fey|phb.name: Summon Fey
summon-fey|phb.summary: Decent summons, but no unique synergy. The Tricksy version’s ability to summon magical darkness is neat, but it doesn’t help you since you can’t see in magical darkness. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-lesser-demons|xgte.name: Summon Lesser Demons
summon-lesser-demons|xgte.summary: You can’t control the demons, and they’re probably not strong enough to win an encounter on their own. The material component may also be problem since it has a 24 freshness timer. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-shadowspan|tcoe.name: Summon Shadowspan
summon-shadowspan|tcoe.summary: The sneakiest summon option, but the ability to hide as a Bonus Action sometimes does not make this any better for a Rogue than for anyone else. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-undead|phb.name: Summon Undead
summon-undead|phb.summary: Several excellent combat options, and the ghostly option can fly around and do stuff for you. The Skeletal option is an effective ranged attacker, and it can easily out damage any of your other spell options if you can fit multiple encounters into the 1-hour duration. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

sylun-s-viper|frhof.name: Syluné’s Viper
sylun-s-viper|frhof.summary: Bonus Action casting time, 1-hour duration, no Concentration. The damage is horrid, and poison immunity is obviously a problem, but the ability to make a target Incapacitated on hit means that you can lock a single target out of a fight for as long as you can reliably hit them with attacks. The Incapacitation effect doesn’t allow a save, so even Legendary Resistance won’t protect enemies from this. You also get a climb speed so that you can climb out of reach and bite enemies from safety. The spell’s biggest weakness is the Temporary Hit Points. You only get 15, and the spell ends early once you’re out of THP. Plan to hide as a Bonus Action to make yourself hard to target and also to get Advantage on the Spell Attack.

thunder-step|xgte.name: Thunder Step
thunder-step|xgte.summary: Use Misty Step and reserve your Action for attacking.

tongues|phb.name: Tongues
tongues|phb.summary: If you’re built to be decent in social situations, this could be useful, but most Arcane Tricksters dump Charisma and related skills.

wall-of-sand|eepc-xgte.name: Wall of Sand
wall-of-sand|eepc-xgte.summary: Passable area control, but Web will be more effective if the terrain supports it.

wall-of-water|eepc-xgte.name: Wall of Water
wall-of-water|eepc-xgte.summary: This makes it hard for you to engage enemies. Wall of Sand is more useful.

arcane-eye|phb.name: Arcane Eye
arcane-eye|phb.summary: Scouting safely is important, and it’s a major part of the Rogue’s role in the party. Still, you’ve been scouting for 18 levels without this and you’ve somehow survived this long.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

backlash|frhof.name: Backlash
backlash|frhof.summary: You have Uncanny Dodge and Evasion, which should cover the vast majority of damage source which might justify using this. If you want additional protection, prepare Absorb Elements and/or Shield.

banishment|phb.name: Banishment
banishment|phb.summary: A fantastic save-or-suck, especially with Magical Ambush. Start an encounter by banishing the biggest thing in the fight that doesn’t have Legendary Resistance, them clean up whatever’s left before your target can come back.

charm-monster|phb.name: Charm Monster
charm-monster|phb.summary: If you’re trying to be friendly, use Enhance Ability. If you’re trying to compel and enemy to do something you want, use Suggestion.

conjure-minor-elementals|phb.name: Conjure Minor Elementals
conjure-minor-elementals|phb.summary: Fantastic more many characters relying on attack rolls, but you’re likely only making two attacks per turn at most, so you won’t benefit as much as most characters who would use this.

dimension-door|phb.name: Dimension Door
dimension-door|phb.summary: While Misty Step solves the vast majority of your teleportation needs (especially in combat), Dimension Door has considerably longer range and doesn’t require line of sight, thus allowing you to quickly infiltrate or escape an area which might otherwise be impenetrable.

fire-shield|phb.name: Fire Shield
fire-shield|phb.summary: You should not be drawing enough attacks to justify this.

greater-invisibility|phb.name: Greater Invisibility
greater-invisibility|phb.summary: Probably the most important spell that anyone can cast on a rogue.

hallucinatory-terrain|phb.name: Hallucinatory Terrain
hallucinatory-terrain|phb.summary: Unless you specifically need the 24-hour duration and the massive area of effect, Major Image will suffice.

ice-storm|phb.name: Ice Storm
ice-storm|phb.summary: Terrible. Bad damage, and the difficult terrain doesn’t last long enough.

mordenkainen-s-faithful-hound|phb.name: Mordenkainen’s Faithful Hound
mordenkainen-s-faithful-hound|phb.summary: Decent for defending a specific point, but not useful enough to be your only level 4 spell each day.

mordenkainen-s-private-sanctum|phb.name: Mordenkainen’s Private Sanctum
mordenkainen-s-private-sanctum|phb.summary: You get one level 4 spell slot every day. Do you really want to spend it on a place to sleep?

otiluke-s-resilient-sphere|phb.name: Otiluke’s Resilient Sphere
otiluke-s-resilient-sphere|phb.summary: Single-target save-or-suck, and you can make it more reliable with Magical Ambush. A good way to take a target out of a fight until you’re ready to handle them.

phantasmal-killer|phb.name: Phantasmal Killer
phantasmal-killer|phb.summary: If you’re going to hit a single target with a spell, you want it to eliminate or incapacitate them in one shot, and Phantasmal Killer simply doesn’t do that.

polymorph|phb.name: Polymorph
polymorph|phb.summary: Normally a fantastic combat option, but your own attacks will greatly exceed anything that you can turn into. You might turn into something just for the massive pool of Temporary Hit Points, but that’s likely not enough to justify your only level 4 spell slot.

spellfire-storm|frhof.name: Spellfire Storm
spellfire-storm|frhof.summary: The damage isn’t great and Constitution saves aren’t reliable, but the AOE is decently large and this can prevent enemies from casting spells. The Con save when casting a spell is identical to Counterspell, so you’re effectively countering every spell that enemies try to cast while in the area. I would only use when facing enemy spellcasters (the damage isn’t good enough otherwise), but with enemy spellcasters on the field this can easily define an encounter. We can also compare Spellfire Storm to Moonbeam, which also creates a column of Radiant damage. Spellfire Storm deals the same damage as Moonbeam cast at the same spell level and uses the same save, but instead of bother Shapeshifters, Spellfire Storm shuts down enemy spellcasters. Spellfire Storm can’t be moved, but the considerably larger radius means that you don’t need to move it in many encounters. In close quarters, enemies may be unable to move out of the area. Of course, that also means that you can’t use forced movement to repeatedly trigger the spell’s damage like you could with area effects which don’t cover the entire battlefield. : 25,000 gp to do this is absolutely insane. This is something that should happen as a plot point, not as a player tactic. Maybe you drop this on an extraplanar gate so that your party can fight waves of demons to shut down the gate or something similarly epic and plot-defining.

spirit-of-death|bomt.name: Spirit of Death
spirit-of-death|bomt.summary: Summon Undead is arguably better, but this is still a good summon. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

stone-shape|phb.name: Stone Shape
stone-shape|phb.summary: This is one of the most useful spells in the game. Castles, dungeons, caves, mountains, and all manner of other locales include an abundance of stone. The ability to reshape that stone to your purposes in an instant is immensely useful. This is a spell limited only by your imagination. A 5-foot cube is plenty of space to wreak all kinds of havoc if you’re clever.

storm-sphere|eepc-xgte.name: Storm Sphere
storm-sphere|eepc-xgte.summary: Passable area control for an extended fight, but the damage is poor, and 1 minute of this probably isn’t enough for your single level 4 spell slot. Sickening Radiance is much better.

summon-aberration|phb.name: Summon Aberration
summon-aberration|phb.summary: Three diverse and effective combat options. If you can keep the summon alive for the full duration, it’s a great way to get an ally into melee with enemies so that you can use Sneak Attack. Even barring that, summons are pretty great in combat. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-construct|phb.name: Summon Construct
summon-construct|phb.summary: Not as effective offensively as Summon Aberration, but all three summoned constructs are unusually durable for creatures summoned by similar spells. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

summon-elemental|phb.name: Summon Elemental
summon-elemental|phb.summary: Summon Aberration is better offensively, and Summon Construct provides a more durable summon. Summon Elemental’s biggest advantage is that you can summon a creature that can fight effectively underwater, but even then it’s not a great summon. For more help, see our Practical Guide to Summoning Spells.

wall-of-fire|phb.name: Wall of Fire
wall-of-fire|phb.summary: Fantastic area control, but you get it so late that the damage isn’t great, and it won’t help you do Rogue things.

watery-sphere|eepc-xgte.name: Watery Sphere
watery-sphere|eepc-xgte.summary: The primary appeal here is the ability to restrain the target, then drag them around for the spell’s duration, but that consumes your Action, which means that you’re not Sneak Attacking.

sorcery-points|unknown.name: Sorcery Points
sorcery-points|unknown.summary: Sorcery points fuel the Sorcerer’s abilities and allow the class to do much more than just casting spells. You have a limited pool per day, but you have the option of consuming spell slots to get additional Sorcery Points. This pool is fairly limited, so budgeting your Sorcery Points is crucial. If you need more, look at the Metamagic Adept feat and items like the Bloodwell Vial.

flexible-casting|unknown.name: Flexible Casting
flexible-casting|unknown.summary: Using Sorcery Points to get additional spell slots is very expensive, so only do it when you absolutely need to do so. Converting spell slots to Sorcery Points is a bit less daunting once you have a large pool of spell slots, but be sure not to do it too much or you will quickly run out of daily resources. That said, it can be very effective to turn a bunch of Sorcery Points into level 1 spell slots to fuel Absorb Elements and Shield.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Great for starting big area control spells or for dropping big area damage spells before allies get in the way or enemies get into melee range. The second benefit allows you to trade initiative with a willing ally. To maximize this benefit, you want to have numerous allies in combat who roll initiative on their own. A familiar is an easy addition. Between Advantage and a familiar, you effectively get to roll initiative 3 times and choose your favorite.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(189); });

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: Very good, but you can’t afford the Wisdom to keep this effective.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

healer|phb.name: Healer
healer|phb.summary: Terrible. Cast Arcane Vigor or Wither and Bloom, or buy a healing potion.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Most spellcasters don’t rely enough on attack rolls to care about the crit feature, and you already have an easy source of Advantage on attacks from Innate Sorcery. If you’re relying heavly on things like Chromatic Orb and Scorching Ray, this might work for you, but it’s unpredictable.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: A good way to expand your spellcasting. There aren’t any great combinations, but Healing Word may be worthwhile.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Proficiency in Persuasion, and give Heroic Inspiration to your whole party once per day. Excellent on any build if you don’t need a different Origin Feat.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: You won’t use weapons enough for this to matter.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: Hex could combine nicely with Spellfire Flare or Socrching Ray for high single-target damage, but that’s the only consistent appeal. But if you’re going that route, take a level of Warlock to get Eldritch Blast so that you can use Quicken Spell to get more attacs into a signle turn.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Great for covering all of the Face skills so that you can make room for other options, especially in a small party with poor skill coverage.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: The resistance to magic damage will apply to many of the ranged effects which will reach past your party’s melee characters to target you, and the ability to cast Sacred Flame as a Bonus Action a few times per day will save you Sorcery Points spent on Quickened Spell.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: You should literally never make an unarmed strike.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Nice on a class with so little hp, but not impactful enough to justify the feat.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: The Opportunity Attack portion of the feat probably won’t do anything for you, but the ability to give your whole party Advantage on initiative is fantastic on anyone.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: A bit of extra Sorcerer stuff. A buff to Con saves, an extra Cantrip, and an extra prepared spell. Aberrant Surge is the most exciting piece of the feat, and literally no one is better suited to use it than the Sorcerer because you can use Font of Magic to get extra level 1 spell slots. You want to select a level 1 spell which you’ll cast frequently in combat, so pick a staple option like Absorb Elements or Shield which will remain equally effective for your whole career.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(190); });

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: Almost everything here is already on your spell list, and the rest isn’t worth having.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: If you’re planning to build around Conjure Minor Elementals, Hunter’s Mark can be a good stand-in at low levels. Combining Hunter’s Mark with Spellfire Flare or Scorching Rays is decent, inexpensive damage.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: Basically the only thing useful here is Command, which is nowhere near enough. Take Magic Initiate or multiclass.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: Access to all of the essential healing spells without playing Divine Soul.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: The bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) will be very useful, but most of the spells are already on your spell list.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Access to some excellent spells including Find Steed, Pass Without Trace, and Phantom Steed.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: Command is the only spell here that’s worth having and not already on your spell list. Take Magic Initiate.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: The Sorcerer does not have the hit points to support things like Vigilant Guardian and Warding Bond.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Almost all of the spells here are already on your spell list.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Mostly mediocre, but you do get Conjue Minor Elementals, and no one can abuse Conjure Minor Elementals as easily as the Sorcerer thanks to Quicken Spell.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Almost all of the spells are already on your spell list.

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: You have spells to solve these problems.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: This won’t contribute anything meaningful to what you do, but passing out snacks for THP always feels nice.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Blocking line of sight can put enemies at a huge disadvantage, then you can spam AOEs while they stumble around in the fog trying to find you. It’s super annoying for your allies, though.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: Sorcerers don’t have enough options for Bludgeoning damage to make this worthwhile.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: You do not have enough hit points to justify using this.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Sorcerers have no business using weapons enough to justify this.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: If you want to heal yourself as a Bonus Action, cast Arcane Vigor.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Excellent for Draconic Sorcerers since you’re expected to focus on a single type of elemental damage.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: Use Quicken Spell to cast an attack Cantrip as a Bonus Action, debuff your target’s saves, then hit them with a nasty save-or-suck spell on the same turn. If it doesn’t work, the debuff lasts until the end of your next turn, so you can try again!

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells and access to some 1st-level spells from outside of your spell list. Misty Step is great on any spellcaster.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: You should not be using weapons.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: If you want this, start with a level of Fighter.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: You should not taking enough hits to want this.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A massive amount of temporary hit points.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Too situational for a feat that doesn’t give you a useful ability score increase.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational to justify unless you’re in a Underdark campaign or a campaign where vampires feature heavily.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Cleric or Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Standard Bearer is only situationally useful and only works once per day, but can basically win encounters against enemies that rely on Charmed or Frightened, and there are quite a few of those.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Good insurance against difficult mental saves, but without a Charisma increase it’s hard to select this at low levels.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: If you’re proficient in Perception and have decent Wisdom, you may be well qualified to use Perception reliably. But even then, this is only helpful if your DM likes to use stealthy enemies and/or likes to include traps in combat encounters.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: This appears to work with all of True Strike’s damage dice, but be careful about over-investing in a tactic that you fall back on to conserve spell slots.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: There aren’t enough poison spells to justify this.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: You should not be using a polearm to attack stuff.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: You can get easy Advantage on Spell Attacks by activating Innate Sorcery. The THP mechanic is great, but Inspiring Leader will have a much bigger impact.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: You’re already proficient in Constitution saves. You could take this with Dexterity at high levels, but it’s not essential.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: There are some great level 1 Ritual spells like Comprehend Languages and Find Familiar, but the fact that this only lets you get level 1 spells significantly limits its usefulness. Getting rituals from outside of your own spell list is nice, but unless there are specific Rituals that you want, this isn’t worth a feat.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: Not a good fit for the Sorcerer.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: More prepared spells is great, but the level 1 spells aren’t as good as Fey Touched.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Sorcerers are not built to use weapons.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: You don’t get proficiency with shields.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: Great for expanding beyond Face skills or for picking up Face skills which you couldn’t get at level 1.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: You’re not going to use weapons, and there are very few spells that deal Slashing damage.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: If cover or range are issues, use a different spell.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: You have a spells that deal Radiant damage, but you really want AOE Radiant damage spells, and there are very few of those until high level. Even then, your d6 hit dice may not feel impactful.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: You don’t have the Strength to support this.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: An easy go-to option. Remember that creatures can willingly fail saving throws, allowing you to use this on allies in order to move them out of dangerous positions, break grapples, or otherwise help them.

telepathic|phb.name: Telepathic
telepathic|phb.summary: Very cool, but usually talking works fine.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: You have numerous ways to make enemies Charmed, but if you can make them Charmed, you can do something better than set them up for an attack.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Nearly all of the qualifying spells are already on your spell list.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Advantage on Concentration saves will make your Concentration almost unbreakable, but you’re unlike to use Reactive Spell.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: Multiclass into a class that gets Weapon Mastery. A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: This is only useful for melee characters planning to be hit with attacks. If you want Expertise, take Skilled.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is nice, but you miss a big chunk of the feat since you’re not using weapons.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: If you want Advantage, use Innate Sorcery.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: The extra THP is nice if you’re relying on spells like Shapechange and Polymorph, but it’s only 5 extra THP. Maximizing Hit Point Die rolls is also not especially useful since you have d6 hit dice. You could use it with Arcane Vigor to heal as a Bonus Action, but the amount healed is pitiful.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Potentially useful if you’re relying on Polymorph, Bigby’s Hand, or Blade of Disaster.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: A nice safey measure, but building yourself to endure damage won’t solve your small hit point pool due to 19+ levels of d6 hit dice. If you’re worried about dying, cast Wish to cast Clone.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: Basically free Misty Step every time that you cast a spell as an Action. Unfortunately, Bonus Action and Reaction spells don’t qualify. According to the Rules Glossary: “When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.” Outside of combat, you can still use this to get around obstacles. Cast a harmless spell like Prestidigitation and you can teleport without making a mess.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Maximizing the damage on Sunburst once per day is a big pile of damage, but it is only once per day.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: 2d4 averages to 5. Adding +5/-5 to a saving throw can rescue you or an ally, or it can cause an enemy to fail a save. On a d20 scale, 5 means that there’s a 25% chance on any given roll that this will have an impact. Granted, it is still a dice roll, so the smaller the gap, the safer this is to use. On a full caster where save-or-suck spells are such a huge part of your arsenal, this is devastatingly effective. The fact that you can use it once per encounter is amazing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: This works nicely with Polymorph, but Polymorph has been obsolete for a long time, and you don’t get access to Shapechange.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: More hit points are great on a class as frail as the Sorcerer.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: You should not be relying on B/P/S damage enough for Resistance to be an issue. The natural 20 effect could lead to big damage spikes with spells like Scorching Ray, but that’s not enough to make this a good choice unless you’re already built around Scorching Ray.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Dodge as a Bonus Action is a really good defensive option, but you’re probably using your Bonus Action for magic.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance is a great save-or-suck spell, and improving it by preventing enemies from using Verbal components is a great way to mess with enemy spellcasters.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: Take Boon of Dimensional Travel instead.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: If you’re using Font of Magic to create lots of low-level spell slots, such as level 1 slots to cast Absorb Elements and Shield, this could be very useful.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: You have tons of spells that can makes enemies Frightened, then use the Reaction to make them flee. Of course, you could also cast Fear, which already does that.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Resistance/immunity to two damage types, and Transmuted spell suddenly becomes an easy way to give all of your enemies Disadvantage on saves against your spells. Imagine forcing Disadvantage on saves against Meteor Swarm. It’s nice.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Be invisible at all times outside of combat. Take advantage of invisibility at the start of combat, then look for ways to become invisible as frequently as possible. Even if you’re not making attack rolls (and you almost certainly aren’t doing so often), the defensive benefits of invisibility are massive. However, remember that a lot of things are an Action, so it’s very easy to break this invisibility. Notable examples that people easily overlook include Hide, Search, and Study.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: Resistance to two damage types. The healing is negligible. Take Boon of Fortitude instead.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Fantastic, but technically only situationally useful. You can already cast both See Invisibility and Truesight. This is objectively good, but don’t make it your first boon unless you have a very specific reason to do so.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Magic Initiate (Cleric) is great, but the skills aren’t.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(185); });

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, great feat, fantastic skills.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Perfect ability scores, and an easy way to cover all of the Face skills that you need while leaving space for other skill proficiencies.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, bad feat, bad skills.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores and Cult of the Dragon Initiate wants high Wisdom.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: The ability scores are good and the Musician feat is welcome in any party, but it’s hard to waste two skill proficiencies on borderline useless skills.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, good skills. If you want Tough, this is the way to get it. But Sorcerers generally aren’t built to draw a lot of attacks in a way that makes Tough a great choice.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and skills. You already share most of your spell list with the Wizard, though, so you won’t get access to many new options from Magic Initiate (Wizard).

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Bad ability scores. If you want Alert, go for Inquisitive.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and one good skill, but the feat is awful.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and Healer may be worthwhile if your party lacks other healing options, but the skills are poor.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores, one good skill, Lucky. Warfarer is a better choice.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Alert is good, but no Charisma increase, and the skills are bad.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: Good ability scores and Alert, but the skills are poor.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: The ability scores are workable, but not great. The skills are good for a Face. It really comes down to the feat, and Lords’ Alliance Agent is only appealing if you’re going to rely heavily on spell attacks.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and Lucky is an easy feat on any character. The only low point is Animal Handling.

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: If you want Magic Initiate (Druid), this is the best way to get it. The ability scores are good, but the skills are not.

mythalkeeper|frhof.name: Mythalkeeper
mythalkeeper|frhof.summary: Crafter is an awful feat, and the skills aren’t a good enough fit to make this appealing.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: Fine, but Charlatan is a much easier choice.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores, good feat, terrible skills.

rashemi-wanderer|frhof.name: Rashemi Wanderer
rashemi-wanderer|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and skills, but you shouldn’t need Tough.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Magic Initiate (Wizard) is good, but the skills aren’t, and the Sorcerer’s spell list already significantly overlaps with the Wizard’s spell list.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and feat, but the skills are a bad fit.

vampire-devotee|aboh.name: Vampire Devotee
vampire-devotee|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, good skills, and Vampire’s Plaything can get you out of melee a few times per day without relying on teleportation.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores, decent skills, and Lucky is good on any character.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and skills, but half of Zhentarim Ruffian won’t help a single-class Sorcerer.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores and a bit of extra Sorcerer spellcasting.

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores, and you already jave most of the spells.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores and skills are fine, but the feat isn’t great.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. The feat is good, but not enough on its own.

house-lyrandar-heir|efota.name: House Lyrandar Heir
house-lyrandar-heir|efota.summary: Decent, but only remarkable if you want Conjure Minor Elementals.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: A good feat, but the ability scores and skills are bad.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: A decent fit, but most of the spells from the feat are already on your spell list.

house-vadalis-heir|efota.name: House Vadalis Heir
house-vadalis-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are the only redeeming quality.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. Heavenly Wings lets you fly without Concentration, and Necrotic Shroud can discourage enemies from closing to melee. It’s only once per day, but that may be all that you need.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(186); });

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: Nothing here contributes to your capabilities in combat, but it will make you an excellent Face.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and once per day flight are great, but you will likely never use the breath weapon beyond very low levels.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. The durability is largely wasted on a spellcaster fighting from a safe distance, and you have spells to handle hidden and invisible enemies.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great, plus you can get access to some spells from outside of the Sorcerer’s spell list, as well as nicely complementing your limited number of prepared spells.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage doesn’t offer a lot of easy options for full casters, but Cloud Jaunt is fantastic non-spell teleportation, so you can use it the same turn that you cast a leveled spell. Stone’s Endurance is also useful for frail spellcasters. Large Form won’t see much use, but Powerful Build might help you escape grapples if you can’t get out by other means (such as Cloud Jaunt).

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Brave and Lucky are both helpful, and Halfling Nimbleness may help you get past enemies to get into a safer position, though it won’t prevent Opportunity Attacks when you need to leave an enemy’s reach. Naturally Stealthy might let you hide before combat starts, but without Cunning Action it won’t see use in combat.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Very similar to the Gnome, but you give up some good things to get resistance to Psychic damage. Gnome is nearly always a better choice.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: If you want extra spellcasting, Human with Magic Initiate is a better choice. But if you’re happy with one Cantrip (potentially from outside of your spell list) and Darkvision, the Khoravar is still good.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is an excellent option for getting out of dangerous positions quickly without a spell, and the Temporary Hit Points are great on a frail spellcaster. If that doesn’t keep you alive, Relentless Endurance provides some insurance.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Darkvision, an extra skill (probably Intimidation), and a good combat buff from Shifting. Beasthide and Swiftstride are both good ways to keep yourself alive. The biggest challenge is that Shifting may compete for space in your action economy with Innate Sorcery.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: The Tiefling’s innate spellcasting is a good way to expand your limited number of prepared spells, but all of the available spells are already on the Sorcerer’s Spell list.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and you learn Ray of Frost. Not terrible, but not especially exciting. The other spells you get are terrible.

arcana|int.name: Arcana
arcana|int.summary: (Int): One of the most important knowledge skills, but you may not have enough Intelligence to back it up.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(188); });

insight|wis.name: Insight
insight|wis.summary: (Wis): Helpful for a Face, but you may not have enough Wisdom to back it up.

religion|int.name: Religion
religion|int.summary: (Int): One of the most important knowledge skills, but you may not have enough Intelligence to back it up.

dagger|function.name: Dagger
dagger|function.summary: Carry one or two for utility purposes at any level, but the damage isn’t good enough to make it a good idea.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(191); });

light-crossbow|unknown.name: Light Crossbow
light-crossbow|unknown.summary: A light crossbow combined with True Strike will deal more damage than Fire Bolt until you reach level 11, making it the Sorcerer’s go-to attack option at least until level 11.

quarterstaff|unknown.name: Quarterstaff
quarterstaff|unknown.summary: If you’re preparing True Strike to use with a light crossbow, you can also use it with a quarterstaff two-handed for the same amount of damage. You don’t want to do this intentionally, but it’s a good backup option.

artificer|though-the-sorcerer-already-ge.name: Artificer
artificer|though-the-sorcerer-already-ge.source:
though the Sorcerer already
		gets proficiency in Constitution saves, so that’s not as appealing for the
		Sorcerer as it is for the Warlock and the Wizard
artificer|though-the-sorcerer-already-ge.summary: Starting with a level in Artificer gets you a lot. Proficiency in medium armor, shields, and Constitution saving throws are really tempting (though the Sorcerer already gets proficiency in Constitution saves, so that’s not as appealing for the Sorcerer as it is for the Warlock and the Wizard), plus artificers get access to some low-level spells which the Sorcerer doesn’t, like Cure Wounds.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(192); });

bard|unknown.name: Bard
bard|unknown.summary: More Charisma-based spellcasting is nice, and the Bard gets access to both Cure Wounds and Healing Word. Two levels gets your Expertise, which is very tempting, but may not be necessary if you prepare Enhance Ability.

cleric|unknown.name: Cleric
cleric|unknown.summary: A single level for proficiency in heavy armor and shields, and there are plenty of level 1 Cleric spells which don’t care if your Wisdom is relatively poor.

fighter|pick-defense-for-the-ac-bonus.name: Fighter
fighter|pick-defense-for-the-ac-bonus.source:
pick Defense for the AC
		bonus
fighter|pick-defense-for-the-ac-bonus.summary: Starting with 1 level in Fighter gets you heavy armor, shields, a Fighting Style (pick Defense for the AC bonus), Weapon Mastery to make True Strike more effective, and you don’t give up proficiency in Constitution saves.

paladin|unknown.name: Paladin
paladin|unknown.summary: Despite having some dependence on Charisma, the Paladin doesn’t offer the Sorcerer as much as the Fighter does.

rogue|unknown.name: Rogue
rogue|unknown.summary: Expertise would be nice for your Face skills, and Cunning Action gives you a great way to get out of melee.

warlock|unknown.name: Warlock
warlock|unknown.summary: Two levels for Eldritch Blast and Agonizing Blast gives you a powerful and reliable offensive cantrip. Pact Magic Slots can be used to create Sorcery Points, and they recharge on a Short Rest, but you’ll get more out of advancing your Sorcerer levels to get higher-level spell slots sooner.

psionic-spells|unknown.name: Psionic Spells
psionic-spells|unknown.summary: Consistently good almost all the way through. : Mind Sliver is fantastic. Easily my favorite offensive cantrip. : Arms of Hadar is passable as a panic option if you can’t cast Misty Step. Dissonant Whispers lets you force movement, allowing you to trigger Opportunity Attacks from your melee allies, and moving enemies away from you safely so that you never need to cast Arms of Hadar. : Two situationally useful spells. : Hunger of Hadar is an absolutely fantastic AOE damage and area control option. Sending is neat but only situationally useful. : Evard’s Black Tentacles is a good spell, but it does less damage and has a smaller AOE than Hunger of Hadar, and also doesn’t scale with spell level, so there’s a lot of redundancy between the two. Summon Aberration is great, offering three very effective choices to suit your needs. : Two excellent utility options. Rary’s Telepathic Bond feels like a weird choice since you get Telepathic Speech at first level, but Telepathic Speech is extremely limited so Rary’s Telepathic Bond is a big upgrade.

cantrip|unknown.name: Cantrip
cantrip|unknown.summary: Mind Sliver is fantastic. Easily my favorite offensive cantrip.

level-1|unknown.name: Level 1
level-1|unknown.summary: Arms of Hadar is passable as a panic option if you can’t cast Misty Step. Dissonant Whispers lets you force movement, allowing you to trigger Opportunity Attacks from your melee allies, and moving enemies away from you safely so that you never need to cast Arms of Hadar.

level-3|unknown.name: Level 3
level-3|unknown.summary: A staple utility option and an important defensive buff. Not glamorous or flashy, but hard to go without.

level-4|unknown.name: Level 4
level-4|unknown.summary: Freedom of Movement is situationally useful, but helpful against enemies which like to grapple. Summon Construct is a Wizard exclusive, and it’s a decent summon option if you need a pet Defender.

level-5|unknown.name: Level 5
level-5|unknown.summary: Two excellent utility options. Rary’s Telepathic Bond feels like a weird choice since you get Telepathic Speech at first level, but Telepathic Speech is extremely limited so Rary’s Telepathic Bond is a big upgrade.

telepathic-speech|unknown.name: Telepathic Speech
telepathic-speech|unknown.summary: A useful utility, but very limited compared to most forms of telepathy. You can communicate, but you still need to share a language, the duration is short, and you can only connect to one creature. That’s enough to send your party’s Scout off on their own with a way to remain in contact, but beyond stealth and subtlety there are few meaningful ways to use this.

psionic-sorcery|depending-on-the-spell-l.name: Psionic Sorcery
psionic-sorcery|depending-on-the-spell-l.summary: This saves you one or two Sorcery Points (depending on the spell level) when you spend Sorcery Points to get extra spell slots with Font of magic, you don’t need to spend the Bonus Action to convert Sorcery Points into spell slots, and you also get to cast the spell without verbal or somatic components (and some material components), so you get the benefits of Subtle Spell for free. If you’re getting a lot of use out of your subclass spells, this is very efficient.

psychic-defenses|unknown.name: Psychic Defenses
psychic-defenses|unknown.summary: Psychic damage is rare, but charm and fear effects are very common.

revelation-in-flesh|unknown.name: Revelation in Flesh
revelation-in-flesh|unknown.summary: For a single Sorcery Point, every one of these effects is excellent. Replicating any of these is at least a 2nd-level spell, so the effects aren’t just good, they’re also cost-efficient. Note that since the fly and swim speeds are based on your walking speed, it’s easy to boost your new movement speed with buffs like Longstrider or Haste. Personal note: Tyler finds the term “writhing sensory tendrils” upsetting.

warping-implosion|unknown.name: Warping Implosion
warping-implosion|unknown.summary: Great for setting up combos with Quicken Spell. Follow this with a quickened AOE damage spell like Meteor Swarm or area control spell like Force Cage and you can eliminate whole encounters in one turn even at this high level. The saving throw is Strength, though, and, with the exceptions of enemies who rely on magic in combat, many enemies will have high Strength saves.

clockwork-spells|function.name: Clockwork Spells
clockwork-spells|function.summary: Several excellent spells, including some cleric options like Aid and wizard options like Summon Construct and Wall of Force. Not everything on the list is a gem, of course. : Protection from Evil and Good is a staple buff at any level, covering a wide range of dangerous creatures. Alarm is useful as a ritual.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); }); : Two staple cleric options. : A staple utility option and an important defensive buff. Not glamorous or flashy, but hard to go without. : Freedom of Movement is situationally useful, but helpful against enemies which like to grapple. Summon Construct is a Wizard exclusive, and it’s a decent summon option if you need a pet Defender. : Greater Restoration isn’t as important as Lesser Restoration, but it’s still very important. The conditions which it fixes are miserable and in many cases borderline lethal. Wall of Force (another Wizard exclusive) is one of the best area control effects around, especially if you have another spellcaster in the party who can drop some ongoing area damage before you put your enemies inside the impenetrable hemisphere.

level-1|function.name: Level 1
level-1|function.summary: Protection from Evil and Good is a staple buff at any level, covering a wide range of dangerous creatures. Alarm is useful as a ritual.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); });

level-5|another-wizard-exclusive.name: Level 5
level-5|another-wizard-exclusive.summary: Greater Restoration isn’t as important as Lesser Restoration, but it’s still very important. The conditions which it fixes are miserable and in many cases borderline lethal. Wall of Force (another Wizard exclusive) is one of the best area control effects around, especially if you have another spellcaster in the party who can drop some ongoing area damage before you put your enemies inside the impenetrable hemisphere.

restore-balance|such-as-because-they-are.name: Restore Balance
restore-balance|such-as-because-they-are.source: such as because they are Restrained or Poisoned
restore-balance|such-as-because-they-are.summary: This solves a lot of problems. Creatures which have Advantage on saves against specific conditions are common, and a Sorcerer encountering those resistances can hinder you a great deal. Similarly, if your allies have Disadvantage on a save (such as because they are Restrained or Poisoned), you can help protect them. The usage pool is limited, so save this for when it really matters.

bastion-of-law|though-you-can-notably-ap.name: Bastion of Law
bastion-of-law|though-you-can-notably-ap.source:
though you can notably apply this on top of
		THP
bastion-of-law|though-you-can-notably-ap.summary: This is similar in many ways to Temporary Hit Points (though you can notably apply this on top of THP). The duration is great, and allowing the target to choose when to use the ward allows you to take a little damage when you know that there’s a Short Rest coming so that you can spend some Hit Point Dice to manage your limited resources. Compare this to casting False Life. False Life is a 1st-level spell, so you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to get a spell slot with which to cast False Life. False Life lasts for grants 2d4+4 (average 9) THP. Each additional spell level adds 5 more THP. For those same 2 Sorcery points, you can give a creature a ward with 2 dice, which will prevent an average of 9 damage. Each additional Sorcery Points adds 4.5 more damage protection, compared to 1 or 2 Sorcery Points for 5 more temporary hit points from False Life. The two are roughly equivalent both in cost and effectiveness.

trance-of-order|provided-that-your-prima.name: Trance of Order
trance-of-order|provided-that-your-prima.source:
provided that your primary
		ability scores hits 16, 18, and 20 at levels 1, 4, and 8
trance-of-order|provided-that-your-prima.summary: The Fundamental Math of DnD 5e assumes that players will succeed on attack rolls against a typical CR-appropriate AC if they roll an 8 or better (provided that your primary ability scores hits 16, 18, and 20 at levels 1, 4, and 8), giving players a 65% chance of hitting an attack against an average, CR-appropriate enemy. Giving you a minimum guaranteed roll of 10 on attacks, saves, and ability checks means that you’re mostly guaranteed to hit with attacks, pass on any saves in which you’re proficient and have a decent ability score, and pass any ability checks with skills in which you’re well-suited. With a 1-minute duration, this is enough to get through one combat or to perform a series of skill checks if you move quickly. This is a great ability on almost any other class, but on the Sorcerer its usefulness is extremely limited. Spells which require attack rolls (with the exception of cantrips) mostly vanished around 2nd-level spells unless you’re upcasting low-level spells like Scorching Ray. Sorcerers are proficient with Constitution saves so this helps with Concentration, so this helps a lot with that. Since Sorcerers are Charisma-based, most of your skills will be, too, and using Persuasion in combat doesn’t work particularly well. So the three best uses for this are cantrips, upcasting low-level spells like Scorching Ray, and Concentration. That’s underwhelming for an ability which costs 5 Sorcery Points to recharge.

clockwork-cavalcade|unknown.name: Clockwork Cavalcade
clockwork-cavalcade|unknown.summary: Even with three effects, this is still only situationally useful. : The 100 points of healing will be the most consistently useful option for adventurers, allowing you to get allies back on their feet and restore a nice chunk of hit points. But at this level, healing options like Mass Cure Wounds and Heal have been around for a while, and Clerics are casting Mass Heal to do the same thing with a pool of 700 points. : Neat, but rarely useful. This could be used to solve some puzzles, though: Picture the Rosetta Stone. Now picture the Rosetta Stone after a Clockwork Soul snaps their fingers and all the broken pieces that have been missing for millennia just reappear in place with complete text and all the wear and tear of time is undone. : This outright ends spell effects without the ability checks required by Dispel Magic. But even then, it’s rare that you’ll face more than a small handful of enemies with magic effects on them, so in most cases you can just upcast Dispel Magic to level 6 to get the same effect if you don’t want to risk making the ability checks.

heal|unknown.name: Heal
heal|unknown.summary: The 100 points of healing will be the most consistently useful option for adventurers, allowing you to get allies back on their feet and restore a nice chunk of hit points. But at this level, healing options like Mass Cure Wounds and Heal have been around for a while, and Clerics are casting Mass Heal to do the same thing with a pool of 700 points.

repair|unknown.name: Repair
repair|unknown.summary: Neat, but rarely useful. This could be used to solve some puzzles, though: Picture the Rosetta Stone. Now picture the Rosetta Stone after a Clockwork Soul snaps their fingers and all the broken pieces that have been missing for millennia just reappear in place with complete text and all the wear and tear of time is undone.

dispel|unknown.name: Dispel
dispel|unknown.summary: This outright ends spell effects without the ability checks required by Dispel Magic. But even then, it’s rare that you’ll face more than a small handful of enemies with magic effects on them, so in most cases you can just upcast Dispel Magic to level 6 to get the same effect if you don’t want to risk making the ability checks.

bolstering-flames|unknown.name: Bolstering Flames
bolstering-flames|unknown.summary: A decent amount of Temporary Hit Points that you get to grant when you do stuff that you were going to do anyway.

radiant-fire|unknown.name: Radiant Fire
radiant-fire|unknown.summary: 1d4 damage. It scales up to 1d8 at level 14, but this is a pointless amount of damage.

level-1-spells|unknown.name: Level 1 Spells
level-1-spells|unknown.summary: You don’t get Healing Word, but you stil get good healing, and Guiding Bolt is a good go-to offensive option at low levels.

level-2-spells|unknown.name: Level 2 Spells
level-2-spells|unknown.summary: Essential condition removal and a good damage option.

level-3-spells|unknown.name: Level 3 Spells
level-3-spells|unknown.summary: Extend Spell on Aura of Vitality is a very efficient way to get a ton of healing for your party without resorting to resting. Dispel Magic is only situationally useful, but essential in any party.

level-4-spells|unknown.name: Level 4 Spells
level-4-spells|unknown.summary: Wall of Fire is excellent area control.

level-5-spells|unknown.name: Level 5 Spells
level-5-spells|unknown.summary: Greater Restoration is essential, but only situationally useful. Flame Strike is only useful if you can’t get Fireball.

absorb-spells|unknown.name: Absorb Spells
absorb-spells|unknown.summary: If you’re not fighting enemy spellcasters, this feature it outright useless. Even if you are fighting enemy spellcasters, you get very few Sorcery Points out of this.

honed-spellfire|unknown.name: Honed Spellfire
honed-spellfire|unknown.summary: A ton of additional Temporary Hit Points, but the damage increase on Radiant Fire is insultingly poor.

crown-of-spellfire|unknown.name: Crown of Spellfire
crown-of-spellfire|unknown.summary: An inefficient use of your Hit Point Dice, but prevention is better than healing, so it may make sense to use this instead of waiting to heal during a Short Rest.

wild-magic|unknown.name: Wild Magic
wild-magic|unknown.summary: A 1 in 20 chance to roll on the Wild Magic table isn’t significant. You don’t get 20 spell slots until you’re level 19, which means that you’re likely to go days at a time without triggering Wild Magic this way even if you try your hardest to do so. Instead, expect to trigger surges by using Tides of Chaos. The effects of Wild Magic are mostly benign, but there are a few options like Polymorphing yourself into a goat or casting Fireball on your party. But, since those options are in the minority, Wild Magic is usually safe and frequently helpful, though the unpredictable effects mean that you can’t count on it to be consistently useful.

tides-of-chaos|unknown.name: Tides of Chaos
tides-of-chaos|unknown.summary: Use this on any ability check or saving throw where the outcome matters more than a handful of hit points. Easy Advantage that you can recharge this easily is incredibly powerful. If you’re not expecting many fights on any given day, you can use level 1 spell slots to easily recharge this, then inexpensively replenish the slots with Font of Magic. This can be fantastic for social situations and for exploration, though Enhance Ability will be less expensive for numerous ability checks of the same type in quick succession.

bend-luck|unknown.name: Bend Luck
bend-luck|unknown.summary: When your allies fail a save against death by 1 or two, it’s heart-breaking. Spend the Sorcery Points and be everyone’s best friend. 2 Sorcery Points is expensive, but your allies’ lives are worth it. Conversely, if an enemy narrowly passes a save against a level 1+, spending 2 Sorcery Points to turn that into a failure is absolutely worth the cost. 2 Sorcery Points could get you a level 1 spell slot, but it will never recover the Action you spent to cast a spell unsuccessfully.

controlled-chaos|unknown.name: Controlled Chaos
controlled-chaos|unknown.summary: This considerably reduces the threat of the Wild Magic table and makes it more of a source of unpredictable buffs and comic relief.

tamed-surge|unknown.name: Tamed Surge
tamed-surge|unknown.summary: Many of the Wild Magic effects can be very beneficial if you can predict when they’ll occur. For example: Misty Step behind your enemies, make all creatures within 30 feet vulnerable to Piercing damage, then Dash and fly to safety. Unfortunately, you only get this once per Long Rest with no way to recharge it early.

draconic-resilience|unknown.name: Draconic Resilience
draconic-resilience|unknown.summary: A fantastic improvement to your durability. Don’t go diving into melee, though.

draconic-spells|unknown.name: Draconic Spells
draconic-spells|unknown.summary: Almost everything on the spell list will be consistently useful, and many of the options are staple Sorcerer choices that I would recommend taking if they weren’t already on your subclass spell list. : Command is a powerful crowd control option at any level. Chromatic Orb is good single-target damage. : Alter Self is only situationally useful, but Dragon’s Breath can be a very efficient AOE damage option, especially if you cast it on a familiar that normally can’t do damage. : A powerful crowd control option and a crucial utility. : Arcane Eye is my favorite scouting option. Charm Monster is only situationally useful. : Legend Lore is only useful if your DM feels like conducting a lore dump. Summon Dragon is great.

level-1|unknown.name: Level 1
level-1|unknown.summary: Command is a powerful crowd control option at any level. Chromatic Orb is good single-target damage.

level-2|unknown.name: Level 2
level-2|unknown.summary: Alter Self is only situationally useful, but Dragon’s Breath can be a very efficient AOE damage option, especially if you cast it on a familiar that normally can’t do damage.

level-3|unknown.name: Level 3
level-3|unknown.summary: A powerful crowd control option and a crucial utility.

level-4|unknown.name: Level 4
level-4|unknown.summary: Arcane Eye is my favorite scouting option. Charm Monster is only situationally useful.

level-5|unknown.name: Level 5
level-5|unknown.summary: Legend Lore is only useful if your DM feels like conducting a lore dump. Summon Dragon is great.

elemental-affinity|unknown.name: Elemental Affinity
elemental-affinity|unknown.summary: Powerful, but the choice is definitely stressful. If you pick a more common damage type like Fire, you’ll get more use offensively, but you’ll run into resistances more often. If you pick a less common damage type like Lightning, you’ll have very few spell options, but damage resistances will be less of an issue. Don’t pick poison. It’s commonly resisted and there are few good spells that deal poison damage.

dragon-wings|unknown.name: Dragon Wings
dragon-wings|unknown.summary: As powerful and effective as casting Fly on yourself, but it doesn’t require Concentration.

dragon-companion|unknown.name: Dragon Companion
dragon-companion|unknown.summary: Summon Dragon is a level 5 spell, and at level 18 when you have level 9 spell slots, a level 5 summon spell isn’t especially impressive unless you upcast it. The free summoning won’t be especially impressive in combat, but since you’re not using a spell slot, you can cast another spell with a spell slot on the same turn, such as casting Misty Step as a Bonus Action. Casting Summon Dragon without Concentration leaves room for you to do a lot of other cool stuff at the same time. Even if you’re repeatedly casting low-level versions of Summon Dragon as canon fodder, it can be a huge tactical advantage simply by flooding the battlefield with bodies for a few turns and wearing down enemies with the dragons’ breath weapons.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Essentially required with the type matching your Elemental Affinity.

wild-magic|unknown.name: Wild Magic
wild-magic|unknown.summary: A 1 in 20 chance to roll on the Wild Magic table isn’t significant. You don’t get 20 spell slots until you’re level 19, which means that you’re likely to go days at a time without triggering Wild Magic this way even if you try your hardest to do so. Instead, expect to trigger surges by using Tides of Chaos. The effects of Wild Magic are mostly benign, but there are a few options like Polymorphing yourself into a goat or casting Fireball on your party. But, since those options are in the minority, Wild Magic is usually safe and frequently helpful, though the unpredictable effects mean that you can’t count on it to be consistently useful.

tides-of-chaos|unknown.name: Tides of Chaos
tides-of-chaos|unknown.summary: Use this on any ability check or saving throw where the outcome matters more than a handful of hit points. Easy Advantage that you can recharge this easily is incredibly powerful. If you’re not expecting many fights on any given day, you can use level 1 spell slots to easily recharge this, then inexpensively replenish the slots with Font of Magic. This can be fantastic for social situations and for exploration, though Enhance Ability will be less expensive for numerous ability checks of the same type in quick succession.

bend-luck|unknown.name: Bend Luck
bend-luck|unknown.summary: When your allies fail a save against death by 1 or two, it’s heart-breaking. Spend the Sorcery Points and be everyone’s best friend. 2 Sorcery Points is expensive, but your allies’ lives are worth it. Conversely, if an enemy narrowly passes a save against a level 1+, spending 2 Sorcery Points to turn that into a failure is absolutely worth the cost. 2 Sorcery Points could get you a level 1 spell slot, but it will never recover the Action you spent to cast a spell unsuccessfully.

controlled-chaos|unknown.name: Controlled Chaos
controlled-chaos|unknown.summary: This considerably reduces the threat of the Wild Magic table and makes it more of a source of unpredictable buffs and comic relief.

tamed-surge|unknown.name: Tamed Surge
tamed-surge|unknown.summary: Many of the Wild Magic effects can be very beneficial if you can predict when they’ll occur. For example: Misty Step behind your enemies, make all creatures within 30 feet vulnerable to Piercing damage, then Dash and fly to safety. Unfortunately, you only get this once per Long Rest with no way to recharge it early.

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Magic Initiate (Cleric) is great, but the skills aren’t.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, great feat, fantastic skills.

charlatan|phb.name: Charlatan
charlatan|phb.summary: Perfect ability scores, and an easy way to cover all of the Face skills that you need while leaving space for other skill proficiencies.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: This can work for a Dexterity-based Pact of the Blade build, but the lack of a Charisma increase is very limiting.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, bad feat, bad skills.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores and Cult of the Dragon Initiate wants high Wisdom.

entertainer|phb.name: Entertainer
entertainer|phb.summary: The ability scores are good and the Musician feat is welcome in any party, but it’s hard to waste two skill proficiencies on borderline useless skills.

flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.name: Flaming Fist Mercenary
flaming-fist-mercenary|frhof.summary: If you want Tough, this is the way to get it. Good ability scores, good skills. For a melee Pact of the Blade build, this could be great.

genie-touched|frhof.name: Genie Touched
genie-touched|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and skills. You already share much of your spell list with the Wizard, but you can get some great options like Mage Armor which aren’t on the Warlock’s spell list.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Bad ability scores. If you want Alert, go for Inquisitive.

harper|frhof.name: Harper
harper|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and one good skill, but the feat is awful.

hermit|phb.name: Hermit
hermit|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and Healer may be worthwhile if your party lacks other healing options, but the skills are poor.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores, one good skill, Lucky. Warfarer is a better choice.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Alert is good, but no Charisma increase, and the skills are bad.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: Good ability scores and Alert, but the skills are poor.

lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Vassal
lords-alliance-vassal|frhof.summary: Since Warlocks depend more on attack rolls than typical spellcasters, this can work. The ability scores are fine, but not great. The skills are great for a Face. It realy comes down to whether or not Lords’ Alliance Agent will work for your build.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and Lucky is an easy feat on any character. The only low point is Animal Handling.

moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.name: Moonwell Pilgrim
moonwell-pilgrim|frhof.summary: If you want Magic Initiate (Druid), this is the best way to get it. The ability scores are good, but the skills are not.

mythalkeeper|frhof.name: Mythalkeeper
mythalkeeper|frhof.summary: Crafter is an awful feat, and the skills aren’t a good enough fit to make this appealing.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: Fine, but Charlatan is a much easier choice.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores, good feat, terrible skills.

rashemi-wanderer|frhof.name: Rashemi Wanderer
rashemi-wanderer|frhof.summary: Great if you’re building a melee Pact of the Blade build.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Magic Initiate (Wizard) is good, but the skills aren’t, and the Warlock’s spell list already significantly overlaps with the Wizard’s spell list.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: Decent for Pact of the Blade builds. You’ll have decent Dexterity, so the Dexterity-based skills and Thieves’ Tools are both great.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: Shadowmoor Hexer’s retaliatory damage could be good on a Pact of the Blade build that’s also using Armor of Agathys.

soldier|phb.name: Soldier
soldier|phb.summary: You could, in theory, build a Dexterity-based Pact of the Blade build. Don’t.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: Good ability scores and feat, but the skills are a bad fit.

vampire-devotee|aboh.name: Vampire Devotee
vampire-devotee|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, good skills, and Vampire’s Plaything can get you out of melee a few times per day without relying on teleportation.

wayfarer|phb.name: Wayfarer
wayfarer|phb.summary: Good ability scores, decent skills, and Lucky is good on any character.

zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.name: Zhentarim Mercenary
zhentarim-mercenary|frhof.summary: Good for a melee Pact of the Blade build.

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores, access to some Sorcerer spellcasting, and one good skill. Using the granted level 1 spell with Pact Magic can make Aberrant Surge consistently useful.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(184); });

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores. Access to Magic Weapon is tempting for Pact of the Blade builds, but it’s not enough to make this a good idea.

house-deneith-heir|efota.name: House Deneith Heir
house-deneith-heir|efota.summary: Passable ability scores for Pact of the Blade builds, but the feat isn’t good enough to make up for the lack of a Charisma increase.

house-ghallanda-heir|efota.name: House Ghallanda Heir
house-ghallanda-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores and skills both work well, and the feat is decent.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. The feat is good, but not enough on its own.

house-kundarak-heir|efota.name: House Kundarak Heir
house-kundarak-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. The feat is good, but not enough on its own.

house-lyrandar-heir|efota.name: House Lyrandar Heir
house-lyrandar-heir|efota.summary: Decent, but only remarkable if you want Conjure Minor Elementals.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: A good feat, but the ability scores and skills are bad.

house-phiarlan-heir|efota.name: House Phiarlan Heir
house-phiarlan-heir|efota.summary: A decent fit, but most of the spells from the feat are already on your spell list.

house-vadalis-heir|efota.name: House Vadalis Heir
house-vadalis-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores are the only redeeming quality.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. Heavenly Wings lets you fly without Concentration, and Necrotic Shroud can discourage enemies from closing to melee. For a Pact of the Blade build, Celestial Revelation is especially helpful in melee.

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: Nothing here contributes to your capabilities in combat, but it will make you an excellent Face.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and once per day flight are great, but you will likely never use the breath weapon beyond very low levels unless you’re building around Pact of the Blade.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. The durability is largely wasted on a spellcaster fighting from a safe distance, and you have spells to handle hidden and invisible enemies, but Pact of the Blade will welcome the additional durability.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great, plus you can get access to some spells from outside of the Warlock’s spell list, as well as nicely complementing your limited number of prepared spells and your extremely limited number of spell slots.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options. Warlocks don’t need much Wisdom, but proficiency in Wisdom saves and Advantage will make your Wisdom saves reliably good.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Form offers some interesting options which can help make up for the Warlock’s relative lack of spell slots. Cloud Jaunt is basically Misty Step, and Stone’s Endurance fills the same niche as Shield. You might consider the on-hit damage options for Pact of the Blade builds, but I would go for Stone’s Endurance in those builds to compensate for the Warlock’s d8 hit dice and poor armor.

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
