halfling|phb.summary: Brave and Lucky are both helpful, and Halfling Nimbleness may help you get past enemies to get into a safer position, though it won’t prevent Opportunity Attacks when you need to leave an enemy’s reach. Naturally Stealthy might let you hide before combat starts, but without Cunning Action it won’t see use in combat.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Very similar to the Gnome, but you give up some good things to get resistance to Psychic damage. Gnome is nearly always a better choice.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: Not necessarily bad, but easily replaced by the Warlock’s features. Devil’s Sight makes Darkvision less appealing, and Pact of the Tome makes the free Cantrip less impressive. This isn’t bad, but you’ll likely get more from Human or from a species that provides traits which the Warlock can’t make obsolete.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is an excellent option for getting out of dangerous positions quickly without a spell, and the Temporary Hit Points are great on a frail spellcaster. If that doesn’t keep you alive, Relentless Endurance provides some insurance. These traits will be especially useful for melee Pact of the Blade builds since you’ll be drawing more attacks.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Darkvision, an extra skill (probably Intimidation), and a good combat buff from Shifting. Beasthide and Swiftstride are both good ways to keep yourself alive.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: The Tiefling’s innate spellcasting is a great compliment to the Warlock’s limited spellcasting. Infernal is the easy choice here, but don’t overlook the other options.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class. The AC bonus is especially helpful for melee Pact of the Blade builds.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(185); });

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and you learn Ray of Frost. Not terrible, but not especially exciting. The other spells you get are terrible.

arcana|int.name: Arcana
arcana|int.summary: (Int): One of the most important knowledge skills in the game.

investigation|int.name: Investigation
investigation|int.summary: (Int): Helpful, but you probably don’t have enough Intelligence or skill choices to justify it.

religion|int.name: Religion
religion|int.summary: (Int): One of the most important knowledge skills in the game.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Great for starting big area control spells or for dropping big area damage spells before allies get in the way or enemies get into melee range. The second benefit allows you to trade initiative with a willing ally. To maximize this benefit, you want to have numerous allies in combat who roll initiative on their own. A familiar is an easy addition with Pact of the Chain. Between Advantage and a familiar, you effectively get to roll initiative 3 times and choose your favorite.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: Very good, but you can’t afford the Wisdom to keep this effective.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: If you’re building around Eldritch Blast, you may get a lot value out of the crit feature. Warlocks have several great options for getting advantage like combining Darkness and Devil’s Sight, and the large number of attacks from Eldritch Blast means that you have a decent chance to crit. You may rarely benefit from the second half of the feat, but also probably won’t need it.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: A good way to expand your spellcasting. Shillelagh is normally a good choice for gish builds, but you want that functionality from Pact of the Blade.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: Proficiency in Persuasion, and give Heroic Inspiration to your whole party once per day. Excellent on any build if you don’t need a different Origin Feat.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: Passable for Pact of the Blade builds.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: You already have Hex on your spell list, so it only makes sense to take this if you want the retaliatory damage. To maximize the effect, cast Armor of Agathys and take Resilient (Con) and/or War Caster to make your Concentration reliable, then run around in melee trying to draw attacks.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Great for covering all of the Face skills so that you can make room for other options, especially in a small party with poor skill coverage.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: The ability to cast Sacred Flame a few times per day as a Bonus Acton will be helpful on turns where you’re not casting or moving Hex. It may actually become more useful once you upgrade to other Concentration spells since you won’t need to commit your Bonus Acion to babysitting Hex.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: You should literally never make an unarmed strike.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Helpful with d8 hit dice and poor armor, but not essential.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: The Opportunity Attack portion of the feat will only be useful if you’re building for melee, but the ability to give your whole party Advantage on initiative is fantastic on anyone. Zhentarim Tactics offers a Charisma increase, so it’s a great follow-up for melee Pact of the Blade builds.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: Very similar to Magic Initiate if you could select Sorcerer, but you trade one Cantrip for a buff to Con saves and Aberrant Surge. It appears that Aberrant Surge still works if you upcast the spell, so pick a spell that scales well like Chromatic Orb.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: A few useful divinations which aren’t on the Warlock’s spell list, but remember that you still need to prepare them, and most of the spells here aren’t worth the trouble.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: Hunter’s Mark can replace Hex as a damage boost, but there are very spells here that aren’t already on your spell list.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: Basically the only thing useful here is Command, which is nowhere near enough. Take Magic Initiate or multiclass.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: Access to all of the essential healing spells without a Celestial patron.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: The bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) will be very useful, and very few of the spells are on your spell list.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: Access to Magic Weapon may be useful for Pact of the Blade builds, but remember that you’ll never get better than a +2 bonus, and you’ll get little value from the other spells.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Access to some excellent spells including Find Steed, Pass Without Trace, and Phantom Steed.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: Command is the only spell here that’s worth having and not already on your spell list. Take Magic Initiate.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: Be very cautious with this. You could use this to feel more like a Paladin, but remember that you don’t have the Paladin’s hit points or healing capabilities, and you don’t have the deep pool of spell slots to spend on Shield that regular spellcasters do.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Almost all of the spells here are already on your spell list.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Mostly mediocre, but you do get a couple great spells including Feather Fall and Conjure Minor Elementals.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: A lot of the spells aren’t on the Warlock’s spell list.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: This could be useful once you’ve hit 20 Charisma and have room to look elsewhere, but by that level this isn’t especially impactful.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: This won’t contribute anything meaningful to what you do, but passing out snacks for THP always feels nice.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Takes Devil’s Sight and cast Darkness.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Pact of the Blade only works with one weapon at a time, and heavy crossbows aren’t so much better than longbows that it justifies a feat.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: A good way to control enemies’ positions if you’re built around Pact of the Blade, but you probably don’t need the ability score increase early in your career. Wait to take this until you have 20 Charisma.

defensive-duelist|phb.name: Defensive Duelist
defensive-duelist|phb.summary: Tempting for Pact of the Blade, but eventually you’ll be running Shadow of Moil, and the ability score increase probably won’t help you.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: This could work with Armor of Agathys, but it is extremely risky.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Pact of the Blade only works with one weapon, but a Dexterity-based Pact of the Blade build could capitalize on the additional Bonus Action attack to get a lot of damage out of Hex, and Dexterity-based builds care less about their Pact of the Blade weapon. The Bonus Action attack will compete with options like Hex, but the ability to make up to 4 attacks per turn could mean a lot of damage output.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: Not as good as you would hope. The Bonus Action to spend a Hit Point Die notably does not add your Constitution modifier, which makes it an expensive and frustrating way to burn through your Hit Point Dice very quickly with minimal impact. Unless your party has some other deep, inexpensive healing resource, you need those dice for Short Rests to refill your massive pool of hit points. Take Chef instead.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: If you’re worried about resistances to elemental damage, use Eldritch Blast.

fairy-trickster|frhof.name: Fairy Trickster
fairy-trickster|frhof.summary: You could use this to debuff your target’s saves, then hit them next turn with a nasty save-or-suck spell.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells and access to some 1st-level spells from outside of your spell list. Misty Step is great on any spellcaster. The free castings also give you options beyond your Pact Magic slots, which is fantastic.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Pact of the Blade works with qualifying weapons. Unfortunately, the Strength increase is useless, so you probably want to wait to take this until you have 20 Charisma. Of course, by then your Proficiency Bonus will be big and probably might have 3 attacks, so this will feel really good.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Cleric or Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: This could be really good for Pact of the Blade builds, but the ability score is useless and you’ll need to get proficienct from somewhere else.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: This is great for your party, but if you only care about yourself, you can use Fiendish Vigor.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: Too situational for a feat that doesn’t give you a useful ability score increase.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational to justify unless you’re in a Underdark campaign or a campaign where vampires feature heavily.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Standard Bearer is only situationally useful and only works once per day, but can basically win encounters against enemies that rely on Charmed or Frightened, and there are quite a few of those.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Maybe useful once you’ve raised Charisma to 20 so that you can more easily shut down enemy spellcasters. The automatic success on a save is great, too.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: Too situational, and not impactful enough without a Charisma increase.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: Great for Dexterity-focused Pact of the Blade builds, but since it can’t increase your Charisma, other builds should wait to take it until you have 20 Charisma.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: Without another built-in way to consistently deal poison damage, there is too little benefit here to justify.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: A fantastic addition to Pact of the Blade builds, but Pole Strike will compete for your Bonus Action with options like Hex, and it doesn’t let you increase your Charisma. You can increase your Dexterity, but there are no Finesse polearms, so the only use case is Charisma-based Pact of the Blade builds that already have 20 Charisma.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: The THP mechanic is great, but Inspiring Leader will have a much bigger impact. Advantage on attacks while Bloodied is great, too, but with only d8 hit dice it’s risky to rely on that.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: (Constitution) will do a lot to help maintain Concentration, which is very important for a class that gets so few spell slots.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: If you want to be better at rituals, take Pact of the Tome.

sentinel|phb.name: Sentinel
sentinel|phb.summary: A good addition to melee Pact of the Blade builds, but it doesn’t let you increase your Charisma.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells and some free castings each day. The 1st-level spells aren’t as good as Fey Touched.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: Even if you’re built around Pact of the Blade, if you run into issues with cover, you can use spells instead.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: Pact of the Blade won’t give you the Strength to back up Shield Bash.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: A great way to expand beyond Face skills or to pick up Face skills that you couldn’t get at level 1.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: Great for Dexterity-focused Pact of the Blade builds, but since it can’t increase your Charisma, other builds should wait to take it until you have 20 Charisma.

speedy|phb.name: Speedy
speedy|phb.summary: You have spells to solve mobility issues.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: Very tempting to improve your effectiveness with Eldritch Blast.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: This could be useful if you’re building to use True Strike for attacks, but Pact of the Blade generally does best when making multiple attacks. There are exceptions, of course: Celestial Warlocks can pile 3 times their Charisma modifier onto True Strike’s Radiant damage (Once for True Strike, once for Agonizing Blast, once for their level 6 subclass feature), and ignoring resistance to that and adding some extra damage dice could be very impactful.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: You don’t have the Strength to support this.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: An easy go-to option. Remember that creatures can willingly fail saving throws, allowing you to use this on allies in order to move them out of dangerous positions, break grapples, or otherwise help them.

telepathic|phb.name: Telepathic
telepathic|phb.summary: Very cool, but usually talking works fine.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: Too difficult to use, too low impact.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Fantastic for melee Pact of the Blade builds.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: An easy way to trigger Opportunity Attacks and Expertise in one skill. Excellent for Pact of the Blade builds, especially paired with Armor of Agathys for the retaliatory damage.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immnunity to Radiant damage is nice, but the ability to change weapon damage types doesn’t get you anything new since Pact of the Blade already lets you do that.

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Fine, but occasonal Advantage and a minor damage boost won’t have a huge impact.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: The extra THP is nice if you’re relying on spells like Armor of Agathys, but it’s only 5 extra THP. Maximizing Hit Point Die rolls is also not especially useful since you have d6 hit dice. You could use it with Arcane Vigor to heal as a Bonus Action, but the amount healed is pitiful.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Simple and consistently useful for Pact of the Blade.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: Great for melee Pact of the Blade builds. Wait to fall below half hp, then cast Armor of Agathys. The broad damage resistance will effectively double the THP value of Armor of Agathys.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: Basically free Misty Step every time that you cast a spell as an Action. Unfortunately, Bonus Action and Reaction spells don’t qualify. According to the Rules Glossary: “When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.” Outside of combat, you can still use this to get around obstacles. Cast a harmless spell like Prestidigitation and you can teleport without making a mess.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Warlocks don’t have a big radiant damage nuke, so you don’t have anything that justifies taking this.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: 2d4 averages to 5. Adding +5/-5 to a saving throw can rescue you or an ally, or it can cause an enemy to fail a save. On a d20 scale, 5 means that there’s a 25% chance on any given roll that this will have an impact. Granted, it is still a dice roll, so the smaller the gap, the safer this is to use. On a full caster where save-or-suck spells are such a huge part of your arsenal, this is devastatingly effective. The fact that you can use it once per encounter is amazing.

boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.name: Boon of Fluid Forms
boon-of-fluid-forms|frhof.summary: This works nicely with Polymorph, but Polymorph has been obsolete for a long time, and you don’t get access to Shapechange.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: More hit points are great on a class as frail as the Warlock, but given the choice between this and Resilient (Constitution), you need proficiency in Constitution saves much more than 40 hp and some extra healing.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: Tempting for the natural 20 damage bonus. Ignoring resistance to B/P/S seems useful for Pact of the Blade, but Pact of the Blade already allows you to change the damage type to get around resistances.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Great for Pact of the Blade, but if you’re relying heavily on Shadow of Moil, there’s little benefit here.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but definitely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance is a great save-or-suck spell, and improving it by preventing enemies from using Verbal components is a great way to mess with enemy spellcasters. Unfortunately, you don’t have spell slots that you can use to cast it more than once.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Potentially useful in a small party with poor skill coverage.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: Take Boon of Dimensional Travel instead.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: All of your spell slots are 5th level, so they don’t qualify.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: You have tons of spells that can makes enemies Frightened, then use the Reaction to make them flee. Of course, you could also cast Fear, which already does that.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Resistance/immunity to two damage types. The Disadvantage mechanic won’t help you, unfortunately, because Warlocks don’t have good spells for dealing Lightning or Thunder damage which require saves.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Take Devil’s Sight, cast Darkness, and go about your day with Resistance to almost all damage. The invisibility is also nice.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: Resistance to two damage types. The healing is negligible. Take Boon of Fortitude instead.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Probably your only option for handling invisible enemies. If you’ve made it this far, your party is covering for you or you’ve found a creative solution.

dagger|unknown.name: Dagger
dagger|unknown.summary: Carry one or two for utility purposes at any level, but the damage isn’t good enough to make it a good idea.

light-crossbow|unknown.name: Light Crossbow
light-crossbow|unknown.summary: A light crossbow combined with True Strike will deal more damage than Fire Bolt until you reach level 11, making it the Warlock’s go-to attack option at least until level 11.

quarterstaff|unknown.name: Quarterstaff
quarterstaff|unknown.summary: If you’re preparing True Strike to use with a light crossbow, you can also use it with a quarterstaff two-handed for the same amount of damage. You don’t want to do this intentionally, but it’s a good backup option.

battleaxe-flail-longsword-morningstar-tr.name: Battleaxe / Flail / Longsword / Morningstar / Trident / Warhammer / War Pick
battleaxe-flail-longsword-morningstar-tr.summary: Frequently your go-to options for melee builds. Using a Versatile (d10) weapon in two hands is the most damage that you can get without running into the Heavy property or relying on Shillelagh, and avoiding the need for 13 Strength makes your build much simpler.

club-quarterstaff|which-will-require-eit.name: Club / Quarterstaff
club-quarterstaff|which-will-require-eit.source: which will require either Magic Initiate or Pact of the Tome
club-quarterstaff|which-will-require-eit.summary: Combined with Shillelagh (which will require either Magic Initiate or Pact of the Tome), you can upgrade the damage and eventually get up to 2d6 damage with a one-handed weapon at high levels. But the cost in both actions and decision points is significant for a fairly minor improvement to damage output, so you may prefer to stick to other weapons

greataxe-greatsword-maul|light-armor.name: Greataxe / Greatsword / Maul
greataxe-greatsword-maul|light-armor.summary: Your best damage, but you will need 13 Strength, or the Heavy property will impose Disadvantage on your attacks. Since you already need high Dexterity (light armor), Constitution, and Charisma, this may not be feasible.

hand-crossbow|unknown.name: Hand Crossbow
hand-crossbow|unknown.summary: Two-weapon fighting via Crossbow Expert. Throwing daggers gets you as many attacks, but for Dexterity-based builds, Crossbow Expert will get you better range and better damage.

heavy-crossbow|unknown.name: Heavy Crossbow
heavy-crossbow|unknown.summary: Briefly useful at low levels because of its large damage die, but obsolete once you get Thirsting Blade. Crossbow Expert negates the Loading property, but you’re going to take a feat, either take Gunner and grab a pistol or a musket or use hand crossbows.

longbow|unknown.name: Longbow
longbow|unknown.summary: The go-to weapon for ranged builds.

musket|unknown.name: Musket
musket|unknown.summary: With the Gunner feat, this is a linear upgrade from the Longbow, at least in terms of damage. Range might be an issue occasionally, but if that worries you, take Sharpshooter. This has the Loading property, which will present a problem as soon as you get Extra Attack.

pistol|unknown.name: Pistol
pistol|unknown.summary: Good damage for a one-handed weapon, and the Vex mastery. Advantage from Vex will make your DPR with a pistol better than DPR with a musket so long as you’re repeatedly attacking the same target. If you have enough gold, you can bring a whole bunch of loaded pistols and repeatedly draw and fire them instead of reloading. Or you could take the Gunner feat.

rapier|unknown.name: Rapier
rapier|unknown.summary: Charisma-based builds want a bigger weapon. Dexterity-based builds want a shortsword for two-weapon fighting. If you get proficiency in shields, this becomes a much better option.

scimitar-shortsword|unknown.name: Scimitar / Shortsword
scimitar-shortsword|unknown.summary: Your go-to weapons or two-weapon fighting.

whip|unknown.name: Whip
whip|unknown.summary: If you want reach, there’s no reason not to use a polearm.

studded-leather|unknown.name: Studded Leather
studded-leather|unknown.summary: You’re going to live in this.

bard|function.name: Bard
bard|function.summary: One level gets you some spellcasting, including great options like Guidance and Healing Word. Two gets you Expertise. Bards are also Charisma-based spellcasters, so multiclassing between the two is relatively easy.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(192); });

fighter|unknown.name: Fighter
fighter|unknown.summary: Starting as a Fighter gets you proficiency in Constitution saves, heavy armor, and shields, which opens up a lot of options for a Pact of the Blade Warlock. Fighting Style and Weapon Mastery make you even more effective with weapons.

paladin|unknown.name: Paladin
paladin|unknown.summary: Like a Fighter, you can get heavy armor, shields, and Weapon Mastery. Divine Smite kets you you to burn your spell slots to add a bunch of radiant damage to the attack, but you can take Eldritch Smite instead.

rogue|unknown.name: Rogue
rogue|unknown.summary: Sneak Attack only works with weapons, so Pact of the Blade is the only good combination with rogue unless you’re taking a class dip solely for Expertise.

sorcerer|with-the-exception-of-metamagic.name: Sorcerer
sorcerer|with-the-exception-of-metamagic.summary: s are also Charisma-based spellcasters, but their features (with the exception of Metamagic) are very level-dependent, so you need to devote yourself to leveling as a Sorcerer to benefit from Sorcerer levels unless you’re just take a class dip for Font of Magic and Metamagic. If you go that route, it’s probably so that you can quicken Eldrith Blast. 2 levels of Sorcerer gets you 2 types of Metamagic, and if you convert all of your Sorcerer spell slots to Sorcery Points, you’ll get a 3 moe per day. You can also convert your Pact Magic spell slots into Sorcery Points, allowing you to recharge on a Short Rest.

archfey-spells|unknown.name: Archfey Spells
archfey-spells|unknown.summary: Generally good, but few truly amazing spells. : Faerie Fire is a great spell. Sleep is complicated, but can be a very effective save-or-suck spell for your entire career. Sadly, it doesn’t benefit from your spell slot progression. : You get three level 2 spells instead of the usual 2. Calm Emotions can diffuse combat situations if you’re lucky. Misty Step is fantastic on any character, and it’s central to the subclass. Phantasmal Force is an incredibly powerful save-or-suck spell. : Blink is unreliable. Plant Growth can be excellent area control if you keep a potted plant handy to trigger the effect in places where there aren’t already plants. : Dominate Beast negates an entire creature type, but by this level beasts are a rarity. Greater Invisibility is amazing. : Dominate Person is powerful, but only situationally useful because humanoid enemies are rare by this level. Seeming is only situationally useful.

level-1|unknown.name: Level 1
level-1|unknown.summary: Two great single-target control effects, but they will become obsolete beyond low levels since they don’t scale with upcasting.

level-2|unknown.name: Level 2
level-2|unknown.summary: Detect Thoughts is only situationally useful. Phantasmal Force is a powerful save-or-suck option.

level-3|unknown.name: Level 3
level-3|unknown.summary: Clairvoyance is a fantastic scouting option if you have a normal number of spell slots like literally any other spellcaster, but Warlocks really need to save their spell slots for something more significant and impactful. Hunger of Hadar is absolutely amazing area control.

level-4|unknown.name: Level 4
level-4|unknown.summary: Confusion is unreliable, but Summon Aberration is great.

level-5|unknown.name: Level 5
level-5|unknown.summary: Modify Memory is only situationally useful, but with Eldritch Hex you can cast it without Somatic/Verbal components, allowing you to safely use it mid-conversation, thereby making it much more powerful. Telekinesis is a great utility, and you can use it to hoist melee-only enemies into mid-air.

steps-of-the-fey|function.name: Steps of the Fey
steps-of-the-fey|function.summary: Misty Step is a powerful tactical option for any character, allowing you to quickly get into or out of a dangerous position. A few free castings per day is a nice complement to your limited Pact Magic slots, and the added rider effects make it much more interesting. Remember that you get to use the rider effects whether you cast Misty Step using a spell slot or using Steps of the Fey. Because Steps of the Fey allows you to cast Misty Step without a spell slot, doing so doesn’t conflict with the “one spell with a spell slot per turn” rule, which means that you could cast a spell with a spell slot in the same turn. This doesn’t apply if you use a Pact Magic spell slot to cast Misty Step; it will only work if you use the free castings provided by Steps of the Fey. The biggest problem here is the incredibly tight resource constraints. You’ll get 3 to 5 free castings of Misty Step plus whatever you’re willing to cast with your limited spell slots. You won’t be able to use Misty Step every turn unless Misty Step is the only level 1+ spell that you cast, and even then, you won’t get through a full adventuring day without running out of resources.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); }); : Not a lot of Temporary Hit Points, but it’s consistently useful, and the THP last until the target finishes a Long Rest. : Fantastic if you’re teleporting out of melee. If you put yourself out of reach of the creatures that were within range, they’ll spend the next round attacking with Disadvantage.

refreshing-step|unknown.name: Refreshing Step
refreshing-step|unknown.summary: Not a lot of Temporary Hit Points, but it’s consistently useful, and the THP last until the target finishes a Long Rest.

taunting-step|unknown.name: Taunting Step
taunting-step|unknown.summary: Fantastic if you’re teleporting out of melee. If you put yourself out of reach of the creatures that were within range, they’ll spend the next round attacking with Disadvantage.

misty-escape|unknown.name: Misty Escape
misty-escape|unknown.summary: Using Misty Step as a Reaction means that you don’t need to use it during your own turn, leaving your Bonus Action free for things like Hex. : Get somewhere safe and make yourself untargetable until the beginning of your next turn. You might be able to teleport and then walk behind cover, in which case you should use Refreshing Step or Taunting Step, but that’s not always an option. : The damage doesn’t scale, which means that it will quickly become obsolete. Unless you’re being swarmed or you’re teleporting into a crowd of weak enemies, this is a bad idea.

disappearing-step|unknown.name: Disappearing Step
disappearing-step|unknown.summary: Get somewhere safe and make yourself untargetable until the beginning of your next turn. You might be able to teleport and then walk behind cover, in which case you should use Refreshing Step or Taunting Step, but that’s not always an option.

dreadful-step|unknown.name: Dreadful Step
dreadful-step|unknown.summary: The damage doesn’t scale, which means that it will quickly become obsolete. Unless you’re being swarmed or you’re teleporting into a crowd of weak enemies, this is a bad idea.

beguiling-defenses|unknown.name: Beguiling Defenses
beguiling-defenses|unknown.summary: This conflicts with Misty Escape, and one use per day will rarely have a significant impact. Your best bet is to use this when you suffer a critical hit. Even then, I doubt that this will be worth a spell slot to recharge.

bewitching-magic|unknown.name: Bewitching Magic
bewitching-magic|unknown.summary: Fantastically efficient. This goes a long way to correct the resource constraints of the subclass, allowing you to cast something that isn’t Misty Step without sacrificing the bulk of the subclass’s functionality.

celestial-spells|function.name: Celestial Spells
celestial-spells|function.summary: Mostly good. Includes essential options to play your party’s Healer, though you may struggle to keep up with a Cleric or a Druid. You don’t get Healing Word, but Healing Light fills that gap. : Light is a fine utility, and Sacred Flame offers one of the Warlock’s only options for radiant damage. It won’t compete with Eldritch Blast for raw damage, though.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); }); : You don’t really need either spell. Cure Wounds is tempting, but you get Healing Light, which will provide emergency healing without eating your extremely limited spell slots. You can still use Cure Wounds right before a short rest to get some healing out of any leftover spell slots, but I’ve never seen a Warlock make it to a short rest with remaining spell slots. Guiding Bolt is a fine single-target damage option, but you have Eldritch Blast for lasering things to death. : Aid is fantastic, especially with the Warlock’s guaranteed spell slot scaling. You might cast it at the beginning of the day, then immediately take a Short Rest. Lesser Restoration is an essential healing option in any party. : Daylight is only situationally useful. Revivify is amazing, but presents a problem for the Warlock: you only have two spell slots until level 11, and you need to reserve one to cast Revivify if no one else in the party can cast it. This means that fully half of your spell slots may need to go unused just in case someone in the party dies. : Guardian of Faith exists solely for the 8-hour duration. You can use it to post a guard while resting, but it’s otherwise not useful. Wall of Fire is excellent area control, and synergizes well with Eldritch Blast, Repelling Blast, and Grasp of Hadar. : Greater Restoration is a crucial healing option, but you’ll rarely need to actually cast it. Summon Celestial is fantastic, though you won’t be able to upcast it since the Warlock’s spell slots stop advancing at level 5.

cantrips|function.name: Cantrips
cantrips|function.summary: Light is a fine utility, and Sacred Flame offers one of the Warlock’s only options for radiant damage. It won’t compete with Eldritch Blast for raw damage, though.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

healing-light|unknown.name: Healing Light
healing-light|unknown.summary: Roughly equivalent to Healing Word, but without eating into your spell slots. This provides enough healing that the Celestial Warlock made a solid showing in the Healbot Olympics. However, it doesn’t solve problems beyond hit point restoration, so you still need spells to handle status conditions.

radiant-soul|e-g-one-target-of-wall-of-f.name: Radiant Soul
radiant-soul|e-g-one-target-of-wall-of-f.source: e.g. one target of Wall of Fire one time
radiant-soul|e-g-one-target-of-wall-of-f.summary: Most Warlocks deal the vast majority of their damage with Eldritch Blast and Agonizing Blast. Celestial Warlocks get Sacred Flame, which is probably the best way to make use of this feature, and you can use Agonizing Blast on Sacred Flame to add double your Charisma modifier to its damage. Of course, that makes Sacred Flame roughly equivalent to Eldritch Blast from levels 6 through 10, at which point Eldritch Blast’s third ray makes it significantly more damaging, and Sacred Flame has no way to catch up. The Celestial’s expanded spell list offers a tiny handful of extra spells that deal radiant/fire damage, but many of them aren’t a great use of your Warlock spell slots and the damage still only affects one target on one damage roll (e.g. one target of Wall of Fire one time). This also works with True Strike since True Strike can deal radiant damage. This can support a rather unusual Pact of the Blade build which focuses on a big singular attack. With True Strike, Radiant Soul, and Agonizing Blast, you can attack with Charisma and apply your Charisma as a damage bonus a total of 3 times. Comparing the math to Eldritch Blast gets a little messy, but a musket used with this strategy will be better than or comparable to Eldritch Blast until level 17 when you get your 4th ray.

celestial-resilience|unknown.name: Celestial Resilience
celestial-resilience|unknown.summary: This will save a ton of your party’s healing resources. It’s not quite as good as the Inspiring Leader feat since your allies don’t get as many Temporary Hit Points, but it’s very close.

searing-vengeance|or-your-turn-if-you-re.name: Searing Vengeance
searing-vengeance|or-your-turn-if-you-re.source: or your turn if you’re the one dying
searing-vengeance|or-your-turn-if-you-re.summary: A good emergency option for your whole party, though you need to be sure to keep everyone within 60 feet to keep them in range. This also only triggers when they make a Death Saving Throw, so you need to wait for your ally’s turn to trigger this (or your turn if you’re the one dying). There is no save to resist the blinding effect, so you can stand up and safely walk yourself to somewhere safe before going back to lasering stuff to death. Creatures that you damage are blinded, which gives you Advantage on attacks against them, so it’s a great time for Eldritch Blast.

dark-one-s-blessing|unknown.name: Dark One’s Blessing
dark-one-s-blessing|unknown.summary: An excellent amount of Temporary Hit Points. This makes Fiendish Vigor considerably less important. It also makes it important that you occasionally pick off weak foes to ensure that your temporary hit points are up before you focus on more important foes. Unfortunately, you either need to kill the creature yourself or you need to be within 10 feet of the dying creature, which is a very dangerous prospect unless you’re building around Pact of the Blade. Of course, you can also use a bag of rats. Kill a rat, get THP. Easy. This combines very well with Armor of Agathys. Armor of Agathys ends when you have no Temporary Hit Points, but it doesn’t require that the THP come from the spell itself. Using Dark One’s Blessing to maintain a pool of THP allows you to maintain Armor of Agathys for an exceptionally long time.

fiend-spells|unknown.name: Fiend Spells
fiend-spells|unknown.summary: Warlocks get few instantaneous AOE blast spells, which means that they may struggle against crowds of enemies. The Fiend’s spell list offers several excellent options to address this. : Burning Hands is passable AOE damage at low levels, and, since Warlocks get armor and more hp than Sorcerers and Wizards, you can survive being close enough to melee to use it. However, I wouldn’t use it beyond very low levels despite the automatic spell slot scaling. You’ll get more total damage out of Hex or other spell options despite Burning Hands’ scaling. Command is a great control/debuff effect and scales really well with your spell slots. : Scorching Ray is a bit redundant with Eldritch Blast, but it scales very well and benefits from the same tactics. Suggestion can be a useful save-or-suck, but does have some limitations. : A good AOE blast and a good area control effect. Fireball remains the best instantaneous AOE damage spell at every spell level until around spell level 8, and, while the Warlock can’t cast Fireball past level 5 spell slots, it still remains a perfect go-to AOE blast option. However, remember that you will often get better results out of spells with ongoing effects like Hunger of Hadar, and, with so few spell slots, you need to squeeze as much out of them as you can. Stinking Cloud is an ongoing AOE save-or-suck effect, but creatures within the area are Heavily Obscured, so it’s hard to attack them. Hunger of Hadar is likely a better choice in most cases. : Fire Shield is fine for Pact of the Blade builds. It does seem redundant with Armor of Agathys, which notably lasts longer, provides Temporary Hit Points, deals more damage to attackers, and scales with spell level. Wall of Fire is one of the best area control spells in the game and, with the right invocations, you can push and pull enemies through it to repeatedly capitalize on the guaranteed damage dealt when a creature passes through the wall. : Geas is very situational. Insect Plague fills a very similar niche to Hunger of Hadar, but the damage is much better.

dark-one-s-own-luck|advantage-is-worth-s.name: Dark One’s Own Luck
dark-one-s-own-luck|advantage-is-worth-s.source: Advantage is worth slightly more than +3
dark-one-s-own-luck|advantage-is-worth-s.summary: Adds an average of 5.5 to your roll, which is mathematically much better than what you get from Advantage (Advantage is worth slightly more than +3). Unfortunately, you need to declare that you’re using it before you roll, so you can’t use this to rescue failed checks/saves. Save this for saving throws.

fiendish-resilience|unknown.name: Fiendish Resilience
fiendish-resilience|unknown.summary: Powerful and flexible. If you’re not sure what to pick, Slashing and Fire are both reliable choices.

hurl-through-hell|unknown.name: Hurl Through Hell
hurl-through-hell|unknown.summary: 8d10 damage is pretty great on top of whatever your attack was, and the Incapacitated condition will prevent them from acting, break Concentration, and end some ongoing abilities like the Barbarian’s Rage. The creature is also functionally removed from the game until the end of your next turn, allowing you to place hazards in and around its space like Hunger of Hadar, Wall of Fire, or the rest of your party. You only get to use this once per Long Rest, but you can recharge it by spending a Pact Magic spell slot. At this level all of your slots are level 5, so we need to compare this to a level 5 spell. This won’t match the damage or versatility of your spells, so we can’t look at this as our go-to use for spell slots. Instead, use it for high-priority targets when the benefits will be especially useful, such as hitting an enemy spellcaster to break Concentration or a bulky enemy who is blocking your party from attacking their less durable allies.

awakened-mind|unknown.name: Awakened Mind
awakened-mind|unknown.summary: Initially this is just a way to communicate telepathically. The duration is short, so you’re going to use it at short range simply because you can’t get very far before the duration expires. It has almost no mechanical impact until you pick up Clairvoyant Combatant.

great-old-one-spells|unknown.name: Great Old One Spells.
great-old-one-spells|unknown.summary: An eclectic mix with a good mix of debuffs, save-or-suck, area control, and utility options. : Two great single-target control effects, but they will become obsolete beyond low levels since they don’t scale with upcasting. : Detect Thoughts is only situationally useful. Phantasmal Force is a powerful save-or-suck option. : Clairvoyance is a fantastic scouting option if you have a normal number of spell slots like literally any other spellcaster, but Warlocks really need to save their spell slots for something more significant and impactful. Hunger of Hadar is absolutely amazing area control. : Confusion is unreliable, but Summon Aberration is great. : Modify Memory is only situationally useful, but with Eldritch Hex you can cast it without Somatic/Verbal components, allowing you to safely use it mid-conversation, thereby making it much more powerful. Telekinesis is a great utility, and you can use it to hoist melee-only enemies into mid-air.

psychic-spells|unknown.name: Psychic Spells
psychic-spells|unknown.summary: Psychic damage is rarely resisted, allowing you to use direct damage spells with much less caution than many spellcasters. The ability to cast Enchantment/Illusion components subtly can be very helpful in social situations where casting spells can be considered hostile.

clairvoyant-combatant|unknown.name: Clairvoyant Combatant
clairvoyant-combatant|unknown.summary: Excellent both offensively and defensively. Melee Pact of the Blade builds will enjoy the defensive benefits more than most Warlocks, but any Warlock will enjoy Advantage with Eldritch Blast. Of course, you can do the same thing with Darkness and Devil’s Sight with a better duration and no saving throws. This competes for your Bonus Action with Hex, so you’ll need to pick which one you want to use first. You can reapply Hex, but not Clairvoyant Combatant, so save Clairvoyant Combatant for powerful single enemies, then use it before applying Hex until you get Eldritch Hex, at which point you should reverse the order so that your target has Disadvantage on the Wisdom save. You only get to use this once per Short or Long Rest, so you can’t afford to use it in every fight. You can recharge it with a spell slot, but only do that if you have multiple fights with single powerful foes that justify it.

eldritch-hex|unknown.name: Eldritch Hex
eldritch-hex|unknown.summary: Disadvantage on saves against a chosen ability score allows you and your party to easily save-or-suck your target to death. The only problem is that most save-or-suck spells require Concentration, and, if you cast a Concentration spell, you stop concentrating on Hex, thereby losing the benefits of Eldritch Hex. You’ll need to rely on your friends or look for spells that don’t need Concentration. This works very well with Clairvoyant Combatant.

create-thrall|unknown.name: Create Thrall
create-thrall|unknown.summary: Summon Aberration is a good spell. The ability to remove the Concentration requirement is great, too, allowing you to keep Concentration on Hex so that you and your aberration can get a damage bonus. The Temporary Hit Points also mean that your aberration is unusually durable. However, you’re casting Summon Aberration at level 5, and it will never improve. This means that your aberration will become relatively less threatening as you gain levels, making it less and less impactful over time. It’s still good, but it won’t keep pace with regular spellcasters who are summoning creatures.

armor-of-shadows|phb.name: Armor of Shadows
armor-of-shadows|phb.summary: Take Magic Initiate. Mage Armor’s duration is 8 hours, so one casting will get you through the day.The one use case for this is School of Abjurer wizards, who can use this to repeatedly cast Mage Armor in order to recharge your Arcane Ward without spending spell slots.

eldritch-mind|phb.name: Eldritch Mind
eldritch-mind|phb.summary: Excellent on nearly any spellcaster, but War Caster provides the same benefit plus some other stuff, and since War Caster can get you a +1 Charisma increase, it’s a very easy feat choice.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });Eldritch Mind is only appealing if there’s no way to fit War Caster into your build because you need other other feats instead. Remember that you can replace an Invocation each time that you gain a Warlock level, allowing you to take this temporarily and then replace it when you’re ready to take War Caster.

pact-of-the-blade|phb.name: Pact of the Blade
pact-of-the-blade|phb.summary: Pact of the Blade is the primary way in which Warlocks are expected to use weapons. By using Charisma for attack and damage, you remove MAD (Multiple Ability Dependent) issues, allowing you to easily transition between weapons and spells. There is a clear progression of Invocations which will fill most of your Invocation slots and add scaling benefits which will make you feel a lot like a Fighter.However, the reality of Pact of the Blade is a bit more complex. General Feats which improve your weapon use like Great Weapon Master and Piercer all provide increases to Strength or Dexterity. This means that if you’re focusing on Charisma, you won’t want to take these feats until you hit 20 Charisma, which may not be until you reach level 12.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });It is fine to build Pact of the Blade around Charisma, ignore weapon-focused Feat options, and rely on Invocations and spells. But if you want to lean heavily into weapon use, you’ll need to build around Charisma.Note that until you can get Thirsting Blade at level 5, using Shillelagh and/or True Strike is just as using Pact of the Blade, if not better in all respects except Opportunity Attacks. You don’t get Weapon Mastery (at least not from Warlock levels), so there’s little difference between the 1d8 damage of a Shillelagh and the 1d10 damage of a Longsword wielded in two hands. Strongly consider Pact of the Tome at least until level 5, then replace Pact of the Tome with Pact of the Blade if you want to go that route.Even then, using a weapon isn’t significantly better on its own. You’ll need to add the other Pact of the Blade cantrips before weapons start having more impact than Shillelagh+True Strike.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

pact-of-the-chain|phb.name: Pact of the Chain
pact-of-the-chain|phb.summary: Find Familiar is already a fantastic spell, and the added forms give you better options than those available to any other spellcaster. Imp: CR 1 and a lot to like. Immunity to the two most common non-weapon damage types, plus resistance to Cold damage, magic resistance, and a respectable 21 hp make the Imp reasonably durable. With Devil’s Sight, the ability to turn invisible, a Fly speed, and Shape-Shift to both disguise itself and change movement types, it’s also very effective as a scout. In combat, the Imp’s sting attack does a respectable 13 average damage, though poison damage is commonly resisted, so it’s not a fantastic option. You may be better served by casting Darkness on an object, sending your familiar to carry the Darkness effect over your enemies, then using Devil’s Sight to attack them. If you’re worried about your familiar’s safety, cast Darkness on an object hanging from a string, and have your imp dangle it down from above like a weird, aggressive lakitu. Pseudodragon: With only 10 hit points and no damage resistances, the Pseudodragon is extremely frail, though Blindsight and Sting offer some tempting options. The Pseudodragon’s Sting can poison enemies for a full hour, and could even knock them unconscious. However, it targets a Constitution save, and Constitution saves are consistently high. Even with Investment of the Chain Master. you can’t rely on it, and without an easy way for your pseudodragon to move in and out of melee safely, it’s dangerous for your familiar to actually use. Despite how effective Sting can be if it works, the unreliability, the Pseudodragon’s poor durability, and its comparably poor scouting options make it a poor choice. Quasit: CR 1, and plenty durable. 25 hp, three damage resistances, and immunity to poison. The Quasit can also change its movement options with Shape-Shift, making it fantastically versatile. With +5 Stealth and the ability to turn invisible at will, it’s also an excellent scout. The Quasit isn’t an obvious combat threat since its single attack doesn’t deal much damage, but making a target Poisoned without a save is a huge debuff for many enemies, which is worth the relatively poor damage, especially at high levels where other familiars’ damage feels less impactful. The Quasit’s Scare feature won’t be much use without Investment of the Chain Master. Skeleton: It can use equipment like weapons, it has Darkvision, and it’s immune to fatigue. But it also had 13 gp and its attacks are underwhelming. This isn’t a combat pet, and it certainly isn’t a scout. Its best advantages are its ability to use objects, to carry things for you, and to keep watch without getting tired. Slaad Tadpole: With 5 damage resistances and Magic Resistance, the Slaad Tadpole seems very tanky until you notice its 7 hit points. The tadpole’s biggest advantage is that it’s the only option with a burrow speed. But with no hands, it can’t do much more than burrow to a place, look around, and maybe deliver touch spells. Sphinx of Wonder: 24 hp, 3 damage resistances, one attack dealing 12 average damage, flight, 24 hp, and Magic Resistance all make your sphinx an appealing combatant. It’s proficient in Arcana and Religion, and can speak, making it a useful substitute for proficiency in those skills. On top of that, Burst of Ingenuity can help you and your allies pass crucial saving throws, thought it does need to be applied when you make the saving throw rather than after you see the result. No other familiar options ha similar proficiencies or support options, giving the Sphinx of Wonder an exciting niche. Where the Sphinx of Wonder falls short is as a scout. Despite proficiency in Stealth, without the ability to turn invisible, it can’t compete on scouting with options like the Imp or the Sprite. If your party has an effective scout already, that may not be an issue. Just be prepared to have your familiar run away and hide in combat if it takes any damage at all. 24 hit points doesn’t go very far beyond low levels. Sprite: Flight, invisibility at will, good Perception and Stealth modifiers, and it can speak three languages. It’s notably the only option added by Pact of the Chain with proficiency in Perception. Heart Sight seems interesting, but you could arguably use an Insight check for the same purpose. The Sprite’s bow attack automatically charms its target on hit, but that only prevents the target from attacking the sprite. This is a great scout, but it is not a combat pet. Venomous Snake: 10 feet of blindsight, a swim speed, and a passable attack. If you want blindsight, get a bat. If you want good attacks or a familiar with a swim speed, look elsewhere.

venomous-snake|unknown.name: Venomous Snake
venomous-snake|unknown.summary: 10 feet of blindsight, a swim speed, and a passable attack. If you want blindsight, get a bat. If you want good attacks or a familiar with a swim speed, look elsewhere.

pact-of-the-tome|phb.name: Pact of the Tome
pact-of-the-tome|phb.summary: Three cantrips and 2 Rituals offer quite a bit of utility. You can’t add additional Rituals to the book, but you can get a new book. You can re-select the Cantrips and Rituals “when the book appears”, not “when you select this Invocation” or “when this book first appears.” Since you can resummon the book on a Short or Long Rest, you can change these very frequently.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(182); });

agonizing-blast|phb.name: Agonizing Blast
agonizing-blast|phb.summary: Absolutely essential on any build that’s not relying solely on Pact of the Blade. While you can apply this to any damaging cantrip, Eldritch Blast is the best choice since it gets multiple damage rolls. Area cantrips like Thunderclap or ongoing damage cantrips like Create Bonfire are similarly effective, as they can apply the damage bonus multiple times.This can also be effective with Booming Blade and Green-Flame Blade, making them very effective options for melee Pact of the Blade builds. Melee cantrips already outpace unmodified weapon attacks, and the bonus damage from Agonizing Blast stretches that gap even further. The math gets a little fuzzy with options like Hex and Spirit Shroud, but it’s still a powerful option for Pact of the Blade builds.It’s not totally clear if this works with True Strike before it deals additional damage, though I believe that it would do so. Consult with your DM before making assumptions.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(183); });

devil-s-sight|phb.name: Devil’s Sight
devil-s-sight|phb.summary: Darkvision can be an immense tactical advantage, but it’s negated by a torch. Devil’s Sight allows you to use magical darkness, including the Darkness spell, to gain a massive advantage over your foes. However, keep in mind that your allies may still struggle to fight in magical darkness so using this option can often lead to selfish tactics which are frustrating for your allies.

eldritch-spear|phb.name: Eldritch Spear
eldritch-spear|phb.summary: Eldritch Blast’s 120-foot range is already excellent, giving you a reliable long-range attack option. Eldritch Spear can massively improve that range, but that capability is rarely impactful.

fiendish-vigor|phb.name: Fiendish Vigor
fiendish-vigor|phb.summary: Guaranteed 12 Temporary Hit Points, and the hit points last until your next Long Rest. This is consistently useful on any Warlock, but it’s absolutely essential on melee-focused Pact of the Blade builds.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(184); });

lessons-of-the-first-ones|phb.name: Lessons of the First Ones
lessons-of-the-first-ones|phb.summary: Many Origin Feats are excellent, but without an Ability Score Increase they can be hard to select when you get a normal ASI/Feat. This makes Origin Feats much more accessible without slowing your ability scores and potentially falling behind the Fundamental Math.

mask-of-many-faces|phb.name: Mask of Many Faces
mask-of-many-faces|phb.summary: In a game involving stealth or intrigue, the ability to disguise yourself is a big advantage. The ability to do it at a moment’s notice at no cost allows you to be anyone any time. However, in a simple dungeon crawl, this will be almost completely useless.

misty-visions|phb.name: Misty Visions
misty-visions|phb.summary: A clever player with a DM who is willing to play along can accomplish a lot with even a basic illusion. A 15-foot cube is a huge amount of space, too. Place illusory walls, doors, statues, or other objects which creatures don’t expect to move or produce other stimuli like heat or smells, and in many cases that’s just as good as creating something. If creatures don’t realize that your illusory wall is an illusion, they’re going to treat it like a wall.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(185); });

otherworldly-leap|phb.name: Otherworldly Leap
otherworldly-leap|phb.summary: A passable way to get around the battlefield without worrying about difficult terrain or other obstacles on the ground, but it becomes obsolete as soon as you have a way to fly, so expect to retrain this.

repelling-blast|phb.name: Repelling Blast
repelling-blast|phb.summary: Similar to the Push Weapon Mastery, this allows you to keep enemies at a safe distance, to break grapples, or to force enemies into dangerous positions. The go-to use is with Eldritch Blast, but you can also apply it to cantrips like Shocking Grasp or Thunderclap in order to launch enemies away from you at melee range.As you add additional shots from Eldritch Blast, the ability to repeatedly push enemies away can become very powerful. Combining this with speed reductions can easily lock enemies out of melee or keep enemies inside a small, dangerous area, allowing to win many combat encounters with minimal resource cost.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(186); });

ascendant-step|phb.name: Ascendant Step
ascendant-step|phb.summary: Warlocks get access to Fly, but it’s hard to justify spending your precious few spell slots on it. Levitate gets you the biggest benefit of flight (distance from the ground) at much lower cost. However, you still need to Concentrate, which makes it hard to use in combat since you’re giving up the benefits of a damage buff like Hex.

eldritch-smite|phb.name: Eldritch Smite
eldritch-smite|phb.summary: Pact of the BladeThis is rarely worth a spell slot to activate. The damage is decent, but you can usually do a lot more by using that spell slot to cast a spell, even if the spell only does damage. Knocking enemies prone is tempting, but it also makes them hard for you to hit with ranged attacks, including Eldritch Blast.Your best bet is to reserve this for when you score a critical hit, at which point you can choose to use Eldritch Smite and double the damage dice. You can also use this to knock flying enemies prone, causing most flying creatures to fall.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(187); });

gaze-of-two-minds|phb.name: Gaze of Two Minds
gaze-of-two-minds|phb.summary: Cast Invisibility on an ally, then hit them with Gaze of Two Minds. Send them into a room with enemies. Cast spells without an obvious source like Toll the Dead or Hunger of Hadar. Your ally’s position won’t be revealed, their Invisibility won’t be broken, and you’re in another room, completely safe.

gift-of-the-depths|phb.name: Gift of the Depths
gift-of-the-depths|phb.summary: Only useful in aquatic campaigns, and, if you’re in an aquatic campaign, you probably want the ability to function underwater much sooner than level 5. Even if this does look appealing, you can take Master of Myriad forms to use the Aquatic Adaptation option.

investment-of-the-chain-master|phb.name: Investment of the Chain Master
investment-of-the-chain-master|phb.summary: Pact of the ChainOnly essential if you want your familiar to be a combat pet, which isn’t necessarily a good idea. You familiar is at most CR 1, and their stats will never improve, making their attacks unreliable and their low AC and hit points a huge liability. Giving them Resistance to damage as a Reaction helps, but maybe not enough.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(188); });If you want to turn your familiar into a reliable combat pet, you’ll need to make other investments to improve their durability. Sources of Temporary Hit Points like Inspiring Leader and boosts to their AC like Mage Armor are a must. If your familiar can turn invisible, have them use their Action on their turn to become invisible, and use your Bonus Action to activate the Quick Attack feature, allowing your familiar to remain invisible and therefore relatively safe most of the time.Strongly consider the Swim Speed over the Fly Speed. The best familiar options can already fly.

master-of-myriad-forms|phb.name: Master of Myriad Forms
master-of-myriad-forms|phb.summary: Aquatic adaptation is rarely useful. Change Appearance is fine, but Mask of Many Faces is available at lower level. Natural Weapons is neat, but there’s no reason for the Warlock to use unarmed strikes. Between the three options you may find some use, but it won’t be consistent.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(189); });You might choose to replace Mask of Many Faces with this since Alter Self’s Change Appearance option has some advantages over Disguise Self (it’s not an illusion), but remember that Alter Self requires Concentration, so it’s not strictly better in every way.

one-with-shadows|phb.name: One With Shadows
one-with-shadows|phb.summary: Consistently amazing. You’re probably now your party’s best Scout.

thirsting-blade|phb.name: Thirsting Blade
thirsting-blade|phb.summary: Pact of the BladeAbsolutely essential if you plan to use weapons consistently. If you don’t take this at level 5, you immediately fall behind Eldritch Blast builds and any martial character that gets Extra Attack.

whispers-of-the-grave|phb.name: Whispers of the Grave
whispers-of-the-grave|phb.summary: Speak with Dead is one of my favorite divinations because it grants you easy access to information which is otherwise lost forever. With the ability to cast it at will with no cost means that you can interrogate every random mook you kill in your long, sordid career of murder-hoboing. But keep in mind that the target isn’t compelled to tell you anything helpful, so this isn’t always reliable.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(190); });

gift-of-the-protectors|phb.name: Gift of the Protectors
gift-of-the-protectors|phb.summary: Pact of the TomeImagine the Half-Orc’s Relentless Endurance trait, but shared between your entire party. While it won’t help you actively accomplish anything, this is a great support option that any party should welcome.

lifedrinker|phb.name: Lifedrinker
lifedrinker|phb.summary: Pact of the BladeThe damage bonus is small, but consistent. The ability to spend a Hit Point Die to heal mid-combat adds a but of durability which you almost certainly need with light armor and d8 hit dice.

visions-of-distant-realms|phb.name: Visions of Distant Realms
visions-of-distant-realms|phb.summary: Arcane Eye is one of my favorite scouting options, and the ability to cast it at will makes it even better. Never go into a room without knowing exactly what’s inside.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(191); });

devouring-blade|phb.name: Devouring Blade
devouring-blade|phb.summary: Pact of the BladeA must for Pact of the Blade builds.

witch-sight|phb.name: Witch Sight
witch-sight|phb.summary: Extremely powerful, though not consistently impactful. Very few characters have access to Truesight, and the ones that do usually need to cast a high-level spell to get it.

beast-speech|2014-phb.name: Beast Speech
beast-speech|2014-phb.summary: This is on the Warlock’s spell list now.

beguiling-influence|2014-phb.name: Beguiling Influence
beguiling-influence|2014-phb.summary: Functionally obsolete. Take Lessons of the First Ones to take the Skilled feat.

eldritch-sight|2014-phb.name: Eldritch Sight
eldritch-sight|2014-phb.summary: You can cast Detect Magic as a Ritual.

eyes-of-the-rune-keeper|2014-phb.name: Eyes of the Rune Keeper
eyes-of-the-rune-keeper|2014-phb.summary: You can cast Comprehend Languages as a ritual.

grasp-of-hadar|xgte.name: Grasp of Hadar
grasp-of-hadar|xgte.summary: If you’re using Eldritch Blast enough to justify investing in it, you generally want to keep enemies away from you. However, the option to pull enemies closer may be helpful for your allies, and you may be able to use this to keep enemies inside ongoing area effects like Hunger of Hadar. You won’t use this on every attack or even in every encounter, but sometimes it’s helpful.

lance-of-lethargy|xgte.name: Lance of Lethargy
lance-of-lethargy|xgte.summary: In the 2024 rules, speed penalties are easy and abundant, making it easy for parties to reduce enemies’ speeds to 0. Stack this with the Slow mastery, Ray of Frost, and any number of other speed reductions, and you can prevent enemies from moving. Combine that with ongoing area damage, and you can win fights with stunningly little resource cost.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(193); });

thief-of-five-fates|phb.name: Thief of Five Fates
thief-of-five-fates|phb.summary: Not worth an Invocation. Rarely worth a spell slot.

cloak-of-flies|xgte.name: Cloak of Flies
cloak-of-flies|xgte.summary: This remains in effect until you dismiss it, making it an excellent buff both offensively and defensively. Melee Warlocks can capitalize on this by diving into groups of enemies and attempting to catch as many as possible in the area. If enemies attempt to flee, take opportunity attacks, then chase them down on the following turn. Against enemies that are especially hard to hit, force them into a corner, block their escape, stand next to them, and Dodge. The damage is guaranteed and doesn’t allow a save, so against many enemies you can stand still and wait for them to fall over.Despite its benefits, I wouldn’t take this on any Warlock without Pact of the Blade and some investments in durability. Poison damage is also commonly resisted, so you can’t always count on Cloak of Flies to be effective.

far-scribe|tcoe.name: Far Scribe
far-scribe|tcoe.summary: Pact of the TomeVery cool, but very dependent on your game and you DM, so it’s hard to objectively assess this. I love the way that this invocation works, but it’s just not very useful for most Warlocks. Your DM could make this appealing by adding powerful NPCs to the pool of creatures with whom you can communicate, but that’s heavily dependent both on your DM’s willingness to play along and on those NPCs being conscious, helpful, and willing to respond at any given point. If you’re repeatedly Sending “You up?” to people at all hours of the night, they’re eventually going to get sick of you.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(197); });As a DM, I would consider adding the Warlock’s patron to the list of creatures. That would be a really interesting way to provide semi-direct interaction with the Warlock’s patron, and it could give the DM a great way to feed the players information or just generally mess with them.

maddening-hex|xgte.name: Maddening Hex
maddening-hex|xgte.summary: 5 damage as a Bonus Action to the target and targets of your choice within 5 feet. If you run Hex all day long, this will be constistent, nearly free damage during most rounds. You could maximize the benefits by using Repelling Blast and Grasp of Hadar to push/pull enemies into a group, but remember that spending Eldritch Blast rays to attack other creatures means giving up the Hex bonus damage on your primary target, so you’re trading for roughly equivalent damage.

mire-the-mind|2014-phb.name: Mire the Mind
mire-the-mind|2014-phb.summary: Slow is a good spell, but it doesn’t scale with spell slot and you only get to use it once per day. Save your spell slots for more powerful options.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(198); });

sign-of-ill-omen|2014-phb.name: Sign of Ill Omen
sign-of-ill-omen|2014-phb.summary: Bestow Curse is a great single-target debuff with some challenges. It only affects one target and since you can only cast it once per day with Sign of Ill Omen your best bet is to cast it on powerful single targets. However, it requires Concentration and allows a saving throw, so there’s a good chance that the target passes their save and your once-per-day Bestow Curse is wasted.Even if it does work, you’re stuck Concentrating on it and, unlike Hex, you can’t move the effect between targets. Hex has some overlap with Bestow Curse, providing a similar debuff to ability scores and a similar damage buff, but Hex doesn’t allow the target a saving throw and allows you to move the spell between targets so you get considerably more benefit from your tiny number of spell slots.

tomb-of-levistus|xgte.name: Tomb of Levistus
tomb-of-levistus|xgte.summary: This is a passable panic option, and at 10 temporary hit points per warlock level, it should be able to absorb basically anything that hits you unless you’re fighting something with a CR well above your level. However, you’re incapacitated for the turn after you use this, which means you give up your turn to use it. Unless your allies can come to your aid, that could be a serious problem. Because 5e’s death mechanics are so gentle, it may actually be safer to take the damage and fall unconscious, then have an ally heal you later.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(199); });

undying-servitude|tcoe.name: Undying Servitude
undying-servitude|tcoe.summary: You get one skeleton or zombie, and not even a cool one. It’s a generic humanoid skeleton/zombie. CR 1/4. You can’t upcast the spell to get more of them since you’re not using a spell slot. I guess they could carry your loot or something? Set off traps? If you want a pet, go get a familiar. If you want an undead warrior, cast Summon Undead. I honestly can’t explain why they didn’t just add Animate Dead to the Warlock’s spell list.

bewitching-whispers|2014-phb.name: Bewitching Whispers
bewitching-whispers|2014-phb.summary: Compulsion is a fun crowd-control effect, but it doesn’t scale with spell slot level, you only get to use it once per day, and it’s not effective enough to justify an Invocation.

dreadful-word|2014-phb.name: Dreadful Word
dreadful-word|2014-phb.summary: Confusion is an unreliable debuff in the best of cases.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(600); });

ghostly-gaze|xgte.name: Ghostly Gaze
ghostly-gaze|xgte.summary: The ability to see through walls, even with limited range, is a huge benefit for adventurers. Knowing what’s in the next room of a dungeon can often turn a difficult fight into a cakewalk, or it might help you totally circumvent a problematic encounter.

protection-of-the-talisman|tcoe.name: Protection of the Talisman
protection-of-the-talisman|tcoe.summary: Pact of the TalismanPact of the Talisman wasn’t published in the 2024 PHB, and the 2014 Pact Boon feature is gone, so Talisman is not available to 2024 Warlocks.

relentless-hex|xgte.name: Relentless Hex
relentless-hex|xgte.summary: Potentially useful for Pact of the Blade builds. Your movement and options like Misty Step are typically sufficient, but if an enemy is especially fast or there are barriers in the way you may find this situationally useful.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(601); });

sculptor-of-flesh|2014-phb.name: Sculptor of Flesh
sculptor-of-flesh|2014-phb.summary: Even once per day, Polymorph is a fantastic single-target save-or-suck spell combined with a fantastic utility spell.
