Turn your enemies into harmless animals, or turn yourself or an ally into something which allows you to escape, explore, or fight better. However, remember that the target’s mental statistics change, so don’t go turning your allies into animals or they might forget who they are temporarily.

trickster-s-escape|xgte.name: Trickster’s Escape
trickster-s-escape|xgte.summary: Situational. Freedom of Movement is occasionally great, but you don’t get enough Invocation options to make this an easy choice, and the fact that you can only target yourself doesn’t help.

minions-of-chaos|2014-phb.name: Minions of Chaos
minions-of-chaos|2014-phb.summary: The 2024 PHB rewrote Conjure Elemental, and the new version is fantastic for the Warlock. Combine Grasp of Hadar and Repelling Blast to forcibly move enemies so that an enemy is always within the elemental’s reach. This gets even better if your party includes characters who can grapple enemies and drag them around and drop them adjacent to your elemental.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(602); });Unfortunately, the damage won’t scale since Pact Magic spell slots stop at 5th level, but don’t let that stop you. Restraining an enemy repeatedly for the duration of an encounter is useful at any level, and, even at high levels, many enemies have poor Dexterity saves.

bond-of-the-talisman|tcoe.name: Bond of the Talisman
bond-of-the-talisman|tcoe.summary: Pact of the TalismanPact of the Talisman wasn’t published in the 2024 PHB, and the 2014 Pact Boon feature is gone, so Talisman is not available to 2024 Warlocks.

chains-of-carceri|2014-phb.name: Chains of Carceri
chains-of-carceri|2014-phb.summary: Pact of the ChainHold Monster is really good, but limiting the targets to three specific creature types dramatically reduces how useful it is. You do get to use this at will, though, which is tempting. You can’t use it on the same target until you complete a long rest, but if you’re facing creatures of the right types you can use this several times in a day, making it a go-to option similar to Eldritch Blast. But, again, it’s limited to just three creature types.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(603); });

shroud-of-shadow|xgte.name: Shroud of Shadow
shroud-of-shadow|xgte.summary: This is so good that they made it into an Epic Boon. If you have a free moment, you should turn invisible. The only times you should be visible are when you’re talking to people or when you’ve broken invisibility.

aspect-of-the-moon|2014-phb.name: Aspect of the Moon
aspect-of-the-moon|2014-phb.summary: Pact of the TomeIf you really feel like you need this, you should have played an elf or a race that doesn’t sleep like the Warforged. Even then, the benefits here are extremely minor compared to most invocations.

book-of-ancient-secrets|2014-phb.name: Book of Ancient Secrets
book-of-ancient-secrets|2014-phb.summary: Pact of the TomePartially obsolete, but not entirely. The updated version of Pact of the Tome already gives you 2 free Rituals, and in the 2024 rules everyone is a Ritual caster.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(194); });However, the new Pact of the Tome doesn’t give you the ability to learn additional Rituals, which is where Book of Ancient Secrets remains useful. The Ritualist feat similarly only gets you level 1 Rituals. How useful this Invocation is comes down to how much use you will get out of Ritual spells from other classes.

gift-of-the-ever-living-ones|2014-phb.name: Gift of the Ever-Living Ones
gift-of-the-ever-living-ones|2014-phb.summary: Pact of the ChainThis includes healing spells like Healing Word and Cure Wounds, but it also includes Hit Dice rolled while resting. This is good, especially if you take damage a lot, but Pact of the Chain builds shouldn’t be drawing enough fire that this is important.This may be more useful for builds that take both Pact of the Blade and Pact of the Chain. If you’re built to fight in melee, you’re doing it in light armor with d8 hit dice, so the ability to heal quickly may prove useful, especially since Cure Wounds and Healing Word heal for twice as many dice as in the 2014 rules.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(195); });

improved-pact-weapon|2014-phb.name: Improved Pact Weapon
improved-pact-weapon|2014-phb.summary: Pact of the BladeThe only remaining value here is the +1 to attack and damage, but that’s still a pretty good benefit if your game doesn’t have abundant magic weapons.

rebuke-of-the-talisman|tcoe.name: Rebuke of the Talisman
rebuke-of-the-talisman|tcoe.summary: Pact of the TalismanPact of the Talisman wasn’t published in the 2024 PHB, and the 2014 Pact Boon feature is gone, so Talisman is not available to 2024 Warlocks.

voice-of-the-chain-master|2014-phb.name: Voice of the Chain Master
voice-of-the-chain-master|2014-phb.summary: Pact of the ChainFamiliars make great scouts, so exploring dangerous places through your familiar is a great way to do things. It’s also helpful for communicating with other creatures at a safe distance. Take Investment of the Chain Master first, but give this some consideration after that.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(196); });

aberrant-heir|efota.name: Aberrant Heir
aberrant-heir|efota.summary: The ability scores aren’t a good fit. You’ll get more value out of a background which gives you Magic Initiate.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(186); });

acolyte|phb.name: Acolyte
acolyte|phb.summary: Sage’s skills are a significantly better choice for the Wizard, but Acolyte can get you spells from outside of the Wizard’s spell list like Guidance and Healing Word.

archaeologist|efota.name: Archaeologist
archaeologist|efota.summary: An easy go-to option if you don’t want a lot of complexity or if you’re in a party that needs more skill coverage. Basically the same as Scribe, but you get different skills.

artisan|phb.name: Artisan
artisan|phb.summary: Dexterity, Intelligence, and one Intelligence-based skill. Not awful, but Crafter isn’t a very good feat.

carouser|aboh.name: Carouser
carouser|aboh.summary: Good ability scores, great feat, terrible skills.

criminal|phb.name: Criminal
criminal|phb.summary: Excellent ability scores, and Alert is great on a full caster who can make a huge impact by acting early. You may not get a lot of use out of the skills or proficiency in Thieves’ tools, but the ability scores and the feat are good enough that it may not be an issue.

dead-magic-dweller|frhof.name: Dead Magic Dweller
dead-magic-dweller|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, bad feat, bad skills.

dragon-cultist|frhof.name: Dragon Cultist
dragon-cultist|frhof.summary: Perfect ability scores, but the skills aren’t great, and you can’t afford to invest in Cult of the Dragon Initiate enough to keep it reliable.

emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Caretaker
emerald-enclave-caretaker|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, but the feat and skills are bad.

farmer|phb.name: Farmer
farmer|phb.summary: Bad ability scores, only one good skill.

guard|phb.name: Guard
guard|phb.summary: Intelligence and Wisdom can work for the Wizard, and Alert is a great feat for spellcasters. The skills aren’t great, but Perception never hurts.

house-agent|frhof.name: House Agent
house-agent|frhof.summary: Workable ability scores, one good skill, Lucky. Mulhorandi Tomb Raider is a much better choice.

ice-fisher|frhof.name: Ice Fisher
ice-fisher|frhof.summary: Alert is good, but no Charisma increase, and the skills are bad.

inquisitive|efota.name: Inquisitive
inquisitive|efota.summary: Good ability scores, decent skills, and Alert.

merchant|phb.name: Merchant
merchant|phb.summary: Good ability scores, and Lucky is an easy choice on any character, but the skills are a bad match.

mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.name: Mulhorandi Tomb Raider
mulhorandi-tomb-raider|frhof.summary: Perfect ability scores, Lucky, and two good Intelligence-based feats.

mythalkeeper|frhof.name: Mythalkeeper
mythalkeeper|frhof.summary: Crafter is an awful feat. The rest is great, but you have so many better options for getting comparable ability scores and skills.

noble|phb.name: Noble
noble|phb.summary: You can get the crucial Intelligence increase, and between History and Skilled you can expand your skill options, but I wouldn’t go this route unless you’re in a small party that needs more skill coverage.

purple-dragon-squire|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Squire
purple-dragon-squire|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, bad skills, but the feat is decent. Not enough to make up for the rest, though.

sage|phb.name: Sage
sage|phb.summary: Excellent for the Wizard even though it doesn’t let you go beyond your own spell list.

scribe|phb.name: Scribe
scribe|phb.summary: An easy go-to option if you don’t want a lot of complexity or if you’re in a party that needs more skill coverage, but it won’t do anything to improve your capabilities as a spellcaster beyond the Intelligence bonus. If you want different skills, consider Archaeologist.

shadowmasters-exile|frhof.name: Shadowmasters Exile
shadowmasters-exile|frhof.summary: Savage Attacker isn’t a good choice even if you’re building a Bladesinger.

shadowmoor-expert|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Expert
shadowmoor-expert|lfl.summary: Only worthwhile if you really want to build aroun Scorching Ray.

spellfire-initiate|frhof.name: Spellfire Initiate
spellfire-initiate|frhof.summary: Good ability scores, good feat, good skills.

house-cannith-heir|efota.name: House Cannith Heir
house-cannith-heir|efota.summary: Good ability scores, but you already get all of the spells worth having here.

house-jorasco-heir|efota.name: House Jorasco Heir
house-jorasco-heir|efota.summary: Bad ability scores and skills. The feat is good, but not enough on its own.

house-orien-heir|efota.name: House Orien Heir
house-orien-heir|efota.summary: Excellent ability scores and a good feat, but the skills are bad.

house-thuranni-heir|efota.name: House Thuranni Heir
house-thuranni-heir|efota.summary: The only redeeming quality is the Intelligence increase.

aasimar|phb.name: Aasimar
aasimar|phb.summary: Two damage resistances, Darkvision, a once per day heal, and a once per day combat transformation. Heavenly Wings lets you fly without Concentration, and Necrotic Shroud can discourage enemies from closing to melee. It’s only once per day, but that may be all that you need.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(187); });

changeling|efota.name: Changeling
changeling|efota.summary: You are not a Face, and this won’t solve that issue.

dragonborn|phb.name: Dragonborn
dragonborn|phb.summary: Darkvision, a damage resistance, and once per day flight are great, but you will likely never use the breath weapon beyond very low levels.

dwarf|phb.name: Dwarf
dwarf|phb.summary: Darkvision, resistance to the most common non-weapon damage type, and more hit points. The durability is largely wasted on a spellcaster fighting from a safe distance, and you have spells to handle hidden and invisible enemies.

elf|phb.name: Elf
elf|phb.summary: Darkvision and an extra skill are both great, plus you can get access to some spells from outside of the Wizard’s spell list.

gnome|phb.name: Gnome
gnome|phb.summary: Darkvision and Gnomish Cunning are both great, and the added cantrips from Gnomish Lineage offer some interesting utility options. Wizards don’t need much Wisdom, but proficiency in Wisdom saves and Advantage from Gnome Cunning will make your Wisdom saves reliably good.

goliath|phb.name: Goliath
goliath|phb.summary: Giant Heritage doesn’t offer a lot of easy options for full casters, but Cloud Jaunt is fantastic non-spell teleportation, so you can use it the same turn that you cast a leveled spell. Stone’s Endurance is also useful for frail spellcasters. Large Form won’t see much use, but Powerful Build might help you escape grapples if you can’t get out by other means (such as Cloud Jaunt).

halfling|phb.name: Halfling
halfling|phb.summary: Brave and Lucky are both helpful, and Halfling Nimbleness may help you get past enemies to get into a safer position, though it won’t prevent Opportunity Attacks when you need to leave an enemy’s reach. Naturally Stealthy might let you hide before combat starts, but without Cunning Action it won’t see use in combat.

human|phb.name: Human
human|phb.summary: An additional skill and origin feat are an easy choice on any build.

kalashtar|efota.name: Kalashtar
kalashtar|efota.summary: Very similar to the Gnome, but you give up some good things to get resistance to Psychic damage. Gnome is nearly always a better choice.

khoravar|efota.name: Khoravar
khoravar|efota.summary: If you want extra spellcasting, Human with Magic Initiate is a better choice. But if you’re happy with one Cantrip (potentially from outside of your spell list) and Darkvision, the Khoravar is still good.

orc|phb.name: Orc
orc|phb.summary: Adrenaline Rush is an excellent option for getting out of dangerous positions quickly without a spell, and the Temporary Hit Points are great on a frail spellcaster. If that doesn’t keep you alive, Relentless Endurance provides some insurance.

shifter|efota.name: Shifter
shifter|efota.summary: Darkvision, an extra skill (none of which work for the Wizard), and a good combat buff from Shifting. Beasthide and Swiftstride are both good ways to keep yourself alive.

tiefling|phb.name: Tiefling
tiefling|phb.summary: The Tiefling’s innate spellcasting is a good way to expand your prepared spells, but all of the available spells are already on the Wizard’s Spell list.

warforged|efota.name: Warforged
warforged|efota.summary: Durable and versatile. A good fit for literally any class. The AC bonus is especially helpful for Bladesinger builds.

lorwyn-changeling|lfl.name: Lorwyn Changeling
lorwyn-changeling|lfl.summary: Darkvision, one Charisma-based skill, and some free movement when you roll initiative. Unless absolutely desperate for that free movement, look elsewhere.

rimekin|lfl.name: Rimekin
rimekin|lfl.summary: Cold Cold Resistance, Darkvision, and you learn Ray of Frost. Not terrible, but not especially exciting. The other spells you get are terrible.

arcana|int.name: Arcana
arcana|int.summary: (Int): Wizards are all about Arcana, so it’s reasonable to assume that you know it.

history|int.name: History
history|int.summary: (Int): Helpful, especially in campaigns which go into history frequently.

insight|wis.name: Insight
insight|wis.summary: (Wis): You likely don’t have enough Wisdom to be particularly good at this, but it can be helpful if your party’s Face doesn’t have it.

investigation|int.name: Investigation
investigation|int.summary: (Int): Helpful, but likely best left for the party’s Scout.

medicine|wis.name: Medicine
medicine|wis.summary: (Wis): This skill is useless. Medicine is best done magically.

alert|phb.name: Alert
alert|phb.summary: Great for starting big area control spells or for dropping big area damage spells before allies get in the way or enemies get into melee range. The second benefit allows you to trade initiative with a willing ally. To maximize this benefit, you want to have numerous allies in combat who roll initiative on their own. A familiar is an easy addition, and at high levels you can add a homunculus. Between Advantage and two allies that you control entirely, you effectively get to roll initiative 4 times and choose your favorite.

crafter|phb.name: Crafter
crafter|phb.summary: Neat, but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops being impactful early in the game as players quickly accumulate enough to afford nearly anything in the Player’s Handbook. This notably omits the Herbalist Kit as a choice, so you can’t even use this to craft Potions of Healing.

cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.name: Cult of the Dragon Initiate
cult-of-the-dragon-initiate|frhof.summary: Very good, but you can’t afford the Wisdom to keep this effective.

emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.name: Emerald Enclave Fledgling
emerald-enclave-fledgling|frhof.summary: Bad. Take Ritual Caster if you want to talk to animals.

harper-agent|frhof.name: Harper Agent
harper-agent|frhof.summary: The Help Action isn’t useful enough to justify this unless you’re a Hobgoblin.

healer|phb.name: Healer
healer|phb.summary: Terrible. Cast Arcane Vigor or Wither and Bloom, or buy a healing potion.

lords-alliance-agent|frhof.name: Lords’ Alliance Agent
lords-alliance-agent|frhof.summary: Wizards don’t rely enough on attack rolls to care about the crit feature, and standing next to allies to get Advantage on one attack roll is not going to change that.

lucky|phb.name: Lucky
lucky|phb.summary: An easy choice on any character. It won’t directly impact your build, but it’s a great default if you don’t need anything else.

magic-initiate|phb.name: Magic Initiate
magic-initiate|phb.summary: A good way to expand your spellcasting. There aren’t any great combinations, but Healing Word may be worthwhile.

musician|phb.name: Musician
musician|phb.summary: A great way to contribute to any party.

purple-dragon-rook|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Rook
purple-dragon-rook|frhof.summary: No easy skill choice, but you can give Heroic Inspiration to your whole party once per day. Excellent on any build if you don’t need a different Origin Feat.

savage-attacker|phb.name: Savage Attacker
savage-attacker|phb.summary: You won’t use weapons enough for this to matter. Even the Bladesinger will get very little value here.

shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.name: Shadowmoor Hexer
shadowmoor-hexer|lfl.summary: The Wizard has too many better spells to spend a feat getting Hex. Until you can get spells like Conjure Minor Elementals and Spirit Shroud, it could combine nicely with Spellfire Flare or Socrching Ray for high single-target damage, but that’s the only consistent appeal.

skilled|phb.name: Skilled
skilled|phb.summary: Helpful if you couldn’t get all of the Intelligence-based skills from your class skills and your Background.

spellfire-spark|frhof.name: Spellfire Spark
spellfire-spark|frhof.summary: The resistance to magic damage will apply to many of the ranged effects which will reach past your party’s melee characters to target you. Wizards don’t all have built-in ways to use their Bonus Action, and the ability to cast Sacred Flame a times per day can make that unused acton economy impactful.

tavern-brawler|phb.name: Tavern Brawler
tavern-brawler|phb.summary: You should literally never make an unarmed strike.

tireless-reveler|aboh.name: Tireless Reveler
tireless-reveler|aboh.summary: A great choice on literally any character. While it doesn’t set you up for any specific build, Heroic Inspiration is always useful.

tough|phb.name: Tough
tough|phb.summary: Nice on a class with so little hp, but not impactful enough to justify the feat.

zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.name: Zhentarim Ruffian
zhentarim-ruffian|frhof.summary: The Opportunity Attack portion of the feat probably won’t do anything for you unless you’re a Bladesinger, but the ability to give your whole party Advantage on initiative is fantastic on anyone.

aberrant-dragonmark|efota.name: Aberrant Dragonmark
aberrant-dragonmark|efota.summary: Very similar to Magic Initiate if you could select Sorcerer, but you trade one Cantrip for a buff to Con saves and the THP/damage thing. To maximize the value of Aberrant Surge, you want to select a level 1 spell which you’ll cast frequently in combat, so pick a staple option like Absorb Elements or Shield which will remain equally effective for your whole career.

mark-of-detection|efota.name: Mark of Detection
mark-of-detection|efota.summary: Almost everything here is already on your spell list, and the rest isn’t worth having.

mark-of-finding|efota.name: Mark of Finding
mark-of-finding|efota.summary: If you’re planning to build around Conjure Minor Elementals, Hunter’s Mark can be a good stand-in at low levels. Combining Hunter’s Mark with Spellfire Flare or Scorching Rays is decent, inexpensive damage. Bladesingers may also find this useful.

mark-of-handling|efota.name: Mark of Handling
mark-of-handling|efota.summary: Basically the only thing useful here is Command, which is nowhere near enough. Take Magic Initiate or multiclass.

mark-of-healing|efota.name: Mark of Healing
mark-of-healing|efota.summary: Access to all of the essential healing spells.

mark-of-hospitality|efota.name: Mark of Hospitality
mark-of-hospitality|efota.summary: You’ll never use the skills, and most of the spells are already on your spell list.

mark-of-making|efota.name: Mark of Making
mark-of-making|efota.summary: Every spell worth having is already on your spell list.

mark-of-passage|efota.name: Mark of Passage
mark-of-passage|efota.summary: Access to some excellent spells including Find Steed, Pass Without Trace, and Phantom Steed.

mark-of-scribing|efota.name: Mark of Scribing
mark-of-scribing|efota.summary: Command is the only spell here that’s worth having and not already on your spell list. Take Magic Initiate.

mark-of-sentinel|efota.name: Mark of Sentinel
mark-of-sentinel|efota.summary: The Wizard does not have the hit points to support things like Vigilant Guardian and Warding Bond.

mark-of-shadow|efota.name: Mark of Shadow
mark-of-shadow|efota.summary: Almost all of the spells here are already on your spell list.

mark-of-storm|efota.name: Mark of Storm
mark-of-storm|efota.summary: Largely mediocre, and almost entirely from the Wizard’s spell list.

mark-of-warding|efota.name: Mark of Warding
mark-of-warding|efota.summary: Almost entirely already on your spell list.

athlete|phb.name: Athlete
athlete|phb.summary: You have spells to solve these problems.

charger|phb.name: Charger
charger|phb.summary: This could be useful for Bladesingers once you’ve hit 20 Intelligence and have room to look elsewhere, but by that level this isn’t especially impactful.

chef|phb.name: Chef
chef|phb.summary: This won’t contribute anything meaningful to what you do, but passing out snacks for THP always feels nice.

cloying-mists|aboh.name: Cloying Mists
cloying-mists|aboh.summary: Blocking line of sight can put enemies at a huge disadvantage, then you can spam AOEs while they stumble around in the fog trying to find you. It’s super annoying for your allies, though.

crossbow-expert|phb.name: Crossbow Expert
crossbow-expert|phb.summary: Even a Bladesinger should not be focused enough on weapons to justify this.

crusher|phb.name: Crusher
crusher|phb.summary: Wizards don’t have enough options for Bludgeoning damage to make this worthwhile.

delicious-pain|aboh.name: Delicious Pain
delicious-pain|aboh.summary: You do not have enough hit points to justify using this.

dual-wielder|phb.name: Dual Wielder
dual-wielder|phb.summary: Potentially useful for a Bladesinger build, but you’re much more likely to use your Bonus Action to cast spells.

durable|phb.name: Durable
durable|phb.summary: If you want to heal yourself as a Bonus Action, cast Arcane Vigor.

elemental-adept|phb.name: Elemental Adept
elemental-adept|phb.summary: Appealing for Evokers, but most wizards can’t afford to focus on a single element enough to justify this.

fey-touched|phb.name: Fey Touched
fey-touched|phb.summary: Two additional prepared spells each day, plus free castings. The 1st-level spell options can get you some great spells from outside of the Wizard’s spell list, and Misty Step is a staple spell for anyone who can cast it.

great-weapon-master|phb.name: Great Weapon Master
great-weapon-master|phb.summary: Bladesigners don’t get to use any of the qualifying weapons.

harper-teamwork|frhof.name: Harper Teamwork
harper-teamwork|frhof.summary: The Harper Agent feat is too heavy a text to justify this.

heavily-armored|phb.name: Heavily Armored
heavily-armored|phb.summary: Armor on a wizard is great, but if you’re taking 3 feats to get this far, you should have started with a level in Fighter.

heavy-armor-master|phb.name: Heavy Armor Master
heavy-armor-master|phb.summary: You should not taking enough hits to want this.

inspiring-leader|phb.name: Inspiring Leader
inspiring-leader|phb.summary: A fantastic buff for the whole party, but you may not meet the ability score requirements.

keen-mind|phb.name: Keen Mind
keen-mind|phb.summary: In concept at least, this is a great feat for the Wizard. In practice, it comes down to how useful your DM makes the Study action. If your DM is going to let you use Study in combat to gain useful information about enemies, this is great. If not, take Skill Expert instead.

light-bringer|aboh.name: Light Bringer
light-bringer|aboh.summary: Too situational to justify unless you’re in a Underdark campaign or a campaign where vampires feature heavily.

lightly-armored|phb.name: Lightly Armored
lightly-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Cleric or Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

lordly-resolve|frhof.name: Lordly Resolve
lordly-resolve|frhof.summary: Bad ability scores, and Standard Bearer is only situationally useful.

mage-slayer|phb.name: Mage Slayer
mage-slayer|phb.summary: Maybe useful once you’ve raised Intelligence to 20 so that you can more easily shut down enemy spellcasters. The automatic success on a save is great, too.

martial-weapon-training|phb.name: Martial Weapon Training
martial-weapon-training|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

medium-armor-master|phb.name: Medium Armor Master
medium-armor-master|phb.summary: Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and use Mage Armor.

moderately-armored|phb.name: Moderately Armored
moderately-armored|phb.summary: A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level. If you took Lightly Armored to get here, you absolutely should have multiclassed. Medium armor is nice, but it’s not worth two feats, especially when Mage Armor is an option.

mounted-combatant|phb.name: Mounted Combatant
mounted-combatant|phb.summary: With no way to get a special mount of any kind, there’s no reliable way to make this work.

observant|phb.name: Observant
observant|phb.summary: If you’re proficienct in Perception and have decent Wisdom, you may be well qualified to use Perception reliably. But even then, this is only helpful if your DM likes to use stealthy enemies and/or likes to include traps in combat encounters.

piercer|phb.name: Piercer
piercer|phb.summary: This appears to work with all of True Strike’s damage dice, but be careful about over-investing in a tactic that you fall back on to conserve spell slots.

poisoner|phb.name: Poisoner
poisoner|phb.summary: This does work with spells, but not enough spells deal poison damage to justify this.

polearm-master|phb.name: Polearm Master
polearm-master|phb.summary: You should not be using a polearm to attack stuff.

potent-dragonmark|efota.name: Potent Dragonmark
potent-dragonmark|efota.summary: Basically a Pact Magic spell slot and 10 additional prepared spells. If you took a Dragonmark feat and the spell list is even remotely useful, this is amazing.

purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.name: Purple Dragon Commandant
purple-dragon-commandant|frhof.summary: If you want THP, consider Chef or Inspiring Leader. If you want Advantage on attacks, look elsewhere.

resilient|phb.name: Resilient
resilient|phb.summary: Proficiency in Constitution saves really helps with Concentration, not to mention how common Constitution saves are. If you care primarily about Concentration it’s easy to compare this to War Caster. Advantage works out to a little more than +3, so once your Proficiency Bonus hits +4 Resilient becomes the more effective option of the two. However, Concentration only becomes a factor if you’re taking damage. If you’re taking damage, you have much bigger problems than Concentration. Instead, boost your Intelligence and use the extra prepared spell to pick up something that will keep you from getting hit like Shield, Invisibility, Blink, or Mirror Image.

ritual-caster|phb.name: Ritual Caster
ritual-caster|phb.summary: This only gets you access to level 1 Ritual spells, and there aren’t many of those which aren’t already on your spell list.

shadow-touched|phb.name: Shadow-Touched
shadow-touched|phb.summary: Two more prepared spells are always nice, and Invisibility is a staple spell, but Shadow Magic’s options for 1st-level spells simply aren’t as good as those available via Fey Touched.

sharpshooter|phb.name: Sharpshooter
sharpshooter|phb.summary: You could build a Bladesinger around using ranged weapons, but that’s what spells are for. If you’re worried about cover, cast a spell that relies on saves instead of spell attacks.

shield-master|phb.name: Shield Master
shield-master|phb.summary: You don’t get proficiency with shields.

skill-expert|phb.name: Skill Expert
skill-expert|phb.summary: A nice way to expand your skill options while enhancing whatever ability score you like.

skulker|phb.name: Skulker
skulker|phb.summary: Without Cunning Action to allow you to Hide as a Bonus Action, you lose much of the benefit.

slasher|phb.name: Slasher
slasher|phb.summary: This would work with True Strike, but be careful about over-investing in a tactic that you fall back on to conserve spell slots. You’ll need to throw a handaxe, since that’s the only simple weapon capable of dealing slashing damage at range.

spell-sniper|phb.name: Spell Sniper
spell-sniper|phb.summary: The range increase does not appear to affect True Strike since True Strike uses the weapon’s range rather than the spell’s range.

spellfire-adept|frhof.name: Spellfire Adept
spellfire-adept|frhof.summary: You have a spells that deal Radiant damage, but you really want AOE Radiant damage spells, and there are very few of those until high level. Even then, your d6 hit dice may not feel impactful.

street-justice|frhof.name: Street Justice
street-justice|frhof.summary: You don’t have the Strength to support this.

telekinetic|phb.name: Telekinetic
telekinetic|phb.summary: An easy go-to option. Remember that creatures can willingly fail saving throws, allowing you to use this on allies in order to move them out of dangerous positions, break grapples, or otherwise help them.

telepathic|phb.name: Telepathic
telepathic|phb.summary: Very cool, but usually talking works fine.

treacherous-allure|aboh.name: Treacherous Allure
treacherous-allure|aboh.summary: You have numerous ways to make enemies Charmed, but if you can make them Charmed, you can do something better than set them up for an attack.

vampire-touched|aboh.name: Vampire Touched
vampire-touched|aboh.summary: Nearly all of the qualifying spells are already on your spell list.

war-caster|phb.name: War Caster
war-caster|phb.summary: Advantage on Concentration isn’t as good as proficiency in Constitution saves, but it’s still very good. Reactive Spell is great, but you should not be in melee where you’re making Opportunity Attacks. The wording of the Opportunity Attack rules allows you to make an Opportunity Attack on any creature when it leaves your reach. When combined with Reactive Spell, you can cast spells on allies when they walk past you, allowing you quickly buff them in combat without cutting into your turn. This is clearly an abuse case, but RAW it appears to work.

weapon-master|phb.name: Weapon Master
weapon-master|phb.summary: Multiclass into a class that gets Weapon Mastery. A 1-level class dip into Fighter is almost always a better idea unless you’re expecting to reach 20th level.

zhentarim-tactics|frhof.name: Zhentarim Tactics
zhentarim-tactics|frhof.summary: This is only useful for melee characters planning to be hit with attacks, which isn’t you even if you’re a Bladesinger. If you want Expertise, take Skilled.

boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.name: Boon of Blazing Dawn
boon-of-blazing-dawn|aboh.summary: Immunity to a damage type is nice, but you miss a big chunk of the feat since you’re not likely using weapons. Even if you’re a Bladesinger, you’re probably getting most of your damage from spells anyway.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(192); });

boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.name: Boon of Bloodshed
boon-of-bloodshed|frhof.summary: Not good enough that making attack rolls is suddenly a good idea.

boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.name: Boon of Bountiful Health
boon-of-bountiful-health|frhof.summary: The extra THP is nice if you’re relying on spells like Shapechange and Polymorph, but it’s only 5 extra THP. Maximizing Hit Point Die rolls is also not especially useful since you have d6 hit dice. You could use it with Arcane Vigor to heal as a Bonus Action, but the amount healed is pitiful.

boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
boon-of-combat-prowess|phb.summary: Potentially useful if you’re relying on Polymorph, Bigby’s Hand, or Blade of Disaster.

boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.name: Boon of Desperate Resilience
boon-of-desperate-resilience|frhof.summary: A nice safey measure, but building yourself to endure damage won’t solve your small hit point pool due to 19+ levels of d6 hit dice. If you’re worried about dying, cast Wish to cast Clone.

boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
boon-of-dimensional-travel|phb.summary: Basically free Misty Step every time that you cast a spell as an Action. Unfortunately, Bonus Action and Reaction spells don’t qualify. According to the Rules Glossary: “When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.” Outside of combat, you can still use this to get around obstacles. Cast a harmless spell like Prestidigitation and you can teleport without making a mess.

boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.name: Boon of Energy Resistance
boon-of-energy-resistance|phb.summary: A powerful defense on any character. If legacy content is available, grab Absorb Elements and ignore this.

boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.name: Boon of Exquisite Radiance
boon-of-exquisite-radiance|frhof.summary: Maximizing the damage on Sunburst once per day is a big pile of damage, but it is only once per day.

boon-of-fate|phb.name: Boon of Fate
boon-of-fate|phb.summary: 2d4 averages to 5. Adding +5/-5 to a saving throw can rescue you or an ally, or it can cause an enemy to fail a save. On a d20 scale, 5 means that there’s a 25% chance on any given roll that this will have an impact. Granted, it is still a dice roll, so the smaller the gap, the safer this is to use. On a full caster where save-or-suck spells are such a huge part of your arsenal, this is devastatingly effective. The fact that you can use it once per encounter is amazing.

boon-of-fortitude|phb.name: Boon of Fortitude
boon-of-fortitude|phb.summary: More hit points are great on a class as frail as the Wizard, but given the choice between this and Resilient (Constitution), you need proficiency in Constitution saves much more than 40 hp and some extra healing.

boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
boon-of-irresistible-offense|phb.summary: You should not be relying on B/P/S damage enough for Resistance to be an issue. The natural 20 effect could lead to big damage spikes with spells like Scorching Ray, but that’s not enough to make this a good choice unless you’re already built around Scorching Ray.

boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.name: Boon of Looming Shadows
boon-of-looming-shadows|aboh.summary: Dodge as a Bonus Action is a really good defensive option, but you’re probably using your Bonus Action for magic.

boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.name: Boon of Misty Escape
boon-of-misty-escape|aboh.summary: Great insurance for any character. Compare this to Boon of Recovery.

boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.name: Boon of Poison Mastery
boon-of-poison-mastery|frhof.summary: Immunity to poison is great, but you’re not likely to benefit from the damage reroll.

boon-of-recovery|phb.name: Boon of Recovery
boon-of-recovery|phb.summary: The Last Stand feature is great insurance, but defintiely not enough to justify your first Epic Boon. Try to get someone to cast Death Ward on you.

boon-of-revelry|frhof.name: Boon of Revelry
boon-of-revelry|frhof.summary: Otto’s Irresistible Dance is a great save-or-suck spell, and improving it by preventing enemies from using Verbal components is a great way to mess with enemy spellcasters.

boon-of-siberys|efota.name: Boon of Siberys
boon-of-siberys|efota.summary: Yes, the spells come from your spell list, but you can cast it without components and it’s usable once per Short Rest. Heroes’ Feast is a passable default because the effect is so good and the component cost is so high, but you don’t benefit from using it every Short Rest. If you want a combat option, you can get Maze from Mark of Warding, or Dominate Monster or Power Word Stun from the Sorcerer spell list.

boon-of-skill|phb.name: Boon of Skill
boon-of-skill|phb.summary: Always a good fallback once you’ve grabbed a few other boons, but Wizards don’t do a lot with skills beyond the Intelligence-based skills which you likely started with at level 1.

boon-of-speed|phb.name: Boon of Speed
boon-of-speed|phb.summary: Take Boon of Dimensional Travel instead.

boon-of-spell-recall|phb.name: Boon of Spell Recall
boon-of-spell-recall|phb.summary: This gives you a 25% chance to retain your spell slot when casting spells of up to level 4. You get 4 level 1 spell slots and 3 of each of levels 2, 3, and 4. On average, you get 1 extra level 1 spell slot, and slightly less than 1 for levels 2, 3, and 4. This is fine, but definitely don’t make it your first boon.

boon-of-terror|frhof.name: Boon of Terror
boon-of-terror|frhof.summary: You have tons of spells that can makes enemies Frightened, then use the Reaction to make them flee. Of course, you could also cast Fear, which already does that.

boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.name: Boon of the Bright Sun
boon-of-the-bright-sun|frhof.summary: Give yourself and your allies 10 Temporary Hit Points each turn. Boon of Bountiful Health is a a good complement to this, giving you extra THP whenever you gain any.

boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.name: Boon of the Furious Storm
boon-of-the-furious-storm|frhof.summary: Resistance/immunity to two damage types. The Disadvantage mechanic may be useful, but you have frustratingly few good options for Lighting or Thunder damage. Chain Lightning and Jallarzi’s Storm of Radiance both work, but that may not be enough to justify this.

boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
boon-of-the-night-spirit|phb.summary: Be invisible at all times outside of combat. Take advantage of invisibility at the start of combat, then look for ways to become invisible as frequently as possible. Even if you’re not making attack rolls (and you almost certainly aren’t doing so often), the defensive benefits of invisibility are massive. However, remember that a lot of things are an Action, so it’s very easy to break this invisibility. Notable examples that people easily overlook include Hide, Search, and Study.

boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.name: Boon of the Soul Drinker
boon-of-the-soul-drinker|frhof.summary: Resistance to two damage types. The healing is negligible. Take Boon of Fortitude instead.

boon-of-truesight|phb.name: Boon of Truesight
boon-of-truesight|phb.summary: Fantastic, but technically only situationally useful. You can already cast both See Invisibility and Truesight. This is objectively good, but don’t make it your first boon unless you have a very specific reason to do so.

dagger|unknown.name: Dagger
dagger|unknown.summary: Carry one or two for utility purposes at any level, but the damage isn’t good enough to make it a good idea.

light-crossbow|unknown.name: Light Crossbow
light-crossbow|unknown.summary: A light crossbow combined with True Strike will deal more damage than Fire Bolt until you reach level 11, making it the Wizard’s go-to attack option at least until level 11.

quarterstaff|unknown.name: Quarterstaff
quarterstaff|unknown.summary: If you’re preparing True Strike to use with a light crossbow, you can also use it with a quarterstaff two-handed for the same amount of damage. You don’t want to do this intentionally, but it’s a good backup option.

artificer|unknown.name: Artificer
artificer|unknown.summary: Starting with a level in artificer gets you a lot. Proficiency in medium armor, shields, and Constitution saving throws are really tempting, plus Artificers get access to some low-level spells which the Wizard doesn’t like Cure Wounds.

cleric|unknown.name: Cleric
cleric|unknown.summary: A single level with the right domain can get you heavy armor proficiency, not to mention how many great low-level spells the Cleric gets. You’ll also advance your spellcasting, though remember that your prepared spells are always based on your levels in a single class.

fighter|unknown.name: Fighter
fighter|unknown.summary: Starting with a level in Fighter gets you martial weapons, heavy armor, shields, Weapon Mastery, and proficiency in Constitution saves. Using a martial weapon, Weapon Mastery, and True Strike is startlingly effective as a cantrip, allowing you to get better damage, better range, and different Weapon Mastery properties like Push, Slow, or Vex.

acid-splash|phb.name: Acid Splash
acid-splash|phb.summary: If you have allies using Push weapons, you may be able to use this to reliably hit multiple enemies. Otherwise, it’s rare to find enemies clustered enough to justify this and it’s only appealing if you can hit multiple targets.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(178); });

blade-ward|phb.name: Blade Ward
blade-ward|phb.summary: At very low levels, this can be a good defensive option. As you gain levels and get more spell slots, you’ll want to reserve your Concentration for more impactful spells.

booming-blade|scag-tcoe.name: Booming Blade
booming-blade|scag-tcoe.summary: Excellent for Bladesingers, but most Wizards should never be in a position to use this.

buzzing-bee|drops.name: Buzzing Bee
buzzing-bee|drops.summary: Long range, no save, and it inhibits stealth, Perception, and Concentration. It’s somehow both broadly useful but also very difficult to justify. Buzzing Bee prevents the target from benefiting from invisibility, which means that they can’t benefit from hiding. But you need to be able to see them, which means that most enemies that rely on invisiblity won’t care. This doesn’t allow a save like Faerie Fire does, but Faerie Fire also don’t require you to see the target, and Faerie Fire also works as a great support option even when enemies aren’t invisibile. Imposing Disadvantage on Perception may be helpful for sneaking past enemies, but since Buzzing Bee is single-target and has a Verbal component, which makes it difficult to use in most stealth situations. The Concentration option may be helpful against enemy spellcasters, but for the same action cost and spell slot you can use any number of other spells that could actually break Concentration.

chill-touch|phb.name: Chill Touch
chill-touch|phb.summary: Bad damage at touch range with a secondary effect that rarely matters.

control-flames|eepc-xgte.name: Control Flames
control-flames|eepc-xgte.summary: Notably omitted from the function of Control Flames is the ability to create or extinguish them. Druidcraft and Prestidigitation both grant the ability to light or snuff out small flames. Control Flames will let you spread flames, extinguish them, change their color, etc., but if you want to light a torch you need to use flint and tinder like a commoner. You can use this to dramatically improve the effectiveness of torches, or to snuff out enemy light sources at a distance, but those are situational uses that you can address with better light sources like the Daylight spell or by using water. Neither function is frequent or useful enough to justify a Cantrip with so little functionality.

create-bonfire|eepc.name: Create Bonfire
create-bonfire|eepc.summary: A low-budget area control spell. It does as much initial damage as most Cantrips, but the ongoing damage only applies when a creature enters the area or ends their turn there, so you can only get extra damage if you can force an enemy into the space or if you cast it on them and they remain in their space. If you have an ally who likes to grapple enemies, or if you need to block a narrow space like a hall or doorway, this is extremely useful if you’re not already committing Concentration to something else. However, Create Bonfire’s reliance on Concentration can become a problem as you gain levels because Concentration is such a precious resource, and many of the best spells require Concentration.

dancing-lights|phb.name: Dancing Lights
dancing-lights|phb.summary: An amusing distraction, but you can usually accomplish the same thing using Mage Hand and a candle or torch.

encode-thoughts|ggtr.name: Encode Thoughts
encode-thoughts|ggtr.summary: Interesting, but insanely situational. The only way to consume the thought strand is to cast this spell within the 8-hour duration, so this isn’t even a great option for communicating over long distances.

fire-bolt|phb.name: Fire Bolt
fire-bolt|phb.summary: Great range and solid damage. A good go-to option when all you need is damage. Toll the Dead will do more damage and has a better damage type, but Fire Bolt has twice the range. At low levels, True Strike with a crossbow will be more effective.

friends|phb.name: Friends
friends|phb.summary: High risk, high reward. This is great for dealing with brief social interactions with NPCs that you’ll never see again or that have no way to cause trouble for you, or who you might end up attacking anyway for whatever reason. There’s no Verbal component, so you can safely use this while hidden.

frostbite|eepc-xgte.name: Frostbite
frostbite|eepc-xgte.summary: Low damage for a Cantrip (d6-based), but the big appeal is Disadvantage on the target’s next weapon attack. Unfortunately, it works on Constitution saving throws, and those tend to be relatively high compared to other saving throws. If someone in your party is using Sap weapons, don’t take this.

green-flame-blade|scag.name: Green-Flame Blade
green-flame-blade|scag.summary: Excellent for Bladesingers, but most Wizards should never be in a position to use this.

gust|eepc-xgte.name: Gust
gust|eepc-xgte.summary: If this scaled somehow, I would be interested. If it had more options, I would be interested. If it had better range, I would be interested. But, as it stands, this spell is almost totally useless.

infestation|xgte.name: Infestation
infestation|xgte.summary: Low damage, unpredictable, and it targets Constitution saves.

light|phb.name: Light
light|phb.summary: Disposable magic light is fantastic, but you’ll do fine with torches if you don’t have room for the Cantrip.

lightning-lure|scag-tcoe.name: Lightning Lure
lightning-lure|scag-tcoe.summary: Situational, but potentially useful for Bladesingers to pull enemies into melee or if you’re running Yolande’s Regal Presence. If you’re flying, you may even be able to pull enemies into the air to cause a small amount of falling damage.

mage-hand|phb.name: Mage Hand
mage-hand|phb.summary: The ability to move objects at a safe distance is profoundly useful. Use it to pull levers, open doors, sort your laundry, and all manner of other important but potentially hazardous tasks where you wouldn’t want to risk your own hands.

mending|phb.name: Mending
mending|phb.summary: Too situational. Short of Rust Monsters and a few oozes, nearly nothing in 5e deals damage to your equipment. If you’re playing Spelljammer, this is essential, but otherwise you can skip it.

message|phb.name: Message
message|phb.summary: Situational. Use this to send messages without revealing your position.

mind-sliver|tcoe-phb.name: Mind Sliver
mind-sliver|tcoe-phb.summary: Psychic damage on an Intelligence save is spectacular on its own. Intelligence saves are consistently among the lowest, and psychic damage resistance/immunity is rare (though it does exist, especially on mindless enemies like zombies). That alone makes Mind Sliver arguably the most reliable Cantrip damage in 5e, but it gets better from there. With only Verbal components, Mind Sliver works while you’re tied up or have your hands full, making it a great option for War Caster. It also imposes a -1d4 penalty on the target’s next saving throw making them an easier target for save-or-suck spells, or you can just repeatedly hit them with Mind Sliver and watch enemies try to beat your spell save DC with a +0 save bonus and the -1d4 penalty from your previous hit.

minor-illusion|phb.name: Minor Illusion
minor-illusion|phb.summary: : Room for plenty of creative, deceptive uses. The 5-foot cube is easily enough to create something to hide behind, provided that your enemies don’t see you create the illusion.

mold-earth|eepc-xgte.name: Mold Earth
mold-earth|eepc-xgte.summary: You know what else can do this? A shovel. Sure, shoveling will take a long time, but you get at most 4 Cantrips, and, if you can replace a Cantrip with a mundane item, it’s probably a bad Cantrip. The only important function is to create difficult terrain, but you’re limited to two ongoing effects, which means you only get two 5-foot squares. And, again, you could do that with a shovel. You’re about as likely to use this in combat as you are to use a shovel, too.

poison-spray|phb.name: Poison Spray
poison-spray|phb.summary: Excellent damage on a spell attack, but the range isn’t great, and resistance/immunity to poison is common, so it can’t be your only attack option.

prestidigitation|phb.name: Prestidigitation
prestidigitation|phb.summary: Whenever you want to do something small and magical that’s not covered by another spell, it’s usually covered by prestidigitation. This spell is exceptionally versatile. For suggestions on how to use Prestidigitation to its fullest, see our Practical Guide to Prestidigitation.

ray-of-frost|phb.name: Ray of Frost
ray-of-frost|phb.summary: Stacking speed penalties is easy and very powerful in the 2024 DnD rules thanks to the addition of the Slow Weapon Mastery. By teaming up with an ally with a Slow weapon and Slasher, you can drop many creatures’ speeds to 0, leaving entirely unable to move.

shape-water|eepc-xgte.name: Shape Water
shape-water|eepc-xgte.summary: This is as abusable and versatile as Prestidigitation. Freeze a solid 5 foot cube of water and drop it on someone. Pour water into a lock, freeze it, and allow the ice expansion to break the lock. Put a dome of ice over something you’re protecting. Build a small bridge in 5-foot segments. Block a hallway. Freeze a door in place. The uses are numerous and fantastic. If you have a barrel of water and this Cantrip, you have a solution to most problems. Honestly the fact that this spell is so much better than its other elemental equivalents (Control Flames, Gust, and Mold Earth) is a good indication of just how awful those spells are. See our Practical Guide to Shape Water for more on how great Shape Water is.

shocking-grasp|phb.name: Shocking Grasp
shocking-grasp|phb.summary: Touch range, disappointing damage, unimpressive secondary effect.

sword-burst|scag-tcoe.name: Sword Burst
sword-burst|scag-tcoe.summary: If you are in a position where it makes sense to use this, you should probably be running away unless you’re a Bladesinger. For the Bladesinger, this is a fantastic way to handle crowds while you’re in melee. Other Wizards should avoid this.

thunderclap|eepc-phb.name: Thunderclap
thunderclap|eepc-phb.summary: Thunder damage is worse than Sword Burst’s force damage, and Thunderclap uses Constitution saves, which tend to be high.

toll-the-dead|xgte-phb.name: Toll the Dead
toll-the-dead|xgte-phb.summary: 60 ft. range, the damage is measured in d12’s most of the time, and almost nothing will resist it since it’s Necrotic damage.

true-strike|phb.name: True Strike
true-strike|phb.summary: Your go-to attack Cantrip until at least level 5, but possibly until level 11. A crossbow with True Strike will do more damage and have better range than most damaging Cantrips until their damage has scaled at least once. If you increase your spellcasting modifier to +4 at level 4, a crossbow with True Strike will deal more damage (average 12) than d10-based Cantrips like Fire Bolt (average 11).

absorb-elements|eepc-xgte.name: Absorb Elements
absorb-elements|eepc-xgte.summary: A fantastic defensive option at any level, this will save your life when you encounter an unpredictable source of elemental damage like a trap or a spell. The bonus damage on your next attack is largely useless, but it still feels cool when you use it.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(179); });

alarm|phb.name: Alarm
alarm|phb.summary: Never prepare this, but cast this at least once as a Ritual any time that you take a Long Rest.

burning-hands|phb.name: Burning Hands
burning-hands|phb.summary: The cone is just 15 feet, so it’s unlikely that you’ll hit more than two targets. The 3d6 damage is fine, but it’s not enough to justify rushing into melee unless you have enough movement to retreat to safety after doing so.

catapult|eepc.name: Catapult
catapult|eepc.summary: Equivalent damage to Chromatic Orb, but Chromatic Orb is more versatile, has better range, and can bounce. Where Catapult shines is its reliability: If a target passes their saving throw, the object continues moving until it hits something or runs out of range. If you can line up two or more targets, yout odds of hitting and dealing damage improve considerably. If your DM allows it, you might be able to Catapult items like Acid or Alchemist’s Fire to add additional damage. RAW, this has no additional effect, but it sure would be fun if it did.

cause-fear|xgte.name: Cause Fear
cause-fear|xgte.summary: A decent low-level crowd control option, but it has some drawbacks and it becomes obsolete as other options come online. Frightened foes can’t move toward you, which is great for melee enemies which tend to have poor mental stats like many beasts and many non-caster humanoids at low levels. Still, targets are able to attack (albeit with Disadvantage) and cast spells, and resistance/immunity to fear is common.

charm-person|phb.name: Charm Person
charm-person|phb.summary: If you can cast this on a target outside of combat without them noticing, this can be a great way to defuse a potentially hostile situation. However, the spell has some complications. Charm Person has no visual effect like a ball of fire, so there’s no visual indication that the spell succeeded or failed. The target doesn’t know that they’ve been targeted by the spell if they succeed on the saving throw, but you don’t know if they succeeded or failed unless your DM decides to tell you (and they are under no obligation to do so). So generally your best bet is to cast this once or twice and hope for the best before presenting yourself to your target.

chromatic-orb|phb.name: Chromatic Orb
chromatic-orb|phb.summary: Solid damage with good range, and the ability to pick the damage type means that you can always avoid damage resistances if you know what the target is resistant to. The ability to jump to additional targets is nice, but the Wizard doesn’t have options like Metamagic to artificially boost their chance to roll doubles. For an example of how to put Chromatic Orb to good use, see our Draconic Sorcery Sorcerer Subclass Guide.

color-spray|phb.name: Color spray
color-spray|phb.summary: The effect is not powerful enough and the duration is not long enough to justify the spell slot.

comprehend-languages|phb.name: Comprehend languages
comprehend-languages|phb.summary: Cast this as a ritual. Unfortunately it’s a self-targeting spell so your communication will be one-way unless whatever you’re talking to also has a solution.

detect-magic|phb.name: Detect Magic
detect-magic|phb.summary: Essential. If you’re not concentrating on anything else, it’s often a good idea to cast this as a ritual and walk around with it.

disguise-self|phb.name: Disguise Self
disguise-self|phb.summary: Learning a single spell is cheaper than proficiency in a Disguise Kit. Buying a scroll is even cheaper.

earth-tremor|eepc-xgte.name: Earth Tremor
earth-tremor|eepc-xgte.summary: Not nearly enough damage, and being prone isn’t enough of a problem in 5e. The difficult terrain effect is the real draw. It only works on “loose earth or stone”, but that covers nearly anything you’ll stand on except wood, so it’s an easy way to create difficult terrain. Unfortunately, it also affects you, so be careful not to trap yourself among enemies.

elementalism|unknown.name: Elementalism
elementalism|unknown.summary: Very flavorful, but almost totally useless.

expeditious-retreat|phb.name: Expeditious Retreat
expeditious-retreat|phb.summary: Situational and poorly named. Expeditious Retreat is great for chases and for running long distances, but those situations aren’t common enough to justify preparing this unless you know it’s going to happen. The duration is good and Dash as a bonus action offers a lot of extra speed, but since this requires Concentration you’ll almost always want a different buff instead.

false-life|phb.name: False Life
false-life|phb.summary: A great use for your low-level spell slots when they stop being effective in combat. 2d4+4 hit points is far more than most Wizards get from an extra hit die, which can make a huge difference for a class that’s typically very frail.

feather-fall|phb.name: Feather Fall
feather-fall|phb.summary: Someone in the party needs to have this at all times, and you’re someone. Falling damage is a silly, embarrassing way to die.

find-familiar|phb.name: Find Familiar
find-familiar|phb.summary: A familiar is a fantastically useful asset. It can’t attack, but it can still do other useful things like carrying items between party members, taking the Help action, and scouting for danger. Familiars have terribly few hit points, but you can always resummon them if you have the 10gp worth of components handy, so after very low levels your familiar’s death is more of an inconvenience than a real loss. You may also find specific buffs like Dragon Breath which you can cast on your familiar to turn it into a serious threat in combat. The Owl is a go-to option because it has Flyby, allowing it to fly in and out of enemies’ reach without provoking Opportunity Attacks so that it can use the Help action. The Giant Fly is also a great option because it can fly and it’s large enough that you can ride it. Have it take the Dodge Action in combat to make up for its horrid AC, or you might find yourself needing Feather Fall.

fog-cloud|phb.name: Fog Cloud
fog-cloud|phb.summary: An excellent way to cover your escape, but you can’t see through the fog any better than anyone else, so don’t expect to fight in this without some other advantage most of the time. Fog Cloud can be a way to negate Advantage if your enemies have the upper hand, so if you’re facing enemies who are invisible, hidden, or have some other source of Advantage, Fog Cloud can take that away, effectively leveling the playing field so that no one can see each other. Such situations are rare, but it’s nice to know that there’s a countermeasure when those situations do arise.

frost-fingers|id-rotf.name: Frost Fingers
frost-fingers|id-rotf.summary: Burning Hands, but it’s cold damage and less damage on average. It does scale better than Burning Hands due to the larger damage die, but not by enough to make this worthwhile.

grease|phb.name: Grease
grease|phb.summary: Even if creatures fall prone, that only eats half of their movement, and with a radius of just 10 feet most creatures can walk out unimpeded once they’re no longer prone. For the record: Grease was never flammable. The 2024 rules are now explicit about that.

ice-knife|eepc-xgte-phb.name: Ice Knife
ice-knife|eepc-xgte-phb.summary: The closest you’ll get to Fireball at this level. Allowing both an attack and a save seems weird, and while it makes it likely that foes will avoid partial damage, they’ll also likely take at least part of the damage. The only problem is that the splash damage radius is so small that Acid Splash can fill the same role until better spells come online.

identify|phb.name: Identify
identify|phb.summary: Only situationally useful. Even if you encounter a magic item, this typically isn’t necessary because you can usually identify a magic item by spending a Short Rest in contact with it. Some (but not all) cursed magic items can be identified using the Identify spell.

illusory-script|phb.name: Illusory Script
illusory-script|phb.summary: A fun party trick, but 10 gp is expensive if you want to use this often.

jim-s-magic-missile|ai.name: Jim’s Magic Missile
jim-s-magic-missile|ai.summary: This spell is fun, but it’s risky unless you can mitigate the risks with Advantage on the attacks and/or with a way to negate natural 1’s like the Halfling’s Lucky trait. If you can get Advantage on all of the attacks (maybe by making the target Restrained) you can easily outdo the average damage of most other 1st-level spell since Jim’s Magic Missile does more damage than usual on a critical hit.

jump|phb.name: Jump
jump|phb.summary: An excellent mobility boost. The 30-foot jump can be vertical, allowing you to reach high places and navigate around many obstacles, but remember that you still fall afterward.

longstrider|phb.name: Longstrider
longstrider|phb.summary: A helpful buff for highly mobile characters, and with an hour-long duration it can be a great use of low-level spell slots once your level 1 spells start lagging in combat.

mage-armor|phb.name: Mage Armor
mage-armor|phb.summary: A great source of AC, but it provides a perpetual tax on your spell slots and 13+Dex will stop being effective as enemies’ attack bonuses scale while your Dexterity remains static so that you can focus on Intelligence. Mage Armor’s usefulness improves if you have other lightly-armored characters in the party. Learning Mage Armor just for yourself can feel like a waste, but when you’re casting it on bards, druids, fighters, rangers, rogues, and warlocks, suddenly learning and preparing one low-level spell becomes a staple defensive option for your whole party.

magic-missile|phb.name: Magic Missile
magic-missile|phb.summary: A great option with long range and reliable damage of what is probably the best damage type in the game. The math is mildly complicated, but Magic Missile is the best single-target damage of any 1st-level spell.

protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.name: Protection From Evil and Good
protection-from-evil-and-good|phb.summary: An absolutely fantastic defensive option, but it’s technically situational.

ray-of-sickness|phb.name: Ray of Sickness
ray-of-sickness|phb.summary: Less damage than other spells of the same level, but poisoning a target for a turn means Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks for the full turn. Against martial enemies that you can hit reliably, this can be a low-cost way to make them much less effective.

shield|phb.name: Shield
shield|phb.summary: The fact that you can cast this after hearing the result of the attack roll means that you can frequently turn a hit into a miss. On top of Mage Armor, you can effectively have an AC of 17+Dex so long as you have 1st-level spell slots to spend.

silent-image|phb.name: Silent Image
silent-image|phb.summary: While not nearly so powerful as Major Image, if you just want an object or a visual effect, Silent Image does the job just as well. Throw up a fake wall, door, or portcullis to slow pursuers. Create a piece of furniture, then hide inside it and stab people when they try to open it. Illusions are limited more by your creativity (and your DM’s willingness to play along) than by the spell’s text.

silvery-barbs|scoc.name: Silvery Barbs
silvery-barbs|scoc.summary: Extremely powerful, but also very complicated. See our blog post on Silvery Barbs for details on the numerous abuse cases which the spell allows.

sleep|phb.name: Sleep
sleep|phb.summary: Making your targets Incapacitated will rob them of most of their turn and break Concentration. You may get lucky and have targets fall asleep after the second save, especially if you can debuff their save with Mind Sliver or some other effect. This is an incredibly powerful save-or-suck spell that will work for your whole career and doesn’t need to be upcast. Sure, the AOE is tiny, but if this were a single-target spell it would still be really good.

snare|xgte.name: Snare
snare|xgte.summary: Good for setting a trap, or if you’re resting somewhere dangerous with a convenient choke point like a narrow hallway. Targets are restrained for at least one round, which is hopefully enough for you to fight your way out of your bedroll and grab a weapon.

spellfire-flare|frhof.name: Spellfire Flare
spellfire-flare|frhof.summary: 2d10 damage is good for a level 1 spell, and the ability to ignore cover means that you can still use this in situations where you might otherwise use Magic Missile or a spells which calls for a saving throw. But if you’re only using this as a level 1 spell, you’re missing a lot of the value. Upcasting Spellfire Flare adds additional attacks much like Scorching Rays, but Spellfire Flare’s 2d10 damage better damage type, and ability to ignore partial cover make Spellfire Flare a much better choice. At level 2, Scorching Ray deals 6d6 total damage (avg. 21), while Spellfire Flare deals 4d10 (avg. 22) damage, and the gap widens with every spell level. The one exception is combining the two spells with Conjure Minor Elementals, and even then it’s only because the additional attack could yield more total damage. The math gets complicated depending on the spell levels at which you cast both spells since Spellfire Flare’s damage dice are so much better. We should also compare Spellfire Flare to Chromatic Orb. At level 1, Chromatic Orb’s 3d8 (avg. 13.5) damage is better than Spellfire Flare’s, but the use cases are different. Spellfire Flare is a machine gun that’s great for eliminating single targets, and its damage scales linearly as you add spell levels. Chromatic Orb’s damage per target increases less quickly (1d8 vs. 2d10), but it’s value comes form bouncing the orb to successive targets, which becomes more reliable as you add more spell levels.

tasha-s-caustic-brew|tcoe.name: Tasha’s Caustic Brew
tasha-s-caustic-brew|tcoe.summary: This is a challenging spell; if you just want damage, cast Burning Hands. With a 1-minute duration and 2d4 damage each round, you can deal a total of 20d4 damage to each target (average 50) which is enough to kill many creatures up to CR 2 or 3 (ignore the table in the “creating a monster” rules in the DMG; real monster stats tend to have high “offensive CR” and low “defensive CR” so very few of them have hit points which line up with those rules). However, you’re almost certainly not going to get the full damage, and that’s probably fine. If you spend an Action and a spell slot to cast this and a target spends their Action to remove the effect, you have traded your Action for theirs and probably also did a bunch of damage. In encounters where your party outnumbers your enemies, that’s a winning trade for you. In encounters where your enemies outnumber your party, you’re in a target-rich environment and may be able to hit 3 or more targets, in which case trading your own Action for one Action from several enemies is a great way to offset your enemies’ numerical advantage. Lines are a difficult AOE because it’s often difficult to catch more than two enemies in a straight 5-foot wide line. It’s also all-or-nothing, so creatures which pass the save are totally unharmed. This requires Concentration, so if you don’t affect multiple targets you may need to weigh the benefits of whatever ongoing damage you’re getting against the ability to spend your Concentration on a different spell instead.

tasha-s-hideous-laughter|phb.name: Tasha’s Hideous Laughter
tasha-s-hideous-laughter|phb.summary: A great low-level save or suck, but generally you want to use this on a creature then leave it alone until you’ve dealt with anything else in the encounter. The best comparison at this level is to Sleep. Sleep is an AOE (though a small one), and if your target fails the second save, they fall Unconscious. Sleep will be more impactful, but it’s also easier to remove.

tenser-s-floating-disk|phb.name: Tenser’s Floating Disk
tenser-s-floating-disk|phb.summary: While you can get off the ground with Floating Disk, you can’t ride it around without some very complicated shenanigans like have a second Wizard and casting Gust on each other repeatedly. Generally you’ll use this to carry heavy things like loot or unconscious party members. It’s very specifically written to have almost no use beyond carrying heavy objects for you, so you’ll likely never cast this unless you cast it as a ritual.

thunderwave|phb.name: Thunderwave
thunderwave|phb.summary: With the exception of Gust, this is one of your very few options for pushing enemies away from you. It’s especially appealing if you can push an enemy into an area control effect, but otherwise it’s not a good go-to option for damage output in combat.

unseen-servant|phb.name: Unseen Servant
unseen-servant|phb.summary: This has very limited utility in combat or in dangerous situations, but that doesn’t mean that it has none. With a 1-hour duration you can get a lot done with a single casting. Interacting with items can mean opening doors and chests, carrying items, using potions on allies, and other things which you might not have time or patience to do. 2 Strength isn’t enough to carry anything heavy or to break down a door, but it’s often enough to trigger traps.

wardaway|frhof.name: Wardaway
wardaway|frhof.summary: A weaker version of Tasha’s Mind Whip, Wardaway makes some huge trades to fit into a level 1 spell. The damage is obviously much worse, but that’s not why you’re here. The target still gets to move and act in the same turn, but halving their speed is still impactful. The biggest limitation is that Wardaway uses a Constitution save instead of a much more reliable Intelligence save. At low levels where enemies have very few saving throw proficiencies, Wardaway may be decently reliable. But enemies at low levels also rarely have Bonus Actions, so they’re likely to fail the save and barely notice the spell’s effect. If you are going to upcast this, cast Tasha’s Mind Whip instead.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(180); });

witch-bolt|phb.name: Witch Bolt
witch-bolt|phb.summary: Spending the same spell slot on Magic Missile is frequently a better choice, but Witch Bolt is useful against large single foes, especially at low levels where you likely have few uses for your Bonus Action. You still get to use the Bonus Action effect even if your initial attack misses, so Witch Bolt can be very effective against enemies with high AC. However, the secondary damage doesn’t scale, so Witch Bolt will become obsolete quickly. It’s a good go-to spell at low levels, but I would drop it for something else by level 5 at the latest. The primary use case for Witch Bolt is when you’re facing large single foes where combat will last five rounds or more, which is a rarity since most combats last around 3 rounds.

aganazzar-s-scorcher|eepc.name: Aganazzar’s Scorcher
aganazzar-s-scorcher|eepc.summary: Lines are frequently hard to aim, so you’re likely to only hit 2 creatures in most cases. With that same assumption, compare the 3d8 damage of Aganazzar’s Scorcher to the 3d6 damage of Burning Hands which will also likely only hit two targets. The difference in average damage is just 3 damage, so it’s not enough to justify the higher-level spell slot.

air-bubble|unknown.name: Air Bubble
air-bubble|unknown.summary: Only situationally useful, but the 24-hour duration means that you can cast it before a Long Rest and still enjoy the effect all day.

alter-self|phb.name: Alter Self
alter-self|phb.summary: Two situational effects and a combat buff that you can’t risk using. Until you get something more powerful like Polymorph, Alter Self allows you to handle breathing underwater and can replace the benefits of Disguise Self. If you’re eyeing the natural weapons, remember that True Strike also uses your spellcasting modifier.

arcane-lock|phb.name: Arcane Lock
arcane-lock|phb.summary: Easy to overlook and definitely situational, but very good at its intended purpose. With a permanent duration and the ability to designate creatures who can pass unimpeded and a verbal password, if your party has a permanent base, you should put this on every door and window. You could use this in dungeons to gradually claim space, but the the 25gp material component cost could become annoying.

arcane-vigor|phb.name: Arcane Vigor
arcane-vigor|phb.summary: Casting False Life, even if you only cast it as a level 1 spell, will give you more Temporary Hit Points than a level 2 Arcane Vigor will heal on average. You only add your ability modifier once when using Arcane Vigor, so you’re losing efficiency from your Hit Point Dice in exchange for a panicked burst of healing.

augury|phb.name: Augury
augury|phb.summary: This is my absolute favorite divination spell because it allows players to politely ask their DM for hints. Castable as a ritual with a reusable material component, if you have time you can cast this repeatedly to questions all sorts of decisions.

blindness-deafness|phb.name: Blindness/Deafness
blindness-deafness|phb.summary: Blindness is crippling, especially for enemies who fight at range like archers and spellcasters. It’s also helpful against melee enemies, but Constitution saves tend to be high, so it’s often best to use this on enemies which are more physically frail. Deafness is a mild annoyance.

blur|phb.name: Blur
blur|phb.summary: A great defensive option, but with a short duration and it requires Concentration. If you’re considering Blur, also consider Warding Wind because they have similar effects.

borrowed-knowledge|scoc.name: Borrowed Knowledge
borrowed-knowledge|scoc.summary: A great way to compensate for limited skill proficiencies, Borrowed Knowledge lasts and hour and doesn’t require Concentration, so you can combine it with Enhance Ability to become instantly excellent at any skill. Enhance Ability is more broadly useful because you can cast it on other allies to support them when their best skills come into play, but when there’s a gap in your party’s skillset, you can use this to come to the rescue.

cloud-of-daggers|phb.name: Cloud of Daggers
cloud-of-daggers|phb.summary: 4d4 damage (average 10) isn’t great, and a 5-foot cloud is not a big AOE, but this applies the damage without a save, and you can apply it repeatedly over the spell’s duration. Since you can move this as an Action, you can cast this on your first turn and use it every turn for an entire fight, dealing comparable single-target damage to Magic Missile. Provided that you don’t need Concentration for something else, Cloud of Daggers is exceptionally reliable damage with very little resource cost compared to single-target damage spells like Chromatic Orb, Magic Missile, and Guiding Bolt. There are important trade-offs between each of these spells, but Cloud of Daggers fits comfortably alongside side them at low levels even if you only use it as a direct damage spell. If you can force enemies into the cloud repeatedly, you can abuse it using many of the same tactics as Spirit Guadians. But, if you can’t manage that, 10 guaranteed damage and blocking one square is not worth the spell slot and Concentration. Allies who can grapple, the Push Weapon Mastery, and other forced movement effects will do a lot to make this effective. Holding an enemy in place will guarantee damage every round, but dragging the enemy out and then back in will also trigger the damage, multiplying your damage output depending on how many times your party can do this. The rules for area effects notably don’t require area effects to “snap” to the grid, so you can place Cloud of Daggers in between squares to affect two squares. An effect simply needs to cover 50% or more of a square to affect it, so a single 5-foot cube can affect two adjacent squares. I always play with effects snapping to grids, but RAW this is allowed.ezstandalone.cmd.push(function () { ezstandalone.showAds(181); });

continual-flame|phb.name: Continual Flame
continual-flame|phb.summary: Having reliable, constant light is really nice. Cast this on a shield, a necklace, a weapon, or maybe a whole bunch of different things to guarantee that you always have adequate light without casting light or lighting a torch.

crown-of-madness|phb.name: Crown of Madness
crown-of-madness|phb.summary: “The charmed target must use its Action before moving on each of its turns to make a melee attack”. Unless your enemies are dumb enough to stand next to their ally while they’re clearly under the effects of a harmful spell, you’re going to get maybe one attack out of this.

darkness|phb.name: Darkness
darkness|phb.summary: Situational. Typically you can solve the same challenges with Fog Cloud, and you don’t need to worry about the possibility of enemies being able to see through the effect using magic or by being devils or something. Fog Cloud also has 6 times the duration and a radius 5 feet larger and can be expanded using higher-level spell slots. Darkness’s one unique advantage over Fog Cloud is that it’s portable: you can cast Darkness on a rock and toss it into a room or stick it into your pocket to produce in the middle of combat by using your item interaction to take it out of your pocket rather than spending an Action to cast a spell. The wording for targeting an object is a bit silly. You can’t target an object that you’re holding, so drop something on the ground first. The range also becomes an Emanation from the object’s outer edges, so you could pick an especially large object like a shed or a small house and have Darkness radiate from its outer walls. As per the Emanation rules, you get to pick if the object’s space is included in the Emanation, so you could make the interior of that magically dark house normal. I don’t know why you would, but sometimes you need to perform some wacky magical nonsense.

darkvision|phb.name: Darkvision
darkvision|phb.summary: Fantastic at any level. 8-hour duration, no Concentration, and almost nothing in the game can match 150 feet of Darkvision. If you can afford the spell slots, cast this on everyone in the party who doesn’t get it from their race.

death-armor|frhof.name: Death Armor
death-armor|frhof.summary: The damage is tiny, but the duration is decent and you can cast this on an ally. If you stack this with other options like Fire Shield and Armor of Agathys, you might be able to deal a lot of retaliatory damage. But for 50 gp per casting, I would look for any other source of retaliatory damage before you consider this.

deryan-s-helpful-homunculi|frhof.name: Deryan’s Helpful Homunculi
deryan-s-helpful-homunculi|frhof.summary: Since you can cast this as a Ritual, you’re effectively turning gold into short-lived assistance while crafting an item. This is only useful if you’re leaning into the 2024 rules’ extremely lackluster crafting system, and even then it’s only useful if you’re in a hurry but also have a ton of extramoney lying around.

detect-thoughts|phb.name: Detect Thoughts
